## Copilot

# Parse + Extraction Phases for the 2025 ACC/AHA HBP Guideline PDF

## A Rigorous, Atomic, End-to-End Breakdown

> **Posture: caution over velocity, fidelity over coverage, verbatim over paraphrase.**
> The North Star metric is **zero unattributed claims**. Every extracted fact carries a verifiable anchor (PDF page + bounding box + SHA-256 of the source bytes). Anything we cannot anchor, we do not publish.

This document covers Phases **2 (PARSE)** and **3 (EXTRACT)** of the `cpg-htn-2025-acc-aha` pipeline. Phase 1 (ACQUIRE) is assumed complete: the source PDF, the data supplement, the executive summary, and the 2017 predecessor are pinned by DOI + URL + SHA-256, staged at `.aiwg/cpg-htn/raw/<source-id>/`, and have a W3C PROV `Entity` + ACC/AHA license envelope recorded.

---

## 0. Why the PDF Is Hard (Threat Model for Extraction)

Before designing the pipeline, we name the failure modes. Every downstream control maps to one of these.

| # | Failure mode | Consequence if undetected |
|---|---|---|
| F1 | Multi-column reflow errors (text from col 2 inserted into col 1) | Sentence-level scrambling, false recommendations |
| F2 | Recommendation-box / evidence-table cell mis-association | COR/LOE attached to the wrong recommendation — catastrophic |
| F3 | Footnote / superscript loss or attachment to wrong sentence | Citations and caveats vanish or migrate |
| F4 | Header/footer/running-title bleed into body text | False sentences inserted into recommendation text |
| F5 | Hyphenated line-break joins (`hyper-` `tension` → `hyper tension`) | Token-level corruption, vocabulary lookup failures |
| F6 | Ligatures, smart quotes, soft hyphens, non-breaking spaces | Silent string-mismatch with terminology services |
| F7 | Math/units rendered as glyphs (`≥`, `μ`, `mm Hg` non-breaking) | Threshold misparsing (e.g., `≥130/80`) |
| F8 | Tables with merged cells, rotated text, nested headers | Row/column attribution errors |
| F9 | Figures/flowcharts encoding clinical logic in image-only form | Logic invisible to text extractors |
| F10 | Graphs/charts whose only data live in axes + legend | Numeric thresholds inferred from pixels |
| F11 | Embedded raster images of tables (scanned inserts) | OCR required; OCR errors |
| F12 | Reference list cross-attribution (numeric superscripts) | Provenance to evidence base broken |
| F13 | Page splits mid-recommendation, mid-table, mid-figure | Recommendation truncated; table fragmented |
| F14 | "Recommendation-Specific Supportive Text" interleaved with rec boxes | Text intended as commentary parsed as a recommendation |
| F15 | Synonym/abbreviation drift (BP/SBP/DBP/MAP, AOBP/HBPM/ABPM) | Wrong concept binding |
| F16 | Right-to-left or special-script artifacts in author names | Provenance metadata corruption (low clinical risk, real audit risk) |
| F17 | PDF security / font-subsetting corruption | Silent character substitution |
| F18 | Errata/correction overlays after publication | Stale extraction undetected |
| F19 | LLM hallucination during extraction | Invented or mis-graded recommendations |
| F20 | Encoder/decoder drift across pipeline runs | Non-reproducibility |

Every numbered task below cites which threats it controls.

---

## 1. Architectural Principles (Locked Before Any Code)

1. **Determinism first, ML second.** Any task achievable with deterministic parsers (PDF object model, table grids, regex over normalized Unicode) MUST be done that way. ML and LLMs are used only where determinism cannot reach (image OCR, flowchart logic, ambiguous boundaries) and **always** behind a verification gate.
2. **Three independent extractors per critical artifact.** Every recommendation is independently extracted by (a) a PDF-text pipeline, (b) a layout-vision pipeline, and (c) an OCR pipeline. Disagreement triggers SME review. This is **triple-modal redundancy**, not three tries of the same method.
3. **Verbatim quote requirement.** Each extracted recommendation stores the exact source bytes (UTF-8 NFC) plus its bounding box. Any normalization is stored as a reversible transform, not a destructive edit.
4. **Anchor everything.** Every claim has `{pdf_sha256, page, bbox, char_span, line_span, run_id}`. No anchor → no publication.
5. **Fail-closed.** Ambiguity is escalated, never resolved silently. The default action on any uncertainty is to STOP and route to a named human reviewer.
6. **Reproducibility is a property of the build, not a hope.** Every tool is version-pinned; every run records seeds; every artifact is hashed.
7. **Two-person rule for clinical content.** No recommendation reaches Gate 1 SME review without two independent extractor agreements (or an explicit "needs human" disagreement record).
8. **No paraphrase, ever, in the recommendation text field.** Paraphrase lives in a separate, clearly-labeled `editorial_summary` field that never feeds CQL or CDS Hooks.

---

## 2. Pre-Parse Conditioning (Phase 2.0)

Goal: produce a **canonicalized, fixity-anchored** working set from the raw PDF before any parser sees it. Controls F5, F6, F17, F18, F20.

### Task 2.0.1 — Fixity and integrity verification
- **Inputs:** `raw/<source-id>/hbp-2025.pdf`, `raw/<source-id>/hbp-2025-supplement.pdf`, `raw/<source-id>/hbp-2025-execsummary.pdf`, manifest entries from Phase 1.
- **Actions:**
  1. Re-compute SHA-256 of each file; compare against manifest. Mismatch → BLOCK build; emit a `Provenance` event and stop.
  2. Verify PDF signature/structure with `qpdf --check` and `pdfcpu validate`. Any structural complaint → BLOCK and surface to operator.
  3. Strip nothing. Make a working copy at `work/<run-id>/01-fixity-ok/` with original filenames; original `raw/` is immutable.
- **Exit gate:** all three files pass; report `01-fixity.json` written.

### Task 2.0.2 — Errata / version drift watch
- **Actions:**
  1. Re-resolve the publisher DOI; capture HTTP headers, `Last-Modified`, ETag, current PDF SHA at the source URL.
  2. If publisher SHA differs from manifest SHA → BLOCK with a `version-drift` report; do not auto-update.
  3. Query the journal's errata/correction feed (CrossRef `relation: is-corrected-by` + publisher errata RSS where available); record any hits.
- **Exit gate:** drift report written; build proceeds only if SHA matches and no unreviewed errata are open.
- **Threats controlled:** F18, F20.

### Task 2.0.3 — PDF normalization (non-destructive)
- **Actions:**
  1. Run `qpdf --linearize --object-streams=disable` to produce a re-streamed copy at `work/<run-id>/02-normalized.pdf`. This stabilizes object ordering for downstream extractors without altering content.
  2. Embed all fonts via `mutool clean -d` if any font is referenced but not embedded (otherwise glyph-to-Unicode mapping can fail silently — F17).
  3. Compute and store: page count, page sizes, font inventory, embedded image inventory, ToUnicode CMap presence per font.
- **Exit gate:** every font has a ToUnicode CMap **or** a documented exception with OCR fallback flagged. No exceptions silently accepted.

### Task 2.0.4 — Page rasterization for vision pipelines
- **Actions:**
  1. Render each page at 300 DPI (PNG, lossless) to `work/<run-id>/03-pages-300dpi/page-NNNN.png`. Also render at 600 DPI for any page later flagged as containing fine-grained tables or figures.
  2. Record per-page rendering metadata (renderer version, DPI, color profile).
- **Exit gate:** raster set complete; SHA manifest written.

### Task 2.0.5 — Tooling and version pinning
- Lock and record SHA / version of every tool used: `pdfminer.six`, `pdfplumber`, `PyMuPDF` (`mutool`/`fitz`), `qpdf`, `pdfcpu`, `Camelot`, `Tabula`, `unstructured`, `Marker`, `Nougat`, `LayoutParser`, `Detectron2`/`PaddleOCR`/`Surya`, `Tesseract` + LangData, `presidio-analyzer`, spaCy `en_core_med7_lg`, OpenCV, the LLM model + version, the embedding model + version. Recorded into `manifest.tools.lock` and reproduced into PROV.

---

## 3. Phase 2 — PARSE

Phase 2 produces a **structured, anchored intermediate representation** (`SAIR`, defined in §3.7) that downstream extraction (Phase 3) consumes. Phase 2 does **not** decide what is a recommendation; it decides what is a paragraph, a column, a cell, a footnote, a figure, a caption.

### 3.1 Document segmentation and layout analysis

#### Task 2.1.1 — Logical structure tree from PDF tags (if present)
- **Actions:** Read tagged-PDF structure tree (StructTreeRoot) via PyMuPDF if the publisher embeds tags. Capture as a candidate `LogicalTree-A`.
- **Why:** When present, tagged PDFs are the highest-fidelity source of structure (controls F1, F4, F8, F13).
- **If absent:** mark `LogicalTree-A = null` and rely entirely on layout vision.

#### Task 2.1.2 — Layout detection (vision pipeline)
- **Actions:**
  1. Run a layout model (PubLayNet-trained Detectron2 or Surya) over each 300-DPI page raster; output bounding boxes with classes: `title`, `text`, `list`, `table`, `figure`, `caption`, `header`, `footer`, `page-number`, `running-title`, `footnote`, `equation`.
  2. Run a second, independent layout detector (PaddleOCR-Layout or LayoutLMv3) and capture its boxes.
  3. Compute per-region IoU between the two detectors. Regions with IoU ≥ 0.85 and matching class → `agree`. IoU < 0.85 or class disagreement → `disputed-layout`.
- **Exit gate:** ≥ 98% of body-text regions in `agree`. Disputed regions queued for §3.6 reconciliation.
- **Threats controlled:** F1, F4, F8.

#### Task 2.1.3 — Column model
- **Actions:** From `agree` text regions per page, infer the column count by k-means on x-centroids; classify each page as 1-col, 2-col, or mixed. Persist column polygons.
- **Exit gate:** column model present for every page.
- **Threats controlled:** F1.

#### Task 2.1.4 — Header/footer/running-title removal
- **Actions:** Identify repeated regions across ≥ 30% of pages with the same y-band and similar text; mark as `chrome` and exclude from body text. Persist them separately (still anchored) for audit.
- **Threats controlled:** F4.

#### Task 2.1.5 — Reading-order resolution
- **Actions:** For each page, compute reading order via XY-cut on the column model, then refine with the LayoutReader heuristic; produce an ordered list of regions per page. Persist alternative orderings; flag pages where two methods disagree on > 5% of region transitions.
- **Threats controlled:** F1, F13.

### 3.2 Text extraction at the glyph level

#### Task 2.2.1 — Glyph-faithful text extraction
- **Actions:**
  1. Use PyMuPDF's `get_text("rawdict")` to get glyph-level (not word-level) data with bbox, font, size, color per glyph.
  2. Apply ToUnicode CMap. Any glyph without a ToUnicode mapping is recorded with its `cid:NNN` placeholder and routed to OCR fallback for that span.
- **Threats controlled:** F6, F17.

#### Task 2.2.2 — Unicode normalization (reversible)
- **Actions:**
  1. Convert to NFC; record the NFD↔NFC delta map per character span so reverse mapping is possible.
  2. Replace soft hyphens (U+00AD), zero-width joiners, non-breaking spaces only when the substitution is recorded; never silently.
  3. Keep ligatures (`ﬁ`, `ﬂ`) as logical sequences (`fi`, `fl`) but store the original code point and offset.
- **Threats controlled:** F5, F6.

#### Task 2.2.3 — Hyphenation / line-break repair
- **Actions:**
  1. Detect end-of-line hyphens. If the joined token exists in (a) the medical lexicon (UMLS preferred terms within HTN scope), (b) the SNOMED/RxNorm cache, or (c) a general English dictionary, join. Otherwise keep both forms and emit a `hyphen-uncertain` flag for §3.6 review.
- **Threats controlled:** F5.

#### Task 2.2.4 — Symbol and unit normalization
- **Actions:**
  1. Detect threshold expressions (`≥`, `≤`, `<`, `>`, `±`, `–` em/en dashes used as ranges). Store both the original glyph and its canonical operator.
  2. Detect units: `mm Hg`, `mmHg`, `mm/Hg`, `mEq/L`, `mg`, `g/day`, `mL/min/1.73 m^2`, `µg`, `mcg`. Store original and bind to UCUM canonical form. Mismatches go to §3.6.
- **Threats controlled:** F7.

#### Task 2.2.5 — Footnote and superscript association
- **Actions:**
  1. Identify superscript glyphs (font size delta vs. baseline + y-offset).
  2. Match each superscript token to the in-page footnote whose marker matches and whose region class is `footnote`.
  3. Bind the resulting `footnote-ref` to the *originating sentence span*, not the page.
  4. Output unresolved superscripts as `footnote-orphan` for §3.6.
- **Threats controlled:** F3, F12.

#### Task 2.2.6 — Multi-engine text reconciliation
- **Actions:**
  1. Run, in parallel, three text extractors: PyMuPDF (glyph), `pdfminer.six` (text+layout), and `Marker`/`Nougat` (vision-language for academic PDFs).
  2. Align outputs at the sentence level; compute per-sentence Levenshtein and Jaccard similarities.
  3. Sentences with all three pairwise similarities ≥ 0.98 → `text-consensus`. Otherwise → `text-disputed` (route to §3.6).
- **Threats controlled:** F1, F5, F6, F11, F17.

### 3.3 Tables — recommendation boxes, evidence tables, drug tables

ACC/AHA recommendations are typically presented in **structured boxes with a COR column, an LOE column, and a recommendation-text column**, often followed by **"Recommendation-Specific Supportive Text"** paragraphs. Drug tables and evidence-summary tables also appear. We extract these with a dedicated, multi-engine, schema-aware path.

#### Task 2.3.1 — Table region candidate generation
- **Actions:**
  1. Combine layout-model `table` boxes with ruling-line detection from `pdfplumber` (vector lines) and OpenCV line detection on rasters.
  2. Union the candidates; persist as `table-candidate` regions.
- **Threats controlled:** F8, F11.

#### Task 2.3.2 — Multi-engine table extraction
- **Actions:** For each candidate, run all of:
  1. `Camelot` lattice mode (for ruled tables).
  2. `Camelot` stream mode (for whitespace-ruled tables).
  3. `Tabula` (lattice + stream).
  4. `pdfplumber` `extract_table` with custom horizontal/vertical line strategy.
  5. A vision-language extractor (Marker / TableMaster) on the rasterized region.
- Persist all five candidate parses with their cell bboxes.

#### Task 2.3.3 — Cell-level reconciliation
- **Actions:**
  1. Align the five candidate grids by row/col header text; compute majority vote per cell.
  2. Cells where ≥ 4 of 5 agree → `cell-consensus`. Cells where 3 of 5 → `cell-quorum` (logged). Cells where < 3 of 5 agree → `cell-disputed` (route to §3.6).
- **Threats controlled:** F8, F13.

#### Task 2.3.4 — Recommendation-box schema detection
- **Actions:**
  1. Detect ACC/AHA recommendation boxes by (a) presence of a header row containing the strings `COR` and `LOE` (or `Class of Recommendation` / `Level of Evidence`), and (b) a third "Recommendations" column.
  2. Validate each row's COR cell against the closed enum `{I, IIa, IIb, III: No Benefit, III: Harm}`. Validate LOE against `{A, B-R, B-NR, C-LD, C-EO}`. Any value outside the enum → `enum-violation` (escalate; never auto-correct).
  3. Capture the recommendation text **verbatim** (NFC, with reversible-transform metadata) plus its bounding box.
- **Threats controlled:** F2, F8, F14.

#### Task 2.3.5 — Recommendation-Specific Supportive Text association
- **Actions:**
  1. The paragraphs immediately following a recommendation box, before the next recommendation box or section heading, are candidate `supportive-text` blocks for that recommendation.
  2. Confirm via heading regex (`Recommendation-Specific Supportive Text`, or section formatting cue) and reading-order continuity.
  3. Persist supportive text as a separate field; **never merge with the recommendation text**.
- **Threats controlled:** F14.

#### Task 2.3.6 — Drug and lab tables
- **Actions:**
  1. For tables whose headers indicate drug class, dose, or laboratory thresholds, validate header text against expected vocabulary (RxNorm ingredient class names; LOINC analyte families).
  2. Persist with explicit row schema; do not flatten merged-cell ranges.
- **Threats controlled:** F8.

### 3.4 Figures, flowcharts, graphs, charts, diagrams

These often encode clinical logic that the body text only references. We treat them as *first-class evidence* but never as *primary* clinical truth without a corresponding body-text or table assertion.

#### Task 2.4.1 — Figure detection and isolation
- **Actions:** Use layout-detector `figure` regions; raster-crop at 600 DPI; persist as `figures/<page>-<seq>.png` with bbox.

#### Task 2.4.2 — Caption association
- **Actions:** Captions are the nearest text region below or beside the figure with a `Figure NN.` lead. Persist caption text + anchor + figure pairing. Captions whose number does not match any figure → `caption-orphan` (escalate).

#### Task 2.4.3 — Figure type classification
- **Actions:** Classify each figure into `flowchart`, `bar-chart`, `line-chart`, `forest-plot`, `nomogram`, `algorithm-diagram`, `anatomical`, `photograph`, `other` using a vision classifier.

#### Task 2.4.4 — Flowcharts and algorithm diagrams (logic-bearing)
- **Actions:**
  1. Run a diagram-parsing pipeline: shape detection (rectangles, diamonds, arrows) via OpenCV + `pix2struct`/`Donut`/`Florence-2` to recover node text.
  2. Build a directed graph of decision nodes and edges; render as DOT and as a JSON graph keyed to node bounding boxes.
  3. Cross-validate every edge by a second, independent VLM extraction. Edges that disagree → `flowchart-disputed`.
  4. **Hard rule:** the flowchart graph is **only** an aid; any clinical decision derived from a flowchart must also have a body-text or recommendation-box anchor. If it does not, the flowchart-only fact is held as `awaiting-corroboration` and never enters CQL.
- **Threats controlled:** F9.

#### Task 2.4.5 — Graphs and charts (numeric content)
- **Actions:**
  1. Use a chart-parsing model (`Deplot`, `MatCha`, `ChartQA`-tuned) to extract axes, legend, series, and data points.
  2. Cross-check extracted numbers against any table or text in the same section that names the same quantities. If the chart's numbers contradict the table or text, prefer the **table or text** and flag the chart as `chart-discrepancy`.
- **Threats controlled:** F10.

#### Task 2.4.6 — Embedded raster tables / scanned inserts
- **Actions:** Apply OCR pipeline (§3.5) to the cropped region; route output back through §3.3 with a `source: ocr-on-raster` flag.
- **Threats controlled:** F11.

#### Task 2.4.7 — Figure→body-text cross-reference resolution
- **Actions:** For every body-text reference like "Figure 3" or "see Algorithm 2", confirm that the named figure exists; resolve to a `figure-id`. Unresolved references → escalate.

### 3.5 OCR fallback (only where required)

#### Task 2.5.1 — OCR triggers
- OCR is invoked only when (a) glyphs lack ToUnicode, (b) a region is rasterized within a figure, or (c) text-engine reconciliation flags `text-disputed` and the raster is the tiebreaker.

#### Task 2.5.2 — Multi-engine OCR
- **Actions:** Run `Tesseract` (LSTM, English + medical dictionary), `PaddleOCR`, and `Surya` on the region. Reconcile by character-level majority vote with confidence weighting.

#### Task 2.5.3 — OCR confidence gating
- **Actions:** Per-region average confidence < 0.95 → `ocr-low-confidence`; route to §3.6 (human transcription) and never feed extraction without resolution.
- **Threats controlled:** F11, F17.

### 3.6 Disagreement reconciliation queue (the parse-time human-in-the-loop)

A **single queue** receives every flagged item: `disputed-layout`, `text-disputed`, `cell-disputed`, `enum-violation`, `caption-orphan`, `flowchart-disputed`, `chart-discrepancy`, `ocr-low-confidence`, `hyphen-uncertain`, `footnote-orphan`, `unit-mismatch`.

- **Actions:** Each item is rendered with the source raster, the candidate parses, and the bounding box. A trained operator (medical editor + biomedical informaticist) accepts, edits with rationale, or escalates to the SME panel.
- **Two-person rule:** Any change that affects a recommendation, COR, LOE, threshold, drug name, or population scope requires a second reviewer.
- **No silent resolutions.** Every queue action emits a `Provenance` event linking before-state, after-state, reviewer identity, timestamp, and rationale.

### 3.7 The Structured Anchored Intermediate Representation (SAIR)

The output of Phase 2 is a single, schema-validated JSON document plus side-car files. Schema (abridged):

```yaml
sair:
  document_id: <uuid>
  source:
    pdf_sha256: <hex>
    doi: <doi>
    publisher: ACC/AHA
    publication_date: <iso>
  pages:
    - page_number: 12
      size: { w: 612, h: 792 }
      column_model: 2col
      regions:
        - region_id: r-12-007
          class: text|table|figure|caption|footnote|chrome
          bbox: [x0, y0, x1, y1]
          reading_order_index: 7
          provenance: { extractor_consensus: text-consensus|cell-consensus|... }
          content:
            text:
              raw_utf8_nfc: "..."
              char_spans: [[start, end, page, bbox], ...]
              footnote_refs: ["fn-12-3", ...]
              normalization_log: [ ... reversible transforms ... ]
            table:
              headers: [...]
              rows: [[ {value, cell_bbox, consensus}, ... ], ...]
              schema_detected: acc-aha-recommendation-box | drug-table | evidence-table | other
            figure:
              file: figures/12-2.png
              caption_id: cap-12-2
              type: flowchart|bar-chart|...
              graph: { nodes: [...], edges: [...] }   # if logic-bearing
              chart_data: { series: [...], axes: {...} }   # if numeric
  flagged_items: [ ... pointers into the regions ... ]
  tools_lock: { ... pinned versions ... }
  run_id: <uuid>
```

Validation:
- Every `region_id` referenced anywhere must exist.
- Every `text` region with `acc-aha-recommendation-box` schema must have COR ∈ enum and LOE ∈ enum.
- Every `flagged_items` entry must be resolved or have an open queue ticket.

### 3.8 Phase 2 DQA gates (must all pass to advance)

| Gate | Criterion |
|---|---|
| **G2-A** Coverage | 100% of body-text regions have `text-consensus` or a resolved queue entry |
| **G2-B** Recommendation-box integrity | 100% of detected recommendation boxes have COR/LOE within enum and verbatim text captured |
| **G2-C** Figure caption pairing | 100% of figures paired to a caption or escalated |
| **G2-D** Footnote attachment | 100% of superscripts resolved to a footnote or escalated |
| **G2-E** Reading-order stability | ≥ 99% of region transitions agree across two ordering methods, or resolved |
| **G2-F** Reproducibility | A re-run of Phase 2 from the same inputs yields identical SAIR SHA-256 (modulo timestamps in metadata) |
| **G2-G** Tooling lockfile | Present, signed, all versions pinned |

Any failure → BLOCK; nothing in Phase 3 starts until Phase 2 is green.

---

## 4. Phase 3 — EXTRACT

Phase 3 reads the SAIR and produces **typed clinical knowledge records** that downstream phases (terminology binding, FHIR structuring, CQL authoring) consume. Phase 3 is where atomic recommendations, PICO decompositions, BP thresholds, drug rules, contraindications, secondary-HTN triggers, and special-population modifiers come into being.

The phase ends at **Gate 1 (SME extraction review)** which is non-overridable.

### 4.1 Recommendation candidate construction

#### Task 3.1.1 — Candidate emission from recommendation boxes
- **Source of truth:** SAIR regions with `schema_detected: acc-aha-recommendation-box`.
- **Actions:**
  1. For each row of every recommendation box, emit a candidate `RecommendationDraft`:
     - `recommendation_id`: deterministic from `(pdf_sha256, page, row_bbox)`.
     - `cor`: verbatim, validated against the closed enum.
     - `loe`: verbatim, validated against the closed enum.
     - `text_verbatim`: NFC-normalized verbatim content (with reversible transforms recorded).
     - `text_bbox`, `page`.
     - `supportive_text_ids`: pointers into the supportive-text blocks identified in Task 2.3.5.
     - `references`: footnote-resolved citation IDs (Task 2.2.5).
     - `section_path`: derived from the section headings stack at this position in the document outline.
- **No paraphrase.** No edits. Verbatim only.
- **Threats controlled:** F2, F14, F19.

#### Task 3.1.2 — Section-context capture
- **Actions:** For each `RecommendationDraft`, capture the chain of section headings (e.g., `7. Treatment > 7.3 Special Populations > 7.3.4 Pregnancy`). This becomes a feature for population scoping in §4.4 but is **not** a substitute for explicit population text in the recommendation itself.

#### Task 3.1.3 — Independent re-extraction (vision pipeline)
- **Actions:** Run a layout-vision LLM (e.g., Florence-2 / Donut / GPT-class VLM) over the *raster crop* of each recommendation box and emit an independent `RecommendationDraft-V`. Compare to the SAIR-derived draft.
- **Decision rule:** Identical (modulo whitespace/case in COR/LOE labels) → `extraction-consensus`. Any difference → `extraction-disputed` and route to §4.10.
- **Threats controlled:** F2, F19.

#### Task 3.1.4 — Independent re-extraction (OCR pipeline)
- **Actions:** Run OCR over the same raster crop and emit `RecommendationDraft-O`. Compare to A and V.
- **Three-way consensus:** All three agree on COR, LOE, and text similarity ≥ 0.99 → `triple-consensus`. Otherwise → escalate.
- **Threats controlled:** F11, F17, F19.

### 4.2 Atomicity decomposition

ACC/AHA recommendation rows often bundle several atomic clinical assertions (e.g., "In adults with X, lifestyle and pharmacologic therapy are recommended; thiazide-type diuretics, ACE inhibitors, ARBs, or CCBs are first-line."). Atomicity is required so that each computable rule maps to exactly one CQL branch.

#### Task 3.2.1 — Atomicity policy
- A unit is **atomic** when it can be expressed as a single (subject, action, modifier-set, condition-set, source-anchor) tuple without losing meaning.
- Atomic decomposition **never** changes wording; it **only** splits using rule-based sentence segmentation plus an LLM proposer that operates on the verbatim text and is required to return spans (start/end character offsets into `text_verbatim`) — not new prose.

#### Task 3.2.2 — Decomposition workflow
- **Actions:**
  1. Run a rule-based clause segmenter (semicolon-and-conjunction-aware, list-aware) on `text_verbatim`.
  2. Run an LLM with a strict tool schema that **must** return `[ { start, end, kind } ]` spans where `kind ∈ {atomic-recommendation, qualifier, exclusion, monitoring, citation}`. The LLM cannot return free text.
  3. Validate each span as a contiguous substring of `text_verbatim`. Any non-substring output → reject the LLM response, retry once, then escalate.
  4. Run a second LLM (different family) with the same schema; require span-level agreement ≥ 0.95 (Jaccard over character offsets).
- **Threats controlled:** F19.

#### Task 3.2.3 — Inheritance
- Each atomic unit inherits the parent recommendation's COR/LOE, references, and source anchor. Inheritance is recorded explicitly; it is never assumed.
- If an atomic unit appears to require a different COR/LOE than the parent, that is by definition a parsing error and goes to escalation, not auto-correction.

### 4.3 PICO decomposition (HTN-typed)

#### Task 3.3.1 — Population (P)
- **Closed enum (HBP-2025-specific):** `general-adult`, `older-adult-≥65`, `older-adult-≥75`, `pregnant`, `postpartum`, `ckd-G1..G5/A1..A3`, `t2d`, `t1d`, `post-stroke`, `hfref`, `hfpef`, `hfmref`, `cad`, `black-adult`, `resistant-htn`, `secondary-htn-suspected`, `urgency`, `emergency`.
- **Action:** Map population text spans to the enum; multi-population recs produce one record per population. Anything not mapping → escalate.

#### Task 3.3.2 — Intervention (I), Comparator (C), Outcome (O)
- **Action:** Same span-anchored LLM tool schema as §4.2; outputs are spans, classified into I/C/O. Comparator may legitimately be `none-stated`; outcomes may be implicit and that fact is recorded as `outcome-implicit-by-source`.

#### Task 3.3.3 — PICO completeness gate
- **Action:** Each atomic recommendation must have a non-null Population and Intervention. C and O may be `none-stated` only when the source itself does not state them; that condition must be cross-checked by the second LLM.

### 4.4 Numeric and structured fact extraction

#### Task 3.4.1 — BP threshold extractor
- **Action:** Regex + grammar over `text_verbatim` and supportive text to capture every threshold (`SBP ≥ 130 mm Hg`, `SBP/DBP ≥ 130/80 mm Hg`, `< 140/90 mm Hg`, etc.). Store each as:
  ```yaml
  bp_threshold:
    component: SBP|DBP|MAP|SBP/DBP
    operator: ge|le|gt|lt|range
    value:
      low_mmHg: <int>
      high_mmHg: <int|null>
    measurement_context: in-office|hbpm|abpm-daytime|abpm-nighttime|abpm-24h|aobp|unspecified
    source_span: [start, end]
  ```
- **Cross-check:** Independently re-extract via the second LLM with the same schema; require exact-equal value structure. Mismatch → escalate.
- **Threats controlled:** F7, F19.

#### Task 3.4.2 — Drug-class and ingredient extractor
- **Action:** Map mentioned drugs / classes to RxNorm ingredient classes (`thiazide-or-thiazide-like`, `ace-inhibitor`, `arb`, `dihydropyridine-ccb`, `non-dihydropyridine-ccb`, `mra`, `beta-blocker-cardioselective`, `beta-blocker-non-selective`, `alpha-blocker`, `central-alpha2-agonist`, `direct-renin-inhibitor`, `arni`, `loop-diuretic`, `potassium-sparing-diuretic`).
- **Hard rule:** Brand names are not stored in the computable fields; only ingredient classes. Brand names appearing in source go to a `mentions[]` field for audit only.
- **Threats controlled:** F15.

#### Task 3.4.3 — Contraindications and hard-blocks
- **Action:** Extract negative recommendations (`COR III: Harm` and explicit "should not", "is not recommended", "is potentially harmful"). Pregnancy denylist (RAAS inhibitors, MRA, direct renin inhibitor) is **detected and tagged as hard-block**, never as soft warning, regardless of how the source phrases it. The parser does not invent the hard-block class — it asserts it only when an explicit "should not" / "Class III: Harm" anchor exists in source.

#### Task 3.4.4 — Monitoring requirements
- **Action:** Extract follow-up cadence, lab monitoring (K+, Cr/eGFR, BP, glucose), self-measurement requirements; bind to LOINC where applicable.

#### Task 3.4.5 — Resistant-HTN definition components
- **Action:** Capture (a) number of agents, (b) inclusion of a diuretic, (c) maximally-tolerated-dose qualifier, (d) BP target context. Persist as a structured `resistant_htn_definition` record sourced from the specific recommendation row(s).

#### Task 3.4.6 — Secondary-HTN triggers
- **Action:** Each trigger (primary aldosteronism, renovascular disease, pheochromocytoma, OSA, CKD, drug-induced) is captured with (a) trigger condition span, (b) recommended workup span, (c) source anchor. The trigger is not allowed to be invented from clinical knowledge — it must be span-anchored to the source.

#### Task 3.4.7 — Risk-engine binding
- **Action:** Where the source invokes risk thresholds (e.g., a CVD risk threshold for treatment), record the explicit risk engine cited (PREVENT) and the threshold value. PCE references are recorded with a `legacy: true` flag and never feed CQL.

### 4.5 Cross-document deduplication and consolidation

#### Task 3.5.1 — Within-document dedup
- **Action:** When the same recommendation appears in (a) the main guideline, (b) the executive summary, and (c) the supplement, consolidate into a single canonical recommendation with all three anchors recorded. Differences in wording → escalate; the main guideline is the prime source on resolution.

#### Task 3.5.2 — Predecessor mapping (2017 → 2025)
- **Action:** For each 2025 recommendation, identify the closest 2017 predecessor by section-path + topic + intervention; tag with `relation ∈ {unchanged, revised, new, removed}`. **This is advisory metadata only**; clinical validity is governed by the 2025 source alone. SME confirms each mapping at Gate 1.

### 4.6 Reference and citation resolution

#### Task 3.6.1 — Reference list parsing
- **Action:** Parse the reference list using a citation parser (`anystyle`, GROBID); resolve to DOIs/PMIDs where possible.

#### Task 3.6.2 — In-text citation linking
- **Action:** For each footnote-resolved superscript on a recommendation, link to the parsed reference; emit a `Provenance.entity` chain `recommendation → cites → reference`.

### 4.7 PHI and copyright safety in extraction outputs

#### Task 3.7.1 — PHI scrub on every text field
- **Action:** Run Presidio + spaCy `med7` + regex (US identifiers + addresses + phone + email + MRN patterns) on every extracted text field. Any hit → BLOCK and route to a separate hazard handler. The 2025 HBP Guideline is not expected to contain PHI; if any is detected, that fact itself is a quality alarm, not just a redaction.

#### Task 3.7.2 — Copyright envelope check
- **Action:** Compute the verbatim quotation footprint per page and per total document; compare against the publisher's allowed envelope. If any threshold is exceeded, escalate to legal review before publication. This control sits in Phase 9 of the overall pipeline but is *measured* at the end of Phase 3.

### 4.8 Output: typed knowledge records

Phase 3 emits, for every atomic recommendation, a record validated against `recommendation-record-htn.yaml`. Required fields:

```yaml
recommendation_id: <stable-id>
parent_recommendation_id: <id|null>
text_verbatim: "..."
editorial_summary: null   # always null at end of Phase 3; Phase 5 may add, never replace
acc_aha_cor: I|IIa|IIb|III: No Benefit|III: Harm
acc_aha_loe: A|B-R|B-NR|C-LD|C-EO
section_path: ["7", "7.3", "7.3.4 Pregnancy"]
pico:
  population: { code: pregnant, span: [s,e] }
  intervention: { spans: [...], drug_classes: [...], non_pharm: [...] }
  comparator: { kind: none-stated|placebo|active|lifestyle, spans: [...] }
  outcome: { kind: stated|implicit-by-source, spans: [...] }
bp_thresholds: [ ... ]
drug_rules: { allowlist: [...], denylist: [...], first_line: [...] }
contraindications: [ ... ]
monitoring: [ ... ]
risk_engine: { name: PREVENT, threshold: ... }   # if applicable
references: [ { ref_id, doi|pmid|null, span } ]
predecessor_2017: { id|null, relation: unchanged|revised|new|removed }
anchors:
  pdf_sha256: <hex>
  page: <int>
  bbox: [x0, y0, x1, y1]
  char_spans: [ [start, end] ]
provenance:
  extractors: [ a, v, o ]
  consensus: triple-consensus|escalated-and-resolved
  reviewer_signoffs: [ ... at Gate 1 ... ]
  run_id: <uuid>
```

### 4.9 Phase 3 DQA gates (must all pass to reach Gate 1)

| Gate | Criterion |
|---|---|
| **G3-A** Recommendation completeness | Number of `RecommendationDraft`s emitted equals number of recommendation-box rows detected in Phase 2 (no losses, no extras) |
| **G3-B** Triple-consensus rate | ≥ 99.0% of recommendations at `triple-consensus`; the rest must each have a documented escalation |
| **G3-C** Atomicity validity | Every atomic unit is a contiguous substring of its parent `text_verbatim`; no fabricated text |
| **G3-D** PICO completeness | Every atomic recommendation has Population and Intervention; nulls only when explicitly `none-stated` and re-confirmed |
| **G3-E** Numeric fact reproducibility | Independent re-runs produce identical `bp_thresholds` and `drug_rules` structures byte-for-byte |
| **G3-F** Reference linkage | ≥ 99% of in-text citations resolve to a parsed reference list entry; the rest escalated |
| **G3-G** PHI clean | Zero PHI detections in any output field |
| **G3-H** Copyright envelope | Verbatim quotation footprint ≤ publisher-agreed threshold |
| **G3-I** Predecessor mapping | Every 2025 recommendation has a predecessor mapping (including `new`/`removed`) and SME-acknowledgable rationale |
| **G3-J** Tools lockfile | Identical to Phase 2 lockfile or amended via change-controlled diff |

### 4.10 Escalation queue (extraction-time)

Mirrors §3.6 but with extraction-specific item types: `extraction-disputed`, `pico-unmapped`, `threshold-mismatch`, `drug-class-unmapped`, `predecessor-uncertain`, `denylist-without-anchor`, `risk-engine-ambiguous`, `reference-unresolved`. **Two-person rule applies to every clinical-content edit.** All resolutions emit `Provenance` events.

### 4.11 Gate 1 — SME extraction review (non-overridable)

#### Composition
Two board-certified specialists from the panel defined in the framework spec:
- **Hypertension specialist** (cardiology / nephrology / ASH-certified) — required reviewer for every recommendation.
- **Domain co-reviewer** (pharmacology for drug-rule-bearing recs; MFM for pregnancy; geriatrics for older-adult; primary care for implementation/measurement; clinical informaticist as cross-cutting).

#### Workflow
1. The reviewer interface presents, side-by-side: the source PDF region (raster) at the recommendation's bbox; the verbatim text; the atomic units; the PICO mapping; the BP thresholds; the drug rules; the predecessor relation; the consensus state.
2. Each reviewer independently chooses `accept`, `accept-with-edit`, `reject-rework`, or `escalate-panel`.
3. Disagreement → automatic escalation to the panel chair.
4. **No batch acceptance.** Each recommendation is signed individually.
5. Each acceptance emits a `Provenance` event recording reviewer identity, credential evidence, timestamp, decision, and rationale.

#### Exit conditions
- 100% of recommendations have two independent acceptances **and** zero open escalations.
- The Gate 1 register is signed by the panel chair.
- The combined SAIR + extracted records are sealed by SHA-256 and become the input to Phase 4 (terminology binding).

---

## 5. Reproducibility, Audit, and Change Control

- **Run identity.** Every Phase 2 + Phase 3 run produces a `run_id` and a `manifest.run.lock` recording: input SHAs, tool versions, model versions and seeds, prompts, schema versions, queue resolutions, reviewer identities. The lockfile is part of the published artifact.
- **Re-run determinism.** A re-run with identical inputs and lockfile must produce byte-identical SAIR (modulo timestamps recorded with `now-skew-tolerance`) and identical extracted records. This is a release gate, not an aspiration.
- **Change control.** Any prompt, schema, model, or tool change requires a change-controlled diff with regression evaluation against the **golden set** (§7).

## 6. Logging, Telemetry, and Provenance

- All operations emit structured logs (JSONL) with: `run_id`, `step_id`, `region_id`, `recommendation_id`, `tool`, `decision`, `confidence`, `escalation_state`.
- A W3C PROV-O bundle is generated per run, with `Activity` for each atomic step, `Entity` for each artifact (SAIR sections, recommendation records, gate decisions), and `Agent` for tools and humans.
- A FHIR `Provenance` resource is generated per recommendation at the end of Phase 3 and updated through the rest of the pipeline. SME signatures appear as `Provenance.signature` entries.

## 7. Validation Strategy: the Golden Set and the Adversarial Set

### Golden set
- A panel-curated, manually-validated subset of the 2025 HBP Guideline: e.g., 30 recommendations spanning every domain (diagnosis, lifestyle, general pharm, special populations including pregnancy, resistant, secondary, urgency/emergency, implementation), 5 tables, 5 figures (including at least 2 flowcharts), 3 graphs.
- Curated by the SME panel from the source PDF in a separate authoring environment, not by the pipeline. Treated as ground truth.

### Pipeline acceptance metrics against the golden set
| Metric | Target |
|---|---|
| Recommendation recall (no missed rec rows) | 100% |
| Recommendation precision (no spurious recs) | 100% |
| COR/LOE exact match | 100% |
| Verbatim text exact match (NFC) | 100% |
| Atomic unit span agreement (Jaccard) | ≥ 0.98 |
| BP-threshold structural match | 100% |
| Drug-class mapping accuracy | 100% |
| Pregnancy denylist anchor recall | 100% |
| Flowchart graph node/edge F1 against SME graph | ≥ 0.95, with no clinical edge missing |
| Reference resolution rate | ≥ 99% |
| End-to-end re-run determinism | byte-identical SAIR + records |

### Adversarial set
- Synthetic perturbations applied to copies of curated source pages: column merges, hyphenation noise, font substitution, ligature replacement, soft-hyphen injection, mild raster rotation, OCR of an otherwise text-extractable page, table-rule erosion, footnote re-numbering. The pipeline must either still produce identical extractions or escalate; silent miscounting is a release blocker.

## 8. Caveats, Open Questions, Honest Limits

1. **Source-text licensing.** The "verbatim quotation" approach relies on a quote-extent envelope agreed with ACC/AHA and the publishing journal. If the envelope forbids storing full verbatim text, the approach changes: we store only the SHA-anchored bbox + a content-addressed pointer, and verbatim text lives only in the reviewer's signed-off transient buffer. **This must be settled before Phase 3 starts.**
2. **Flowchart parsing is the highest-residual-risk step.** Vision models on diagrams remain imperfect. Mitigation: any clinical decision derived only from a flowchart is held in `awaiting-corroboration` until a body-text or recommendation-box anchor is found; otherwise it does not enter CQL or CDS Hooks.
3. **OCR-only regions** are inherently lower-confidence; the 0.95 confidence threshold is non-negotiable, and any OCR-only recommendation requires explicit Gate 1 reviewer acknowledgement that the rec is OCR-derived.
4. **Errata-after-publish.** A separate Phase 0 watcher must continue to run after publication; an erratum triggers re-parse of affected pages, not a quiet rebuild.
5. **PCE vs. PREVENT.** The framework decision (ADR-HTN-001 D5) treats PREVENT as canonical. If during extraction we find recommendations that explicitly invoke PCE, they are recorded faithfully and surfaced at Gate 1; the SME panel decides whether they propagate to CQL or are documented as out-of-scope-by-design. The pipeline never silently substitutes one risk engine for the other.
6. **The pipeline is a force multiplier, not an oracle.** The published artifact's clinical warrant is the named SME signatures and the medical-director attestation. Extraction quality, however high, does not transfer that warrant.

---

## 9. End-to-End Sequence (atomic checklist)

1. Phase 1 ACQUIRE complete; manifest signed.
2. **Phase 2.0** Pre-parse conditioning: 2.0.1 fixity → 2.0.2 drift → 2.0.3 normalize → 2.0.4 raster → 2.0.5 lockfile.
3. **Phase 2.1** Layout: 2.1.1 tags (if any) → 2.1.2 dual-detector layout → 2.1.3 columns → 2.1.4 chrome removal → 2.1.5 reading order.
4. **Phase 2.2** Text: 2.2.1 glyph extraction → 2.2.2 NFC + reversible normalization → 2.2.3 hyphen repair → 2.2.4 symbols/units → 2.2.5 footnotes → 2.2.6 multi-engine reconciliation.
5. **Phase 2.3** Tables: 2.3.1 candidates → 2.3.2 multi-engine extraction → 2.3.3 cell consensus → 2.3.4 recommendation-box schema → 2.3.5 supportive text → 2.3.6 drug/lab tables.
6. **Phase 2.4** Figures: 2.4.1 isolation → 2.4.2 captions → 2.4.3 typing → 2.4.4 flowcharts → 2.4.5 graphs/charts → 2.4.6 raster tables → 2.4.7 cross-references.
7. **Phase 2.5** OCR fallback only where required; multi-engine reconciliation; ≥ 0.95 confidence or escalate.
8. **Phase 2.6** Reconcile flagged items; two-person rule; PROV events.
9. **Phase 2 DQA gates G2-A..G2-G must all be green.**
10. **Phase 3.1** Recommendation candidates: SAIR-derived → vision re-extraction → OCR re-extraction → triple-consensus or escalate.
11. **Phase 3.2** Atomicity decomposition with span-only LLM tool calls and dual-LLM agreement.
12. **Phase 3.3** PICO decomposition into HTN-typed enums.
13. **Phase 3.4** Numeric and structured fact extraction: BP thresholds, drug rules, contraindications/hard-blocks (denylist-with-anchor), monitoring, resistant definition, secondary triggers, risk engine.
14. **Phase 3.5** Within-document dedup; predecessor 2017 mapping (advisory).
15. **Phase 3.6** Reference list and citation linking.
16. **Phase 3.7** PHI scrub; copyright envelope measurement.
17. **Phase 3 DQA gates G3-A..G3-J must all be green.**
18. **Gate 1** Two-SME independent signoff per recommendation; Provenance recorded.
19. Sealed Phase 2+3 artifact set is handed to Phase 4 (terminology binding).

---

## 10. What I Would Build First (smallest credible vertical slice)

If you want a step-zero proof, build the slice that exercises every threat at minimum scale:

1. Pick **3 pages**: one body-text-heavy page, one with a recommendation box + supportive text, and one with a flowchart and a graph.
2. Implement Phase 2.0 + 2.1 + 2.2 + 2.3.4 + 2.4.4 + 2.4.5 + 2.5 with the multi-engine reconciliation as specified.
3. Implement Phase 3.1 + 3.2 + 3.4.1 + 3.4.2 + 3.4.3 against those pages.
4. Curate the 3-page golden set with the SME panel.
5. Run the acceptance metrics in §7.
6. Only then expand to the full document.

This slice will surface — and force resolution of — the publisher-licensing question, the flowchart-corroboration policy, and the SME bandwidth required for Gate 1. None of those should be discovered late.

# parse-acc-aha-recbox

Parse ACC/AHA-formatted recommendation boxes, their Recommendation-Specific Supportive Text, and adjacent evidence/drug tables from the conditioned 2025 HBP Guideline working set into the Structured Anchored Intermediate Representation (SAIR). Every cell is established via multi-engine consensus, every COR/LOE value is validated against a closed enum, and every emitted region is anchored to `(pdf_sha256, page, bbox, char_span)`.

This skill is the source-of-truth producer for downstream `extract-recommendation-cor-loe`. It does **not** decide what is "a recommendation"; it deterministically reconstructs the rows, cells, and adjacent paragraphs that recommendation extraction will consume. It refuses to publish ambiguous parses and routes every dispute to the parse-time reconciliation queue.

Posture: **caution over velocity, fidelity over coverage, verbatim over paraphrase.** Fail-closed on every unresolved disagreement. Two-person rule on every queue resolution that touches a recommendation row, COR, LOE, threshold, drug, or population scope.

## When to Use

Invoke this skill **after** the pre-parse conditioning skills (`parse-prepare-pdf`, `parse-detect-layout`, `parse-extract-text`) have produced:

- A fixity-verified, normalized working PDF at `work/<run-id>/02-normalized.pdf`
- A 300 DPI page raster set at `work/<run-id>/03-pages-300dpi/`
- Layout regions with dual-detector consensus per page
- Glyph-level text with reversible Unicode normalization
- A column model and a resolved reading order per page
- Footnote and superscript anchors

Typical trigger points:

- First parse of a freshly acquired 2025 HBP Guideline PDF (full document run)
- Re-parse of a page range after errata detection or tooling-lockfile change
- Targeted re-run of disputed regions following Phase 2 reconciliation queue resolutions

Do **not** invoke this skill on raw, unconditioned PDFs. Skipping pre-parse conditioning bypasses the controls that this skill assumes.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sair-path` | yes | — | Path to the in-progress SAIR JSON document at `work/<run-id>/sair.json`. Must already contain Phase 2.0–2.2 outputs and a valid `tools_lock`. The skill writes back into this document atomically. |
| `--pages <range>` | no | `all` | Page range to process (e.g., `1-12,40-44`). Defaults to every page whose layout regions include a `table` candidate. |
| `--engines <list>` | no | `camelot-lattice,camelot-stream,tabula-lattice,tabula-stream,pdfplumber,vlm-tablemaster` | Comma-separated table extraction engines to run in parallel. At least four must be enabled; the skill refuses to run with fewer. |
| `--dpi <int>` | no | `300` | Re-render DPI for vision-language fallback on disputed cells. `600` is auto-elevated for any region flagged as fine-ruled or merged-cell. |
| `--strict` | no | `true` | Fail-closed on any enum violation, cell-disputed state, or schema mismatch. Setting `--strict false` is **never permitted** for clinical-content regions; the flag exists only for parser development against fixtures. |
| `--resume` | no | `false` | Resume from the last persisted region in `sair.json`. Required when re-running after a queue resolution. |

## Operation

### 1. Preflight

1. Validate `sair-path` against `schemas/sair.yaml`. Fail-fast if `tools_lock`, `pages[].regions`, `column_model`, or `reading_order_index` are missing for any page in scope.
2. Confirm `pdf_sha256` in `sair.source` matches the on-disk normalized PDF; mismatch → BLOCK.
3. Confirm at least four table extraction engines are configured and reachable; otherwise BLOCK.
4. Load the closed enums:
   - `COR ∈ { I, IIa, IIb, III: No Benefit, III: Harm }`
   - `LOE ∈ { A, B-R, B-NR, C-LD, C-EO }`
   These are loaded from `schemas/acc-aha-grading.yaml` and never inlined.

### 2. Table region candidate generation (encodes §3.3 Task 2.3.1)

For each in-scope page:

1. Take the union of:
   - Layout-detector `table` boxes (from Phase 2.1.2 dual-detector consensus).
   - Vector ruling lines from `pdfplumber` (horizontal + vertical line clusters).
   - OpenCV-detected line segments on the 300 DPI raster (Hough + morphology).
2. Merge overlapping candidates whose IoU ≥ 0.6 into a single `table-candidate` region.
3. Persist each candidate with: `region_id`, `page`, `bbox`, `evidence: [layout|vector|raster]`, and `provisional_class: unknown`.
4. Threats controlled: F8 (table structure), F11 (raster-only tables), F13 (page-split tables — flagged when a candidate touches the bottom margin and a sibling candidate touches the top of the next page).

### 3. Multi-engine extraction (encodes §3.3 Task 2.3.2)

For each `table-candidate`, run **all** configured engines independently:

1. `camelot-lattice` (ruled tables).
2. `camelot-stream` (whitespace-ruled tables).
3. `tabula-lattice` and `tabula-stream`.
4. `pdfplumber.extract_table` with explicit `vertical_strategy` and `horizontal_strategy` derived from the candidate's vector lines.
5. A vision-language extractor (`Marker` / `TableMaster` / Donut-table) on the rasterized region at the selected DPI.

For each engine output, persist:

- The full grid with per-cell text, cell `bbox`, and engine name.
- The engine's confidence score (where exposed).
- A `parse_log` entry with engine version (from `tools_lock`).

Engines run in parallel; failures of one engine do not block the others, but at least four must succeed per candidate. Otherwise the candidate is escalated as `engine-quorum-failure`.

### 4. Cell-level reconciliation (encodes §3.3 Task 2.3.3)

For each candidate that produced ≥ 4 successful parses:

1. Align grids by row and column header text using normalized-string matching (NFC, case-folded, whitespace-collapsed). Header alignment failures themselves are escalated as `header-alignment-failure`.
2. For every aligned cell, compute the majority value across engines after the same normalization.
3. Classify each cell:
   - `cell-consensus` when ≥ 4 of 5 engines agree.
   - `cell-quorum` when exactly 3 of 5 agree (logged; advances only for non-clinical-content cells).
   - `cell-disputed` when < 3 of 5 agree.
4. Any `cell-disputed` state in a row that is later classified as `acc-aha-recommendation-box` (see §5) is a **hard escalation**; the row does not enter the SAIR's recommendation-box channel until resolved.
5. Cells where original NFC text differs from the consensus form retain both: `text_consensus` (the canonical value) and `text_variants` (per-engine outputs with bboxes).

### 5. Recommendation-box schema detection (encodes §3.3 Task 2.3.4)

For each reconciled table:

1. Detect the ACC/AHA recommendation-box schema by all of the following, evaluated together:
   - The header row (after consensus) contains tokens matching `^COR$` or `^Class of Recommendation$` **and** `^LOE$` or `^Level of Evidence$`, with exact, case-insensitive match modulo NFC.
   - A third column exists whose header matches `^Recommendation(s)?$`.
   - The number of body rows is ≥ 1 and each body row has non-empty cells in all three columns after consensus.
2. If the schema matches, set `schema_detected: acc-aha-recommendation-box` on the table region. If only some heuristics match, set `schema_detected: acc-aha-recommendation-box-candidate` and escalate as `schema-partial-match`.
3. For each body row of a confirmed recommendation box, validate:
   - The COR cell value, after NFC + whitespace-collapse, is exactly one member of the COR enum. Any deviation → `enum-violation`. **Never auto-correct.** Examples like `IIA`, `2a`, `Class IIa`, or stray footnote markers in the COR cell all escalate.
   - The LOE cell value is exactly one member of the LOE enum. Identical fail-closed handling.
4. Capture the recommendation cell's text **verbatim** (NFC, with the reversible normalization log retained) along with:
   - The cell `bbox` and the per-character `char_span` covering that bbox in the underlying glyph stream.
   - Any superscripts present, resolved to footnote IDs from Phase 2.2.5. Unresolved superscripts → `footnote-orphan` and the row is held.
5. Emit one `recommendation-box-row` SAIR record per validated row, with:
   - `region_id` (deterministic from `pdf_sha256 + page + row_bbox`).
   - `cor`, `loe`, `text_verbatim`, `cell_bboxes`, `char_spans`, `footnote_refs`, `section_path` (resolved from the heading stack at this position in the reading order).
   - `consensus_state: cell-consensus`.
   - `parent_table_region_id`.

Threats controlled: F2 (cell mis-association), F8 (merged/rotated cells), F14 (supportive text mistaken for recommendation).

### 6. Recommendation-Specific Supportive Text association (encodes §3.3 Task 2.3.5)

For each emitted recommendation-box row:

1. Walk forward in reading order from the recommendation box. Collect contiguous text regions (class `text`) until one of these stop conditions:
   - The next region is another `acc-aha-recommendation-box`.
   - A section heading is encountered (heading-stack depth changes).
   - A figure or non-supportive table appears.
   - The reading-order continuity check fails (column or page break without a continuation cue).
2. Confirm the candidate block is supportive text using both:
   - A heading regex in the immediately-preceding text region matching `Recommendation-Specific Supportive Text` (case-insensitive, hyphen-tolerant), **or**
   - The block immediately follows the recommendation box in reading order with no intervening heading and the typographic style matches the supportive-text body style learned for this document.
3. Persist as a separate `supportive_text` field on the row, with its own `region_ids`, `char_spans`, and `footnote_refs`. **Never merge supportive text into the recommendation text.**
4. Where a supportive block could plausibly bind to two adjacent recommendations (e.g., a single block following two recommendation boxes that share a numbered group), bind it to **all** plausible parents and flag `supportive-multi-bind` for §8 reconciliation.

### 7. Drug, lab, and evidence tables (encodes §3.3 Task 2.3.6)

For tables that did **not** match the recommendation-box schema:

1. Classify against the additional schemas in `schemas/acc-aha-table-schemas.yaml`:
   - `drug-table` when header tokens include any of `Drug`, `Class`, `Dose`, `Daily Dose`, `Usual Dose`, `Comments` and the body rows match RxNorm ingredient class headers within the HTN scope.
   - `lab-table` when headers match LOINC analyte families (e.g., `K+`, `Cr`, `eGFR`, `Aldosterone`, `Renin`).
   - `evidence-table` when headers include `Trial`, `N`, `Comparator`, `Outcome`, `Effect`.
   - `other` otherwise.
2. Validate header text against the controlled vocabulary for that schema. Header tokens not in the controlled vocabulary → `header-unmapped` and the table is held until §8 review.
3. Preserve merged-cell ranges explicitly with `cell_span: { row_start, row_end, col_start, col_end }`. Do **not** flatten merged cells; downstream skills depend on the merge geometry.
4. Persist row schemas explicitly. Multi-line cells retain internal newlines; bullet markers and en/em dashes used as range separators are preserved verbatim with normalization metadata.

### 8. Reconciliation queue handoff

For every flagged item — `engine-quorum-failure`, `header-alignment-failure`, `cell-disputed`, `enum-violation`, `schema-partial-match`, `footnote-orphan`, `supportive-multi-bind`, `header-unmapped`, `page-split-table` — emit a queue entry containing:

- The raster crop of the disputed region at 600 DPI.
- All engine outputs for affected cells, side-by-side.
- The proposed parse and the specific failure reason.
- A `decision_required` field listing the exact options (e.g., for `enum-violation`: `accept-as-typo`, `correct-and-record`, `defer-to-SME-panel`).

The skill never resolves these itself. Two-person rule applies to every clinical-content resolution. Each resolution emits a W3C PROV `Activity` and an updated `consensus_state` on the affected row.

### 9. SAIR write-back

1. Acquire an exclusive lock on `sair.json`.
2. Append/upsert all new and updated regions atomically.
3. Update `sair.run.steps[]` with this skill's invocation: tool versions, pages processed, engines used, counts of consensus / quorum / disputed cells, counts of recommendation-box rows emitted, queue entries created.
4. Compute and persist a SHA-256 of the SAIR document; record into `sair.fixity.sair_sha256`.
5. Release the lock.

### 10. Determinism and reproducibility

- All engines are version-pinned via `tools_lock`.
- Engine input bytes (cropped page rasters, vector-line strategies) are hashed; identical inputs produce identical outputs across runs (excluding engines that are not deterministic — those are flagged in `tools_lock` as `nondeterministic` and cannot be the sole basis for `cell-consensus`).
- Re-running this skill on the same SAIR with the same parameters and lockfile must produce a byte-identical SAIR section for the in-scope pages, modulo `processed_at` timestamps recorded with `now-skew-tolerance`.

## DQA Gates Enforced By This Skill

| Gate | Condition for advance |
|---|---|
| **G2.3-A** Recommendation-box completeness | Every detected recommendation box on in-scope pages has every row reconciled to `cell-consensus` or escalated. No silent drops. |
| **G2.3-B** Enum strictness | 100% of COR and LOE cells in confirmed recommendation boxes match the closed enums verbatim (NFC, whitespace-collapsed). |
| **G2.3-C** Verbatim capture | 100% of recommendation cells have `text_verbatim` plus reversible normalization log; no paraphrase, no ASCII fold. |
| **G2.3-D** Footnote integrity | 100% of superscripts in recommendation cells are resolved to footnote IDs or escalated. |
| **G2.3-E** Supportive-text disjointness | 0 recommendation rows have supportive text merged into `text_verbatim`. |
| **G2.3-F** Engine quorum | Every advanced row reached `cell-consensus` (≥ 4 of 5 engines). `cell-quorum` rows are not allowed in recommendation boxes. |
| **G2.3-G** Reproducibility | Re-run on identical inputs and lockfile produces byte-identical recommendation-box section in SAIR. |

Failure of any gate → BLOCK. The orchestrator (`flow-hbp-2025-build`) does not proceed to `extract-recommendation-cor-loe` until all gates are green.

## Outputs

- Updated SAIR document at `<sair-path>` containing:
  - Reconciled `table` regions with `schema_detected` set.
  - Per-row `recommendation-box-row` records with COR, LOE, verbatim text, anchors, and supportive-text references.
  - Drug, lab, and evidence tables with explicit row schemas and merged-cell geometry.
- Reconciliation queue entries at `work/<run-id>/queue/parse/recbox/`.
- Per-run report at `reports/parse-recbox-<run-id>.md` with:
  - Counts: pages processed, candidates generated, engines per candidate, consensus distribution, recommendation rows emitted, queue entries opened.
  - Per-page heatmap of disputed cells.
  - Lockfile diff vs. previous run (if any).
- W3C PROV bundle update at `provenance/parse-recbox-<run-id>.jsonld`.
- An `activity.log` append documenting invocation, parameters, gates passed/failed, and operator identity.

## Error Handling

- **Pre-parse outputs missing or stale.** Fail-fast with the missing field path; instruct operator to rerun the relevant Phase 2.0–2.2 skills.
- **PDF SHA mismatch.** BLOCK; emit a `version-drift` event; do not auto-update.
- **Insufficient engines.** BLOCK; surface which engines failed to initialize (binary missing, license check, model unavailable).
- **Enum violation in COR/LOE.** Never auto-correct. Hold the row, escalate to queue, continue with remaining rows.
- **Footnote-orphan.** Hold the row; remaining rows continue.
- **Cell-disputed in recommendation row.** Hold the row; remaining rows continue.
- **Schema partial match.** Persist as `acc-aha-recommendation-box-candidate`; escalate; do not emit recommendation-box rows from it.
- **Engine-side crash mid-page.** Retry once with the same input; on second failure, log the engine as `quorum-failed` for that candidate and continue with remaining engines.
- **SAIR lock contention.** Wait up to a configured timeout, then fail-closed; concurrent writers are not supported on the same SAIR document.

## Examples

```bash
# Full-document first parse over the conditioned 2025 HBP Guideline working set
parse-acc-aha-recbox work/run-2026-04-30/sair.json

# Targeted re-run of pages 40–44 after a queue resolution, resuming from the last persisted region
parse-acc-aha-recbox work/run-2026-04-30/sair.json \
  --pages 40-44 \
  --resume

# Disputed-region re-render at 600 DPI with the vision-language engine emphasized
parse-acc-aha-recbox work/run-2026-04-30/sair.json \
  --pages 12,57 \
  --engines camelot-lattice,camelot-stream,pdfplumber,vlm-tablemaster \
  --dpi 600
```

- `schemas/acc-aha-table-schemas.yaml` — Recommendation-box, drug-table, lab-table, evidence-table schemas with controlled vocabularies.
- `schemas/recommendation-record-htn.yaml` — Downstream target shape; this skill produces the row-level inputs that `extract-recommendation-cor-loe` will populate.

## Authority Boundaries

**Can do**
- Detect, reconcile, and emit recommendation-box rows that meet all DQA gates.
- Persist drug, lab, and evidence tables with explicit row schemas.
- Open reconciliation queue entries on any flagged item.

**Requires approval (queue + two-person rule)**
- Any cell or row resolution affecting COR, LOE, recommendation text, drug, threshold, or population scope.
- Any header-vocabulary mapping not present in the controlled vocabulary file.
- Any acceptance of a `nondeterministic` engine as a basis for consensus.

**Never**
- Paraphrase, ASCII-fold, or otherwise destructively normalize recommendation text.
- Auto-correct an enum violation.
- Advance a row to consensus on fewer than four engine agreements.
- Merge supportive text into recommendation text.
- Operate on a raw, unconditioned PDF.
- Run with `--strict false` against clinical-content regions in production.
