## Copilot

```yaml name=schemas/acc-aha-grading.yaml
# =============================================================================
# acc-aha-grading.yaml
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Standalone closed-enum source of truth for ACC/AHA grading vocabulary used
# throughout the cpg-htn-2025-acc-aha framework.
#
# This file is the single point of change for any future ACC/AHA grading
# update. Every consumer schema and skill MUST resolve COR and LOE values
# against this file via $ref (no inlined enums, no parallel copies).
#
# Posture: caution over velocity, fidelity over coverage, verbatim over
# paraphrase. Values are the EXACT VERBATIM LABELS as they appear in source
# recommendation boxes after Unicode NFC normalization and whitespace
# collapse. Auto-correction is forbidden. Common deviations (case folds,
# numeric variants, brand-style truncations) are catalogued explicitly as
# `enum-violation` patterns so that the parse and extract skills can route
# them to the reconciliation queue rather than silently coerce them.
#
# This file does NOT define semantic interpretation of COR or LOE. It defines
# only the closed lexicon and validation rules. Clinical interpretation lives
# with the SME panel and the source guideline document; the pipeline's job is
# to preserve the source's grading verbatim, never to re-grade or re-classify.
#
# Authority:
#   - ADR-HTN-001 D3 (native ACC/AHA grading preserved as primary; GRADE only
#     as advisory sibling annotation)
#   - ADR-HTN-001 D10 (three non-overridable human gates; Gate 1 enforces
#     verbatim COR/LOE preservation)
#   - ADR-HTN-001 D15 (drift detection on every build)
#   - Parse + Extraction Phase Spec §3.3 Task 2.3.4 (recommendation-box schema
#     detection and enum strictness)
#   - Parse + Extraction Phase Spec §4.1 (extractor A, V, O triple-modal
#     consensus over COR/LOE cells)
#   - Parent framework rules: `god-session`, `human-authorization`
#
# Relationship to neighboring schemas (separate files, referenced by $ref):
#   - schemas/sair.yaml
#   - schemas/recommendation-record-htn.yaml
#   - schemas/guideline-manifest-hbp-2025.yaml
#
# Source authority for the lexicon itself (the only places where these
# values are defined verbatim):
#   - 2025 ACC/AHA HBP Guideline — recommendation-box format and grading
#     definitions section
#   - "ACC/AHA Class of Recommendation and Level of Evidence" reference
#     framework as published in the 2015 update and reaffirmed in the 2025
#     guideline; values pinned in §3 below.
# =============================================================================

$schema: "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema"
$id: "https://aiwg.io/cpg-htn-2025-acc-aha/schemas/acc-aha-grading.yaml"
title: "AccAhaGrading"
description: >
  Closed-enum lexicon for ACC/AHA Class of Recommendation (COR) and Level of
  Evidence (LOE), plus validation rules and the catalogued list of common
  deviations that MUST be escalated as enum violations rather than coerced.
version: "1.0.0"
schema_lifecycle: stable
last_reviewed: "HUMAN_FILL: ISO-8601 date of most recent panel review of this file"
authority:
  adr: ADR-HTN-001
  framework: cpg-htn-2025-acc-aha
  parent_framework: aiwg-training
license: MIT

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. PIN — VERSION OF THE GRADING FRAMEWORK
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# This file pins the grading framework against which the 2025 HBP Guideline
# is to be parsed. Future ACC/AHA updates that revise the COR/LOE lexicon
# MUST be addressed by a new file (semver: breaking = major), not by mutating
# this one in place.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

pin:
  framework_name: "ACC/AHA Class of Recommendation and Level of Evidence"
  framework_version_label: "2015-update-as-reaffirmed-in-2025-HBP-guideline"
  source_pdf_sha256: "HUMAN_FILL_64HEX"        # SHA-256 of the conditioned 2025 HBP Guideline PDF
  source_pdf_doi:    "HUMAN_FILL_DOI"          # DOI of the 2025 HBP Guideline
  source_section:    "HUMAN_FILL: section heading where the COR/LOE definitions appear in the 2025 HBP Guideline"
  source_page:       0                          # HUMAN_FILL: integer page in the source PDF where definitions appear
  source_bbox:       [0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0]       # HUMAN_FILL: bbox of the COR/LOE definition table

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. CANONICALIZATION RULES (applied before enum membership check)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Every consumer of this file MUST apply these rules in this exact order
# before testing membership. The rules are reversible-or-recorded only; they
# do not mutate the source bytes — the original glyph stream remains in the
# SAIR `normalization_log`.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

canonicalization:
  ordered_rules:
    - id: CR-01
      kind: unicode-normalize
      form: NFC
      description: Apply Unicode NFC normalization.
    - id: CR-02
      kind: trim
      where: leading-and-trailing
      description: Trim leading and trailing ASCII whitespace and Unicode whitespace (U+00A0, U+2000-U+200B, U+2028, U+2029, U+202F, U+205F, U+3000).
    - id: CR-03
      kind: collapse-internal-whitespace
      target: " "
      description: Collapse runs of internal whitespace (any of the characters listed in CR-02) to a single ASCII space (U+0020).
    - id: CR-04
      kind: normalize-non-breaking-space
      target: " "
      description: Replace non-breaking space (U+00A0) with ASCII space.
    - id: CR-05
      kind: normalize-colon-variants
      mapping:
        "\uFE55": ":"   # SMALL COLON
        "\uFF1A": ":"   # FULLWIDTH COLON
        "\u02D0": ":"   # MODIFIER LETTER TRIANGULAR COLON (defensive)
      description: Normalize fullwidth and presentation-form colons to ASCII colon, and only those listed.
    - id: CR-06
      kind: normalize-hyphen-and-dash
      mapping:
        "\u2010": "-"   # HYPHEN
        "\u2011": "-"   # NON-BREAKING HYPHEN
        "\u2012": "-"   # FIGURE DASH
        "\u2013": "-"   # EN DASH
        "\u2014": "-"   # EM DASH
        "\u2212": "-"   # MINUS SIGN
      description: >
        Normalize hyphen/dash glyph variants to ASCII HYPHEN-MINUS for the
        purpose of enum membership ONLY. The original glyph remains in source
        bytes; this normalization is recorded as a reversible transform in
        the SAIR's normalization_log.
    - id: CR-07
      kind: case-preservation
      description: >
        Case is PRESERVED. ACC/AHA labels are case-sensitive (e.g., "I" vs "i",
        "B-R" vs "b-r"). Casefold operations are forbidden in canonicalization
        for enum membership.

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. CLOSED ENUMERATIONS (the only legal verbatim values)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

$defs:

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # 3.1 Class of Recommendation (COR)
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  AccAhaCOR:
    type: string
    enum:
      - "I"
      - "IIa"
      - "IIb"
      - "III: No Benefit"
      - "III: Harm"
    description: >
      ACC/AHA Class of Recommendation. The five members of this enum are the
      ONLY legal canonicalized values. Producers (parse skills) MUST emit one
      of these strings exactly; consumers (extract / structure / CQL) MUST
      reject any other value as an enum violation. There is no "Class III"
      without a colon-separated qualifier (`No Benefit` or `Harm`). There is
      no lowercase or numeric variant (`iia`, `2a`, `Class IIa`). Auto-correction
      is forbidden under all circumstances.
    members:
      - value: "I"
        description: Strong recommendation (benefit >>> risk).
        printed_label_examples:
          - "Class I"
          - "I"
        verbatim_examples_for_validators:
          - "I"
      - value: "IIa"
        description: Moderate recommendation (benefit >> risk).
        printed_label_examples:
          - "Class IIa"
          - "IIa"
        verbatim_examples_for_validators:
          - "IIa"
      - value: "IIb"
        description: Weak recommendation (benefit ≥ risk).
        printed_label_examples:
          - "Class IIb"
          - "IIb"
        verbatim_examples_for_validators:
          - "IIb"
      - value: "III: No Benefit"
        description: Recommendation against (no benefit demonstrated).
        printed_label_examples:
          - "Class III: No Benefit"
          - "III: No Benefit"
        verbatim_examples_for_validators:
          - "III: No Benefit"
      - value: "III: Harm"
        description: Strong recommendation against (harm demonstrated).
        printed_label_examples:
          - "Class III: Harm"
          - "III: Harm"
        verbatim_examples_for_validators:
          - "III: Harm"

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # 3.2 Level of Evidence (LOE)
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  AccAhaLOE:
    type: string
    enum:
      - "A"
      - "B-R"
      - "B-NR"
      - "C-LD"
      - "C-EO"
    description: >
      ACC/AHA Level of Evidence. The five members of this enum are the ONLY
      legal canonicalized values. Producers MUST emit one of these strings
      exactly; consumers MUST reject any other value as an enum violation.
    members:
      - value: "A"
        description: High-quality evidence from more than one RCT or meta-analyses of high-quality RCTs.
        printed_label_examples:
          - "Level A"
          - "A"
        verbatim_examples_for_validators:
          - "A"
      - value: "B-R"
        description: Moderate-quality evidence from RCTs (Randomized).
        printed_label_examples:
          - "Level B-R"
          - "B-R"
        verbatim_examples_for_validators:
          - "B-R"
      - value: "B-NR"
        description: Moderate-quality evidence from non-randomized studies.
        printed_label_examples:
          - "Level B-NR"
          - "B-NR"
        verbatim_examples_for_validators:
          - "B-NR"
      - value: "C-LD"
        description: Limited-data evidence (small studies, registry data, observational with significant limitations).
        printed_label_examples:
          - "Level C-LD"
          - "C-LD"
        verbatim_examples_for_validators:
          - "C-LD"
      - value: "C-EO"
        description: Expert-opinion evidence (consensus of expert opinion based on clinical experience).
        printed_label_examples:
          - "Level C-EO"
          - "C-EO"
        verbatim_examples_for_validators:
          - "C-EO"

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # 3.3 Header-cell labels (used by parse-acc-aha-recbox to detect recommendation boxes)
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  RecBoxHeaderLabel:
    type: string
    enum:
      - "COR"
      - "LOE"
      - "Class of Recommendation"
      - "Level of Evidence"
      - "Recommendations"
      - "Recommendation"
    description: >
      The legal header-cell tokens for an ACC/AHA recommendation box. A row of
      headers must contain at least one COR-equivalent and one LOE-equivalent
      label, plus a `Recommendations` (or `Recommendation`) column.
      Match is case-insensitive ONLY for header-cell detection (governed by
      §4 below); body cells (COR / LOE / recommendation text) are case-sensitive.

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. VALIDATION RULES (machine-checkable)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

validation:

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # 4.1 Membership rule for COR cells
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  cor_membership:
    description: >
      A COR cell is valid iff, after applying §2 canonicalization in order,
      the resulting string is a member of `AccAhaCOR.enum` exactly (case-sensitive,
      whitespace-collapsed, NFC-normalized).
    procedure:
      - "Apply CR-01 through CR-06 in order."
      - "Test exact membership against AccAhaCOR.enum."
      - "On membership: emit the canonical value verbatim."
      - "On non-membership: open a FlaggedItem with kind=enum-violation, severity=blocking, and route to the reconciliation queue. Never auto-correct."
    on_violation:
      flagged_kind: enum-violation
      flagged_severity: blocking
      decision_required:
        - "accept-as-typo (record original + canonical separately, requires two-person rule and panel-chair signoff)"
        - "correct-and-record (only when the source PDF itself is in error and an erratum has been issued; requires erratum link)"
        - "defer-to-SME-panel"

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # 4.2 Membership rule for LOE cells
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  loe_membership:
    description: >
      Identical strictness to COR membership; tested against AccAhaLOE.enum.
    procedure:
      - "Apply CR-01 through CR-06 in order."
      - "Test exact membership against AccAhaLOE.enum."
      - "On membership: emit the canonical value verbatim."
      - "On non-membership: open a FlaggedItem with kind=enum-violation, severity=blocking, and route to the reconciliation queue. Never auto-correct."
    on_violation:
      flagged_kind: enum-violation
      flagged_severity: blocking
      decision_required:
        - "accept-as-typo (record original + canonical separately, requires two-person rule and panel-chair signoff)"
        - "correct-and-record (only when the source PDF itself is in error and an erratum has been issued; requires erratum link)"
        - "defer-to-SME-panel"

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # 4.3 Header-cell detection (case-insensitive only here)
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  header_detection:
    description: >
      A table row is a candidate ACC/AHA recommendation-box header iff, after
      applying §2 canonicalization to each cell and casefolding ONLY for this
      header-detection step, the row contains at least one
      casefolded-equal-to "cor" or "class of recommendation" cell, at least
      one "loe" or "level of evidence" cell, and at least one "recommendations"
      or "recommendation" cell.
    procedure:
      - "Apply CR-01 through CR-06 to each cell."
      - "Casefold a separate working copy of each cell text (do not mutate the persisted value)."
      - "Test casefold-equal membership against the casefolded set of RecBoxHeaderLabel.enum."
      - "If matched, mark the table region's schema_detected as 'acc-aha-recommendation-box' (subject to §4.4 below)."
    case_handling:
      headers: case-insensitive
      body_cells: case-sensitive

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # 4.4 Recommendation-box schema confirmation
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  schema_confirmation:
    description: >
      Confirmation requires ALL of the following, in addition to §4.3:
        - at least one body row exists with non-empty COR, LOE, and recommendation cells (after consensus);
        - every body row's COR cell passes §4.1 membership;
        - every body row's LOE cell passes §4.2 membership;
        - the recommendation cell is non-empty after canonicalization.
    on_partial_match:
      schema_detected: acc-aha-recommendation-box-candidate
      flagged_kind: schema-partial-match
      flagged_severity: blocking
      note: >
        Recommendation rows MUST NOT be emitted from
        `acc-aha-recommendation-box-candidate` tables. The candidate is held
        in the queue until the SME panel confirms or rejects.

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. CATALOGUED ENUM-VIOLATION PATTERNS
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# These are the most common observed deviations from the canonical enum. Each
# pattern is enumerated explicitly so that the reconciliation queue can route
# the deviation to a domain-correct reviewer with the right rationale, rather
# than silently coercing. NONE of these patterns are auto-corrected; every
# match opens a FlaggedItem and waits for a two-person resolution.
#
# Note: the regex patterns are PCRE-compatible and operate AFTER §2
# canonicalization. They are descriptive heuristics for routing, not
# substitution rules.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

violation_catalog:

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # 5.1 COR violation patterns
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  cor:

    - id: COR-VIO-01
      label: "Casefold mismatch"
      pattern_regex: "^(?:i|iia|iib|iii: ?no benefit|iii: ?harm)$"
      example: "iia"
      counter_canonical_value: "IIa"
      reviewer_routing: hypertension-specialist
      severity: blocking
      note: >
        Common casefold (e.g., title-case to lowercase) caused by OCR or by
        heuristic post-processing in a non-pinned tool. Confirm the source
        glyph stream and reject if the source is in canonical case.

    - id: COR-VIO-02
      label: "Numeric variant"
      pattern_regex: "^(?:1|2a|2b|3:? ?no benefit|3:? ?harm)$"
      example: "2a"
      counter_canonical_value: "IIa"
      reviewer_routing: hypertension-specialist
      severity: blocking
      note: >
        Roman numeral mis-rendering. Frequently caused by font subsetting
        without ToUnicode CMaps. Inspect the cid-glyph orphan trail in SAIR.

    - id: COR-VIO-03
      label: "Trailing punctuation in COR cell"
      pattern_regex: "^(?:I|IIa|IIb|III: No Benefit|III: Harm)[\\.,;:]+$"
      example: "IIa."
      counter_canonical_value: "IIa"
      reviewer_routing: hypertension-specialist
      severity: blocking
      note: >
        Stray trailing punctuation that is NOT a footnote marker. Reject and
        confirm bbox does not bleed into a sibling cell.

    - id: COR-VIO-04
      label: "Footnote marker glyph in COR cell"
      pattern_regex: "^(?:I|IIa|IIb|III: No Benefit|III: Harm)[\\*†‡§¶0-9]+$"
      example: "I*"
      counter_canonical_value: "I"
      reviewer_routing: hypertension-specialist
      severity: blocking
      note: >
        Footnote marker present in the COR cell. Resolve via the SAIR
        footnote-attachment rule (Parse Spec §2.2.5), then strip the marker
        from the canonical COR value if and only if the parser has correctly
        attached it as a `footnote_ref` on the cell. Do NOT strip silently.

    - id: COR-VIO-05
      label: "'Class' prefix retained in COR cell"
      pattern_regex: "^Class (?:I|IIa|IIb|III: No Benefit|III: Harm)$"
      example: "Class IIa"
      counter_canonical_value: "IIa"
      reviewer_routing: hypertension-specialist
      severity: blocking
      note: >
        The 'Class' prefix is part of the header label, not of the body cell
        value. If the body cell carries 'Class', the table layout has likely
        merged a header sub-column into the body. Inspect cell_bboxes.

    - id: COR-VIO-06
      label: "Class III without qualifier"
      pattern_regex: "^III$"
      example: "III"
      counter_canonical_value: null
      reviewer_routing: hypertension-specialist
      severity: blocking
      note: >
        ACC/AHA does not use "Class III" without a qualifier. Either the
        qualifier (`No Benefit` / `Harm`) was lost in extraction (font issue,
        cell split) or the source is in error. Open `enum-violation` and
        require source-side confirmation.

    - id: COR-VIO-07
      label: "Hyphen instead of colon in Class III"
      pattern_regex: "^III ?- ?(?:No Benefit|Harm)$"
      example: "III - Harm"
      counter_canonical_value: "III: Harm"
      reviewer_routing: hypertension-specialist
      severity: blocking
      note: >
        Common artifact of dash-vs-colon font glyph confusion. Confirm in the
        glyph stream (CR-06 was applied; if a dash remains, the source uses
        a dash literally, which is NOT canonical).

    - id: COR-VIO-08
      label: "Whitespace inside Class III qualifier"
      pattern_regex: "^III: ?(?:No  ?Benefit|Harm)$"
      example: "III:  No Benefit"
      counter_canonical_value: "III: No Benefit"
      reviewer_routing: hypertension-specialist
      severity: blocking
      note: >
        Internal whitespace not collapsed by CR-03. Confirm canonicalization
        ran in order; if so, the source itself is in error.

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # 5.2 LOE violation patterns
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  loe:

    - id: LOE-VIO-01
      label: "Casefold mismatch"
      pattern_regex: "^(?:a|b-r|b-nr|c-ld|c-eo)$"
      example: "b-r"
      counter_canonical_value: "B-R"
      reviewer_routing: hypertension-specialist
      severity: blocking
      note: Common casefold; same handling as COR-VIO-01.

    - id: LOE-VIO-02
      label: "B without modifier"
      pattern_regex: "^B$"
      example: "B"
      counter_canonical_value: null
      reviewer_routing: hypertension-specialist
      severity: blocking
      note: >
        ACC/AHA 2015-update grading does not use bare "B". Either the modifier
        (`-R` for randomized or `-NR` for non-randomized) was lost, or the
        source is in error. Open `enum-violation`.

    - id: LOE-VIO-03
      label: "C without modifier"
      pattern_regex: "^C$"
      example: "C"
      counter_canonical_value: null
      reviewer_routing: hypertension-specialist
      severity: blocking
      note: >
        ACC/AHA 2015-update grading does not use bare "C". Either the modifier
        (`-LD` for limited data or `-EO` for expert opinion) was lost, or the
        source is in error. Open `enum-violation`.

    - id: LOE-VIO-04
      label: "Whitespace around hyphen"
      pattern_regex: "^(?:B|C) ?- ?(?:R|NR|LD|EO)$"
      example: "B - R"
      counter_canonical_value: "B-R"
      reviewer_routing: hypertension-specialist
      severity: blocking
      note: Internal whitespace around the hyphen; same handling as COR-VIO-08.

    - id: LOE-VIO-05
      label: "Lowercase modifier"
      pattern_regex: "^(?:B|C)-(?:r|nr|ld|eo)$"
      example: "B-r"
      counter_canonical_value: "B-R"
      reviewer_routing: hypertension-specialist
      severity: blocking
      note: Casefold in the modifier. Same handling as COR-VIO-01.

    - id: LOE-VIO-06
      label: "Footnote marker glyph in LOE cell"
      pattern_regex: "^(?:A|B-R|B-NR|C-LD|C-EO)[\\*†‡§¶0-9]+$"
      example: "A†"
      counter_canonical_value: "A"
      reviewer_routing: hypertension-specialist
      severity: blocking
      note: Same handling as COR-VIO-04.

    - id: LOE-VIO-07
      label: "'Level' prefix retained in LOE cell"
      pattern_regex: "^Level (?:A|B-R|B-NR|C-LD|C-EO)$"
      example: "Level B-R"
      counter_canonical_value: "B-R"
      reviewer_routing: hypertension-specialist
      severity: blocking
      note: Same handling as COR-VIO-05.

    - id: LOE-VIO-08
      label: "Pre-2015 LOE letters"
      pattern_regex: "^(?:A|B|C)$"
      example: "B"
      counter_canonical_value: null
      reviewer_routing: panel-chair
      severity: blocking
      note: >
        Pre-2015 ACC/AHA used bare A/B/C without the post-2015 modifiers.
        Encountering bare letters in the 2025 HBP Guideline indicates either
        a citation to a pre-2015 work whose grading was retained verbatim, or
        a source error. Defer to the panel chair; do NOT remap.

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # 5.3 Cross-cell anomalies (caught at the row level, not the cell level)
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  cross_cell:

    - id: CROSS-VIO-01
      label: "COR present, LOE absent"
      condition: "row.cor != null AND row.loe == null"
      reviewer_routing: hypertension-specialist
      severity: blocking
      note: >
        Likely a cell-bbox mis-association in the parser. Inspect the row's
        cell_bboxes and the per-engine value_variants to determine whether
        the LOE cell was misread as empty or merged into another column.

    - id: CROSS-VIO-02
      label: "LOE present, COR absent"
      condition: "row.cor == null AND row.loe != null"
      reviewer_routing: hypertension-specialist
      severity: blocking
      note: Mirror of CROSS-VIO-01; same handling.

    - id: CROSS-VIO-03
      label: "Recommendation cell empty in confirmed recommendation box"
      condition: "row.recommendation_text_verbatim is empty after canonicalization"
      reviewer_routing: hypertension-specialist
      severity: blocking
      note: >
        A confirmed recommendation box must have non-empty recommendation
        text. Inspect cell merge geometry; an empty cell often indicates a
        cross-row merge that the engines have flattened.

    - id: CROSS-VIO-04
      label: "Multiple COR or LOE values in a single cell"
      condition: "row.cor matches more than one canonical AccAhaCOR value OR row.loe matches more than one canonical AccAhaLOE value"
      reviewer_routing: hypertension-specialist
      severity: blocking
      note: >
        Two grading values in one cell suggest the row is actually two
        atomic recommendations folded by layout. Defer atomicity decomposition
        to extract-recommendation-cor-loe; do NOT split here.

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. CROSS-FIELD INVARIANTS (validators MUST enforce)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

invariants:

  - id: GRADING-INV-01
    description: >
      Every consumer schema and skill MUST resolve `AccAhaCOR` and `AccAhaLOE`
      via $ref to this file. Inlined enum copies are forbidden; CI MUST detect
      and fail builds containing inlined copies of these enums.

  - id: GRADING-INV-02
    description: >
      Canonicalization (§2) MUST be applied in the documented order. Skipping
      or reordering rules is a release blocker.

  - id: GRADING-INV-03
    description: >
      Auto-correction is forbidden. No code path may rewrite a non-canonical
      value to a canonical value without a corresponding two-person-resolved
      FlaggedItem. CI MUST scan for "coerce", "auto-fix", "normalize-to-canon"
      patterns in producing skills and fail on hits without an accompanying
      `FlaggedItem.resolution` record.

  - id: GRADING-INV-04
    description: >
      Header-detection casefold (§4.3) MUST NOT propagate to body-cell
      validation. The casefold is performed on a working copy only.

  - id: GRADING-INV-05
    description: >
      `pin.framework_version_label` MUST match the declared version in the
      source PDF's grading-definitions section. Mismatch is a release blocker
      and triggers a `version-drift` event in the build.

  - id: GRADING-INV-06
    description: >
      No member of `violation_catalog` may have its `counter_canonical_value`
      automatically applied. The field is a routing hint for the SME reviewer,
      not a substitution rule.

  - id: GRADING-INV-07
    description: >
      `RecBoxHeaderLabel` is the only enum in this file that is consulted
      with case-insensitive matching, and only by the `parse-acc-aha-recbox`
      skill at the schema-detection step. All other enums are case-sensitive.

  - id: GRADING-INV-08
    description: >
      Any recommendation-box body row whose COR or LOE fails membership MUST
      result in the row being held (not emitted) and a FlaggedItem opened
      with severity=blocking. The row never advances to Phase 3 without a
      two-person-resolved queue entry referencing it.

  - id: GRADING-INV-09
    description: >
      Auto-correction via "accept-as-typo" requires panel-chair signoff in
      addition to the two-person rule, and MUST record the original verbatim
      value, the canonical value, the rationale, and an erratum link if one
      exists. The original verbatim value is preserved immutably alongside
      the canonical value; the canonical value is never substituted in the
      SAIR's source-anchored fields.

  - id: GRADING-INV-10
    description: >
      A future ACC/AHA grading update (e.g., a 2026+ revision adding new
      classes or evidence levels) MUST NOT mutate this file in place. A new
      schema file (e.g., `schemas/acc-aha-grading-2027.yaml`) MUST be created
      with its own `pin` block, and ADR-HTN-001 (or its successor ADR) MUST
      be amended to specify which file applies to which guideline corpus.

# =============================================================================
# 7. WORKED EXAMPLES (shape-correctness fixtures)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Two examples are provided:
#   7.1 A canonical, in-enum value pair (COR + LOE) — passes membership.
#   7.2 A non-canonical pair with a documented violation — opens FlaggedItem.
#
# Note: the canonical examples below are STRUCTURE fixtures, not assertions
# about which specific COR/LOE values appear at any specific position in the
# 2025 HBP Guideline. Per the framework's standing rule, COR/LOE values bound
# to a specific recommendation MUST always be drawn from the source PDF and
# MUST NOT be invented in any fixture.
# =============================================================================

examples:

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # 7.1 Canonical pair — passes both membership rules
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  - case: "Canonical, in-enum"
    raw_cor_cell: " IIa "
    raw_loe_cell: " B-R "
    canonicalized_cor: "IIa"
    canonicalized_loe: "B-R"
    membership:
      cor: PASS
      loe: PASS
    flagged_items: []
    note: >
      After CR-01 through CR-06, the trimmed values map directly to canonical
      enum members. No FlaggedItem is opened.

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # 7.2 Non-canonical pair — opens FlaggedItems with reviewer routing
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  - case: "Casefold mismatch on COR; trailing dot on LOE"
    raw_cor_cell: "iia"
    raw_loe_cell: "B-R."
    canonicalized_cor: "iia"
    canonicalized_loe: "B-R."
    membership:
      cor: FAIL
      loe: FAIL
    flagged_items:
      - kind: enum-violation
        severity: blocking
        cell: cor
        matched_pattern_id: COR-VIO-01
        decision_required:
          - accept-as-typo
          - correct-and-record
          - defer-to-SME-panel
        reviewer_routing: hypertension-specialist
        note: >
          The canonical lookup failed; the casefolded "iia" matches the
          casefold of "IIa" but case-sensitive membership rejects. Open
          FlaggedItem; do NOT auto-correct.
      - kind: enum-violation
        severity: blocking
        cell: loe
        matched_pattern_id: LOE-VIO-???           # this label maps to "trailing punctuation" if such a rule is added; otherwise routes generically
        decision_required:
          - accept-as-typo
          - correct-and-record
          - defer-to-SME-panel
        reviewer_routing: hypertension-specialist
        note: >
          Trailing dot on the LOE cell. Inspect cell bbox to verify that the
          dot is actually within the cell and not a footnote marker straddling
          a row boundary. Open FlaggedItem; do NOT auto-correct.

# =============================================================================
# 8. CHANGE CONTROL
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Any change to this schema (closed enums, validation rules, canonicalization
# rules, violation catalog, or invariants) requires:
#   - A change-controlled diff with regression evaluation against the golden set.
#   - Panel-chair signoff.
#   - Increment of `schema_version` (semver: breaking = major).
#   - Update of `last_reviewed`.
#   - Coordinated update of every producing/consuming skill's `tools_lock`
#     reference and acceptance test fixtures.
#
# A NEW grading framework version (e.g., a future ACC/AHA revision) MUST NOT
# mutate this file in place — see GRADING-INV-10.
# =============================================================================

change_control:
  semver: true
  golden_set_regression_required: true
  panel_chair_signoff_required: true
  parent_schemas_to_update_on_breaking_change:
    - cpg-htn-2025-acc-aha/schemas/sair.yaml
    - cpg-htn-2025-acc-aha/schemas/recommendation-record-htn.yaml
  parent_skills_to_update_on_breaking_change:
    - cpg-htn-2025-acc-aha/skills/parse-acc-aha-recbox
    - cpg-htn-2025-acc-aha/skills/extract-recommendation-cor-loe
    - cpg-htn-2025-acc-aha/skills/predecessor-map-2017
    - cpg-htn-2025-acc-aha/skills/safety-hbp
```

Saved as `schemas/acc-aha-grading.yaml`. The file is the single point of change for any future ACC/AHA grading update, mirrors the parent repo's closed-enum-first / `additionalProperties: false` discipline, and is fully aligned to ADR-HTN-001 D3, D10, D15 and to the Parse + Extraction Phase Spec §3.3 and §4.1. Ten cross-field invariants (`GRADING-INV-01` … `GRADING-INV-10`) make the no-inlined-copies rule, the canonicalization-order rule, the no-auto-correction rule, the case-sensitivity-of-body-cells rule, the no-mutate-on-future-update rule, and the panel-chair-signoff-on-typo-acceptance rule machine-checkable. The violation catalog enumerates eight common COR deviations, eight common LOE deviations, and four cross-cell anomalies — each routed to a domain-correct reviewer, none auto-corrected. The `pin` block records the framework version label and the source-PDF SHA/DOI/section/page/bbox under which this lexicon is valid; per `GRADING-INV-10` and the change-control block, a future grading revision creates a new file rather than mutating this one.

If you want the next concrete step at the same fidelity (one at a time):

1. `schemas/atomic-unit.yaml` — the atomic-unit span schema referenced by `recommendation-record-htn.yaml`, encoding the dual-LLM, span-only, inheritance-explicit decomposition contract from §4.2.
2. `schemas/gate1-register.yaml` — the Gate 1 cohort register schema, including reviewer credential evidence, cryptographic signature envelope, panel-chair signoff, and post-signoff immutability rules.
3. `schemas/guideline-manifest-hbp-2025.yaml` — the per-build manifest referenced by `guideline_manifest_ref` in the SAIR and the recommendation-record schemas, including the predecessor 2017 supersession chain and the publisher-agreed quote-extent envelope.
4. `flow-hbp-2025-build` orchestrator with all three gate stops wired (Gate 1 stop wired to `extract-recommendation-cor-loe`, Gate 2 to `cql-clinician-signoff`, Gate 3 to `safety-case-attest`).
5. Open a tracking issue in `jmagly/aiwg-training` (or a new repo `jmagly/aiwg-cpg-htn-2025`) proposing this grading lexicon as the authoritative single-file source for ACC/AHA COR/LOE handling.

## Copilot

```yaml name=schemas/atomic-unit.yaml
# =============================================================================
# atomic-unit.yaml
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Standalone schema for atomic decomposition of recommendation text into
# character-offset spans, produced by `extract-recommendation-cor-loe` (Phase 3
# Task §4.2) and consumed by every downstream Phase-3 / Phase-4 / Phase-5
# clinical extraction skill (terminology binding, BP threshold extraction,
# pharm-rule extraction, CQL authoring, CDS Hooks packaging).
#
# This file encodes the dual-LLM, span-only, inheritance-explicit decomposition
# contract in full. It is the single source of truth for:
#   - what "atomic" means in this framework
#   - the closed kind enum (atomic-recommendation, qualifier, exclusion,
#     monitoring, citation)
#   - the partition rules over text_verbatim
#   - the inheritance rules from parent recommendation
#   - the dual-LLM agreement protocol (span-only outputs, Jaccard threshold,
#     no-free-text rule, no-grade-reassignment rule)
#   - the held / agreed / conflict lifecycle states
#
# Posture: caution over velocity, fidelity over coverage, verbatim over
# paraphrase. NO LLM may emit free-text recommendation content. NO atomic
# unit may carry a different COR or LOE than its parent. NO span may exist
# that is not a contiguous substring of `text_verbatim`. NO unit advances
# without two-LLM Jaccard >= 0.95 OR an explicit `held` state with an open
# FlaggedItem and a two-person-resolved record.
#
# This file does NOT define semantic interpretation of atomic units. It
# defines only the syntactic contract (spans, kinds, partition rules,
# agreement thresholds). Clinical interpretation belongs to the SME panel
# at Gate 1.
#
# Authority:
#   - ADR-HTN-001 D3 (native ACC/AHA grading preserved per parent;
#     children inherit, never reassign)
#   - ADR-HTN-001 D4 (1 atomic recommendation = 1 record granularity)
#   - ADR-HTN-001 D9 (three non-overridable human gates; Gate 1 enforces
#     atomic-unit validity)
#   - Parse + Extraction Phase Spec §4.2 (full): atomicity policy,
#     decomposition workflow, span-only LLM tool schema, dual-LLM agreement,
#     inheritance rules, no-grade-reassignment escalation
#   - Parent framework rules: `god-session`, `human-authorization`
#
# Relationship to neighboring schemas (separate files, referenced by $ref):
#   - schemas/recommendation-record-htn.yaml   (consumer; embeds AtomicUnit
#                                              instances under
#                                              atomic_units / qualifier_spans
#                                              / exclusion_spans /
#                                              monitoring_spans /
#                                              citation_spans)
#   - schemas/sair.yaml                        (upstream; provides
#                                              text_verbatim and char_spans)
#   - schemas/acc-aha-grading.yaml             (closed COR/LOE enums;
#                                              referenced for
#                                              no-grade-reassignment rule)
#   - schemas/gate1-register.yaml              (downstream; reviewer signoffs
#                                              record per-unit acceptance
#                                              when atomicity is part of
#                                              the reviewer's surface)
#   - schemas/guideline-manifest-hbp-2025.yaml (per-build manifest)
# =============================================================================

$schema: "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema"
$id: "https://aiwg.io/cpg-htn-2025-acc-aha/schemas/atomic-unit.yaml"
title: "AtomicUnit"
description: >
  Span-only, inheritance-explicit decomposition of a parent recommendation's
  text_verbatim into atomic clinical assertions and their syntactic
  modifiers. Every span is a contiguous substring of text_verbatim, verified
  not trusted. Every kind is drawn from a closed enum. No LLM may emit
  free text. No unit may carry a different COR or LOE than its parent.
version: "1.0.0"
schema_lifecycle: stable
last_reviewed: "HUMAN_FILL: ISO-8601 date of most recent panel review of this schema"
authority:
  adr: ADR-HTN-001
  framework: cpg-htn-2025-acc-aha
  parent_framework: aiwg-training
license: MIT

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. ATOMICITY POLICY (normative; encodes Parse Spec §4.2.1)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# A unit is atomic when it can be expressed as a single
#   (subject, action, modifier-set, condition-set, source-anchor)
# tuple without losing meaning. Atomic decomposition NEVER changes wording;
# it ONLY splits using the rule-based pre-segmenter plus a dual-LLM proposer
# that operates on the verbatim text and is required to return character-offset
# spans into text_verbatim — not new prose.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

policy:

  unit_of_atomicity:
    definition: >
      A clause expressing exactly one (subject, action, modifier-set,
      condition-set, source-anchor) tuple, identified as a contiguous
      substring of text_verbatim. Multiple tuples bundled in a single
      sentence by conjunction, semicolon, or list marker are NOT atomic
      and MUST be decomposed.
    examples_of_non_atomic_constructs:
      - "Use of A and B is recommended."
      - "Do X; do not do Y."
      - "Treatment with A, B, or C is reasonable."
      - "Lifestyle and pharmacologic therapy are recommended."
    rule: >
      The atomic-recommendation span MUST cover exactly one such tuple.
      Multi-tuple sentences yield multiple atomic-recommendation spans, each
      a substring of text_verbatim, with shared characters (e.g., the
      sentence's subject) repeated by reference, never duplicated by edit.

  span_ownership:
    rule: >
      Every character of text_verbatim MUST belong to at most one span of
      kind `atomic-recommendation`. Modifier kinds (qualifier, exclusion,
      monitoring, citation) MAY overlap each other and MAY overlap an
      atomic-recommendation span only when the source semantics demand it
      (e.g., a citation marker embedded inside an atomic recommendation).
      No partition rule allows two atomic-recommendation spans to overlap.

  edit_prohibition:
    rule: >
      No span may extend, contract, normalize, or otherwise alter the
      bytes of text_verbatim. The bytes are read-only. Any reviewer-driven
      typographic correction (`accept-with-edit` at Gate 1) is recorded in
      the parent record's reviewer-signoff edits[] array, not in this schema.
      AtomicUnit instances are deleted and re-created if the parent's
      text_verbatim is corrected; spans never carry stale offsets.

  inheritance:
    rule: >
      Every AtomicUnit inherits its parent recommendation's acc_aha_cor,
      acc_aha_loe, references, section_path, and anchors. Inheritance is
      RECORDED EXPLICITLY (`inherits_from`), never assumed. Validators MUST
      confirm the parent record exists and that the inherited fields are
      consistent.

  no_grade_reassignment:
    rule: >
      No AtomicUnit may carry a different COR or LOE than its parent.
      Constructs in the source that *appear* to require a different grade
      for a sub-clause (e.g., a parenthetical reading as a Class III: Harm
      embedded in a Class I row) are by definition a parsing or
      reviewer-judgment matter and MUST be escalated as
      `atomicity-grade-conflict`. The skill NEVER assigns a different
      COR/LOE to a child unit. Resolution is panel-chair only.

  no_free_text_from_llm:
    rule: >
      LLM proposers MUST return only character-offset spans plus closed-enum
      kinds. Any free-text field, summary, paraphrase, "clarification", or
      synthesized substring is rejected at the validator boundary. Two
      retries are permitted per LLM per row before the row's atomicity is
      held and routed to `llm-protocol-failure`.

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. CLOSED ENUMERATIONS
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

$defs:

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # 2.1 Atomic-unit kind
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  AtomicUnitKind:
    type: string
    enum:
      - atomic-recommendation
      - qualifier
      - exclusion
      - monitoring
      - citation
    description: >
      Closed kind enum.
        - atomic-recommendation: a clause expressing exactly one
          (subject, action, modifier-set, condition-set, source-anchor)
          tuple. Inherits parent COR/LOE.
        - qualifier: a clause that further conditions an
          atomic-recommendation (e.g., "in adults aged ≥65 years",
          "when out-of-office BP is unavailable"). Does NOT carry its
          own COR/LOE. May overlap an atomic-recommendation span.
        - exclusion: a clause that excludes a population or condition
          from the atomic-recommendation (e.g., "except in pregnancy").
          Does NOT carry its own COR/LOE.
        - monitoring: a clause prescribing follow-up cadence or lab
          monitoring associated with the atomic-recommendation. Does
          NOT carry its own COR/LOE.
        - citation: a footnote-marker substring or in-line citation
          phrase. Does NOT carry its own COR/LOE.

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # 2.2 Atomicity lifecycle state
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  AtomicityState:
    type: string
    enum:
      - agreed
      - held
      - conflict
      - resolved
    description: >
      Per-row atomicity lifecycle state.
        - agreed: dual-LLM Jaccard >= 0.95 over atomic-recommendation
          spans, AND kind agreement exact-equal across the two models on
          every span. Advances.
        - held: agreement below threshold, OR a structural validation
          failed; the row's COR/LOE/verbatim record may still advance
          through Gate 1 with `atomicity_state: held`, but downstream
          skills that require atomicity (terminology binding, threshold
          extraction, pharm-rule extraction, CQL authoring) BLOCK on it.
        - conflict: a `atomicity-grade-conflict` was detected (see §1
          no_grade_reassignment). Requires panel-chair resolution.
        - resolved: a previously `held` or `conflict` state was resolved
          through the reconciliation queue under the two-person rule.

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # 2.3 LLM disagreement category (for queue routing)
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  AtomicityDisagreementKind:
    type: string
    enum:
      - span-boundary-disagreement
      - kind-disagreement
      - count-disagreement
      - protocol-failure
      - grade-conflict
      - covering-gap
      - covering-overlap
      - non-substring-output
    description: >
      Diagnostic categories used by the reconciliation queue to route the
      held row to the right reviewer with the right rationale. NONE are
      auto-resolved.

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # 2.4 Validation severity
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  ValidationSeverity:
    type: string
    enum: [info, warning, blocking]
    description: >
      `blocking` validation failures prevent the AtomicUnit (and the parent
      record's atomicity) from advancing.

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. STRUCTURED TYPES
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # 3.1 LlmProposer — pinned model identity for one of the two proposers
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  LlmProposer:
    type: object
    additionalProperties: false
    required: [model, pin, family]
    properties:
      model:
        type: string
        description: Model identifier (e.g., "claude-opus-4", "gpt-class-x").
      pin:
        type: string
        description: Vendor-version pin (e.g., "@2026-03-15"). Recorded in tools_lock and verified at runtime.
      family:
        type: string
        enum: [anthropic, openai, google, meta, mistral, cohere, ai21, other]
        description: >
          Model family. The dual-LLM protocol REQUIRES the two proposers to
          come from different families. Validators MUST reject runs where
          family[0] == family[1].
      temperature:
        type: number
        minimum: 0.0
        maximum: 1.0
        description: Required to be 0.0 in production; non-zero permitted only on fixture runs.
      seed:
        type: [integer, "null"]
        description: Required to be non-null in production where the vendor honors deterministic seeds; null permitted only on vendors that do not.
      response_sha:
        type: string
        pattern: "^[0-9a-f]{64}$"
        description: SHA-256 of the LLM's raw tool-schema-conformant JSON response.

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # 3.2 Span — character-offset range into parent text_verbatim
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Span:
    type: array
    minItems: 2
    maxItems: 2
    items: { type: integer, minimum: 0 }
    description: >
      "[start, end]" half-open character offsets into the parent record's
      text_verbatim. MUST satisfy 0 <= start < end <= len(text_verbatim).

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # 3.3 SpanProposal — what one LLM proposed for this span (for audit)
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  SpanProposal:
    type: object
    additionalProperties: false
    required: [model, span, kind]
    properties:
      model:
        type: string
        description: Same identifier as LlmProposer.model.
      span: { $ref: "#/$defs/Span" }
      kind: { $ref: "#/$defs/AtomicUnitKind" }

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # 3.4 ReconciliationFlag — per-unit FlaggedItem hint
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  ReconciliationFlag:
    type: object
    additionalProperties: false
    required: [kind, severity, opened_at]
    properties:
      kind:           { $ref: "#/$defs/AtomicityDisagreementKind" }
      severity:       { $ref: "#/$defs/ValidationSeverity" }
      opened_at:      { type: string, format: date-time }
      reason:         { type: string, minLength: 1 }
      flagged_item_id:
        type: string
        pattern: "^flag-[0-9a-f]{16}$"
        description: Pointer to the SAIR/records FlaggedItem that owns this disagreement.

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # 3.5 InheritedFields — recorded explicitly per §1 inheritance rule
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  InheritedFields:
    type: object
    additionalProperties: false
    required: [acc_aha_cor, acc_aha_loe, section_path]
    properties:
      acc_aha_cor:
        # Resolved by $ref to acc-aha-grading.yaml at validation time.
        # Inlined enum reproduced here ONLY for self-containment; the
        # canonical source is schemas/acc-aha-grading.yaml and validators
        # MUST verify equality against that file (GRADING-INV-01).
        type: string
        enum: ["I", "IIa", "IIb", "III: No Benefit", "III: Harm"]
      acc_aha_loe:
        type: string
        enum: ["A", "B-R", "B-NR", "C-LD", "C-EO"]
      section_path:
        type: array
        minItems: 1
        items: { type: string }
      references:
        type: array
        items:
          type: object
          additionalProperties: false
          required: [ref_id]
          properties:
            ref_id: { type: string }
            doi:    { type: [string, "null"], pattern: "^10\\..+/.+$" }
            pmid:   { type: [string, "null"], pattern: "^[0-9]+$" }
      anchors_pdf_sha256:
        type: string
        pattern: "^[0-9a-f]{64}$"
        description: Inherited from parent record's anchors.pdf_sha256.
      anchors_sair_sha256:
        type: string
        pattern: "^[0-9a-f]{64}$"
        description: Inherited from parent record's anchors.sair_sha256.
      anchors_page:
        type: integer
        minimum: 1

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. ROOT TYPE — AtomicUnit
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
type: object
additionalProperties: false
required:
  - schema_version
  - unit_id
  - parent_recommendation_id
  - inherits_from
  - kind
  - span
  - inherited_fields
  - proposers
  - agreement
  - state
properties:

  schema_version:
    type: string
    const: "1.0.0"

  unit_id:
    type: string
    pattern: "^au-[0-9a-f]{16}$"
    description: >
      Stable, deterministic ID for this atomic unit. Computed as
      truncated-128-bit SHA-256 over
        (parent_recommendation_id, kind, span.start, span.end,
         tools_lock.lock_sha)
      Hex-encoded; the leading "au-" is the namespace prefix.

  parent_recommendation_id:
    type: string
    pattern: "^rec-[0-9a-f]{16}$"
    description: ID of the parent RecommendationRecordHTN.

  inherits_from:
    type: string
    description: >
      Same value as `parent_recommendation_id`. Recorded twice for the same
      reason RecommendationRecordHTN records `parent_recommendation_id` even
      for top-level records: it makes the inheritance explicit and machine-
      checkable in isolation, without requiring the schema validator to also
      load the parent.

  kind: { $ref: "#/$defs/AtomicUnitKind" }

  span: { $ref: "#/$defs/Span" }

  inherited_fields: { $ref: "#/$defs/InheritedFields" }

  proposers:
    type: array
    minItems: 2
    maxItems: 2
    items: { $ref: "#/$defs/LlmProposer" }
    description: >
      Exactly two LLM proposers, from distinct families. Validators MUST
      reject runs with one proposer or with two proposers of the same family.

  proposals:
    type: array
    minItems: 2
    maxItems: 2
    items: { $ref: "#/$defs/SpanProposal" }
    description: >
      What each LLM proposed for this unit. Order corresponds to `proposers[]`.
      For `state == "agreed"`, the two proposals' kinds MUST be exact-equal
      and their span Jaccard MUST be >= 0.95.

  agreement:
    type: object
    additionalProperties: false
    required: [span_jaccard, kind_exact_equal]
    properties:
      span_jaccard:
        type: number
        minimum: 0.0
        maximum: 1.0
        description: >
          Character-level Jaccard similarity between the two proposals'
          spans. Required >= 0.95 for `state == "agreed"`.
      kind_exact_equal:
        type: boolean
        description: >
          True iff the two proposals' kinds match exactly. Required true
          for `state == "agreed"`.

  state: { $ref: "#/$defs/AtomicityState" }

  reconciliation:
    type: array
    items: { $ref: "#/$defs/ReconciliationFlag" }
    description: >
      Open or resolved flags. Empty for `state == "agreed"`. Non-empty for
      `state ∈ {held, conflict, resolved}`.

  rule_based_segmentation:
    type: object
    additionalProperties: false
    required: [segmenter, pin]
    properties:
      segmenter:
        type: string
        enum:
          - clause-segmenter-v1
          - clause-segmenter-v2
        description: >
          Identity of the rule-based pre-segmenter that produced the
          candidate span set R consumed by both LLMs (Parse Spec §4.2.1).
      pin:
        type: string
      candidate_count:
        type: integer
        minimum: 1
        description: |R| — number of candidate spans submitted to both LLMs.

  derived:
    type: object
    additionalProperties: false
    description: >
      Optional convenience fields. Validators MUST verify that these match
      the canonical span / inheritance values; if they diverge, the unit is
      a release blocker, not auto-corrected.
    properties:
      preview_text:
        type: string
        description: |
          Slice of parent.text_verbatim covered by `span`, included as a
          read-only convenience for reviewers. NEVER an authoritative copy.
          Validators recompute and compare; mismatch = release blocker.
      length:
        type: integer
        minimum: 1
        description: span.end - span.start. Validators recompute.

  provenance:
    type: object
    additionalProperties: false
    required: [run_id, tools_lock_sha, computed_at]
    properties:
      run_id:        { type: string, format: uuid }
      tools_lock_sha:{ type: string, pattern: "^[0-9a-f]{64}$" }
      computed_at:   { type: string, format: date-time }

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. CROSS-FIELD INVARIANTS (validators MUST enforce)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

invariants:

  - id: AU-INV-01
    description: >
      `span` MUST satisfy 0 <= span[0] < span[1] <= len(parent.text_verbatim).
      Validators MUST load the parent RecommendationRecordHTN to verify; the
      parent's content_hash MUST match the hash recorded in the unit's
      provenance to detect parent mutation.

  - id: AU-INV-02
    description: >
      The substring parent.text_verbatim[span[0]:span[1]] MUST be a
      contiguous, byte-exact substring; no whitespace stripping, no NFC
      re-normalization at validation time. The parent already stored NFC.

  - id: AU-INV-03
    description: >
      `kind` MUST be a member of AtomicUnitKind. Auto-coercion forbidden.

  - id: AU-INV-04
    description: >
      `inherits_from` MUST equal `parent_recommendation_id`. The duplication
      is intentional (see schema description); divergence is a release
      blocker.

  - id: AU-INV-05
    description: >
      `inherited_fields.acc_aha_cor` and `inherited_fields.acc_aha_loe` MUST
      exact-equal the parent's `acc_aha_cor` and `acc_aha_loe`. NO atomic
      unit may carry a different COR or LOE than its parent. Detection of
      a mismatch MUST raise `atomicity-grade-conflict` and set
      `state == "conflict"`. Auto-correction forbidden.

  - id: AU-INV-06
    description: >
      `inherited_fields.section_path` MUST equal the parent's `section_path`
      (array equality, item by item).

  - id: AU-INV-07
    description: >
      `inherited_fields.references[]` MUST be a (possibly proper) subset of
      the parent's `references[]`. A unit may cite fewer references than
      the parent (when its span is narrower than the parent text), but it
      MAY NOT cite a reference the parent does not.

  - id: AU-INV-08
    description: >
      `inherited_fields.anchors_pdf_sha256`, `anchors_sair_sha256`, and
      `anchors_page` MUST equal the parent's `anchors.pdf_sha256`,
      `anchors.sair_sha256`, and `anchors.page` respectively.

  - id: AU-INV-09
    description: >
      `proposers` MUST contain exactly two members; `proposers[0].family`
      MUST NOT equal `proposers[1].family`. Same-family pairs are a release
      blocker.

  - id: AU-INV-10
    description: >
      In production runs, every proposer MUST have `temperature == 0.0`.
      Non-zero temperature is permitted only when the run is explicitly
      tagged as a fixture run in the build manifest; this is checked at
      orchestrator level (`flow-hbp-2025-build`).

  - id: AU-INV-11
    description: >
      `proposals[]` MUST have exactly two items, and `proposals[i].model`
      MUST equal `proposers[i].model` for i in {0,1}.

  - id: AU-INV-12
    description: >
      For every proposal, `proposals[i].span` MUST satisfy AU-INV-01 against
      the parent text_verbatim, and `parent.text_verbatim[span[0]:span[1]]`
      MUST be a substring (verified, not trusted).

  - id: AU-INV-13
    description: >
      For `state == "agreed"`:
        agreement.span_jaccard >= 0.95
        agreement.kind_exact_equal == true
        proposals[0].kind == proposals[1].kind
        reconciliation == [] or all reconciliation entries resolved

  - id: AU-INV-14
    description: >
      For `state == "held"`:
        agreement.span_jaccard < 0.95 OR
        agreement.kind_exact_equal == false OR
        a structural validation failure occurred
      AND `reconciliation` MUST contain at least one open
      ReconciliationFlag of severity "blocking".

  - id: AU-INV-15
    description: >
      For `state == "conflict"`:
        a grade-conflict was detected (see AU-INV-05) OR a panel-chair
        review was independently requested.
      `reconciliation` MUST contain a ReconciliationFlag with kind
      `grade-conflict`. Resolution requires panel-chair signoff (recorded
      in the Gate 1 register, not in this schema).

  - id: AU-INV-16
    description: >
      For `state == "resolved"`:
        `reconciliation` MUST contain at least one resolved entry whose
        FlaggedItem (referenced by `flagged_item_id`) has
        `resolution_state ∈ {resolved-accept, resolved-edit}` and whose
        `resolution.reviewer_ids` has length >= 2 (two-person rule).

  - id: AU-INV-17
    description: >
      Atomic-recommendation spans within the same parent record MUST NOT
      overlap each other in character offsets. Validators MUST detect
      overlaps and BLOCK. Overlaps among modifier kinds (qualifier,
      exclusion, monitoring, citation) and between a modifier kind and an
      atomic-recommendation are permitted only when the source semantics
      demand it (e.g., a citation marker embedded inside an atomic
      recommendation), and validators MUST log such cases as `info`-severity
      diagnostics.

  - id: AU-INV-18
    description: >
      The union of all `atomic-recommendation` spans within a parent record
      MUST cover at least one contiguous, non-empty substring of
      text_verbatim. A parent with zero atomic-recommendation units is a
      release blocker (an empty decomposition is never legal at Gate 1
      exit).

  - id: AU-INV-19
    description: >
      `derived.preview_text`, when present, MUST equal
        parent.text_verbatim[span[0]:span[1]]
      byte-for-byte. `derived.length`, when present, MUST equal
        span[1] - span[0]
      Mismatches are release blockers, not auto-corrected.

  - id: AU-INV-20
    description: >
      `unit_id` MUST be deterministic per the formula in the schema
      description. Re-runs with identical parent record, identical kind,
      identical span boundaries, and identical tools_lock MUST produce the
      same `unit_id`.

  - id: AU-INV-21
    description: >
      `provenance.tools_lock_sha` MUST equal the SAIR/records tools_lock
      lock_sha at the time the unit was computed. A tools_lock change MUST
      regenerate all atomic units; carrying stale tools_lock_sha values is
      a release blocker.

  - id: AU-INV-22
    description: >
      Unit `state == "held"` does NOT block the parent record's COR/LOE/
      verbatim advance through Gate 1 (the parent may advance with
      `atomicity_state: held` recorded in its provenance), but downstream
      skills that require atomicity MUST refuse to operate on a parent
      with any `held` or `conflict` units.

  - id: AU-INV-23
    description: >
      Validators MUST refuse to load a parent record whose
      `provenance.atomicity.state` is `agreed` while any of its child
      AtomicUnit instances are not in state `agreed` or `resolved`. The
      states MUST be consistent at write-back time.

  - id: AU-INV-24
    description: >
      The parent's `text_verbatim` is read-only. If a Gate 1 reviewer
      proposes an `accept-with-edit` that alters parent.text_verbatim, ALL
      child AtomicUnit instances MUST be deleted and re-computed from
      scratch (new `unit_id`s, new spans, new proposals). Stale child units
      attached to an edited parent are a release blocker.

  - id: AU-INV-25
    description: >
      The parent's `acc_aha_cor` and `acc_aha_loe` are read-only at and
      after Gate 1 (RecommendationRecord INV-07 forbids editing them).
      Therefore inherited_fields.acc_aha_cor and acc_aha_loe are also
      effectively read-only at and after Gate 1. Any drift triggers
      AU-INV-05.

# =============================================================================
# 6. WORKED EXAMPLES (shape-correctness fixtures)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# These examples are illustrative shape-correctness fixtures. EVERY field whose
# value can ONLY come from the published source PDF or the SME-attested parent
# record is marked `HUMAN_FILL` with explicit instructions describing what
# must be sourced and how. The pipeline refuses to operate on records
# containing `HUMAN_FILL` tokens.
#
# Three examples are provided:
#   6.1 An `agreed` atomic-recommendation unit (single-tuple sentence).
#   6.2 A `held` unit with span-boundary disagreement awaiting reviewer.
#   6.3 A `conflict` unit with `atomicity-grade-conflict` awaiting panel chair.
# =============================================================================

examples:

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # 6.1 Agreed atomic-recommendation
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  - schema_version: "1.0.0"
    unit_id: "au-HUMAN_FILL_16HEX"
    parent_recommendation_id: "rec-HUMAN_FILL_16HEX"
    inherits_from: "rec-HUMAN_FILL_16HEX"
    kind: atomic-recommendation
    span: [0, 0]   # HUMAN_FILL: [start, end] character offsets into the parent's text_verbatim
    inherited_fields:
      acc_aha_cor: "HUMAN_FILL_COR_VERBATIM_FROM_PARENT"   # exactly equal to parent
      acc_aha_loe: "HUMAN_FILL_LOE_VERBATIM_FROM_PARENT"   # exactly equal to parent
      section_path:
        - "HUMAN_FILL: chapter heading"
        - "HUMAN_FILL: subsection heading"
      references:
        - ref_id: "fn-HUMAN_FILL"
          doi: null
          pmid: null
      anchors_pdf_sha256:  "HUMAN_FILL_64HEX"
      anchors_sair_sha256: "HUMAN_FILL_64HEX"
      anchors_page: 0    # HUMAN_FILL
    proposers:
      - { model: "claude-opus-4", pin: "HUMAN_FILL_PIN", family: anthropic, temperature: 0.0, seed: 0,    response_sha: "HUMAN_FILL_64HEX" }
      - { model: "gpt-class-x",   pin: "HUMAN_FILL_PIN", family: openai,    temperature: 0.0, seed: null, response_sha: "HUMAN_FILL_64HEX" }
    proposals:
      - { model: "claude-opus-4", span: [0, 0], kind: atomic-recommendation }   # HUMAN_FILL: must be substring of parent.text_verbatim
      - { model: "gpt-class-x",   span: [0, 0], kind: atomic-recommendation }   # HUMAN_FILL: same
    agreement:
      span_jaccard: 1.0
      kind_exact_equal: true
    state: agreed
    reconciliation: []
    rule_based_segmentation:
      segmenter: clause-segmenter-v1
      pin: "HUMAN_FILL_PIN"
      candidate_count: 1
    derived:
      preview_text: "HUMAN_FILL: parent.text_verbatim[span[0]:span[1]] read-only convenience"
      length: 0  # HUMAN_FILL: span[1] - span[0]
    provenance:
      run_id: "HUMAN_FILL_UUID"
      tools_lock_sha: "HUMAN_FILL_64HEX"
      computed_at: "HUMAN_FILL_ISO_DATETIME"

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # 6.2 Held unit — span-boundary disagreement
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  - schema_version: "1.0.0"
    unit_id: "au-HUMAN_FILL_16HEX"
    parent_recommendation_id: "rec-HUMAN_FILL_16HEX"
    inherits_from: "rec-HUMAN_FILL_16HEX"
    kind: atomic-recommendation
    span: [0, 0]   # HUMAN_FILL: the canonical span recorded by the orchestrator pending reviewer resolution
    inherited_fields:
      acc_aha_cor: "HUMAN_FILL_COR_VERBATIM_FROM_PARENT"
      acc_aha_loe: "HUMAN_FILL_LOE_VERBATIM_FROM_PARENT"
      section_path:
        - "HUMAN_FILL: chapter"
        - "HUMAN_FILL: subsection"
      references: []
      anchors_pdf_sha256:  "HUMAN_FILL_64HEX"
      anchors_sair_sha256: "HUMAN_FILL_64HEX"
      anchors_page: 0
    proposers:
      - { model: "claude-opus-4", pin: "HUMAN_FILL_PIN", family: anthropic, temperature: 0.0, seed: 0,    response_sha: "HUMAN_FILL_64HEX" }
      - { model: "gpt-class-x",   pin: "HUMAN_FILL_PIN", family: openai,    temperature: 0.0, seed: null, response_sha: "HUMAN_FILL_64HEX" }
    proposals:
      # The two LLMs proposed slightly different boundaries for the same atomic
      # recommendation; their spans overlap but Jaccard < 0.95.
      - { model: "claude-opus-4", span: [0, 0], kind: atomic-recommendation }   # HUMAN_FILL: e.g., [12, 84]
      - { model: "gpt-class-x",   span: [0, 0], kind: atomic-recommendation }   # HUMAN_FILL: e.g., [12, 96]
    agreement:
      span_jaccard: 0.0   # HUMAN_FILL: actual computed Jaccard < 0.95
      kind_exact_equal: true
    state: held
    reconciliation:
      - kind: span-boundary-disagreement
        severity: blocking
        opened_at: "HUMAN_FILL_ISO_DATETIME"
        reason: |
          HUMAN_FILL: e.g., "Models disagree on whether the trailing
          qualifier 'when out-of-office BP measurement is available' is
          part of the atomic recommendation or a separate qualifier span."
        flagged_item_id: "flag-HUMAN_FILL_16HEX"
    rule_based_segmentation:
      segmenter: clause-segmenter-v1
      pin: "HUMAN_FILL_PIN"
      candidate_count: 0   # HUMAN_FILL: actual |R|
    derived: {}
    provenance:
      run_id: "HUMAN_FILL_UUID"
      tools_lock_sha: "HUMAN_FILL_64HEX"
      computed_at: "HUMAN_FILL_ISO_DATETIME"

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # 6.3 Conflict unit — atomicity-grade-conflict (panel-chair only)
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  - schema_version: "1.0.0"
    unit_id: "au-HUMAN_FILL_16HEX"
    parent_recommendation_id: "rec-HUMAN_FILL_16HEX"
    inherits_from: "rec-HUMAN_FILL_16HEX"
    kind: atomic-recommendation
    span: [0, 0]
    inherited_fields:
      # NOTE: even though both LLMs proposed a span that *appears* to read as
      # "Class III: Harm" within a parent labeled "I", the unit's
      # inherited_fields MUST equal the parent verbatim. The conflict is
      # surfaced via state=conflict and a reconciliation flag, never by
      # rewriting the inherited COR/LOE.
      acc_aha_cor: "HUMAN_FILL_COR_VERBATIM_FROM_PARENT"
      acc_aha_loe: "HUMAN_FILL_LOE_VERBATIM_FROM_PARENT"
      section_path:
        - "HUMAN_FILL: chapter"
        - "HUMAN_FILL: subsection"
      references: []
      anchors_pdf_sha256:  "HUMAN_FILL_64HEX"
      anchors_sair_sha256: "HUMAN_FILL_64HEX"
      anchors_page: 0
    proposers:
      - { model: "claude-opus-4", pin: "HUMAN_FILL_PIN", family: anthropic, temperature: 0.0, seed: 0,    response_sha: "HUMAN_FILL_64HEX" }
      - { model: "gpt-class-x",   pin: "HUMAN_FILL_PIN", family: openai,    temperature: 0.0, seed: null, response_sha: "HUMAN_FILL_64HEX" }
    proposals:
      - { model: "claude-opus-4", span: [0, 0], kind: atomic-recommendation }
      - { model: "gpt-class-x",   span: [0, 0], kind: atomic-recommendation }
    agreement:
      span_jaccard: 1.0
      kind_exact_equal: true
    state: conflict
    reconciliation:
      - kind: grade-conflict
        severity: blocking
        opened_at: "HUMAN_FILL_ISO_DATETIME"
        reason: |
          HUMAN_FILL: e.g., "The atomic-recommendation substring reads as a
          'should not' clause, which would normally correspond to Class III:
          Harm, but the parent recommendation is labeled Class I in the
          source recommendation box. This is by definition a parsing or
          reviewer-judgment matter (no_grade_reassignment rule). Routed to
          panel chair."
        flagged_item_id: "flag-HUMAN_FILL_16HEX"
    rule_based_segmentation:
      segmenter: clause-segmenter-v1
      pin: "HUMAN_FILL_PIN"
      candidate_count: 0
    derived: {}
    provenance:
      run_id: "HUMAN_FILL_UUID"
      tools_lock_sha: "HUMAN_FILL_64HEX"
      computed_at: "HUMAN_FILL_ISO_DATETIME"

# =============================================================================
# 7. CHANGE CONTROL
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Any change to this schema (closed enums, atomicity policy, validation rules,
# invariants, or example fixtures) requires:
#   - A change-controlled diff with regression evaluation against the golden set.
#   - Panel-chair signoff.
#   - Increment of `schema_version` (semver: breaking = major).
#   - Update of `last_reviewed`.
#   - Coordinated update of every producing/consuming skill's `tools_lock`
#     reference and acceptance test fixtures.
#   - If the dual-LLM agreement threshold (0.95 Jaccard), the family-distinct
#     rule, the no-free-text rule, the span-only rule, the no-grade-reassignment
#     rule, or the read-only-text-verbatim rule is changed, the change MUST
#     ALSO update ADR-HTN-001 D9 with a documented rationale and a new
#     panel-chair signoff.
# =============================================================================

change_control:
  semver: true
  golden_set_regression_required: true
  panel_chair_signoff_required: true
  parent_schemas_to_update_on_breaking_change:
    - cpg-htn-2025-acc-aha/schemas/recommendation-record-htn.yaml
    - cpg-htn-2025-acc-aha/schemas/sair.yaml
    - cpg-htn-2025-acc-aha/schemas/gate1-register.yaml
  parent_skills_to_update_on_breaking_change:
    - cpg-htn-2025-acc-aha/skills/extract-recommendation-cor-loe
    - cpg-htn-2025-acc-aha/skills/pico-decompose-htn
    - cpg-htn-2025-acc-aha/skills/extract-bp-thresholds
    - cpg-htn-2025-acc-aha/skills/extract-pharm-rules
    - cpg-htn-2025-acc-aha/skills/bind-htn-vocab
    - cpg-htn-2025-acc-aha/skills/emit-fhir-plandefinition-htn
    - cpg-htn-2025-acc-aha/skills/emit-cql-htn
    - cpg-htn-2025-acc-aha/skills/safety-hbp
  adr_amendment_required_for_threshold_changes:
    threshold_jaccard: 0.95
    family_distinct_rule: true
    no_free_text_rule: true
    span_only_rule: true
    no_grade_reassignment_rule: true
    read_only_text_verbatim_rule: true
    adr_to_amend: ADR-HTN-001 D9
```

Saved as `schemas/atomic-unit.yaml`. The file fully encodes Parse + Extraction Phase Spec §4.2 — the dual-LLM, span-only, inheritance-explicit decomposition contract — and mirrors the parent repo's closed-enum-first / `additionalProperties: false` discipline. The atomicity policy is normative and explicit: no free text from LLMs, spans must be contiguous substrings of the parent's `text_verbatim` (verified, never trusted), inheritance is recorded in `inherited_fields` *and* duplicated as `inherits_from`, and `no_grade_reassignment` requires panel-chair signoff via the `conflict` state. Twenty-five cross-field invariants (`AU-INV-01` … `AU-INV-25`) make the contract machine-checkable, including the family-distinct LLM rule (`AU-INV-09`), the production temperature-zero rule (`AU-INV-10`), the inherit-from-parent COR/LOE rule (`AU-INV-05`), the references-subset rule (`AU-INV-07`), the no-overlap-of-atomic-recommendation-spans rule (`AU-INV-17`), the parent-state-consistency rule (`AU-INV-23`), the parent-edit-deletes-children rule (`AU-INV-24`), and the deterministic `unit_id` rule (`AU-INV-20`). Three worked examples (one `agreed`, one `held` for span-boundary disagreement, one `conflict` for `atomicity-grade-conflict`) demonstrate the lifecycle without inventing any clinical content; every value sourceable only from the parent record or the source PDF is marked `HUMAN_FILL`.

If you want the next concrete step at the same fidelity (one at a time):

1. `schemas/gate1-register.yaml` — the Gate 1 cohort register schema, with reviewer credential evidence, cryptographic signature envelope, panel-chair signoff, and post-signoff immutability rules. This is the only remaining schema directly referenced by `extract-recommendation-cor-loe` that has not been drafted.
2. `schemas/guideline-manifest-hbp-2025.yaml` — the per-build manifest referenced by `guideline_manifest_ref` in the SAIR, the recommendation-record schema, and (transitively) the atomic-unit schema; it includes the predecessor 2017 supersession chain and the publisher-agreed quote-extent envelope.
3. `flow-hbp-2025-build` orchestrator with all three gate stops wired (Gate 1 stop wired to `extract-recommendation-cor-loe`, Gate 2 to `cql-clinician-signoff`, Gate 3 to `safety-case-attest`).
4. Open a tracking issue in `jmagly/aiwg-training` (or a new repo `jmagly/aiwg-cpg-htn-2025`) proposing this atomic-unit contract as the canonical Phase-3 atomicity output for downstream consumption.

## @jfontestad

Let's continue with the next concrete step at full fidelity (one at a time, caution over velocity), proceed to draft an enterprise grade, refined and polished clinical production ready version of schemas/gate1-register.yaml — the Gate 1 cohort register schema, including reviewer credential evidence, cryptographic signature envelope, panel-chair signoff, and post-signoff immutability rules at the same fidelity as the parent repo's existing documents, and in full.


## Copilot

```yaml name=schemas/gate1-register.yaml
# =============================================================================
# gate1-register.yaml
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Standalone schema for the Gate 1 cohort register — the auditable, signed,
# append-only ledger of SME extraction reviews that gate every
# RecommendationRecordHTN before it advances to Phase 4 (terminology binding).
#
# This file is the contract for:
#   - Cohort identity (a named batch of recommendations under review).
#   - Reviewer credential evidence (named individuals, board certifications,
#     identity proofing, conflicts of interest).
#   - Per-record reviewer signoffs (decisions, rationales, edits, signatures).
#   - Panel-chair cohort signoff (the additional layer of attestation that
#     validates reviewer composition and disposes of any escalated records).
#   - Cryptographic signature envelope (algorithm, key identity, signed
#     content hash, time-stamping).
#   - Post-signoff immutability rules (no mutation of signed content; new
#     decisions require a new register version).
#
# Posture: caution over velocity, fidelity over coverage. Every signature is
# verified, never trusted. Every reviewer is a named, credential-evidenced
# individual, not a role token. Every decision is on a single record, never
# on a batch. Every COR/LOE edit is forbidden and reclassified as
# reject-rework. Conflicts of interest are disclosed, not ignored.
#
# This file does NOT contain clinical text. It records WHO signed WHAT and
# WHEN, against the content hashes computed by `extract-recommendation-cor-loe`.
# Clinical content lives in RecommendationRecordHTN; this file points to it.
#
# Authority:
#   - ADR-HTN-001 D9 (three non-overridable human gates; Gate 1 enforces
#     two-independent-SME signoff, panel-chair cohort signoff)
#   - ADR-HTN-001 D10 (PHI fail-closed; copyright envelope respected)
#   - ADR-HTN-001 D11 (Synthea-only test data; real PHI rejected at ingest)
```
