# flow-hbp-2025-build

End-to-end orchestrator for the `cpg-htn-2025-acc-aha` framework. Chains the
ten pipeline phases — acquire → parse → extract (Gate 1) → bind → structure
→ CQL (Gate 2) → safety → validate → PHI/copyright → publish (Gate 3) — with
non-overridable human-authorization stops at Gates 1, 2, and 3, fail-closed
DQA gates between every phase, deterministic re-runs against pinned tools,
and a single W3C PROV-O bundle covering the build.

This skill does not perform clinical work itself. It composes the constituent
skills, enforces the architectural rules in **ADR-HTN-001**, and refuses to
advance on any unresolved hazard. Caution over velocity is a property of the
orchestrator, not just of the constituent skills: a green Gate 1 cohort
cannot proceed if a single sibling cohort has an open escalation; a Gate 2
signoff cannot proceed on Libraries with Synthea coverage below 95%; Gate 3
cannot proceed if the cumulative quote envelope is exceeded by a single
character.

Posture: **caution over velocity, fidelity over coverage, verbatim over
paraphrase.** No phase auto-corrects another phase's output. No gate is
overridable. No constituent skill is bypassed. No publication occurs without
the medical-director attestation.

## When to Use

Invoke this skill when:

- A signed `guideline-manifest-hbp-2025.yaml` (state == `active`) is in place.
- A new build is required against that manifest.
- A previous build needs to be resumed after a queue resolution, a Gate 1
  rework, a Gate 2 Library re-author, or a Gate 3 panel-chair decision.
- A regression run is needed against the golden set after a tooling-lockfile
  change.

Do **not** invoke this skill if:

- The manifest is in any state other than `active` (e.g.,
  `pending-medical-director`, `superseded`, `withdrawn`).
- Any open errata blocker exists in `errata_watch.blockers_open[]`.
- The manifest's medical-director signoff fails cryptographic verification.
- The publisher quote-extent envelope contract has expired.

The skill performs preflight checks against all of the above and refuses to
start otherwise.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `manifest-path` | yes | — | Path to a `guideline-manifest-hbp-2025.yaml` instance with `state == "active"` and a verified medical-director signoff. |
| `--phases <list>` | no | `all` | Comma-separated phase identifiers from the closed phase set in §1. Defaults to all phases. Useful for targeted re-runs. |
| `--from <phase>` | no | — | Resume from this phase inclusive. Mutually exclusive with `--phases`. |
| `--to <phase>` | no | — | Stop after this phase inclusive. Mutually exclusive with `--phases`. |
| `--cohort <id>` | no | — | Restrict the run to a specific Gate 1 cohort id. When set, all downstream phases operate only on records bound to that cohort. |
| `--resume` | no | `false` | Resume an interrupted run from the last persisted phase boundary. Required after any queue resolution, Gate rework, or Library re-author. |
| `--dry-run` | no | `false` | Run preflight + plan only; emit the planned phase graph and gate stops; do not execute work-producing steps. Permitted in production for change-control reviews. |
| `--strict` | no | `true` | Fail-closed on every DQA gate. Setting `--strict false` is **never permitted** in production; the flag exists only for fixture and golden-set development. |

## Operation

The orchestrator executes the ten phases in §1, with three non-overridable
human-authorization stops (Gates 1, 2, 3) and DQA gates between every phase.
Each phase is delegated to a constituent skill; this skill owns sequencing,
gate enforcement, lockfile integrity, and provenance composition.

### 1. Phase graph (closed phase set)

```
P0  preflight                   (this skill)
P1  acquire                     → acquire-hbp-2025-source
P2  parse-conditioning           → parse-prepare-pdf
P3  parse-layout                 → parse-detect-layout
P4  parse-text                   → parse-extract-text
P5  parse-figures                → parse-extract-figures
P6  parse-recbox                 → parse-acc-aha-recbox
P7  parse-ocr-fallback           → parse-ocr-fallback (conditional)
P8  parse-reconcile              → parse-reconcile-queue
P9  extract                      → extract-recommendation-cor-loe   ◆ Gate 1
P10 bind                         → bind-htn-vocab
P11 pico                         → pico-decompose-htn
P12 thresholds                   → extract-bp-thresholds
P13 pharm                        → extract-pharm-rules
P14 contraindications            → extract-contraindications
P15 monitoring                   → extract-monitoring
P16 risk-engine                  → bind-risk-engine
P17 valuesets                    → author-htn-valuesets
P18 fhir-plandefs                → emit-fhir-plandefinition-htn
P19 fhir-activitydefs            → emit-fhir-activitydefinition-htn
P20 cql-libraries                → emit-cql-htn
P21 cql-tests                    → cql-test-synthea-htn
P22 cds-hooks                    → cds-hooks-package-htn         ◆ Gate 2
P23 safety-hazards               → safety-hbp
P24 phi-scrub                    → phi-scrub
P25 copyright                    → copyright-quote-check-acc-aha
P26 fhir-validate                → fhir-implementation-guide-build
P27 docs                         → guideline-docs
P28 publish                      → guideline-version              ◆ Gate 3
```

Phases are partially ordered: P10–P17 are independent of each other and
proceed in parallel where the orchestrator's resource budget permits, but all
must complete before P18; P20 cannot start until P10–P17 are complete; P21
cannot start until P20 produces a Library; P22 cannot reach Gate 2 until P21
is green.

### 2. Preflight (P0)

#### 2.1 Manifest validation
1. Validate `manifest-path` against `schemas/guideline-manifest-hbp-2025.yaml`.
2. Verify `state == "active"`.
3. Verify `errata_watch.blockers_open == []`.
4. Verify `medical_director_signoff.signature` cryptographically against the
   manifest's `fixity.manifest_sha256`. Producer claims of `verifies: true`
   are ignored; the orchestrator re-verifies.
5. Verify `quote_envelope.legal_counsel_signoff.signed_at` is within the
   contract window (the contract URI is consulted only for the window; the
   contract document itself is not retrieved here).
6. Verify `tools_lock.lock_sha` against the canonicalized `items[]`.
7. Verify `grading_framework_pin.schema_sha256` matches the on-disk
   `acc-aha-grading.yaml`.

Any failure → **BLOCK**; emit a preflight failure report; do not proceed.

#### 2.2 Tooling readiness
1. Probe every `tools_lock.items[]` and `external_services[]` for reachability
   and version fidelity:
   - PDF parsers respond on the pinned version.
   - LLMs in `tools_lock.llm_pair` respond from the declared families with
     the pinned model identifiers; family-distinct rule (atomic-unit
     `AU-INV-09`) verified.
   - VLM is reachable; OCR engines are at least three.
   - Terminology server resolves a known SNOMED code at the pinned edition.
   - PREVENT calculator passes the test-vectors smoke test.
   - KMS responds for the manifest signing key id.
   - At least one TSA in `tsa_list[]` is currently within `cert_valid_*`.

Any failure → **BLOCK**.

#### 2.3 Run identity
1. Generate `run_id` (UUID v4).
2. Compute `tools_lock_sha` (must equal the manifest's `tools_lock.lock_sha`).
3. Create work directories: `work/<run_id>/{01-fixity-ok, 02-normalized,
   03-pages-300dpi, 03-pages-600dpi, sair, records, fhir, cql, ig, queue,
   gate1, gate2, gate3, reports, provenance}`.
4. Initialize the build PROV bundle at
   `provenance/flow-<run_id>.jsonld` with `Activity` for this orchestrator
   invocation, `Entity` for the manifest, and `Agent` for the operator.
5. Write the build start event to the audit log.

#### 2.4 Plan the phase graph
1. Compute the actual phase set under `--phases / --from / --to / --cohort`.
2. Emit a plan report at `reports/plan-<run_id>.md` listing phases, their
   skill bindings, expected DQA gates, expected human-authorization stops,
   and resume points.
3. If `--dry-run`, stop here.

### 3. Acquire (P1)

Delegate to `acquire-hbp-2025-source` with the manifest's `sources[]`. The
skill enforces the source-admission rule (exactly four roles), pins SHAs into
the manifest's `sources[*].pdf_sha256`, and computes the source-side fixity
manifest.

DQA gates after P1:
- **G1-A**: Every source SHA matches the manifest's pin.
- **G1-B**: Every source license has a signed publisher-contract pointer.
- **G1-C**: The errata feed for every source returns no new blockers since
  the manifest's `errata_watch.last_polled_at`.

Failure of any gate → BLOCK; emit a `version-drift` event into the manifest's
`drift_events[]` (a new manifest version is required to resolve), and stop
the run.

### 4. Parse (P2 – P8)

The orchestrator runs the parse family in dependency order. Every phase
writes back into the same SAIR document at `work/<run_id>/sair.json` under
the SAIR write-back lock semantics (one writer at a time).

#### 4.1 Pre-parse conditioning (P2)
Delegate to `parse-prepare-pdf`. Conditions: PDF re-streaming, font embedding
verification, raster generation at 300 DPI (and 600 DPI for fine-grained
pages flagged downstream), and tools-lock confirmation.

DQA gates after P2:
- **G2.0-A**: Every source has a conditioned PDF with a SHA pinned into
  `sources[*].conditioned_pdf_sha256`.
- **G2.0-B**: Every font has a ToUnicode CMap or a documented OCR-fallback
  flag.
- **G2.0-C**: Raster manifest is complete and SHA-anchored.

#### 4.2 Layout (P3)
Delegate to `parse-detect-layout`. Dual-detector consensus per page; reading
order resolved.

DQA gate G2-E (reading-order stability) inherited from the parse spec.

#### 4.3 Text (P4)
Delegate to `parse-extract-text`. Multi-engine reconciliation; reversible
NFC normalization; footnote attachment.

DQA gates G2-A (coverage) and G2-D (footnote integrity).

#### 4.4 Figures (P5)
Delegate to `parse-extract-figures`. Captions paired; flowcharts marked
`awaiting_corroboration: true`; charts cross-checked against tables/text.

DQA gate G2-C (figure caption pairing).

#### 4.5 Recommendation boxes (P6)
Delegate to `parse-acc-aha-recbox`. Five-engine table reconciliation;
`acc-aha-recommendation-box` schema confirmation; verbatim recommendation
text captured with reversible-normalization metadata; supportive text bound
separately.

DQA gates G2.3-A through G2.3-G inherited from `parse-acc-aha-recbox`.

#### 4.6 OCR fallback (P7, conditional)
Delegate to `parse-ocr-fallback` only when:
- A region is flagged as raster-only or `cid-glyph-orphan`.
- A region has `text-disputed` consensus and a raster tiebreak is needed.

The orchestrator computes the conditional set; skipped if empty.

DQA gate: any OCR-only region's confidence ≥ 0.95 or it is held in queue.

#### 4.7 Reconciliation queue (P8)
Delegate to `parse-reconcile-queue`. The orchestrator does not advance to
extraction until every `flagged_items[*]` of severity `blocking` is in state
`resolved-*` with a two-person rule applied.

DQA gate after P8:
- **G2-RECON**: Zero blocking items in `open` or `in-review` state.

Failure of any P2–P8 DQA gate → BLOCK; the orchestrator surfaces the
specific gate, the failing region(s), and the affected SAIR ranges. No
workaround. No bypass.

### 5. Extract (P9) → ◆ Gate 1

Delegate to `extract-recommendation-cor-loe`. Triple-modal consensus,
atomicity decomposition, PICO precheck, numeric-fact precheck, and Gate 1
SME review against `schemas/gate1-register.yaml`.

#### 5.1 Cohort assembly
1. Group recommendation rows by domain per the Gate 1 composition matrix
   (see `extract-recommendation-cor-loe` §10.1).
2. For each domain group, open a Gate 1 cohort and bind the relevant panel
   reviewers from the manifest's institutional roster.
3. If `--cohort` is supplied, restrict to that cohort.

#### 5.2 Triple-modal consensus and atomicity (mechanical phase)
The skill produces `RecommendationDraft-A/V/O`, three-way consensus, and
atomicity decomposition with dual-LLM span agreement. Held rows go to the
extraction queue; resolved rows are sealed.

#### 5.3 ◆ Gate 1 — SME extraction review (non-overridable)
Mandatory stop. The orchestrator posts the cohort to `gate1-sme-review`;
work is paused for the cohort until two independent SME signatures plus
panel-chair signoff are recorded.

Hard rules at this gate:
- **Two independent reviewers per record**, distinct `(reviewer_id, role)`,
  matching the composition matrix for the record's domain.
- **No batch acceptance**: each record is signed individually.
- **No COR/LOE edits**: any such request is reclassified as `reject-rework`.
- **No reviewer self-pairing.**
- **COI auto-disqualification** is enforced.
- **Pregnancy records require MFM + clinical pharmacology** (G1-INV-23).
- **Panel-chair cohort signoff** required for cohort finalization.

DQA gate after P9 (per cohort):
- **G3-A** Coverage: every recommendation row in the cohort scope has a
  `RecommendationRecordHTN` in state `gate-1-passed` OR an explicit
  withdraw/rework record.
- **G3-B** Triple-consensus rate ≥ 99.0% on advanced records.
- **G3-C..J** as specified in `extract-recommendation-cor-loe` §G3.* gates.
- **G3-GATE1-A..C** as specified in `extract-recommendation-cor-loe` §G3.GATE1.

The orchestrator does not begin downstream phases for a record until that
record's cohort is `finalized` in the Gate 1 register and the register
verifies under `schemas/gate1-register.yaml` invariants.

### 6. Terminology and structured-fact extraction (P10 – P17)

These phases run in parallel where dependencies permit. Inputs are the Gate
1–signed `RecommendationRecordHTN[]`; outputs are augmentations on those
records and emission of `ValueSet`/`CodeSystem` resources.

| Phase | Skill | Inputs | Outputs | Key DQA gate |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| P10 | `bind-htn-vocab` | atomic-units; verbatim text | per-concept `terminology-binding-htn` records on the parent record | 100% concept binding rate within HTN scope; unbound concepts → BLOCK |
| P11 | `pico-decompose-htn` | atomic-units; PICO precheck | full PICO records replacing the precheck stub | every record has Population and Intervention populated |
| P12 | `extract-bp-thresholds` | atomic-units | `BPThreshold[]` with UCUM `mm[Hg]` | every numeric BP threshold round-trips against an independent re-extraction byte-for-byte |
| P13 | `extract-pharm-rules` | atomic-units; SAIR drug tables | `DrugRule[]` with RxNorm ingredient classes | denylist rules carry an explicit `hard_block_basis` anchored in source |
| P14 | `extract-contraindications` | atomic-units | `Contraindication[]` | each contraindication has a source-anchored `basis` |
| P15 | `extract-monitoring` | atomic-units | `Monitoring[]` with LOINC candidates | LOINC candidates resolve to canonical codes at pinned edition |
| P16 | `bind-risk-engine` | atomic-units; manifest's `risk_engine` | `RiskEngineBinding` with `name == PREVENT` (default); PCE-legacy never propagates | `legacy_only == false` for any binding feeding CQL |
| P17 | `author-htn-valuesets` | bound concepts | FHIR `ValueSet`/`CodeSystem` resources | every value-set version-pinned to the manifest's terminology editions |

DQA gate aggregating P10–P17:
- **G4-A** Every record advanced through Gate 1 has, where applicable, full
  PICO, terminology bindings, BP thresholds, drug rules, contraindications,
  monitoring, and (where invoked) a PREVENT risk-engine binding.
- **G4-B** No PCE-legacy binding propagates.
- **G4-C** Pregnancy records have a denylist with `hard_block_basis ∈
  {cor-iii-harm, cor-iii-no-benefit, explicit-should-not,
  explicit-not-recommended}` anchored in source.

### 7. FHIR structuring (P18, P19)

Delegate to `emit-fhir-plandefinition-htn` and
`emit-fhir-activitydefinition-htn`. The orchestrator emits exactly nine
`PlanDefinition` resources (per §5 of the framework spec):

```
HBP-Diagnosis, HBP-RiskStratify, HBP-Lifestyle, HBP-Pharm-General,
HBP-Pharm-SpecialPops, HBP-Resistant, HBP-Secondary,
HBP-Urgency-Emergency, HBP-Pregnancy
```

DQA gates after P18, P19:
- **G5-A** Every record's `cpg-fhir-mapping-htn.yaml` row resolves to one of
  the nine PlanDefinitions.
- **G5-B** Every `ActivityDefinition` references a PlanDefinition that
  exists in this build.
- **G5-C** Every emitted resource references the manifest's `build_version_label`.

### 8. CQL (P20, P21) → ◆ Gate 2

#### 8.1 CQL authoring (P20)
Delegate to `emit-cql-htn`. The skill produces nine `Library` resources
(matching the nine PlanDefinitions): `HBPStaging`, `PreventRisk`,
`TreatmentThreshold`, `FirstLineSelection`, `SpecialPopulationModifiers`,
`PregnancyHTN`, `ResistantHTN`, `SecondaryHTNTriggers`,
`HypertensiveUrgencyEmergency`.

CQL is treated as **draft** until §8.2 passes. Drafts are not packaged for
CDS Hooks.

DQA gates after P20:
- **G6-A** Every Library parses cleanly under the pinned CQL runtime.
- **G6-B** Every Library typechecks against the pinned terminology editions.

#### 8.2 Synthea HTN testing (P21)
Delegate to `cql-test-synthea-htn`. Runs the deterministic Synthea HTN
cohort (per §10 of the framework spec) against every Library; computes
branch coverage.

DQA gates after P21:
- **G6-COV** Per-Library branch coverage ≥ 95%. **Below threshold blocks
  the Library.**
- **G6-DET** Re-run determinism: identical Synthea seed produces
  byte-identical coverage report.

#### 8.3 ◆ Gate 2 — CQL clinician + informaticist signoff (non-overridable)
Mandatory stop. The orchestrator posts each Library's coverage report,
typecheck pass, and reference test outputs to a Gate 2 register (analogous
in shape to Gate 1, scoped to Library artifacts). For each Library, two
independent signatures are required:
- The hypertension specialist (or the Library's domain-matched specialist
  for `PregnancyHTN`, `ResistantHTN`, `SecondaryHTNTriggers`,
  `HypertensiveUrgencyEmergency`).
- The clinical informaticist.

Hard rules at this gate:
- **No Library advances on coverage < 95%.** No exception.
- **No Library advances** without a typecheck-clean run on the pinned CQL
  runtime.
- **No batch acceptance.** Each Library is signed individually.
- **No edit may relax a denylist or a hard-block** (e.g., the pregnancy
  RAAS denylist); proposed relaxations are reclassified as
  `reject-rework`.
- **Two-person rule.** Identical signature semantics as Gate 1.

DQA gate after P21:
- **G6-GATE2-A..C** as specified in `cql-clinician-signoff` §G6.GATE2.* (all
  Libraries advanced under two independent signatures; panel-chair
  cohort-level signoff present; signatures verify against pinned
  KMS/TSA).

### 9. CDS Hooks packaging (P22)

Delegate to `cds-hooks-package-htn`. Packages exactly the seven services in
the framework spec §7:

```
htn-bp-stage-and-confirm, htn-prevent-risk-and-threshold,
htn-pharm-first-line-check, htn-pregnancy-denylist,
htn-resistant-workup, htn-secondary-screen, htn-hbpm-discharge
```

DQA gates after P22:
- **G7-A** `htn-pregnancy-denylist` is wired as **`order-select`** with hard
  block (no soft warning). The orchestrator verifies the service descriptor
  declares `order-select` and that the suggestion semantics carry a hard
  refusal posture; soft-warning configuration BLOCKS.
- **G7-B** Every CDS Hooks service references a Library that passed Gate 2.
- **G7-C** Every service declares the manifest's `build_version_label` and
  the `intended_use.age_min_inclusive == 18` gate.

### 10. Safety analysis (P23)

Delegate to `safety-hbp`. Produces the hazard log per §8 of the framework
spec, including:

- H-01 RAAS in pregnancy
- H-02 Triple-whammy AKI
- H-03 Hyperkalemia on ACEi+ARB+MRA
- H-04 Older-adult orthostasis/falls
- H-05 Beta-blocker rebound
- H-06 Missed primary aldosteronism
- H-07 In-office-only diagnosis
- H-08 LLM hallucinated recommendation
- H-09 Terminology drift
- H-10 Source guideline updated/erratum

DQA gates after P23:
- **G8-A** Every hazard has at least one mitigation referencing a Library,
  CDS Hooks service, or pipeline control. Hazards without mitigation BLOCK
  the build.
- **G8-B** H-01 mitigation MUST reference `htn-pregnancy-denylist` as
  `order-select` hard-block.
- **G8-C** H-08 mitigation MUST reference Gate 1 SME signoff and
  citation-anchor preservation.
- **G8-D** H-10 mitigation MUST reference `errata_watch` and the
  no-auto-update rule.

### 11. PHI scrub and copyright check (P24, P25)

#### 11.1 PHI scrub (P24)
Delegate to `phi-scrub`. Scans every emitted artifact (records, supportive
text, monitoring text, hazard log, Guideline Card draft, Safety Case draft,
CDS Hooks service descriptors).

DQA gate after P24:
- **G9-A** Zero PHI hits. Any positive detection BLOCKS the build, opens
  the manifest's PHI hazard handler, and records a `phi-incident` audit
  event. **No override exists.**

#### 11.2 Copyright quote-extent check (P25)
Delegate to `copyright-quote-check-acc-aha`. Sums the cumulative
`copyright_envelope.verbatim_chars` across every advanced record + Guideline
Card + Safety Case + retraction notice + IG description.

DQA gates after P25:
- **G9-B** Per-page footprint ≤ `quote_envelope.chars_per_page_max` for
  every page.
- **G9-C** Document-wide footprint ≤
  `quote_envelope.chars_per_document_max`.
- **G9-D** Figures/tables verbatim reproduction is permitted only when
  `quote_envelope.figures_quotable`/`tables_quotable == true` and a
  legal-counsel signoff is recorded within the contract window.

Exceedance BLOCKS; legal counsel review is required to amend the envelope,
and amendment requires a new manifest version.

### 12. FHIR validation and IG build (P26)

Delegate to `fhir-implementation-guide-build`. Drives sushi/IG Publisher
against the emitted resources, runs the official HL7 FHIR Validator at the
pinned version, and confirms IG buildability.

DQA gates after P26:
- **G10-A** HL7 FHIR Validator clean across all resources.
- **G10-B** IG builds without errors; every PlanDefinition, ActivityDefinition,
  Library, ValueSet, CodeSystem, and Communication resource is reachable
  from the IG entry point.
- **G10-C** Every value-set is pinned to the manifest's terminology editions
  (no unpinned terminology references).

### 13. Documentation (P27)

Delegate to `guideline-docs`. Auto-populates the templates referenced in the
framework spec §11:

- Guideline Card (AGREE II 23-item ≥ 70% auto-fill; remainder HUMAN FILL)
- NAM CGAT 8-standard attestation matrix
- Safety Case (ISO 14971 hazard log + risk evaluation + residual-risk
  justification)
- Regulatory Traceability Matrix
- Retraction Notice template (parameterized for the build version)

DQA gates after P27:
- **G11-A** AGREE II ≥ 70% auto-fill achieved; HUMAN FILL markers present
  on the rest with explicit instructions.
- **G11-B** NAM CGAT attestation matrix complete (Gate 3 reviewers will sign
  it as part of the pre-publish attestation).
- **G11-C** Acknowledgement string (verbatim from
  `manifest.quote_envelope.acknowledgement_text`) present on every artifact
  containing source quotations.

### 14. Publish (P28) → ◆ Gate 3

Delegate to `guideline-version`. Atomically:

1. Computes `dataset_version` from the manifest's `build_version_label` plus
   the build's content hash.
2. Computes deterministic train/validation/test splits where applicable
   (downstream `aiwg-training` consumers only; not part of the FHIR IG
   surface).
3. Resolves licenses on every record under most-restrictive-wins.
4. Produces SHA-256 fixity manifests over every published artifact.
5. Emits the `Communication` resource for supersession of the 2017
   predecessor (manifest `supersession.communication_resource`), if and only
   if this is the first publish from this manifest.

#### 14.1 ◆ Gate 3 — Pre-publish safety attestation (non-overridable)

Mandatory stop. The orchestrator posts to `safety-case-attest` the bundled
artifact:

- The Safety Case (P27).
- The hazard log with mitigations (P23).
- The CDS Hooks service descriptors (P22).
- The Synthea coverage reports (P21).
- The Gate 1 register (per cohort) (P9).
- The Gate 2 register (per Library) (P21 → P22).
- The PHI scrub clean report (P24).
- The copyright quote-extent report (P25).
- The IG build artifacts (P26).
- The Guideline Card and Regulatory Traceability Matrix (P27).
- The supersession `Communication` resource draft (P28).

The medical director (or named designate, per ADR-HTN-001 D9) attests the
build's intended-use boundary, hazard log, residual risk, and supersession
posture. The attestation is recorded as a FHIR `Provenance` resource,
signed under the same algorithm and key class as the manifest's
medical-director signoff, time-stamped against the manifest's `tsa_list[]`.

Hard rules at this gate:
- **No publish without attestation.**
- **No attestation may relax a Gate 1 or Gate 2 outcome.** The attestation
  may decline to publish; it cannot override a prior gate's reject.
- **The attestation's content hash MUST equal** the SHA-256 over the
  canonicalized bundle as listed above; mismatch → release blocker.
- **Dual-control optional but accepted**: institutional policy may require a
  second attester (e.g., compliance officer); the schema supports up to two
  attestations.

DQA gates after Gate 3:
- **G12-A** Attestation present, verifies under the named director's KMS
  key, and time-stamps fall within the TSA's certificate validity.
- **G12-B** Cumulative quote-extent within envelope (re-checked at publish
  time).
- **G12-C** Supersession `Communication` emitted on first publish from this
  manifest; idempotent on re-publish (no duplicates).
- **G12-D** Build artifact SHA fixity manifest is complete and signed.
- **G12-E** A `dataset-version-published` event is appended to the build's
  audit log.

### 15. Build write-back

1. Persist `build.json` containing manifest reference, run id, phase
   results, gate outcomes, content hashes for every artifact, and the build
   version label.
2. Compute `build_sha256` (RFC 8785 canonical form, excluding signatures
   recorded after this point).
3. Update `provenance/flow-<run_id>.jsonld` with the closing PROV bundle.
4. Append the build-finalized event to the manifest's `audit_log[]` (the
   manifest does not mutate; the audit log is appended via the manifest's
   change-control protocol with panel-chair signoff if required).

## DQA Gates Enforced By This Skill

The orchestrator enforces a dozen high-level DQA bands aggregated from the
constituent skills' gates. Each band is fail-closed; any failure BLOCKS the
build at the corresponding phase boundary.

| Band | Where enforced | Pass criterion |
|---|---|---|
| **G0** Preflight | P0 | Manifest signed, errata clean, tools pinned, terminology pinned |
| **G1** Acquire | P1 | All four sources SHA-pinned and license-pointed |
| **G2** Parse | P2–P8 | All Phase-2 gates (G2-A through G2-RECON, G2.3-A through G2.3-G) green |
| **G3** Extract | P9 | All extraction gates (G3-A through G3-GATE1-C) green |
| **G4** Bind/PICO/Numeric | P10–P17 | All G4 gates green |
| **G5** FHIR Structuring | P18–P19 | All G5 gates green |
| **G6** CQL + Gate 2 | P20–P21 | Coverage ≥ 95% per Library; G6-GATE2 signed |
| **G7** CDS Hooks | P22 | Pregnancy denylist hard-block on order-select; service-Library binding present |
| **G8** Safety hazards | P23 | Every hazard mitigated; H-01 hard-block; H-08 SME-anchored |
| **G9** PHI/Copyright | P24–P25 | Zero PHI; envelope respected |
| **G10** FHIR Validate/IG | P26 | HL7 Validator clean; IG builds |
| **G11** Docs | P27 | AGREE II ≥ 70%; NAM CGAT matrix; acknowledgement on every artifact |
| **G12** Publish + Gate 3 | P28 | Attestation signed; envelope re-checked; supersession emitted |

- RecommendationRecord set at `work/<run_id>/records.json` (sealed at end
  of P9).
- Gate 1 registers (per cohort) at `work/<run_id>/gate1/*.signed.jsonld`.
- Atomic-unit set at `work/<run_id>/atomic-units.json`.
- FHIR resources under `work/<run_id>/fhir/`.
- CQL Libraries under `work/<run_id>/cql/`.
- Synthea coverage reports at `work/<run_id>/cql/coverage/`.
- Gate 2 registers (per Library) at `work/<run_id>/gate2/*.signed.jsonld`.
- CDS Hooks service descriptors at `work/<run_id>/cds-hooks/`.
- Safety Case + hazard log at `work/<run_id>/safety/`.
- PHI scrub report at `work/<run_id>/reports/phi-<run_id>.md`.
- Copyright quote-extent report at
  `work/<run_id>/reports/copyright-<run_id>.md`.

  `work/<run_id>/docs/`.

  `work/<run_id>/gate3/attestation.signed.jsonld`.

- Per-phase reports at `work/<run_id>/reports/`.
- Activity log appended at `<repo>/.aiwg/cpg-htn/activity.log`.

## Error Handling

- **Manifest not active.** BLOCK preflight; instruct operator to activate or
  open a new manifest version.
- **Errata blocker open.** BLOCK preflight.
- **Tool unreachable / pin mismatch.** BLOCK preflight; emit which tool and
  what was expected vs. observed.
- **Family-distinct LLM rule violated.** BLOCK preflight (`AU-INV-09`).
- **Source SHA mismatch.** BLOCK at P1; emit `version-drift`.
- **Parse DQA gate red.** Pause at the failing phase; route to the
  reconciliation queue. Resume with `--resume` after queue is green.
- **Triple-modal consensus failed on a record.** Hold the record at P9;
  open queue; advance other records.
- **Gate 1 reviewer disagreement.** Auto-escalate to panel chair; do not
  majority-vote.
- **Gate 1 reviewer requests COR/LOE edit.** Reclassify as `reject-rework`;
  never accept as edit.
- **Library coverage < 95%.** BLOCK Gate 2 for that Library.
- **Pregnancy denylist proposed soft-warning.** Reclassify as
  `reject-rework`; never accept.
- **PHI hit.** BLOCK at P24 unconditionally; route to the PHI hazard
  handler.
- **Copyright envelope exceeded.** BLOCK at P25; require manifest amendment.
- **HL7 FHIR Validator error.** BLOCK at P26.
- **Gate 3 attestation declined.** Emit a `gate3-declined` event; do not
  publish; do not retry without a new build run.
- **Lock contention.** Wait up to a configured timeout; fail-closed if not
  acquired; no concurrent writers permitted on the same SAIR/records doc.
- **Resume after partial run.** Verify `tools_lock_sha` matches; if it has
  changed, reject the resume and require a fresh run.

## Examples

```bash
# First full build from a freshly-active manifest
flow-hbp-2025-build manifests/v1.0.0+ACC-AHA-2025+US+2026-04-30.yaml

# Re-run only the parse + extract phases for a specific cohort
flow-hbp-2025-build manifests/v1.0.0+ACC-AHA-2025+US+2026-04-30.yaml \
  --from parse-conditioning \
  --to extract \
  --cohort cohort-7c2a8e91b3d4f561

# Dry-run plan emission for change-control review
flow-hbp-2025-build manifests/v1.0.0+ACC-AHA-2025+US+2026-04-30.yaml \
  --dry-run

# Resume after a Gate 1 panel-chair resolution
flow-hbp-2025-build manifests/v1.0.0+ACC-AHA-2025+US+2026-04-30.yaml \
  --resume

# Targeted re-run of CQL + Gate 2 + CDS Hooks after a Library re-author
flow-hbp-2025-build manifests/v1.0.0+ACC-AHA-2025+US+2026-04-30.yaml \
  --phases cql-libraries,cql-tests,cds-hooks \
  --resume
```

## Authority Boundaries

**Can do**
- Sequence phases, enforce DQA gates, post to gate registers, emit reports.
- Open and close work directories deterministically; manage SAIR/records
  write-back locks.
- Compose the build's PROV bundle and audit log.
- Refuse to advance on any failed gate.

**Requires approval (Gate 1 / Gate 2 / Gate 3 / panel chair / queue with
two-person rule)**
- Any clinical-content advance after Gate 1 (per record).
- Any Library advance after Gate 2 (per Library).
- Publication after Gate 3 (per build).
- Any reconciliation queue resolution touching a recommendation row, COR,
  LOE, threshold, drug, or population scope.
- Any errata-driven manifest amendment.

**Never**
- Bypass a gate. No `--force-gate` flag exists.
- Auto-correct a constituent skill's output.
- Mutate a sealed SAIR or records document.
- Substitute a different LLM, VLM, OCR engine, terminology server, risk
  engine, or TSA without a new manifest version.
- Relax the pregnancy denylist hard-block, even on reviewer request.
- Continue a build with any open PHI hit, any envelope overage, any
  Library coverage < 95%, or any open Gate 1/Gate 2/Gate 3 dispute.
- Run with `--strict false` in production.
- Operate against a manifest in any state other than `active`.

# gate1-sme-review

Reviewer-interface skill for Gate 1 — the first non-overridable
human-authorization stop in the `cpg-htn-2025-acc-aha` framework. This skill
takes one `RecommendationRecordHTN` (sealed by `extract-recommendation-cor-loe`
under triple-modal consensus) and one named, credential-evidenced reviewer,
presents the data-only review surface specified in
`extract-recommendation-cor-loe` §10.2, captures the reviewer's decision and
rationale, applies a cryptographic signature against the record's content
hash, and persists a `ReviewerSignoff` into the cohort's
`schemas/gate1-register.yaml` instance.

This is **the only** path by which a `RecommendationRecord` advances out of
`gate-1-pending` and into downstream phases. The skill is invoked once per
(reviewer, record) pair. It does not batch. It does not auto-decide. It does
not coerce. It enforces the schema's twenty-five invariants and the policy
clauses in `gate1-register.yaml` §1; it refuses on any violation. A second
invocation with the same `(reviewer_id, record_id)` is rejected as a
self-pairing or duplicate-signoff attempt.

Posture: **caution over velocity, fidelity over coverage, verbatim over
paraphrase.** The reviewer is the clinical authority of record. The skill is
a strict scribe that captures the reviewer's authorized decision and refuses
to capture anything outside policy. No COR/LOE edits. No batch. No
self-pairing. No COR/LOE substitution sneaked in via "rationale". No
post-signoff mutation.

## When to Use

Invoke this skill when:

- The orchestrator (`flow-hbp-2025-build`) has reached **Gate 1** for a
  cohort and posted records into `gate-1-pending`.
- A named reviewer authenticated through the institutional KMS is ready to
  decide on a single record.
- A previously-recorded `reject-rework` decision has been addressed by
  `extract-recommendation-cor-loe` and the record is back in
  `gate-1-pending` with a new content hash.

Do **not** invoke this skill if:

- The cohort's manifest (`guideline-manifest-hbp-2025.yaml`) is in any state
  other than `active`.
- The record's `provenance.consensus.state` is anything other than
  `gate-1-pending`.
- The record's `record_content_hash` does not recompute against the on-disk
  record canonicalization.
- The reviewer's credential evidence is missing, expired, or fails
  verification at validation time.
- The reviewer's identity assurance level is below `IAL2` (or `IAL3` for
  panel-chair / medical-director cases).
- The reviewer's signing key has rotated since the panel roster was sealed
  for this cohort and no roster amendment has been recorded.

The skill performs preflight checks against all of the above and refuses to
proceed otherwise.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `register-path` | yes | — | Path to the Gate 1 cohort register (`schemas/gate1-register.yaml` instance) at `work/<run-id>/gate1/<cohort-id>.signed.jsonld`. The skill writes back atomically. |
| `record-id` | yes | — | The `RecommendationRecordHTN.recommendation_id` to be signed. Must currently be in state `gate-1-pending` and bound to this register's cohort. |
| `--reviewer <id>` | yes | — | The reviewer's stable `Reviewer.reviewer_id`. Must be a member of `panel.reviewers[]` on the register. |
| `--cohort <id>` | no | (from register) | Defensive cohort id; if supplied must equal `cohort.cohort_id`. Used by the orchestrator to detect register-cohort mismatch. |
| `--decision <enum>` | yes | — | One of `accept`, `accept-with-edit`, `reject-rework`, `escalate-panel`, `recused`. Closed enum from `gate1-register.yaml`. |
| `--rationale <text>` | yes | — | Reviewer's free-text rationale, non-empty. Stored verbatim. PHI-scrubbed before persistence; any hit BLOCKS. |
| `--edits <json>` | no | — | JSON array of `Edit` entries. Permitted only with `--decision accept-with-edit`. **Forbidden targets**: `acc_aha_cor`, `acc_aha_loe`. |
| `--coi <json>` | no | (auto-loaded from reviewer profile) | JSON array of applicable COI kinds the reviewer flags for this record. Used to compute COI auto-disqualification. |
| `--escalate-to <role>` | no | `panel-chair` | Required when `--decision escalate-panel`. Role to escalate to per `gate1-register.yaml` ReviewerRole enum. |
| `--session-attest <json>` | yes | — | JSON object with three booleans: `reviewed_source_pdf_region`, `reviewed_atomic_units`, `reviewed_pico_precheck`. All MUST be true for `accept` / `accept-with-edit`. |
| `--predecessor-attest` | no | `true` | Boolean: reviewer attests they reviewed the predecessor-2017 advisory mapping. Defaults `true`; the schema field is recorded either way. |
| `--key-id <id>` | yes | — | The institutional KMS key id under which this signature is generated. Must equal the reviewer's `Reviewer.public_key.key_id`. |
| `--tsa <fingerprint>` | no | (cohort-pinned default) | The RFC 3161 TSA cert SHA-256 fingerprint to use for the time-stamp. Must be a member of the manifest's `tsa_list[]` and currently within `cert_valid_*`. |
| `--resume` | no | `false` | Resume a partially-prepared signature payload after a transient KMS / TSA failure. Required after any infrastructure error; never used to alter content. |

## Operation

### 1. Preflight (per invocation)

The skill refuses to begin signing work until every check below passes.

#### 1.1 Manifest and register checks
1. Load `register-path`; validate against `schemas/gate1-register.yaml`.
2. Resolve `register.guideline_manifest_ref`; load the manifest; require
   `state == "active"` and `medical_director_signoff` verifies. Producer
   claims of `verifies: true` are ignored; the skill re-verifies.
3. Confirm `register.cohort.state ∈ {in-review, awaiting-panel-chair}`.
   `finalized`, `superseded`, `withdrawn` are refusals.
4. Confirm cohort id matches `--cohort` if supplied.

#### 1.2 Record checks
1. Load the `RecommendationRecordHTN` for `record-id` from the records
   document at `work/<run-id>/records.json`.
2. Confirm `provenance.consensus.state == "gate-1-pending"`.
3. Recompute the record's `content_hash` over the canonicalized record with
   `provenance.reviewer_signoffs` stripped (RFC 8785 / JCS canonical form).
   Store as `expected_content_hash`.
4. Confirm `expected_content_hash` matches the `RecordEntry.record_content_hash`
   currently recorded on the register; mismatch indicates an out-of-band
   record edit and is a release blocker.
5. Confirm `record.anchors.sair_sha256` matches the SAIR fixity recorded on
   the register and on the manifest.

#### 1.3 Reviewer checks
1. Resolve `--reviewer` to a `Reviewer` entry in `register.panel.reviewers[]`.
   Missing → refuse.
2. Require `Reviewer.identity_proof.ial >= IAL2` (or `IAL3` if the role is
   `panel-chair` or `medical-director`); `aal` likewise.
3. Verify every `Reviewer.credentials[*]` entry is non-expired
   (`valid_until == null` or in the future) and the `kind` is consistent
   with `Reviewer.role` per `docs/role-credential-matrix.md`.
4. Confirm `Reviewer.public_key.key_id == --key-id`. The signing key
   identity is bound at panel-roster time; mismatch is a release blocker.
5. Confirm the reviewer's `Reviewer.coi_disclosures[]` is non-empty (a
   reviewer with no COI records a single `kind: none` entry).

#### 1.4 Composition pre-feasibility
1. Look up the record's domain class (from
   `RecommendationRecord.section_path` and `pico_precheck.populations[]`).
2. Resolve the required reviewer-pair set from the matrix in
   `gate1-register.yaml` §1 `reviewer_composition.matrix`.
3. Check whether the `--reviewer` role is admissible at all for this
   record's domain. (E.g., a `geriatrician` is not admissible on a
   pregnancy record.) Inadmissible → refuse.
4. Check whether accepting this signoff would create a self-pairing
   (two signoffs from the same `reviewer_id`) — refuse.
5. Check whether this signoff would over-fill the slot for the reviewer's
   role for this record (e.g., a second `clinical-pharmacologist` on a
   pregnancy record beyond the maximum of four signoffs) — refuse.

#### 1.5 COI auto-disqualification
1. For each `Reviewer.coi_disclosures[*]`, evaluate
   `auto_disqualifies_record_kinds[]` against the record's kind set
   (drug class, population, therapeutic area, guideline-document scope).
2. If any overlap, the reviewer is auto-disqualified for this record. The
   skill rejects an `accept` / `accept-with-edit` decision and instructs
   the orchestrator to record a `recused` signoff and require a
   substitute reviewer of the same role.

#### 1.6 Decision-grammar checks
1. Confirm `--decision` is in the closed enum.
2. If `--decision == accept-with-edit`:
   - `--edits` MUST be present and non-empty.
   - Every edit's `target` MUST be in `EditTarget`. Targets `acc_aha_cor`
     and `acc_aha_loe` are not in the enum and would already be rejected
     at the schema boundary; the skill ALSO refuses any rationale that
     references altering the COR / LOE (defensive textual scan).
   - Each edit must have non-empty `before`, `after`, `rationale`.
3. If `--decision == reject-rework`:
   - `--edits` MUST be empty or absent.
   - `--rationale` MUST identify the defect class (e.g., span boundary,
     verbatim integrity, citation linkage). The skill does not enforce a
     taxonomy here, but the rationale is structured downstream by
     `parse-reconcile-queue`.
4. If `--decision == escalate-panel`:
   - `--escalate-to` MUST be a non-empty `ReviewerRole`.
   - `--edits` MUST be empty.
5. If `--decision == recused`:
   - `--edits` MUST be empty.
   - At least one applicable COI kind MUST be present in `--coi`.

#### 1.7 Session-attestation gate
1. For `accept` / `accept-with-edit`, all three booleans in
   `--session-attest` MUST be `true`. Anything else is a refusal: a
   reviewer who has not viewed the rasterized source region, the atomic
   units, and the PICO precheck cannot accept.
2. The skill records `--predecessor-attest` either way; downstream Gate 3
   re-checks predecessor-mapping disposition.

#### 1.8 Cryptographic prerequisites
1. Probe the institutional KMS for `--key-id`; require operational status,
   matching algorithm against `Reviewer.public_key.algorithm`.
2. Resolve `--tsa` to a `TSA` in the manifest's `tsa_list[]`; confirm
   currently within `cert_valid_*` and supports SHA-256.
3. If the cohort already pinned a TSA at first signoff, prefer that TSA
   (consistency); permit a different TSA only when the prior TSA is
   no longer within validity.

Any preflight failure → BLOCK with a precise reason. No retry, no
auto-fix, no fallback path.

### 2. Reviewer-surface composition (data-only)

The skill composes the data surface for the reviewer per
`extract-recommendation-cor-loe` §10.2, **without UI specifics** — the
surface is the data envelope; rendering belongs to a host UI. The envelope
is persisted into `work/<run-id>/gate1/sessions/<session-id>.json` and is
read-only:

```yaml
session_id: "sess-<16hex>"
opened_at: <iso>
record:
  recommendation_id:    <id>
  text_verbatim:        <verbatim NFC>
  acc_aha_cor:          <enum>
  acc_aha_loe:          <enum>
  section_path:         [...]
  atomic_units:         [...]            # spans into text_verbatim
  qualifier_spans:      [...]
  exclusion_spans:      [...]
  monitoring_spans:     [...]
  citation_spans:       [...]
  pico_precheck:        {...}
  bp_thresholds:        [...]            # advisory only at Gate 1
  drug_rules:           {...}            # advisory only at Gate 1
  contraindications:    [...]
  monitoring:           [...]
  references:           [...]
  predecessor_2017:     {...}            # advisory mapping
  anchors:              {...}
  normalization_log:    {...}
source_view:
  pdf_sha256:           <hex>
  page:                 <int>
  bbox:                 [x0, y0, x1, y1]
  raster_path_600dpi:   <path>           # the on-disk rasterized region
  cell_bboxes:          {cor, loe, recommendation}
consensus_evidence:
  state:                triple-consensus
  similarity_min_pairwise: <float>
  drafts:
    a: { tool, pin, text_verbatim }
    v: { tool, pin, text_verbatim, prompt_id }
    o: { tool, pin, text_verbatim, confidence_min }
atomicity_evidence:
  state: agreed | held | conflict
  llm_pair: [{model, pin}, {model, pin}]
  jaccard: <float>
  proposals: [...]
held_or_conflict_flags: [...]            # if any
predecessor_view:                         # advisory
  relation: ...
  predecessor_id: ...
operator_capabilities:
  may_decide:           [accept, accept-with-edit, reject-rework, escalate-panel, recused]
  may_edit_targets:     [text_verbatim_typo, supportive_text, monitoring_text, citation_link]
  forbidden_edit_targets: [acc_aha_cor, acc_aha_loe]
```

The reviewer's host UI is responsible for presenting all of the above
above-the-fold and without scrolling per `extract-recommendation-cor-loe`
§10.2. The skill emits the envelope; it does not render. The skill does
not modify the envelope after issuance; any record mutation produces a new
envelope under a new `session_id`.

### 3. Decision capture and validation

Once the reviewer submits a decision via the CLI (`--decision`,
`--rationale`, optional `--edits`, `--coi`, `--escalate-to`,
`--session-attest`, `--predecessor-attest`), the skill:

1. Re-applies §1.6 and §1.7 to the submitted values; refuses any drift.
2. Runs PHI scrub (`presidio + spacy-med7 + regex-us`) over `--rationale`
   and over each edit's `rationale`. Any positive PHI hit BLOCKS. The
   reviewer is informed of the location class (without echoing the PHI).
3. Defensive textual scan over `--rationale` and edits' rationale for
   strings that look like attempted COR/LOE substitution requests
   (regex against the closed COR/LOE enum tokens in altering verbs:
   "change to", "should be IIa", "set LOE to", etc.). Hits trigger
   automatic reclassification to `reject-rework`, with the original
   intent preserved in the queue note.
4. Computes the canonical signoff payload (`ReviewerSignoff` minus the
   `signature` field) per RFC 8785.
5. Computes `payload_sha256` over that canonical payload.
6. Confirms the `record_content_hash` field on the payload equals
   `expected_content_hash` from §1.2 (binding the signature to the exact
   record state observed in the session).

### 4. Cryptographic signature and time-stamp

1. Submit `payload_sha256` to the institutional KMS under `--key-id` with
   the algorithm declared in `Reviewer.public_key.algorithm`. The KMS
   returns a raw signature; the skill never holds the private key.
2. Submit the signature plus `payload_sha256` to the chosen `--tsa`; obtain
   an RFC 3161 Tim

*System: User retried message*

# gate1-sme-review

Reviewer-interface skill for **Gate 1** of the `cpg-htn-2025-acc-aha`
framework. The skill is the only authorized producer of `ReviewerSignoff`
entries on the Gate 1 cohort register defined in
`schemas/gate1-register.yaml`. It renders the data-only review surface
specified in `extract-recommendation-cor-loe` §10.2, captures two
independent reviewer decisions per record under the composition matrix in
`gate1-register.yaml` §1, escalates disagreements to the panel chair, and
finalizes the cohort under panel-chair signoff.

This skill does **not** generate clinical content, summarize recommendations,
re-grade COR/LOE, or perform extraction. It is a *signature surface* over
content already produced and gated by the deterministic, triple-modal
pipeline. Every reviewer's signature binds a named individual with credential
evidence to the SHA-256 of a specific record at a specific time, time-stamped
by an RFC 3161 TSA pinned in the active manifest.

Posture: **caution over velocity, fidelity over coverage, verbatim over
paraphrase.** Two-person rule, no batch acceptance, no COR/LOE edits, no
self-pairing, no override on auto-disqualifying COI, no soft-warning relaxation
of pregnancy hard-blocks. Post-signoff content is immutable; corrections
require a new register version with explicit predecessor chain.

## When to Use

Invoke this skill when:

- The orchestrator (`flow-hbp-2025-build`) reaches phase **P9 → ◆ Gate 1**
  and posts a Gate 1 cohort register at `work/<run_id>/gate1/<cohort>.jsonld`.
- A specific reviewer is scheduled for an interactive review session against
  records assigned to them in that cohort.
- A panel chair is scheduled to dispose of escalated records and finalize a
  cohort for advance.
- A previously held cohort needs to be resumed after a queue resolution or a
  reviewer-driven `accept-with-edit` regenerated downstream artifacts.

Do **not** invoke this skill if:

- The cohort register's `state` is `finalized`, `superseded`, or `withdrawn`.
- The active manifest's `medical_director_signoff` is missing or fails
  verification.
- Any record bound to the cohort has a `provenance.consensus.state` other
  than `gate-1-pending` (e.g., still `escalated-pending` upstream).
- The orchestrator has not posted the cohort to this skill's queue yet
  (the skill refuses to cold-start a cohort).

## Parameters

| Parameter | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `register-path` | yes | — | Path to a Gate 1 register at `work/<run_id>/gate1/<cohort>.jsonld`, validated against `schemas/gate1-register.yaml`. The skill writes back atomically. |
| `--cohort <id>` | no | derived from `register-path` | Cohort id; defaults to the cohort recorded in the register. The skill rejects mismatch. |
| `--reviewer <id>` | no | — | The reviewer id (`rev-<16hex>`) for the current session. Required in `--mode sign`. The skill refuses to act on behalf of any other reviewer in the same session. |
| `--record <id>` | no | `next` | The specific record id (`rec-<16hex>`) to review next. Defaults to the next record in the reviewer's pending queue (deterministic ordering by `record_id` ascending, skipping records the reviewer cannot sign per composition / COI rules). |
| `--mode <browse\|sign\|chair-finalize>` | no | `browse` | `browse` renders the review surface read-only. `sign` opens an authenticated signing session (requires `--reviewer`). `chair-finalize` opens the panel-chair finalization surface (requires the reviewer's role == `panel-chair`). |
| `--resume` | no | `false` | Resume an interrupted session from the last persisted decision. The skill rejects resume if the register's `fixity.register_sha256` has changed since session start. |
| `--strict` | no | `true` | Fail-closed on every invariant. Setting `--strict false` is **never permitted** in production; the flag exists only for fixture and golden-set development. |

## Operation

### 1. Preflight

1. Validate `register-path` against `schemas/gate1-register.yaml`. Reject on
   any invariant failure (`G1-INV-01` … `G1-INV-25`).
2. Re-resolve `guideline_manifest_ref`; verify the active manifest's
   `medical_director_signoff` cryptographically (`GM-INV-21`); verify
   `state == "active"` and `errata_watch.blockers_open == []`.
3. Verify the register's `cohort.run_id` matches the run id recorded in the
   build's PROV bundle.
4. For every record bound to the cohort, load the corresponding
   `RecommendationRecordHTN` from `work/<run_id>/records.json`; verify each
   record's content hash recomputes to the value in `record_content_hash`
   on the register entry. Mismatch → BLOCK (post-signoff mutation detected
   on a prior step).
5. Verify `tsa_list[]` in the manifest has at least one TSA whose
   `cert_valid_until` covers the wall-clock window. Otherwise BLOCK.
6. In `--mode sign`:
   - Resolve `--reviewer` to a `Reviewer` in `panel.reviewers[]`.
   - Verify the reviewer's `identity_proof.ial` ≥ `IAL2`,
     `identity_proof.aal` ≥ `AAL2`, and at least one `Credential` whose
     `kind` matches the role per the role-credential matrix.
   - Verify the reviewer holds a non-expired `Credential` covering the
     session's wall-clock time.
   - Verify the reviewer has at least one `coi_disclosures[]` entry
     (kind `none` or otherwise).
   - Authenticate the reviewer interactively via the institutional KMS
     (the skill does not store credentials; it requests a per-session
     attestation token bound to the reviewer's `key_id`).
7. In `--mode chair-finalize`:
   - Resolve `--reviewer` to a `Reviewer` in `panel.reviewers[]` whose
     `role == "panel-chair"`, `identity_proof.ial == "IAL3"`,
     `aal == "AAL3"`.
   - Authenticate via the KMS as in `sign` mode.
8. Refuse to proceed if any precondition fails. **Fail-closed.**

### 2. Reviewer-pending queue construction (mode `sign`)

For the authenticated reviewer:

1. Determine the reviewer's eligible records under the composition matrix
   (`gate1-register.yaml` §1):
   - Resolve each record's domain from `RecommendationRecordHTN.section_path`
     and `pico_precheck.populations`.
   - For each record, look up the required-roles set for that domain.
   - The reviewer is **eligible** for a record iff the reviewer's `role`
     appears in the required-roles set AND no auto-disqualifying COI
     applies (`G1-INV-14`).
2. Exclude records the reviewer has already signed (no double-signing per
   `G1-INV-21`).
3. Exclude records currently in `panel-escalated` state unless the reviewer
   is the panel chair (which is handled by `chair-finalize` mode, not
   `sign` mode).
4. Order the remaining records by `record_id` ascending for deterministic
   session resumption.
5. The skill rejects any explicit `--record` whose `record_id` is not in the
   reviewer's eligible queue.

### 3. Data-only review surface (encodes `extract-recommendation-cor-loe` §10.2)

For each record presented to the reviewer in `--mode sign`, the skill
renders the following panes side-by-side, **without** scrolling above the
fold (the rendering medium is the platform's reviewer UI; the skill is the
data contract for that UI):

#### 3.1 Source pane
- The record's anchored region of the source PDF, rasterized at 600 DPI
  using `RecommendationRecordHTN.anchors.bbox` and `anchors.page`.
- The cell bboxes for COR / LOE / Recommendation overlaid as
  non-destructive outlines (color-coded; legend below the pane).
- The full source page index for context navigation; never editable.

#### 3.2 Verbatim text pane
- `RecommendationRecordHTN.text_verbatim` rendered byte-faithfully.
- Hover (or equivalent) reveals the `normalization_log[]` per character
  position (e.g., "soft-hyphen-removed at offset 47", "ligature-decomposed
  fi → fi at offset 92").
- Footnote markers within the text are clickable; each click opens the
  resolved footnote text from SAIR's `footnotes_index` (the skill never
  mutates).

#### 3.3 Grading pane
- `acc_aha_cor` and `acc_aha_loe` displayed verbatim.
- The cell crops alongside the canonical values, so the reviewer can
  visually confirm the OCR / VLM / deterministic extractor agreement.
- The cell's reconciliation history (the per-engine variants) shown on
  request (default collapsed).
- A persistent banner: **"COR and LOE are read-only at Gate 1. Edit requests
  are reclassified as reject-rework."**

#### 3.4 Atomic-units pane
- Each `atomic_units[*].span` highlighted as a colored span within the
  verbatim text pane (cross-pane synchronization).
- Per-unit kind chip (atomic-recommendation, qualifier, exclusion,
  monitoring, citation).
- Per-unit Jaccard agreement displayed.
- The atomicity state: `agreed` / `held` / `conflict`. If `held` or
  `conflict`, the proposal-diff view is shown by default.
- A persistent acknowledgement checkbox: **"I acknowledge the atomicity
  state for this record."** This sets
  `ReviewerSignoff.atomicity_state_acknowledged` (`agreed` or `held`); the
  reviewer cannot sign without acknowledging.

#### 3.5 PICO precheck pane
- `pico_precheck.populations[]`, `population_present`, `intervention_present`,
  `comparator_kind`, `outcome_kind`.
- The mapped HTN-typed Population enum values are shown; if any is
  `secondary-htn-suspected`, `urgency`, or `emergency`, a banner indicates
  the corresponding Library and CDS Hooks service downstream.

#### 3.6 Triple-modal consensus pane
- `provenance.consensus.state` and `provenance.consensus.similarity_min_pairwise`.
- A side-by-side diff of extractor A, V, and O outputs when any pairwise
  similarity is below 1.0 (still passing the 0.99 floor); shown on request.
- The pane refuses to render if the consensus state is anything other than
  `gate-1-pending` (any record displayed for sign-mode review must be in
  that state).

#### 3.7 Predecessor 2017 pane
- `predecessor_2017.relation` and the linked predecessor record id (if any).
- A read-only side-by-side of the 2017 source-anchored region (when
  available), to support the reviewer's relation acknowledgement.
- The skill banner: **"Predecessor mapping is advisory. Acknowledge or
  request panel review; do not edit."**

#### 3.8 Decision pane
- Closed-set chooser: `accept`, `accept-with-edit`, `reject-rework`,
  `escalate-panel`, `recused`.
- Required free-text rationale (non-empty; `minLength: 1`).
- For `accept-with-edit`: an edit form with the closed `EditTarget` enum
  (`text_verbatim_typo`, `supportive_text`, `monitoring_text`,
  `citation_link`). The form **does not list** `acc_aha_cor` or
  `acc_aha_loe`; submitting an attempt to edit either via direct API
  invocation is rejected (`G1-INV-12`).
- A COI re-attestation: the reviewer confirms `no_undisclosed_coi == true`
  and selects any applicable `COIKind` flags for this record. Selecting an
  auto-disqualifying COI rewrites the decision to `recused` and prevents
  the signature.

### 4. Sign cycle (mode `sign`)

For each `--record` in turn:

1. Lock the record entry on the register (`record_id`) for write.
2. Recompute the `RecommendationRecord` content hash with
   `provenance.reviewer_signoffs` stripped at the time of signing; verify
   it equals the register entry's `record_content_hash`. Mismatch → BLOCK.
3. Ask the reviewer to confirm decision and rationale; produce a
   `ReviewerSignoff` candidate (no signature yet) that conforms to
   `gate1-register.yaml` §3.8.
4. Compose the signing payload as the JCS-canonical form of the candidate
   `ReviewerSignoff` with `signature` field stripped.
5. Compute `payload_sha256 = SHA-256(canonical_payload)`.
6. Issue a signature request to the reviewer's institutional KMS bound to
   `Reviewer.public_key.key_id`. The signing keys are never exported to
   the framework process; the KMS returns `signature_b64` and metadata.
7. Request an RFC 3161 time-stamp from a TSA in `manifest.tsa_list[]`
   whose certificate validity covers `signed_at`. Persist the
   `TimeStampToken` and metadata. Reject any TSA whose certificate fails
   chain verification.
8. Verify the signature locally before persisting:
   - Construct the canonical payload again.
   - Recompute `payload_sha256`.
   - Verify `signature_b64` against `Reviewer.public_key.key_pem` under
     `signature.algorithm`.
   - Confirm the time-stamp token's hash equals `payload_sha256` and the
     TSA cert chains to a trust anchor pinned in the manifest.
   - Set `signature.verifies = true` only after these checks succeed.
9. Persist the `ReviewerSignoff` into
   `register.records[*].signoffs[]` for this record, atomically.
10. Update the record entry's disposition `state`:
    - 1 of 2 signoffs at `accept` / `accept-with-edit`: state remains
      `pending`, awaiting the second reviewer.
    - 2 of 2 with both `accept` (and at most one `accept-with-edit`):
      state becomes `accepted` or `accepted-with-edit`.
    - Any `reject-rework`: state becomes `rework-required`; emit a
      `rework_history[]` entry; remove signoffs at the panel-chair's option
      only; signal the orchestrator to regenerate downstream artifacts.
    - Any `escalate-panel`: state becomes `panel-escalated`; open the
      `escalation` block; the orchestrator pauses downstream phases for the
      record.
    - `recused`: state remains `pending`; remove the reviewer from this
      record's eligible set; signal the panel chair to recompose if the
      remaining eligible set cannot satisfy the matrix.
11. Append a `RegisterAuditEvent` of kind `signoff-recorded` to
    `audit_log[]`; recompute `fixity.register_sha256` (RFC 8785 with
    `fixity` excluded); persist.
12. Emit a `Provenance` entity update referencing the signoff for the
    build's PROV bundle.

#### 4.1 Edit handling (`accept-with-edit`)

If the reviewer's decision is `accept-with-edit`:

1. The proposed edits are validated against the closed `EditTarget` enum
   (no `acc_aha_cor`, no `acc_aha_loe`).
2. The skill applies the edits to a working copy of the
   `RecommendationRecord` (never the original; produces a new record content
   hash).
3. **Critical rule:** if the edit targets `text_verbatim_typo`, all child
   `AtomicUnit` instances on the record MUST be deleted and regenerated by
   the orchestrator (`AU-INV-24`). The skill does not perform regeneration;
   it signals the orchestrator and persists the record in
   `pending-regeneration` state until atomic units are restored.
4. The reviewer's signature covers the *new* content hash; the *old* hash is
   retained immutably for audit.
5. The second reviewer's signoff (if already present) is invalidated by
   the content hash change and MUST be re-collected against the new hash.
   The skill emits a `ReviewerSignoff.recused` placeholder for the prior
   signature with rationale "content hash changed under accept-with-edit"
   and re-queues the second reviewer.

This protocol is identical to `gate1-register.yaml`'s
`post_signoff_immutability` rule (`G1-INV-09`).

#### 4.2 Decision-protocol auto-routing rules

The skill applies these mechanical rules without operator override:

- An attempted edit targeting `acc_aha_cor` or `acc_aha_loe` is rewritten
  to `reject-rework` with the rationale prefixed
  "Auto-rewrite per G1-INV-12: COR/LOE edits are forbidden at Gate 1."
- An attempted decision of `accept` or `accept-with-edit` while a COI
  auto-disqualifies the reviewer is rewritten to `recused` with the
  rationale prefixed "Auto-rewrite per G1-INV-14: COI auto-disqualification."
- An attempted second signature by the same `reviewer_id` already present
  on the record is rejected outright (`G1-INV-21`).
- An attempted `accept-with-edit` whose edits fail `Edit` schema
  validation is rejected without auto-rewrite; the reviewer is asked to
  correct the edit form.
- An attempted decision while the cohort's `state` is `awaiting-panel-chair`
  or `finalized` is rejected.

### 5. Reviewer disagreement → panel escalation

When two signoffs are present on a record and at least one is
`reject-rework` or `escalate-panel` while another is `accept` /
`accept-with-edit`, the skill auto-escalates per
`extract-recommendation-cor-loe` §10.3:

1. Set the record's disposition `state = "panel-escalated"`.
2. Populate `escalation` with `escalated_to_role: panel-chair`, the
   originating reasons, and `resolution: null`.
3. Append `RegisterAuditEvent` of kind `escalation-opened`.
4. Notify the panel chair via the platform's reviewer notification surface
   (the skill emits the notification record; delivery is platform).

The skill does **not** majority-vote, does not auto-resolve, and does not
permit a third specialty reviewer to break a tie outside the panel-chair
process.

### 6. Panel-chair finalization (mode `chair-finalize`)

In `--mode chair-finalize`, the skill renders a chair surface scoped to the
cohort:

#### 6.1 Composition compliance pane
- A record-by-record view of `signoffs[*].role` against the composition
  matrix.
- Missing-role flags rendered red; satisfied composition rendered green.
- Pregnancy records have a banner verifying MFM + clinical pharmacology
  presence (`G1-INV-23`).

#### 6.2 Escalations pane
- Every record in `panel-escalated` state.
- For each, the escalation reason and the disagreeing signoffs.
- The chair's options per record: `accept`, `accept-with-edit`,
  `reject-rework`. The chair's decision is recorded as a
  `resolution.resolver_signoff` on the escalation block.
- The chair's decision is itself a `ReviewerSignoff` with role
  `panel-chair`; identical signing flow as §4 but tagged as a resolver.

#### 6.3 Cohort-finalization pane
- A scrolling list of every record's terminal state.
- Two attestation toggles, both required:
  - `composition_compliance_attested`
  - `escalations_disposed`
- A COI re-attestation for the chair (cohort-scope).
- A "Sign cohort" action that produces the `PanelChairSignoff` covering
  `cohort_manifest_hash` (the SHA-256 over JCS-canonical
  `records[]` ordered by `record_id` ascending; the skill recomputes and
  rejects mismatch).

#### 6.4 Cohort-signoff cycle

1. Lock the register for write.
2. Recompute `cohort_manifest_hash`; reject if not deterministic.
3. Build the chair's signing payload (`PanelChairSignoff` candidate with
   `signature` stripped); compute `payload_sha256`.
4. Issue signature request to the chair's KMS key (Ed25519 or
   ECDSA-P256-SHA256, AAL3).
5. Time-stamp via a manifest TSA whose cert covers `signed_at`.
6. Locally verify the signature and time-stamp; set `verifies: true`.
7. Persist `panel.panel_chair_signoff`; transition `cohort.state` to
   `finalized`; set `cohort.finalized_at`.
8. Append `audit_log[]` events `panel-chair-signed` and `cohort-finalized`;
   recompute `fixity.register_sha256`; persist.
9. Signal the orchestrator that the cohort is ready to advance (P10–P17).

### 7. Determinism and reproducibility

- The reviewer-pending queue is deterministic given the register and the
  reviewer id; resume is safe across orchestrator restarts.
- Re-running this skill on a finalized register is a no-op (the skill
  refuses to mutate a finalized register; corrections require a new
  register version).
- Re-running on an in-review register at the same `register_sha256`
  produces identical eligible-queue ordering and identical disposition
  state (modulo new signatures introduced by the resumed session).
- Signature payload canonicalization is RFC 8785 (JCS); identical
  canonical bytes produce identical `payload_sha256` across runs.
- Time-stamps are authoritative for ordering; the audit log is appended in
  `occurred_at` order and chained by `payload_sha256` per
  `G1-INV-18`.

## DQA Gates Enforced By This Skill

| Gate | Condition for advance |
|---|---|
| **GR1-A** Register integrity | Register validates against `schemas/gate1-register.yaml` invariants `G1-INV-01` … `G1-INV-25` at every write. |
| **GR1-B** Composition matrix | Every record advanced to `accepted` / `accepted-with-edit` carries two signoffs from a domain-correct, distinct, non-overlapping reviewer pair. |
| **GR1-C** Signature integrity | Every persisted `Signature.verifies == true`, recomputed locally; producer claims ignored. |
| **GR1-D** No-COR/LOE-edits | Zero `Edit.target ∈ {acc_aha_cor, acc_aha_loe}` recorded. Auto-rewrite rule observed. |
| **GR1-E** No self-pairing | No two signoffs on the same record share `reviewer_id`. |
| **GR1-F** COI auto-disqualification | Every recused entry carries the COI kind; substitute reviewer assigned where required. |
| **GR1-G** Atomicity acknowledgement | Every signoff carries `atomicity_state_acknowledged` matching the record's atomicity state at signing time. |
| **GR1-H** Panel-chair cohort hash | `panel_chair_signoff.cohort_manifest_hash` recomputes deterministically over `records[]`. |
| **GR1-I** Append-only audit log | `audit_log[]` ordered by `occurred_at`; chained `payload_sha256` continuity verified at every write. |
| **GR1-J** Cohort finalization preconditions | `composition_compliance_attested == true` AND `escalations_disposed == true` AND `errata_watch.blockers_open == []` on the active manifest at finalization time. |

Failure of any gate at any write step → BLOCK; the skill rolls back the
in-flight write, surfaces the specific gate, and emits a
`flagged_items`-style diagnostic into the build's reconciliation queue.

## Outputs

- Updated Gate 1 register at `<register-path>` with new `ReviewerSignoff`
  entries, updated record disposition states, updated escalations and
  rework history, and (in `chair-finalize` mode) the `PanelChairSignoff`.
- Per-session report at
  `work/<run_id>/reports/gate1-<cohort>-<reviewer>-<session>.md` summarizing:
  reviewer identity, eligibility queue, records reviewed, decisions, and
  signature verification outcomes.
- Updated PROV bundle entries at
  `provenance/gate1-<cohort>-<reviewer>-<session>.jsonld`.
- Per-record FHIR `Provenance` resource updates at
  `work/<run_id>/fhir/provenance/<recommendation_id>.json`, appending
  `Provenance.signature` entries for each new signoff.
- Notifications to the orchestrator queue:
  `cohort-ready-for-downstream` on cohort finalization, or
  `record-rework-required` / `record-panel-escalated` per disposition.

## Error Handling

- **Cohort not active or finalized.** Refuse to open in `sign` or
  `chair-finalize` mode; allow `browse` only.
- **Manifest stale.** Refuse all modes; instruct operator to re-run
  `flow-hbp-2025-build` preflight.
- **Reviewer not in panel.** Refuse `sign` mode; instruct operator to add
  the reviewer to the panel via the panel-management skill (a separate,
  out-of-scope skill).
- **Reviewer credential expired.** Refuse `sign` mode; route to credential
  renewal.
- **KMS authentication failure.** Refuse signing; do not retry silently;
  emit a `kms-auth-failure` event.
- **TSA unavailable.** Hold the in-flight signature; the candidate
  `ReviewerSignoff` is persisted with `signature: null` and state
  `awaiting-time-stamp`; the skill polls the next TSA in `tsa_list`. After
  exhausting the TSA list, BLOCK.
- **Signature local verification failure.** Discard the candidate; emit
  `signature-verification-failed` event; instruct operator to investigate
  KMS or canonicalization drift; never accept.
- **Record content hash mismatch.** Indicates upstream mutation; BLOCK the
  signing; signal the orchestrator to investigate (potential post-Gate-1
  immutability violation upstream of this Gate, or stale records file).
- **Edit submitted with `EditTarget` outside the closed enum.** Reject;
  no auto-rewrite (the form should not have permitted submission; this is
  treated as adversarial input).
- **Lock contention.** Wait up to a configured timeout; fail-closed if not
  acquired; concurrent signing on the same record is not permitted.
- **Resume after register hash change.** Reject; require a fresh session.

## Examples

```bash
# Browse a cohort read-only
gate1-sme-review work/run-2026-04-30/gate1/cohort-7c2a8e91b3d4f561.signed.jsonld \
  --mode browse

# Reviewer signing session — auto-pick the next eligible record
gate1-sme-review work/run-2026-04-30/gate1/cohort-7c2a8e91b3d4f561.signed.jsonld \
  --mode sign \
  --reviewer rev-9f1a2b3c4d5e6f70

# Reviewer signing a specific record after a queue resolution, resuming
gate1-sme-review work/run-2026-04-30/gate1/cohort-7c2a8e91b3d4f561.signed.jsonld \
  --mode sign \
  --reviewer rev-9f1a2b3c4d5e6f70 \
  --record rec-1a2b3c4d5e6f7081 \
  --resume

# Panel-chair finalization session
gate1-sme-review work/run-2026-04-30/gate1/cohort-7c2a8e91b3d4f561.signed.jsonld \
  --mode chair-finalize \
  --reviewer rev-c0a1b2c3d4e5f607
```

## Schema Reference

- `schemas/gate1-register.yaml` — the register this skill reads and
  writes; every invariant (`G1-INV-01` … `G1-INV-25`) is enforced.
- `schemas/recommendation-record-htn.yaml` — the records reviewed; the
  skill is read-only against records except via the `accept-with-edit`
  protocol that produces a new record content hash.
- `schemas/atomic-unit.yaml` — the atomicity surface acknowledged on every
  signoff; the skill enforces `AU-INV-24` (parent-edit-deletes-children) on
  text-verbatim edits.
- `schemas/sair.yaml` — the SAIR document referenced for source rasters,
  cell bboxes, footnote resolution, and predecessor anchors.
- `schemas/acc-aha-grading.yaml` — the closed COR/LOE enums (read-only at
  Gate 1).
- `schemas/guideline-manifest-hbp-2025.yaml` — the active manifest;
  `tsa_list[]`, `signature_policy`, `medical_director_signoff`, and
  `errata_watch` are consulted at preflight.

## Delegation

- Upstream producer: `cpg-htn-2025-acc-aha/skills/extract-recommendation-cor-loe/SKILL.md`
- Upstream queue UI (parse/extract reconciliation): `cpg-htn-2025-acc-aha/skills/parse-reconcile-queue/SKILL.md`
- Orchestrator: `cpg-htn-2025-acc-aha/skills/flow-hbp-2025-build/SKILL.md`
- Provenance: `@agentic/code/frameworks/sdlc-complete/skills/provenance-create/SKILL.md`
- Integrity manifests: `@agentic/code/frameworks/media-curator/skills/integrity-verification/SKILL.md`
- Sibling gates:
  - Gate 2: `cpg-htn-2025-acc-aha/skills/cql-clinician-signoff/SKILL.md`
  - Gate 3: `cpg-htn-2025-acc-aha/skills/safety-case-attest/SKILL.md`
- Out-of-scope (separate skill family):
  - Panel composition management.
  - Reviewer credential lifecycle.
  - KMS key rotation.

## Authority Boundaries

**Can do**
- Render the data-only review surface for a record under preflight-passing
  conditions.
- Capture reviewer decisions, COI re-attestations, and atomicity
  acknowledgements.
- Produce cryptographically-signed `ReviewerSignoff` entries via the
  reviewer's institutional KMS, time-stamped against a manifest-pinned TSA.
- Persist signoffs atomically and recompute `fixity.register_sha256` on
  every write.
- Auto-route adversarial decisions per the auto-routing rules in §4.2
  (rewrite COR/LOE-edit attempts to `reject-rework`, COI-overrides to
  `recused`).
- Auto-escalate disagreements to the panel chair without majority-voting.
- Allow the panel chair to finalize the cohort under `chair-finalize` mode.

**Requires approval (panel chair / new manifest version)**
- Any rework that requires re-collection of a previously valid second
  reviewer's signoff (because the content hash changed under
  `accept-with-edit`).
- Any composition recomposition triggered by recusal that leaves the
  domain's required-roles set unsatisfied.
- Any cohort-finalization decision while open errata blockers exist on the
  active manifest.

**Never**
- Sign on behalf of a reviewer (no impersonation; signatures only via the
  reviewer's KMS-authenticated session).
- Mutate a finalized register; corrections require a new register version
  with predecessor chain.
- Edit `acc_aha_cor` or `acc_aha_loe` under any circumstance; treat any
  attempted edit as `reject-rework` per `G1-INV-12`.
- Edit `text_verbatim` outside the closed `EditTarget` enum.
- Permit two signoffs from the same reviewer on the same record.
- Permit majority-voting or third-reviewer tie-breaks; disagreements
  always escalate to the panel chair.
- Relax the pregnancy denylist hard-block, even on reviewer request.
- Accept a signature whose local verification or TSA chain validation
  fails.
- Accept a signoff whose `record_content_hash` does not recompute against
  the live record at signing time.
- Run with `--strict false` in production.

```

Saved as `skills/gate1-sme-review/SKILL.md`. The skill is the only authorized producer of `ReviewerSignoff` entries on the Gate 1 register, mirrors the parent repo's frontmatter and section discipline established by `acquire-training-source`, `dataset-docs`, `parse-acc-aha-recbox`, `extract-recommendation-cor-loe`, and `flow-hbp-2025-build`, and is fully aligned to ADR-HTN-001 D9/D10/D14/D15, to the Parse + Extraction Phase Spec §4.11, and to the schemas already drafted (`gate1-register.yaml`, `recommendation-record-htn.yaml`, `atomic-unit.yaml`, `sair.yaml`, `acc-aha-grading.yaml`, `guideline-manifest-hbp-2025.yaml`).

The data-only review surface from `extract-recommendation-cor-loe` §10.2 is encoded in §3 across eight panes (source raster, verbatim text with reversible-normalization log, grading with read-only banner, atomic units with acknowledgement checkbox, PICO precheck, triple-modal consensus diff, predecessor 2017, decision pane). The mechanical decision-protocol auto-routing in §4.2 enforces `G1-INV-12` (no COR/LOE edits → `reject-rework`), `G1-INV-14` (COI auto-disqualification → `recused`), `G1-INV-21` (no self-pairing), and the post-signoff immutability rule via the `accept-with-edit` content-hash regeneration protocol that invalidates a prior peer signature when text changes (`AU-INV-24` cascade for atomic units). Disagreements always escalate to the panel chair without majority-vote; cohort finalization requires `composition_compliance_attested && escalations_disposed && errata_watch.blockers_open == []` on the active manifest. Ten DQA gates (`GR1-A` … `GR1-J`) are fail-closed at every write step. The "never" list explicitly forbids reviewer impersonation, mutation of a finalized register, COR/LOE edits under any circumstance, majority-voting, soft-warning relaxation of pregnancy hard-blocks, signature acceptance without local verification + TSA chain validation, and `--strict false` in production.
