## Part 2 — `skills/acquire-hbp-2025-source/SKILL.md`

```markdown name=skills/acquire-hbp-2025-source/SKILL.md
---
name: acquire-hbp-2025-source
description: Phase-1 ingest skill for the cpg-htn-2025-acc-aha framework. Acquires exactly the four source documents named by the active manifest (main guideline, executive summary, supplement, predecessor-2017), verifies cryptographic and license fidelity, polls publisher errata feeds and CrossRef relations, blocks on any drift, persists the immutable raw byte-streams under raw/<source-id>/, and writes back source-side fixity manifests. Source-admission is closed; no auto-update; no override; no PHI; no real patient data; no fifth document.
namespace: cpg-htn-2025-acc-aha
category: ingest
platforms: [claude, copilot, cursor, factory, windsurf, warp, codex, opencode, openclaw, hermes]
commandHint:
  argumentHint: "<manifest-path> [--mode <verify|fetch|verify+fetch>] [--source <role>] [--strict]"
---

# acquire-hbp-2025-source

Phase-1 ingest skill for the `cpg-htn-2025-acc-aha` framework. The skill
is the only authorized producer of source-side fixity manifests and
errata-watch state under `raw/<source-id>/`. It acquires exactly the
four source documents named by the active
`schemas/guideline-manifest-hbp-2025.yaml` instance, verifies
cryptographic and license fidelity against the manifest's pins, polls
the publisher errata feeds and CrossRef `is-corrected-by` relations,
blocks on any drift, and writes back the immutable raw byte-streams plus
a per-source fixity manifest that downstream phases consume.

This skill does **not** parse PDFs, extract text, normalize content, or
modify byte-streams. It is the ingest gate for the build pipeline:
everything that follows assumes the four sources exist on disk in their
publisher-delivered form and that their SHA-256 hashes match the
manifest's pins exactly. If those assumptions fail, this skill refuses
to advance the build.

Posture: **caution over velocity, fidelity over coverage, no-auto-update
over convenience.** Source-admission is closed. The four roles are the
only roles. A new source — including a different edition, a different
language, a different jurisdiction — requires a new manifest version
with explicit predecessor chain and panel-chair signoff; this skill
will refuse to ingest it. Auto-update is forbidden. Errata clear under
human review only; SHA mismatches BLOCK; license-contract drift BLOCKS.

This skill is the operational counterpart to `safety-case-attest` at
the opposite end of the pipeline: where Gate 3 attests that a build
faithfully honors the source, P1 attests that the source the build
descends from is exactly what the manifest declared.

## When to Use

Invoke this skill when:

- The orchestrator (`flow-hbp-2025-build`) reaches phase **P1** for a
  manifest in state `active` with verified medical-director signoff and
  `errata_watch.blockers_open == []`.
- A scheduled errata-watch poll is due (cadence per manifest's
  `errata_watch.poll_cadence_iso8601`); this skill polls and reports,
  but does not silently re-baseline.
- A change-control review needs to verify that the on-disk sources
  still match the manifest's pins, without re-fetching (use
  `--mode verify`).
- A new manifest version has been activated with new source pins and
  fresh sources must be fetched and pinned (use `--mode fetch`, which
  also runs `verify`).

Do **not** invoke this skill if:

- The manifest is in any state other than `active`.
- The medical-director signoff fails verification.
- The publisher contract URI cannot be resolved (this is a release
  blocker; the skill will refuse to ingest sources without contract
  evidence even if the bytes are otherwise available).
- Real patient-bearing PDFs are being substituted for the publisher's
  documents (PHI fail-closed at the manifest's policy; the skill checks
  upstream URLs against the manifest's pins).

## Parameters

| Parameter | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `manifest-path` | yes | — | Path to a `guideline-manifest-hbp-2025.yaml` instance with `state == "active"` and a verified medical-director signoff. |
| `--mode <verify\|fetch\|verify+fetch>` | no | `verify+fetch` | `verify` checks on-disk sources against the manifest's pins; `fetch` retrieves missing sources from the publisher; `verify+fetch` does both (fetch any missing, verify all). The skill never overwrites existing source bytes when their on-disk SHA matches the manifest pin. |
| `--source <role>` | no | `all` | One of `main-guideline`, `executive-summary`, `supplement`, `predecessor-2017`, or `all`. Useful for targeted re-verification. |
| `--strict` | no | `true` | Fail-closed on every gate. Setting `--strict false` is **never permitted** in production; the flag exists only for fixture and golden-set development (e.g., when constructing a draft manifest from non-publisher fixtures during framework bootstrap). |
| `--dry-run` | no | `false` | Emit the planned acquisition steps and pin-comparison report; do not retrieve or write any bytes. Permitted in production for change-control review. |

## Operation

### 1. Preflight

1. Validate `manifest-path` against
   `schemas/guideline-manifest-hbp-2025.yaml`. Reject on any invariant
   failure (`GM-INV-01` … `GM-INV-28`).
2. Verify `state == "active"` and `errata_watch.blockers_open == []`.
3. Cryptographically verify `medical_director_signoff.signature`
   against `fixity.manifest_sha256` per `GM-INV-21`. Producer claims of
   `verifies: true` are ignored; the skill re-verifies.
4. Verify `tools_lock.lock_sha` against the canonicalized
   `tools_lock.items[]` (`GM-INV-08`).
5. Verify the publisher contract URI is well-formed for every source
   under §5.4 of the manifest's policy (`source_admission`); the skill
   does not retrieve the contract document, but it confirms the URI is
   present and the `contract_signed_at` falls within a window the
   skill's tooling considers current (the orchestrator's pre-build
   contract validity check is upstream of this skill's preflight).
6. Verify the framework's resource budget: at least one TSA in
   `tsa_list[]` is currently within `cert_valid_*` (the source-side
   fixity manifest is signed for tamper-evidence).
7. Refuse to proceed if any precondition fails. **Fail-closed.**

### 2. Source-admission policy enforcement

The skill admits **exactly four** roles, and only these four:

```
main-guideline       — the 2025 ACC/AHA HBP Guideline main document
executive-summary    — the executive summary
supplement           — the data supplement
predecessor-2017     — the 2017 ACC/AHA HBP Guideline (advisory predecessor)
```

For each role:

1. Resolve `sources[*]` filtered to that role; verify exactly one entry
   per role per `GM-INV-01`.
2. Reject any `sources[*]` whose role is not in the closed enum
   (the schema enforces this; the skill double-checks).
3. Reject any attempted ingest of a fifth document — including ESC/ESH
   guidelines, ISH guidelines, KDIGO guidelines, board-review banks,
   lay summaries, alternate-language editions, draft preprints.

The skill emits a `source-admission-rejected` event into the manifest's
`audit_log[]` if any out-of-policy source is encountered (e.g., a
fifth file in `raw/<source-id>/` not declared in the manifest); the
event is advisory but is also a release blocker until the operator
removes the file or the manifest is amended.

### 3. Verify mode (`--mode verify`)

For each source role under `--source`:

1. Resolve the source's on-disk path:
   `raw/<source-id>/<role>.pdf`. The `<source-id>` is the
   manifest-version identifier
   (e.g., `2025-acc-aha-hbp-v1.0.0`).
2. If the file is absent, mark the role's verification status as
   `missing-on-disk` and continue. (Verify mode does not fetch; missing
   files are reported but not retrieved.)
3. If the file is present, compute `sha256` of the raw bytes (the
   publisher-delivered byte-stream, before any conditioning).
4. Compare to the manifest's `sources[*].pdf_sha256`:
   - **Match.** Mark the role's verification status as `pin-match`;
     proceed.
   - **Mismatch.** Mark as `pin-mismatch`; emit a `source-sha-mismatch`
     drift event into the manifest's `drift_events[]` (per `GM-INV-18`,
     the action is `blocked-build` or `opened-new-manifest-version`,
     never silent re-baseline). BLOCK.
5. Verify `page_count` against the manifest's pin by inspecting the PDF
   trailer (no parsing of content, only structural counting). Mismatch
   is a release blocker.
6. Verify `license.contract_uri` is reachable (HEAD request only; the
   document body is not retrieved). Unreachable contract URIs are a
   release blocker per the source-admission policy.
7. Compute the source's per-source fixity manifest at
   `raw/<source-id>/<role>.fixity.json`, recording:
   - role, doi, publication_date, publisher
   - pdf_sha256 (recomputed on this run)
   - pdf_path (relative to the build root)
   - byte_count
   - license.spdx and contract_signed_at
   - the manifest_id and manifest_version this source is bound to
   - the run wall-clock timestamp
   - the operator id that ran this verification
8. Sign the per-source fixity manifest with the orchestrator's KMS
   ingest key (Ed25519); time-stamp via a manifest-pinned TSA. The
   signature binds the on-disk source to the manifest pin at the
   verification moment.
9. Append a `source-verified` event to the manifest's `audit_log[]`
   with the per-source fixity manifest SHA-256.

If `--mode verify` finds any role in `pin-mismatch` or
`missing-on-disk` (when in `verify+fetch`, `missing-on-disk` triggers a
fetch attempt; in `verify`-only mode, it BLOCKs), the skill BLOCKS the
build and emits a verification report at
`work/<run_id>/reports/p1-acquire-<run_id>.md` enumerating the failed
roles and remediation guidance.

### 4. Fetch mode (`--mode fetch` or as a sub-step of `verify+fetch`)

For each source role currently in `missing-on-disk`:

1. Resolve the source's URL from the manifest's
   `sources[*].url`. The URL MUST be a publisher-controlled DOI
   resolver or a publisher portal URL declared in the manifest at
   `medical_director_signoff` time.
2. Issue an HTTPS GET via the orchestrator's authenticated fetch
   client (mTLS or API key per institutional policy; institutional
   credentials are managed outside this skill). The request:
   - Pins TLS to publisher's certificate fingerprint per the
     framework's institutional CA bundle.
   - Sends `User-Agent: cpg-htn-2025-acc-aha/<manifest-version>`.
   - Honors the publisher's rate-limit headers; backs off on 429.
   - Refuses to follow redirects to a different publisher domain.
3. On 200 OK, stream the response body into a temp path under
   `raw/<source-id>/.staging/<role>.pdf`. Compute `sha256` while
   streaming.
4. Compare the streamed `sha256` to the manifest's pin:
   - **Match.** Atomically rename the temp file to
     `raw/<source-id>/<role>.pdf`. Proceed to verify per §3 from
     step 5 (page count, contract URI, fixity manifest, signature).
   - **Mismatch.** Discard the temp file. Emit a
     `source-sha-mismatch` drift event. BLOCK. The skill never
     persists bytes whose SHA does not match the manifest's pin —
     that would be silent re-baseline, which is forbidden per
     `policy.no_auto_update` and `GM-INV-18`.
5. On any non-200 response (404 not found, 403 forbidden, 451
   unavailable for legal reasons, etc.), abort the fetch for this
   role; emit a `source-url-unreachable` drift event with the HTTP
   status; BLOCK the build.
6. On TLS pinning failure, certificate validation failure, or
   redirect-cross-origin attempts, abort and emit a
   `source-tls-failure` drift event; BLOCK.

The skill **never** auto-updates a source whose URL has changed; URL
changes are themselves drift events that require a new manifest
version with explicit panel-chair acknowledgement.

### 5. Errata watch poll

For each source whose `errata_feed` is non-null:

1. Resolve `errata_feed.feed_url` and `errata_feed.feed_kind`.
2. Issue an HTTPS GET respecting `last_known_etag` (If-None-Match).
3. On `304 Not Modified`, record `last_polled_at` and continue.
4. On `200 OK` with a feed body:
   a. Compute `feed_sha256` of the response body.
   b. Compare to `errata_feed.last_known_hash`:
      - **Match.** No new errata. Update `last_polled_at`; continue.
      - **Mismatch.** Parse the feed (RSS/Atom/JSON/CrossRef API/
        publisher API per `feed_kind`). Diff against
        `last_known_hash`. For every new entry whose subject is the
        manifest's source DOI:
         * Append an `errata-published` drift event into the
           manifest's `drift_events[]` with the erratum DOI and
           summary.
         * Append an `errata_watch.blockers_open[]` entry on the
           manifest. **The build is now blocked.** Activation of this
           manifest version requires SME panel chair acknowledgement,
           which itself routes via a new manifest version per
           `GM-INV-17` and `GM-INV-28` (an `active` manifest cannot
           mutate; the new acknowledgement appears in a successor
           manifest).
         * Emit a release-blocker report at
           `work/<run_id>/reports/p1-errata-<run_id>.md`.
5. For every CrossRef relation listed in the source's
   `crossref_relations[]`, issue a CrossRef API query for the
   `is-corrected-by` relation on the source DOI. Any new
   `is-corrected-by` target produces a drift event of kind
   `corrigendum-published` and the same blocker behavior as §5.4.

The skill **never** silently dismisses an erratum, even if the
erratum is small or stylistic. Every erratum is a manifest-version
event.

### 6. PHI / patient-data ingest barrier

The skill enforces a hard barrier against real patient data:

1. The fetch client refuses to retrieve from any URL not listed in the
   manifest's `sources[*].url`. URLs outside the manifest set BLOCK
   the build at the fetch step.
2. After a successful fetch, the skill issues a fingerprint check
   against a small block of the file's leading bytes against the
   manifest-pinned `pdf_sha256`. The check happens before any byte is
   exposed to the parse pipeline.
3. The skill refuses to ingest any document whose URL or file
   matches institutional patterns of EHR-export, lab-system-export,
   or patient-portal-export (pattern set is configured at the
   institution's PHI hazard handler URI per the manifest's
   `phi_scrub_policy.hazard_handler_uri`).
4. Any positive PHI-pattern match BLOCKS the build, opens the PHI
   hazard handler, and emits a `phi-incident` audit event. **No
   override exists** per ADR-HTN-001 D10.

### 7. Audit log and provenance

For each source role processed:

1. Append a per-role audit event to the manifest's `audit_log[]` (the
   events are append-only and ordered by `occurred_at` per
   `GM-INV-19`; the skill respects the chained-hash continuity
   convention).
2. Emit a W3C PROV-O record into the build's PROV bundle at
   `provenance/acquire-<run_id>.jsonld`:
   - `Activity`: this acquisition run.
   - `Entity`: each source PDF (with its pinned SHA-256).
   - `Agent`: the operator id and the publisher.
   - `wasGeneratedBy`, `used`, `wasAttributedTo` relations as
     appropriate.
3. Emit a FHIR `Provenance` resource under
   `work/<run_id>/fhir/provenance/source-<role>.json` for each source
   that was successfully acquired and verified, with
   `Provenance.signature` carrying the per-source fixity-manifest
   signature.

### 8. Determinism and reproducibility

- The pin-comparison is deterministic; identical bytes produce
  identical SHA-256.
- The fixity manifest is deterministic; identical inputs produce
  identical canonical JSON and identical `manifest_sha256`.
- Re-running this skill against an already-verified source set is
  idempotent: every role is re-verified and a fresh per-source
  fixity manifest is signed and time-stamped, but the underlying
  bytes are not rewritten.
- Errata-watch state is monotonic: blockers are opened and never
  silently closed.

## DQA Gates Enforced By This Skill

| Gate | Condition for advance |
|---|---|
| **GA-A** Manifest active | Manifest is `state == "active"` with verified medical-director signoff and zero open errata blockers. |
| **GA-B** Source admission | Exactly four sources, one per role; no fifth source on disk in `raw/<source-id>/` outside the manifest set. |
| **GA-C** SHA pin match | Every on-disk source's SHA-256 equals the manifest's `pdf_sha256`. |
| **GA-D** Page count match | Every source's PDF trailer page count equals the manifest's `page_count`. |
| **GA-E** Contract URI reachable | Every source's `license.contract_uri` resolves; `contract_signed_at` is within the contract window. |
| **GA-F** No URL change | Every source URL fetched matches the manifest's `sources[*].url` exactly; cross-origin redirects are forbidden. |
| **GA-G** TLS pinned | TLS handshake validates against the framework's institutional CA bundle. |
| **GA-H** Errata clean | Errata-watch poll returns no new blockers; `last_polled_at` updated. |
| **GA-I** CrossRef clean | CrossRef `is-corrected-by` query returns no new corrigenda. |
| **GA-J** No PHI hits | The leading-bytes pattern scan and URL allow-list both pass. |
| **GA-K** Per-source fixity signed | Every per-source fixity manifest is signed by the institutional KMS ingest key and time-stamped via a manifest-pinned TSA. |
| **GA-L** Audit log appended | The manifest's `audit_log[]` has the per-role events appended in order. |
| **GA-M** Tools lock current | The skill's own pinned tools (`fetch-client`, `tsp-client`, `kms-client`) match the manifest's `tools_lock.items[]`. |

Failure of any gate at any role → BLOCK; the skill rolls back the
in-flight verification, surfaces the specific gate, and emits a report
at `work/<run_id>/reports/p1-acquire-<run_id>.md`. There is **no
override**.

## Outputs

- Per-source raw byte-streams under
  `raw/<source-id>/{main-guideline,executive-summary,supplement,
  predecessor-2017}.pdf` (immutable; rewriting is forbidden).
- Per-source fixity manifests at
  `raw/<source-id>/<role>.fixity.json`, signed by the institutional
  KMS ingest key.
- Per-role FHIR `Provenance` resources at
  `work/<run_id>/fhir/provenance/source-<role>.json`.
- Per-source audit-log entries appended to the manifest's
  `audit_log[]`.
- Per-run errata-watch report at
  `work/<run_id>/reports/p1-errata-<run_id>.md`.
- Per-run acquisition report at
  `work/<run_id>/reports/p1-acquire-<run_id>.md`.
- Build PROV bundle update at `provenance/acquire-<run_id>.jsonld`.
- Notifications to the orchestrator queue:
  - `acquire-complete` on full success;
  - `acquire-blocked` with the failing gate and remediation guidance
    on any failure;
  - `acquire-errata-blocker-opened` on new errata.

## Error Handling

- **Manifest not active.** BLOCK preflight; instruct operator to
  activate or open a new manifest version.
- **Manifest signature fails verification.** BLOCK preflight; route
  to the framework's signing-failure handler.
- **Source SHA mismatch.** BLOCK; emit `source-sha-mismatch` drift
  event; require a new manifest version.
- **Source URL unreachable.** BLOCK; emit `source-url-unreachable`
  drift event; do not retry silently. The orchestrator may schedule
  a delayed retry under operator supervision.
- **Source URL changed (cross-origin redirect).** BLOCK; emit
  `source-url-changed` drift event; require a new manifest version.
- **TLS pin failure.** BLOCK; emit `source-tls-failure`; investigate
  as adversarial input; do not retry against the same endpoint
  without operator review.
- **License contract URI unreachable.** BLOCK; require legal review.
- **Page count mismatch.** BLOCK; emit `source-sha-mismatch`-class
  drift event with annotation.
- **Errata feed returns new blockers.** BLOCK; open the
  `errata_watch.blockers_open[]` entry; require a new manifest
  version with panel-chair acknowledgement.
- **CrossRef relation update.** BLOCK; emit `corrigendum-published`
  drift event; require a new manifest version.
- **PHI pattern match.** BLOCK unconditionally; route to the PHI
  hazard handler; emit `phi-incident` audit event. **No override.**
- **Out-of-policy source on disk** (a fifth file in `raw/<source-id>/`).
  Emit `source-admission-rejected`; BLOCK until removed or the
  manifest is amended.
- **TSA unavailable.** Hold the per-source fixity-manifest signature;
  poll the next TSA in `tsa_list[]`; after exhausting the list,
  BLOCK.
- **KMS authentication failure.** BLOCK; emit `kms-auth-failure`;
  do not retry silently.
- **Lock contention.** Wait up to a configured timeout; fail-closed
  if not acquired; concurrent fetch/verify on the same role is not
  permitted.
- **Direct edit attempt against a verified source byte-stream.**
  Emit `source-mutation-attempt` audit event; BLOCK; investigate as
  adversarial input.

## Examples

```bash
# Verify the on-disk sources against the active manifest's pins
acquire-hbp-2025-source manifests/v1.0.0+ACC-AHA-2025+US+2026-04-30.yaml \
  --mode verify

# First-time fetch + verify for a freshly-active manifest
acquire-hbp-2025-source manifests/v1.0.0+ACC-AHA-2025+US+2026-04-30.yaml \
  --mode verify+fetch

# Targeted re-verify of a single role after a TSA rotation
acquire-hbp-2025-source manifests/v1.0.0+ACC-AHA-2025+US+2026-04-30.yaml \
  --mode verify \
  --source predecessor-2017

# Dry-run plan emission for change-control review
acquire-hbp-2025-source manifests/v1.0.0+ACC-AHA-2025+US+2026-04-30.yaml \
  --dry-run

# Errata watch poll only (no fetch; no re-verify of bytes)
acquire-hbp-2025-source manifests/v1.0.0+ACC-AHA-2025+US+2026-04-30.yaml \
  --mode verify \
  --source all
```

## Schema Reference

- `schemas/guideline-manifest-hbp-2025.yaml` — the active manifest;
  every invariant (`GM-INV-01` … `GM-INV-28`) is consulted at
  preflight or sign time. Specifically:
  - `GM-INV-01` (four-source roles required),
  - `GM-INV-02` (supersession-cross-reference consistency),
  - `GM-INV-04` (SPDX license disposition),
  - `GM-INV-08` (tools-lock SHA),
  - `GM-INV-17` (errata blockers force pending state),
  - `GM-INV-18` (no auto-update; drift events block),
  - `GM-INV-19` (audit-log append-only),
  - `GM-INV-21` (medical-director signature verifies),
  - `GM-INV-23` (active-state preconditions),
  - `GM-INV-25` (Communication resource on first publish — verified
    downstream by `safety-case-attest`, but the source is anchored
    here),
  - `GM-INV-28` (no mutation of an active manifest).
- `schemas/sair.yaml` — downstream consumer; the SAIR document
  references the source's `pdf_sha256` as `anchors.pdf_sha256` per
  the parent record schema.
- `schemas/recommendation-record-htn.yaml` — downstream consumer;
  records reference the source's pdf via the SAIR anchor chain.
- `schemas/gate3-attestation.yaml` — downstream consumer; the Gate-3
  bundle's `mfst` member is exactly this skill's verified manifest,
  and the per-source SHAs flow through to bundle integrity.

## Delegation

- Active manifest source-of-truth:
  `cpg-htn-2025-acc-aha/schemas/guideline-manifest-hbp-2025.yaml`
- Orchestrator: `cpg-htn-2025-acc-aha/skills/flow-hbp-2025-build/SKILL.md`
- Downstream parse phases (consume the verified raw byte-streams):
  - `cpg-htn-2025-acc-aha/skills/parse-prepare-pdf/SKILL.md` (P2)
  - `cpg-htn-2025-acc-aha/skills/parse-detect-layout/SKILL.md` (P3)
  - `cpg-htn-2025-acc-aha/skills/parse-extract-text/SKILL.md` (P4)
  - `cpg-htn-2025-acc-aha/skills/parse-extract-figures/SKILL.md` (P5)
  - `cpg-htn-2025-acc-aha/skills/parse-acc-aha-recbox/SKILL.md` (P6)
- Provenance:
  `@agentic/code/frameworks/sdlc-complete/skills/provenance-create/SKILL.md`
- Integrity manifests:
  `@agentic/code/frameworks/media-curator/skills/integrity-verification/SKILL.md`
- Out-of-scope (separate skill family):
  - PDF parsing (handled by P2 and onward).
  - Manifest amendment / supersession (handled by a separate
    framework-governance skill).
  - KMS key lifecycle.
  - Publisher contract negotiation.
  - PHI hazard handler runbook execution.

## Authority Boundaries

**Can do**
- Verify on-disk source byte-streams against the manifest's SHA pins.
- Fetch missing sources from publisher URLs declared in the manifest
  under TLS pinning and an authenticated client, atomically renaming
  to the canonical path only on SHA match.
- Compute and sign per-source fixity manifests with the institutional
  KMS ingest key, time-stamped via a manifest-pinned TSA.
- Poll publisher errata feeds and CrossRef `is-corrected-by` relations
  on the manifest's cadence.
- Emit drift events into the manifest's `drift_events[]` and audit
  events into `audit_log[]` (the manifest is otherwise immutable;
  these append-only fields are the only legal mutations and are
  themselves chained-hash tamper-evident).
- Emit FHIR `Provenance` resources for each acquired source.
- Refuse to advance on any failed gate; refuse to retry silently;
  refuse to follow cross-origin redirects.
- Emit a `source-admission-rejected` event when an out-of-policy
  source appears in `raw/<source-id>/`.

**Requires approval (panel chair / new manifest version)**
- Any new source role beyond the closed four.
- Any URL change for an existing source role (cross-origin redirects
  or publisher portal moves).
- Any errata acknowledgement.
- Any CrossRef corrigendum acknowledgement.
- Any license-spdx change (e.g., the publisher's contract migrates from
  `Other-Negotiated-Envelope` to a permissive license).
- Any decision to enable `figures_quotable` or `tables_quotable` on
  the manifest (legal-counsel signoff also required by the manifest
  schema).

**Never**
- Auto-update a source byte-stream when its SHA does not match the
  manifest's pin. Mismatches BLOCK; the operator opens a new manifest
  version under panel-chair signoff.
- Persist any byte-stream whose streamed SHA does not match the pin
  (no silent re-baseline; no temp file is promoted to the canonical
  path until SHA match is confirmed).
- Follow a redirect to a different publisher domain.
- Disable TLS pinning under any flag.
- Ingest from a URL not declared in the manifest.
- Ingest a fifth document beyond the four roles.
- Ingest from EHR-export, lab-system-export, or patient-portal-export
  patterns.
- Silently close an errata blocker.
- Mutate a `pin-match` source's bytes; the canonical path is
  write-once for each manifest version.
- Run with `--strict false` in production.

## References

- **ADR-HTN-001** D2 (single authoritative source: the 2025 ACC/AHA
  HBP Guideline + supplement + executive summary; predecessor 2017
  ingested for supersession only), D9 (three non-overridable human
  gates; this skill is the ingest-side complement of those gates), D10
  (PHI fail-closed; no override), D11 (Synthea-only test data; real
  patient data is rejected at ingest), D13 (versioning triple), D14
  (supersession of 2017; predecessor mapping advisory only), D15
  (drift detection on every build; this skill is the drift-detection
  point of entry).
- **`flow-hbp-2025-build` §3 (Acquire P1)** — placement, DQA gates,
  and exit conditions; this skill is the implementation invoked from
  P1.
- **`guideline-manifest-hbp-2025.yaml`** policy (§1) and invariants
  (`GM-INV-01` … `GM-INV-28`).
- **`gate3-attestation.yaml`** invariants `G3A-INV-16` (upstream
  prerequisite re-verification at attest time) — the per-source
  fixity manifests this skill emits are the ground-truth chain that
  Gate 3's bundle hash inherits.
- **REF-475** ML Reproducibility Checklist — informs determinism rules
  applied to fetch-and-verify.
- **REF-062** W3C PROV-O — informs the per-step Activity/Entity/Agent
  emission and per-source FHIR `Provenance` mapping.
- **RFC 3161 / RFC 8785** — time-stamp protocol and JSON
  canonicalization scheme used in the per-source fixity-manifest
  signature envelope.
- **NIST SP 800-63** (IAL/AAL) — informs the institutional ingest
  operator's authentication assurance level (institutional policy
  pins this; the framework defaults to AAL2 for ingest operators and
  AAL3 for the manifest signing key).
- **CrossRef API** — informs the `is-corrected-by` relation polling.
- **DOI Foundation** — informs the source DOI resolution pattern.
- **Parent framework** `aiwg-training` rules: `god-session` (≤ 7
  responsibilities per skill; this skill's responsibilities are
  bounded to: preflight, source-admission enforcement, verify mode,
  fetch mode, errata watch, PHI ingest barrier, fixity-manifest
  signing + audit), `human-authorization` (every drift event routes
  to a manifest-amendment workflow under panel-chair signoff),
  `native-ux-tools` (queue UI invocation pattern for the manifest's
  audit log).
```

Saved as `skills/acquire-hbp-2025-source/SKILL.md`. The skill is the only authorized producer of source-side fixity manifests, mirrors the parent repo's frontmatter and section discipline established by `acquire-training-source`, `dataset-docs`, `parse-acc-aha-recbox`, `extract-recommendation-cor-loe`, `flow-hbp-2025-build`, `gate1-sme-review`, `cql-clinician-signoff`, and `safety-case-attest`, and is fully aligned to ADR-HTN-001 D2/D9/D10/D11/D13/D14/D15 and to the manifest schema's `GM-INV-01`…`GM-INV-28`.

Source admission is closed at four roles (`main-guideline`, `executive-summary`, `supplement`, `predecessor-2017`) — no fifth document, no jurisdictional substitution, no language substitution, no draft substitution. The verify and fetch flows are deterministic and fail-closed: SHA pin mismatch BLOCKs and emits a `source-sha-mismatch` drift event; URL change BLOCKs with `source-url-changed`; cross-origin redirects BLOCK with `source-tls-failure`-class events; license contract URI unreachable BLOCKs; page count mismatch BLOCKs. The `--mode fetch` flow streams to a staging path and only atomically renames to the canonical path on SHA match — silent re-baseline is mechanically impossible. Errata watch and CrossRef `is-corrected-by` polling are append-only and never silently re-baseline; every erratum opens a manifest blocker and forces a new manifest version under panel-chair signoff. The PHI ingest barrier is hard: URL allow-list against the manifest, leading-bytes fingerprint check before any byte is exposed to the parse pipeline, and pattern detection against EHR/lab/portal export patterns — with no override per ADR-HTN-001 D10. Thirteen DQA gates (`GA-A` … `GA-M`) are fail-closed at every role.

The full schema and skill set required for the ingest-through-Gate-3 path is now drafted at the same fidelity as the parent repo's existing documents:

- Schemas: `acc-aha-grading.yaml`, `sair.yaml`, `recommendation-record-htn.yaml`, `atomic-unit.yaml`, `gate1-register.yaml`, `gate2-register.yaml`, `gate3-attestation.yaml`, `guideline-manifest-hbp-2025.yaml`.
- Skills: `flow-hbp-2025-build`, `gate1-sme-review`, `cql-clinician-signoff`, `safety-case-attest`, `acquire-hbp-2025-source`.
- Plus the parse-side data contract `parse-acc-aha-recbox` (drafted earlier) and the extraction-side skill `extract-recommendation-cor-loe` (drafted earlier).

# extract-recommendation-cor-loe (refresh)

Phase-3 (P9) extraction skill for the `cpg-htn-2025-acc-aha` framework.
The skill produces `RecommendationRecordHTN` instances by **triple-modal
consensus** over the recommendation cells already segmented by
`parse-acc-aha-recbox`, decomposes the verbatim text into
`AtomicUnit` instances under a **dual-LLM, family-distinct agreement
rule**, runs the PICO and numeric-fact prechecks, opens **Gate-1
cohorts** against `schemas/gate1-register.yaml`, and is the only
authorized writer of records in state `gate-1-pending`. The skill is
the operational driver of Gate 1; the reviewer-interface is
`gate1-sme-review`.

This refresh aligns the skill exactly to the schemas drafted in this
thread:

- `schemas/acc-aha-grading.yaml` — closed COR/LOE enums.
- `schemas/sair.yaml` — input source-of-truth.
- `schemas/recommendation-record-htn.yaml` — output contract.
- `schemas/atomic-unit.yaml` — atomicity contract for child units.
- `schemas/gate1-register.yaml` — Gate-1 cohort register.
- `schemas/guideline-manifest-hbp-2025.yaml` — pin source for tools, terminology editions, TSAs, signature policy, and risk-engine identity.

Posture: **caution over velocity, fidelity over coverage, verbatim
over paraphrase.** No paraphrase of clinical text. No editing of
ACC/AHA COR or LOE. No batch acceptance. No silent re-extraction. No
LLM-only path. No reviewer self-pairing. No majority-voting on
disagreements. Held rows route to the reconciliation queue, never to a
silent fall-through.

## When to Use

Invoke this skill when:

- The orchestrator (`flow-hbp-2025-build`) reaches phase **P9** for a
  build whose SAIR is sealed (P8 complete) and whose
  `parse-acc-aha-recbox` outputs are present in
  `work/<run_id>/sair.json` under `recommendation_boxes[]`.
- A re-extraction is required after a Gate-1 reviewer recorded
  `accept-with-edit` and the orchestrator regenerated the affected
  record's atomic units (parent-edit-deletes-children per
  `AU-INV-24`).
- A held row in `work/<run_id>/queue/` has been resolved by the
  two-person rule and the orchestrator requests advancement.
- A targeted re-extraction is required after a `tools_lock` change
  authorized by a new manifest version.

Do **not** invoke this skill if:

- The active manifest is not in state `active` or has open errata
  blockers.
- The SAIR document is not sealed (P8 must complete first).
- `parse-acc-aha-recbox` has not produced
  `recommendation_boxes[*]` of consensus state `agreed` or
  `awaiting-corroboration` for the rows under extraction.
- Any record advanced through Gate 1 in a prior cohort is being
  re-extracted (Gate 1 records are immutable; corrections require a
  new register version).

## Parameters

| Parameter | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sair-path` | yes | — | Path to the sealed SAIR document at `work/<run_id>/sair.json`, validated against `schemas/sair.yaml`. |
| `--records <list>` | no | `all` | Comma-separated list of recommendation row ids to extract (`row-<16hex>` per the SAIR's `recommendation_boxes[].rows[].row_id`). Defaults to every row not yet bound to a record. |
| `--cohort-strategy <by-domain\|single>` | no | `by-domain` | `by-domain` opens one Gate-1 cohort per domain group per the matrix in §10; `single` opens one cohort containing every record (used only when the cohort scope is institutional policy). |
| `--resume` | no | `false` | Resume an interrupted run from the last persisted record. The skill rejects resume if the SAIR's `fixity.sair_sha256` has changed since session start. |
| `--dry-run` | no | `false` | Run preflight + plan only; emit the planned record set, the proposed cohort partition, and the dual-LLM family-distinct verification; do not execute extraction or open cohorts. |
| `--strict` | no | `true` | Fail-closed on every gate. Setting `--strict false` is **never permitted** in production. |

## Operation

### 1. Preflight

1. Validate `sair-path` against `schemas/sair.yaml`. Reject on any
   invariant failure.
2. Resolve `guideline_manifest_ref` from the SAIR; verify the active
   manifest's `medical_director_signoff` cryptographically per
   `GM-INV-21`; verify `state == "active"` and
   `errata_watch.blockers_open == []` per `GM-INV-23`.
3. Verify `tools_lock.lock_sha` against canonicalized
   `tools_lock.items[]` per `GM-INV-08`.
4. Verify the **two-LLM family-distinct rule** at preflight:
   - Resolve `manifest.tools_lock.llm_pair[]`. Confirm exactly two
     entries (`GM-INV-09`).
   - Resolve each entry to a `tools_lock.items[]` of `kind == "llm"`.
   - Confirm the two LLMs are from **distinct vendor families** per
     the family-distinct rule (`AU-INV-09`). The schema's family
     classification is the ground-truth list maintained at
     `docs/llm-family-matrix.md`; CI verifies the matrix file exists
     and the two pinned LLMs map to distinct families.
   - Probe each LLM for liveness with a deterministic test prompt;
     record the response signature.
   - **Family-collapse → BLOCK.** If at any point the two LLMs map to
     the same family (vendor reorg, model rebrand, etc.), the build
     blocks with `family-distinct-rule-violated`; remediation is a
     new manifest version with a different pinned pair.
5. Verify the **VLM** referenced in `manifest.tools_lock.vlm` is
   reachable and on the pinned version.
6. Verify the **OCR engines** in `manifest.tools_lock.ocr_engines[]`
   are at least three; probe each.
7. Verify the **terminology server** is reachable at the pinned
   editions (deferred binding occurs at P10, but the server must be
   alive at P9 preflight to fail fast).
8. Verify the **TSAs** in `manifest.tsa_list[]`: at least one cert
   is currently within `cert_valid_*`.
9. Verify **input integrity**:
   - The SAIR is sealed (read-only flag set in
     `meta.write_back_lock_state == "sealed"`).
   - For each row in scope, the parent
     `recommendation_boxes[].consensus.state` is `agreed` or
     `awaiting-corroboration` (only these two are admissible at P9;
     `held` and `text-disputed` route to the queue).
   - Every row's `text_verbatim` is non-empty after Phase-2
     reversible normalization.
   - Every row has anchored `bbox` and `page` references on the
     conditioned PDF, recomputable byte-for-byte.
10. Refuse to proceed if any precondition fails. **Fail-closed.**

### 2. Triple-modal consensus (mechanical)

For each row in scope, three independent extractor stacks produce
candidate records: **A** (deterministic text), **V** (VLM vision), **O**
(OCR-fallback). All three are independent reads against the same
source region; they are not allowed to consult each other's outputs.

#### 2.1 Extractor A — Deterministic text (no LLM)
- Input: `recommendation_boxes[].rows[]` from the SAIR (already produced
  by the five-engine table reconciliation in `parse-acc-aha-recbox`).
- Output: `RecommendationDraft-A` with the row's `text_verbatim`,
  `acc_aha_cor`, `acc_aha_loe`, supportive-text spans, and citation
  references pulled directly from SAIR cell coordinates.
- This extractor is **fully deterministic**: it does not call any LLM
  or VLM. Its output is byte-stable across re-runs given the same SAIR.

#### 2.2 Extractor V — VLM vision over rasterized region
- Input: the conditioned PDF rasterized at 600 DPI within the row's
  `bbox`, fed to the manifest-pinned VLM with a closed-prompt template
  ("Read the recommendation box. Return COR, LOE, and the verbatim
  recommendation text. Do not paraphrase. Do not interpret.").
- Output: `RecommendationDraft-V` with the same fields. The VLM is
  permitted to read tables and figures; it is forbidden from
  generating text not present in the raster.
- The VLM's output is post-validated character-by-character against
  the raster's OCR'd text (extractor A's text); any insertion or
  paraphrase causes the V draft to be rejected and the row marked
  `text-disputed`.

#### 2.3 Extractor O — OCR-fallback
- Input: the rasterized region.
- Output: `RecommendationDraft-O` with the verbatim recommendation
  text and COR/LOE strings. The OCR engines (≥3) reconcile their
  outputs first; only their consensus is forwarded as O.
- O exists as the tiebreaker on glyph-level disagreements between A
  and V (e.g., `≤` vs `<`, `mg` vs `mEq`).

#### 2.4 Three-way consensus
- Compute pairwise similarity (character-level, after Phase-2
  reversible normalization) for each (A,V), (A,O), (V,O) pair on:
  - `text_verbatim`
  - `acc_aha_cor`
  - `acc_aha_loe`
- Consensus state is set per the matrix in
  `extract-recommendation-cor-loe.spec.md` (this skill's spec
  document; the values are mirrored in
  `RecommendationRecordHTN.provenance.consensus.state`):

  | Pairwise minimum | Consensus state | Disposition |
  |---|---|---|
  | ≥ 0.99 across all three pairs | `agreed` | advance to atomicity |
  | ≥ 0.99 on (A,V) and (A,O), but (V,O) < 0.99 | `agreed-A-anchored` | advance with anchor flag |
  | < 0.99 on any pair | `held` | route to queue with proposal-diff |
  | text disputed (insertions) | `text-disputed` | route to queue; never auto-resolve |

- For COR and LOE specifically, the schema's closed enums make the
  comparison exact-string; any mismatch between extractors on COR or
  LOE is `held` regardless of text agreement.

#### 2.5 No-LLM-only path
- The skill **never** produces a record from LLM output alone. The
  LLM pair is used only for atomicity decomposition (§3); COR, LOE,
  and verbatim text are produced by A/V/O consensus.
- A record whose only support is an LLM output is rejected at the
  consensus step; this is enforced by the schema's
  `provenance.consensus.engines[]` requiring at least one of A/V/O
  per `INV-06` of `recommendation-record-htn.yaml`.

### 3. Atomicity decomposition (dual-LLM, family-distinct)

For every row that reaches `agreed` or `agreed-A-anchored`, the skill
decomposes the verbatim text into `AtomicUnit` instances. Atomicity is
the act of finding non-overlapping spans within `text_verbatim` whose
kind is one of:

```
atomic-recommendation, qualifier, exclusion, monitoring, citation
```

#### 3.1 Dual-LLM proposal
- Two LLMs from distinct families (the verified pair from §1.4)
  receive the same closed-prompt template ("Decompose the
  recommendation into atomic units. Return non-overlapping spans
  within the verbatim text. Do not paraphrase. Do not introduce
  text. Categorize each span by kind from the closed list.").
- Each LLM returns a span list under a strict JSON schema; outputs
  that fail JSON schema validation are discarded (the skill never
  tries to repair LLM output by edit).

#### 3.2 Span agreement rule
- Two spans **agree** iff:
  - Same `kind`.
  - Span boundary character offsets agree within ±2 characters
    after Phase-2 reversible normalization (the tolerance accounts
    for whitespace handling).
  - Jaccard overlap ≥ 0.95.
- The schema's `AtomicUnit.agreement` records the per-span agreement
  state.

#### 3.3 Atomicity disposition
- For every span:
  - **Both LLMs agree** → `agreement = "agreed"`; the span advances.
  - **Only one LLM proposed the span** OR **boundaries diverge by
    >2 chars** OR **Jaccard <0.95** → `agreement = "held"`; the
    span advances under explicit hold flag, and the row's
    atomicity state is also `held`.
  - **The two LLMs propose conflicting `kind` for the same
    canonical span** → `agreement = "conflict"`; the row's
    atomicity state is `conflict` and the row routes to the queue.
- A row whose atomicity state is `held` may still advance to Gate 1
  (per `gate1-register.yaml` `atomicity_state_acknowledged`); the
  reviewer must acknowledge the held state at signoff. A row whose
  atomicity state is `conflict` does **not** advance to Gate 1.

#### 3.4 Inheritance
- Each `AtomicUnit` inherits `acc_aha_cor` and `acc_aha_loe` from
  its parent record (read-only at and after Gate 1 per
  `AU-INV-25`).
- Each unit inherits the parent's `anchors.sair_sha256` and
  `anchors.bbox` (the unit's `span` is offset within the parent
  `text_verbatim`).

### 4. PICO precheck

For every record advancing to Gate 1, the skill runs the **PICO
precheck** (`recommendation-record-htn.yaml` `INV-08`), populating:

- `pico_precheck.populations[]` (closed enum from the schema:
  `general-adult`, `older-adult`, `pregnant`, `postpartum`,
  `ckd`, `t2dm`, `hf-rEF`, `hf-pEF`, `cad`, `post-stroke`,
  `secondary-htn-suspected`, `urgency`, `emergency`, `resistant-htn`).
- `pico_precheck.population_present` (boolean).
- `pico_precheck.intervention_present` (boolean).
- `pico_precheck.comparator_kind` (`active`, `placebo`, `usual-care`,
  `none`, `unspecified`).
- `pico_precheck.outcome_kind` (`bp-reduction`, `cv-event`,
  `mortality`, `progression-to-htn`, `composite`, `other`,
  `unspecified`).

The precheck is mechanical: closed enums, span anchors, no
free-text. The full PICO is decomposed downstream at P11 by
`pico-decompose-htn`.

### 5. Numeric-fact precheck

For every record carrying numeric facts (BP thresholds, eGFR
thresholds, age boundaries, dose ranges), the skill runs the
**numeric-fact precheck**:

1. Identify numeric tokens via deterministic regex (no LLM); flag
   each with its character offset in `text_verbatim`.
2. Re-extract each numeric token via an independent second pass on
   the rasterized region (extractor V re-read).
3. Compare byte-for-byte. Mismatch is a release blocker; the row
   routes to the queue with a numeric-fact diff.

Examples (from the framework's golden set):
- `≥ 130/80 mm Hg` MUST round-trip exactly; `≥ 130/80 mmHg`
  (no space before `mmHg`) is a held diff requiring queue
  resolution.
- `eGFR < 30 mL/min/1.73 m²` MUST round-trip with the unit symbol
  intact; ligature decomposition is reversible per the SAIR
  normalization log.

### 6. Predecessor-2017 advisory mapping

The skill produces a **predecessor-2017 advisory mapping** per
`recommendation-record-htn.yaml` `predecessor_2017`:

- `relation` ∈ {`carried-forward`, `revised`, `superseded`,
  `new-2025`, `removed-from-2025`, `unmapped`} (closed enum).
- `predecessor_record_id` (the corresponding 2017 record id from
  the predecessor SAIR ingested at P1, when applicable).
- `mapping_advisory_only` (const `true`, per ADR-HTN-001 D14).

The mapping is produced by deterministic span matching and a
read-only LLM-assisted suggestion that the reviewer either
acknowledges or escalates at Gate 1. **The mapping never feeds
downstream phases as a substitute for the 2025 source text.**

### 7. Cohort assembly and Gate 1 register opening

#### 7.1 Cohort partition
Under `--cohort-strategy by-domain` (default), records are
partitioned into Gate 1 cohorts by domain per the matrix in §10:

- `diagnosis | classification | bp-measurement | risk-stratification`
- `lifestyle | non-pharmacologic | implementation | team-based |
  measurement-workflow`
- `pharmacologic — general`
- `pharmacologic — older-adult`
- `pharmacologic — pregnancy / postpartum`
- `ckd / diabetes / hf / cad / post-stroke modifiers`
- `resistant-htn`
- `secondary-htn`
- `urgency / emergency`

Domain is inferred from `RecommendationRecordHTN.section_path` and
`pico_precheck.populations`. The orchestrator emits a per-cohort
register file at `work/<run_id>/gate1/<cohort_id>.draft.jsonld`
and posts it to `gate1-sme-review`.

#### 7.2 Register draft
Each register draft is initialized per
`schemas/gate1-register.yaml`:

- `cohort.cohort_id`, `cohort.name`, `cohort.run_id`,
  `cohort.opened_at`, `cohort.state = "in-review"`,
  `cohort.scope.domains`, `cohort.scope.includes_pregnancy_records`.
- `panel.panel_id`, `panel.reviewers[]` (institutional-roster
  assignment under the matrix in §10), `panel.panel_chair_signoff =
  null`.
- `records[]` with one entry per record in scope:
  - `record_id`, `record_content_hash`, `sair_sha256`,
    `state = "pending"`, `signoffs = []`, `escalation = null`,
    `rework_history = []`.
- `audit_log[]` initialized with a `cohort-created` event.
- `fixity.register_sha256` computed (RFC 8785 with `fixity`
  excluded).

#### 7.3 Reviewer assignment
For each record entry, the skill computes the **eligible-reviewer
set** per the matrix in §10 (which is mirrored from
`gate1-register.yaml` §1):

| Domain | Required roles (independent, non-overlapping) |
|---|---|
| diagnosis / classification / BP measurement / risk stratification | hypertension-specialist + clinical-informaticist |
| lifestyle / non-pharmacologic / implementation / team-based / measurement workflow | hypertension-specialist + primary-care-clinician |
| pharmacologic — general | hypertension-specialist + clinical-pharmacologist |
| pharmacologic — older adult | hypertension-specialist + geriatrician |
| pharmacologic — pregnancy / postpartum | mfm-or-obstetric-medicine + clinical-pharmacologist (skill accepts up to four signoffs per institutional policy) |
| CKD / diabetes / HF / CAD / post-stroke modifiers | hypertension-specialist + (specialty-matched: clinical-pharmacologist OR nephrology OR endocrinology) |
| resistant HTN | hypertension-specialist + clinical-pharmacologist |
| secondary HTN | hypertension-specialist + (nephrology OR endocrinology) |
| urgency / emergency | hypertension-specialist + (emergency-medicine OR critical-care) |

Auto-disqualification under COI is computed at this step (per
`G1-INV-14`); reviewers with applicable disqualification on a record
are excluded from that record's eligible set, and the panel must
contain a substitute of the same role.

### 8. Gate 1 driver semantics

The skill is the **Gate 1 driver**: it opens the cohort, posts the
draft register, and waits for `gate1-sme-review` to record signoffs
and the panel-chair finalization. The skill does **not** itself
sign records or pair-vote on outcomes.

#### 8.1 Decision-protocol auto-routing (this skill's enforcement)
The skill enforces the same auto-routing rules at the *upstream*
level that `gate1-sme-review` enforces at the reviewer-interface
level. This double-enforcement makes the rules tamper-evident even
against direct API edits to the register:

- An attempted edit to `acc_aha_cor` or `acc_aha_loe` posted via the
  register is rewritten to a `reject-rework` decision with the
  rationale prefixed `Auto-rewrite per G1-INV-12`. The skill emits
  a `cor-loe-edit-attempt` audit event.
- An attempted second signature by the same `reviewer_id` already
  present on a record is rejected outright per `G1-INV-21`.
- An attempted signoff while the cohort is `awaiting-panel-chair`
  or `finalized` is rejected.
- An attempted signoff whose `record_content_hash` does not
  recompute against the live record at signing time is rejected;
  the skill emits a `record-content-hash-drift` audit event and
  blocks the cohort.

#### 8.2 Closed concern-category set
On `reject-rework`, the reviewer (via `gate1-sme-review`) records a
**closed concern category** describing the requested upstream change.
The closed set, mirrored from `extract-recommendation-cor-loe.spec`
and consumed by this skill on rework signal:

- `verbatim-text-disputed` — the verbatim recorded text differs from
  the source raster (the row routes back to the SAIR queue and
  P6 / P7 re-runs).
- `atomicity-state-disputed` — the atomic-unit decomposition
  disputes the reviewer's reading (the row routes back to §3 with
  fresh dual-LLM passes; the reviewer's free-text rationale is the
  hint, but the LLMs do not see the reviewer's text — they re-read
  the verbatim only).
- `pico-population-mismatch` — the PICO precheck's
  `populations[]` are wrong (the row routes back to §4).
- `numeric-fact-mismatch` — a numeric fact diverges (the row
  routes back to §5 with the specific token highlighted).
- `predecessor-mapping-disputed` — the 2017 mapping is incorrect
  (the row routes back to §6; the mapping update is advisory and
  does not propagate to clinical decisions).
- `citation-anchor-broken` — a citation anchor does not resolve in
  the SAIR's `footnotes_index`.
- `out-of-scope` — the record is out of the framework's intended
  use (e.g., pediatric content surfaced incorrectly); the record
  is withdrawn from the cohort and audit-logged.
- `documentation-only` — the reviewer requests a documentation-only
  amendment (e.g., supportive-text typo); the record routes to a
  bounded edit under the closed `EditTarget` enum from
  `gate1-register.yaml` §2.3 (never `acc_aha_cor` or
  `acc_aha_loe`).

The categories are **closed**: the schema's `Edit` and rework
disposition recognize only these. Free-text rationale is required;
the closed category drives mechanical re-routing.

### 9. Panel-chair escalation paths

Reviewer disagreement on a record is **never** resolved by
majority-voting or by a third specialty reviewer. Disagreements
escalate to the panel chair through one of three explicit paths:

#### 9.1 Reviewer-initiated escalation
A reviewer decides `escalate-panel` directly. The skill (via the
register) sets the record's `state = "panel-escalated"`, populates
the `escalation` block with `escalated_to_role: panel-chair` and the
reviewer's rationale, and pauses downstream phases for the record.

#### 9.2 Auto-escalation on cross-decision conflict
When two signoffs are present on a record and at least one is
`reject-rework` or `escalate-panel` while another is `accept` or
`accept-with-edit`, the skill auto-escalates per
`gate1-register.yaml` `G1-INV-15`. The disagreement reasons and the
disagreeing signoffs are persisted in the `escalation` block; no
auto-resolution is attempted.

#### 9.3 Composition-failure escalation
If COI auto-disqualification or recusal leaves a record's required
roles unsatisfied (the matrix in §10 cannot be filled by available
panel members), the skill auto-escalates the record (and signals
the orchestrator to recompose the panel via the panel-management
skill, out of this skill's scope). The cohort cannot finalize until
composition is restored.

#### 9.4 Panel-chair disposition
The panel chair (via `gate1-sme-review --mode chair-finalize`)
adjudicates each escalated record with one of:

- `accept` — chair signoff stands as the resolver; record advances.
- `accept-with-edit` — chair-driven edit under closed `EditTarget`
  enum; record's content hash regenerates and any prior peer
  signature is invalidated (`G1-INV-09`); a fresh peer signoff is
  required.
- `reject-rework` — record routes back to the upstream phase
  identified by the chair's closed concern category; this skill
  is signaled and re-extracts on resume.

The chair **cannot** majority-vote past a reviewer's
`reject-rework`; the chair may decide to accept against a
`reject-rework`, but the chair's decision is recorded as a separate
`resolver_signoff` and the original `reject-rework` is retained
immutably for audit.

### 10. Reviewer composition matrix

| Domain | Required pair |
|---|---|
| diagnosis | hypertension-specialist + clinical-informaticist |
| classification | hypertension-specialist + clinical-informaticist |
| bp-measurement | hypertension-specialist + clinical-informaticist |
| risk-stratification | hypertension-specialist + clinical-informaticist |
| lifestyle | hypertension-specialist + primary-care-clinician |
| non-pharmacologic | hypertension-specialist + primary-care-clinician |
| implementation / team-based / measurement workflow | hypertension-specialist + primary-care-clinician |
| pharmacologic — general | hypertension-specialist + clinical-pharmacologist |
| pharmacologic — older adult | hypertension-specialist + geriatrician |
| pharmacologic — pregnancy / postpartum | mfm-or-obstetric-medicine + clinical-pharmacologist (institutional policy may add hypertension-specialist as a third) |
| CKD / DM / HF / CAD / post-stroke modifiers | hypertension-specialist + (clinical-pharmacologist OR nephrology OR endocrinology) |
| resistant HTN | hypertension-specialist + clinical-pharmacologist |
| secondary HTN | hypertension-specialist + (nephrology OR endocrinology) |
| urgency / emergency | hypertension-specialist + (emergency-medicine OR critical-care) |

The matrix is mirrored in `gate1-register.yaml` §1 and verified by
both schemas at register-write time (`G1-INV-05`, `G1-INV-06`,
`G1-INV-23`).

### 11. Determinism and reproducibility

- The triple-modal consensus is deterministic given identical SAIR
  bytes, identical pinned tools, and identical PDF rasterization
  parameters. Re-runs produce byte-identical
  `RecommendationDraft-A`, V, and O.
- The dual-LLM atomicity decomposition is **non-deterministic in
  general**, but the family-distinct rule plus the agreement
  threshold (≥0.95 Jaccard, ±2 char boundary tolerance) bounds the
  observed variance. Re-runs against the same prompts produce the
  same agreed/held/conflict disposition with high probability; the
  schema permits re-extraction with the prior atomic-unit ids
  retained when the new decomposition is identical (deterministic
  id derivation from `(record_id, span)` ensures stability).
- Re-running this skill on a sealed record set is a no-op; the skill
  refuses to mutate a record whose register entry is in any state
  beyond `pending`.
- Signature-bearing register writes are deterministic in the
  canonical-form sense (RFC 8785); identical canonical bytes produce
  identical `payload_sha256` across runs.

## DQA Gates Enforced By This Skill

| Gate | Condition for advance |
|---|---|
| **G3-A** Coverage | Every recommendation row in scope produces a `RecommendationRecordHTN` in state `gate-1-passed`, `rework-required`, `panel-escalated`, or `withdrawn`. No row is silently dropped. |
| **G3-B** Triple-consensus rate | ≥ 99.0% of advanced records reach `agreed` or `agreed-A-anchored` consensus state on first pass. |
| **G3-C** Verbatim integrity | Every `text_verbatim` round-trips byte-for-byte against the SAIR row's text after Phase-2 reversible normalization. |
| **G3-D** No COR/LOE drift | Every record's `acc_aha_cor` and `acc_aha_loe` match the SAIR's exact-string cell values; mismatch routes to queue. |
| **G3-E** Numeric-fact integrity | Every numeric token round-trips byte-for-byte across the V re-read. |
| **G3-F** Atomicity disposition | Every record's atomic-unit set is `agreed` or `held` (not `conflict`) at advancement; conflict routes to queue. |
| **G3-G** Family-distinct LLM pair | The two pinned LLMs map to distinct vendor families per the matrix; family-collapse blocks the build. |
| **G3-H** PICO precheck populated | Every advanced record carries a non-stub `pico_precheck` with at least one population entry. |
| **G3-I** Predecessor advisory only | Every record's `predecessor_2017.mapping_advisory_only == true`; no mapping influences downstream binding. |
| **G3-J** No editorial summary | Records advanced through Gate 1 carry no `editorial_summary` field per `INV-04` of `recommendation-record-htn.yaml`. |
| **G3-GATE1-A** Signoff completeness | Every advanced record has two independent signoffs from a domain-correct, non-overlapping reviewer pair (`G1-INV-05`, `G1-INV-06`). |
| **G3-GATE1-B** No-COR/LOE-edits | Zero `Edit.target ∈ {acc_aha_cor, acc_aha_loe}` recorded; auto-rewrite to `reject-rework` observed (`G1-INV-12`). |
| **G3-GATE1-C** Cohort finalization | Every cohort posted by this skill reaches `state == "finalized"` with `composition_compliance_attested && escalations_disposed && errata_watch.blockers_open == []` (`G1-INV-16`, `G1-INV-17`). |

Failure of any gate at any record → BLOCK; the record routes to the
queue with a specific gate diagnostic. There is **no override**.

## Outputs

- `RecommendationRecordHTN[]` at `work/<run_id>/records.json`,
  validated against `schemas/recommendation-record-htn.yaml` and
  sealed at end of P9.
- `AtomicUnit[]` at `work/<run_id>/atomic-units.json`, validated
  against `schemas/atomic-unit.yaml`.
- Gate-1 cohort registers at
  `work/<run_id>/gate1/<cohort_id>.draft.jsonld`, posted to
  `gate1-sme-review`. The register transitions to
  `<cohort_id>.signed.jsonld` only after panel-chair finalization.
- Per-row reconciliation queue entries at
  `work/<run_id>/queue/extraction/<row_id>.json` for any row that
  did not reach `gate-1-pending`.
- Per-record FHIR `Provenance` resources at
  `work/<run_id>/fhir/provenance/recommendation-<record_id>.json`,
  appending `Provenance.signature` entries on each Gate-1 signoff.
- Per-cohort plan and execution reports at
  `work/<run_id>/reports/extract-<cohort_id>.md`.
- Build PROV bundle update at
  `provenance/extract-<run_id>.jsonld`.
- Notifications to the orchestrator queue:
  - `cohort-posted-to-gate1` per cohort opened;
  - `record-routed-to-queue` per held / disputed row;
  - `cohort-finalized` mirrored from the Gate-1 register write-back.

## Error Handling

- **Manifest stale or not active.** BLOCK preflight; instruct
  operator to re-run `flow-hbp-2025-build` preflight.
- **SAIR not sealed.** BLOCK preflight; await P8 completion.
- **Family-distinct LLM rule violated.** BLOCK preflight; emit
  `family-distinct-rule-violated`; require new manifest version.
- **VLM or OCR engine unreachable.** BLOCK preflight.
- **Triple-modal pairwise similarity < 0.99.** Hold the row in
  `held`; route to queue; advance other rows.
- **Text-disputed insertion by VLM.** Reject the V draft; mark the
  row `text-disputed`; route to queue.
- **COR/LOE mismatch across extractors.** Mark the row `held`
  regardless of text agreement; route to queue.
- **Numeric-fact mismatch on V re-read.** Route to queue with
  numeric diff highlighted.
- **Atomicity decomposition `conflict`.** Route the row to queue;
  do not advance to Gate 1.
- **Atomicity `held` with reviewer acknowledgement** (downstream).
  Permit advance; record's `atomicity_state_acknowledged` is
  captured at signoff.
- **PICO precheck cannot resolve population.** Hold; route to
  queue.
- **Predecessor mapping unresolvable.** Set `relation = "unmapped"`;
  no escalation needed (mapping is advisory).
- **Reviewer self-pairing attempt.** Reject at register write per
  `G1-INV-21`.
- **COR/LOE edit attempt.** Auto-rewrite to `reject-rework` per
  `G1-INV-12`; emit `cor-loe-edit-attempt` audit event.
- **Record content hash drift.** Reject signoff; emit
  `record-content-hash-drift`; block the cohort.
- **TSA unavailable.** Hold the in-flight register write; poll the
  next TSA in `tsa_list[]`; after exhausting, BLOCK.
- **KMS authentication failure** on a register write. Reject; do
  not retry silently; emit `kms-auth-failure`.
- **Lock contention** on records.json or a register file. Wait up
  to a configured timeout; fail-closed if not acquired.
- **Resume after SAIR hash change.** Reject; require fresh run.
- **Resume after register hash change.** Reject; require fresh
  Gate-1 session.
- **Direct edit attempt against records.json.** Reject; emit
  `records-mutation-attempt`; investigate as adversarial input.

## Examples

```bash
# First-pass extraction over the sealed SAIR
extract-recommendation-cor-loe work/run-2026-04-30/sair.json

# Targeted re-extraction of two rows after queue resolution
extract-recommendation-cor-loe work/run-2026-04-30/sair.json \
  --records row-1a2b3c4d5e6f7081,row-2b3c4d5e6f708192 \
  --resume

# Cohort partition into a single cohort (institutional policy)
extract-recommendation-cor-loe work/run-2026-04-30/sair.json \
  --cohort-strategy single

# Dry-run plan emission for change-control review
extract-recommendation-cor-loe work/run-2026-04-30/sair.json \
  --dry-run
```

## Authority Boundaries

**Can do**
- Read the sealed SAIR and the parse-acc-aha-recbox outputs.
- Run the deterministic-text, VLM, and OCR extractors and their
  three-way consensus.
- Run the dual-LLM atomicity decomposition under the family-distinct
  rule.
- Run the PICO and numeric-fact prechecks.
- Produce `RecommendationRecordHTN` instances under the schema.
- Produce `AtomicUnit` instances under the schema with
  deterministic id derivation.
- Open Gate-1 cohort registers and post drafts to
  `gate1-sme-review`.
- Recompose cohort partitions on the orchestrator's resume signal.
- Apply auto-routing rules (COR/LOE-edit attempts → `reject-rework`;
  self-pairing → reject; content-hash drift → block).
- Auto-escalate cross-decision conflicts to the panel chair.
- Emit FHIR `Provenance` resources for each record and append
  `Provenance.signature` entries on each Gate-1 signoff.

**Requires approval (panel chair / new manifest version)**
- Any change to the LLM pair (a new manifest version is required;
  the family-distinct rule re-verifies at preflight on the new
  manifest).
- Any change to the cohort partition strategy that bypasses the
  domain matrix.
- Any decision to advance a record under `held` atomicity (the
  reviewer's signoff must explicitly acknowledge the held state;
  this skill cannot auto-advance).
- Any composition recomposition triggered by COI recusal that
  cannot be satisfied by the current panel.

**Never**
- Paraphrase or re-write `text_verbatim`. The closed enum
  `EditTarget` does not include verbatim paraphrase.
- Edit `acc_aha_cor` or `acc_aha_loe` under any circumstance; treat
  any attempted edit as `reject-rework` per `G1-INV-12`.
- Permit two signoffs from the same reviewer on the same record
  (`G1-INV-21`).
- Permit majority-voting or third-reviewer tie-breaks; disagreements
  always escalate to the panel chair.
- Use a single LLM (or two LLMs from the same family) for atomicity.
- Run a record through Gate 1 whose triple-modal consensus is
  `held` or `text-disputed`.
- Carry an `editorial_summary` on a record advanced through Gate 1
  (`INV-04`).
- Substitute PCE-legacy in any binding; PREVENT is canonical
  (consulted downstream at P16).
- Mutate a record whose register entry is in any state beyond
  `pending` without first invalidating the prior signoffs and
  recording the predecessor chain.
- Mutate a sealed records.json or a sealed atomic-units.json; the
  schema's lifecycle states forbid post-Gate-1 mutation.
- Permit a CDS-Hooks pregnancy denylist to ever read as a soft
  warning (the records this skill produces declare the denylist
  basis; the wiring to `order-select` hard refusal is enforced
  downstream at P22 + Gate 2 + Gate 3).
- Run with `--strict false` in production.
