# parse-acc-aha-recbox (refresh)

Phase-2 (P6) parse skill for the `cpg-htn-2025-acc-aha` framework. The
skill detects ACC/AHA recommendation boxes on conditioned PDF pages,
segments each box's cells into the canonical
**(COR, LOE, Recommendation, Supportive Text, Citations)** shape, runs
**five-engine table consensus** over each cell, exact-string-validates
COR and LOE against the closed enums declared in
`schemas/acc-aha-grading.yaml`, captures the verbatim recommendation
text under reversible normalization, anchors every cell to `bbox + page`
on the conditioned PDF, and writes back into the
`schemas/sair.yaml`-validated SAIR document at
`work/<run_id>/sair.json` under `recommendation_boxes[]`.

This refresh aligns the skill exactly to the SAIR schema as drafted in
this thread. Disagreements between the five table engines route to the
reconciliation queue; figure-only or chart-derived rows are flagged
`awaiting_corroboration` and held until corroborated by the
text-derived consensus pass at P4 (`parse-extract-text`) or by an OCR
fallback at P7 (`parse-ocr-fallback`).

This skill does **not** extract recommendations as RecommendationRecord
instances — that is P9 (`extract-recommendation-cor-loe`). It does not
bind terminology — that is P10 (`bind-htn-vocab`). It does not run
PICO decomposition, numeric-fact extraction, drug-rule extraction,
contraindication mining, or risk-engine binding. Its single
responsibility is producing the SAIR sub-document
`recommendation_boxes[]` in a form that downstream phases can rely on
byte-for-byte.

Posture: **caution over velocity, fidelity over coverage, verbatim over
paraphrase.** No paraphrase of clinical text. No coercion of COR or
LOE values. No batch acceptance. No silent fall-through. No engine is
bypassed. Every disagreement either advances under explicit consensus
state (`agreed`, `agreed-A-anchored`) or routes to the queue (`held`,
`text-disputed`, `awaiting-corroboration`).

## When to Use

Invoke this skill when:

- The orchestrator (`flow-hbp-2025-build`) reaches phase **P6** for a
  build whose conditioned PDFs are pinned (P2 complete), layout is
  detected (P3 complete), text is extracted (P4 complete), and figures
  are extracted (P5 complete).
- A re-parse of a specific page set is required after a queue
  resolution touched the SAIR's text-derived rows that this skill's
  `awaiting_corroboration` flag depends on.
- A targeted re-run is required after a `tools_lock` change authorized
  by a new manifest version (e.g., a table-engine pin update).
- A regression run is needed against the framework's golden box set
  after a schema or skill change.

Do **not** invoke this skill if:

- The active manifest is not in state `active` or has open errata
  blockers (`GM-INV-23`).
- The SAIR document is already sealed (`meta.write_back_lock_state ==
  "sealed"`); the skill writes into the SAIR's `recommendation_boxes[]`
  region and refuses to do so on a sealed document.
- Pages requested for parsing have not yet been processed by P3, P4,
  and P5 (the box detection consumes layout regions and the
  text-derived corroboration consumes text spans).
- A prior P6 run produced rows in the queue that have not been
  resolved by the two-person rule (the skill refuses to overwrite
  unresolved queue entries).

## Parameters

| Parameter | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sair-path` | yes | — | Path to the in-flight SAIR document at `work/<run_id>/sair.json`, validated against `schemas/sair.yaml`. The skill writes back atomically under the SAIR write-back lock. |
| `--pages <list>` | no | `all` | Comma-separated page indices on the conditioned PDF for the active source role (`main-guideline` by default; the skill accepts a `--source <role>` form for the rare case of supplement-borne boxes; non-default sources require explicit operator authorization). Defaults to all pages where layout detection produced a box-class region. |
| `--engines <list>` | no | the manifest's pinned five | Comma-separated engine ids from `manifest.tools_lock.items[]` of `kind == "table-engine"` and `kind == "vlm"`. The default is the manifest's pinned five (camelot + tabula + pdfplumber + tablemaster + donut-table). Listing fewer than five blocks unless `--strict false` (which is **never permitted in production**). |
| `--strict` | no | `true` | Fail-closed on every gate. Setting `--strict false` is **never permitted** in production; the flag exists only for fixture and golden-set development. |
| `--resume` | no | `false` | Resume an interrupted run from the last persisted page. The skill rejects resume if the SAIR's `fixity.sair_sha256` has changed since session start. |
| `--dry-run` | no | `false` | Run preflight + plan only; emit the planned page set, the engine roster, and the expected output regions; do not modify the SAIR. Permitted in production for change-control reviews. |

## Operation

### 1. Preflight

1. Validate `sair-path` against `schemas/sair.yaml`. Reject on any
   invariant failure.
2. Resolve `guideline_manifest_ref` from the SAIR; verify the active
   manifest's `medical_director_signoff` cryptographically per
   `GM-INV-21`; verify `state == "active"` and
   `errata_watch.blockers_open == []` per `GM-INV-23`.
3. Verify `tools_lock.lock_sha` against canonicalized
   `tools_lock.items[]` per `GM-INV-08`. The skill consumes:
   - At least three `kind == "table-engine"` entries (camelot, tabula,
     pdfplumber are the framework defaults).
   - At least two `kind == "vlm"` entries (tablemaster, donut-table
     are the framework defaults).
   - The manifest's `tools_lock.ocr_engines[]` (≥3) for OCR fallback
     within this skill on raster-only cells.
4. Probe each engine in the run set for liveness with a deterministic
   probe table; confirm version pin matches the manifest's
   `tools_lock.items[*].pin`. Failure → BLOCK with
   `engine-pin-mismatch`.
5. Verify the SAIR is **not sealed**:
   `meta.write_back_lock_state ∈ {"open", "appending"}`. A `sealed`
   SAIR refuses writes; the skill BLOCKs.
6. Verify the SAIR's per-page artifacts produced upstream are
   complete for every page in `--pages`:
   - `pages[*].layout_regions[]` populated by P3 with at least one
     region of class `box`, `table`, or `recbox`.
   - `pages[*].text_spans[]` populated by P4 with reversible-
     normalization log.
   - `pages[*].figures[]` populated by P5.
   - `pages[*].pdf_anchor.bbox` and `pages[*].pdf_anchor.page` non-null
     and recomputable byte-for-byte against the conditioned PDF.
7. Verify the active manifest's pinned **conditioned PDF SHA-256**
   matches the SAIR's recorded `sources[role].conditioned_pdf_sha256`.
   Mismatch → BLOCK; the skill refuses to operate on a PDF whose pin
   does not match the manifest.
8. Acquire the SAIR write-back lock. The skill is the only writer
   into `recommendation_boxes[]` during its run.
9. Refuse to proceed if any precondition fails. **Fail-closed.**

### 2. Box detection

For each page in `--pages`:

1. Resolve the page's layout regions of class `box`, `table`, or
   `recbox`.
2. For each region, compute a **box probability** under the closed
   feature set:
   - Region aspect ratio is consistent with ACC/AHA recbox proportions
     observed in the framework's golden set.
   - Region contains at least one cell whose visual style matches the
     ACC/AHA color-shading scheme for COR and LOE (the scheme is
     pinned in `docs/acc-aha-recbox-style-matrix.md`; CI verifies the
     file exists and is consulted).
   - Region's text-span density is bounded; pure-figure regions are
     excluded by the figure-class filter from P5.
3. A region with box probability ≥ the manifest-pinned threshold
   (default 0.85) is admitted as a candidate recbox. Lower-probability
   regions are emitted as advisory hints only and are **not** parsed
   by this skill (they are visible to operators in the SAIR's
   `pages[*].layout_regions[]` but produce no `recommendation_boxes[]`
   entry).

### 3. Cell segmentation

For each admitted candidate recbox, the skill segments cells under
the canonical ACC/AHA shape:

```
+----------+----------+--------------------------------+
| COR      | LOE      | Recommendation                 |
+----------+----------+--------------------------------+
|          Supportive Text (one or more rows)          |
+------------------------------------------------------+
|          Citations (zero or more rows)               |
+------------------------------------------------------+
```

The cells are segmented by:

1. Detecting the header row (COR / LOE / Recommendation) via deterministic
   text matching against the closed header label set (`COR`, `LOR`
   tolerance, `Class of Recommendation`, `LOE`, `Level of Evidence`).
2. Walking the visual ruling lines to derive cell bounding boxes.
3. Falling back to whitespace-projection cell discovery for ruling-less
   recboxes (the framework's golden set includes both styles; the
   skill is required to handle both).
4. Rejecting any candidate whose cell count is not exactly the canonical
   count plus zero-or-more supportive-text rows plus zero-or-more
   citation rows; rejection routes to a held diagnostic and the row
   does not advance to consensus.

Each segmented cell is anchored by `bbox` and `page` on the conditioned
PDF; the bbox is computed from the engine outputs as the union of the
engine-reported bboxes and snapped to the layout region's grid.

### 4. Five-engine consensus matrix

For every cell in every admitted recbox, the skill runs **five
engines** over the cell region and applies the consensus matrix.
The five engines, in default configuration, are three deterministic
table engines plus two VLMs:

| Slot | Engine | Kind | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| E1 | camelot | table-engine | deterministic ruling-line extractor |
| E2 | tabula | table-engine | deterministic ruling-line extractor |
| E3 | pdfplumber | table-engine | deterministic whitespace-projection extractor |
| E4 | tablemaster | vlm | VLM table extractor |
| E5 | donut-table | vlm | VLM table extractor |

The exact engine identities are pinned per build by the manifest's
`tools_lock.items[]`; the framework's defaults above MUST match the
manifest unless explicitly overridden. The skill never silently
substitutes an engine.

#### 4.1 Cell-value normalization

Before consensus, each engine's per-cell output is normalized under
the SAIR's reversible-normalization rules (the same rules used by
P4):

- Unicode NFC composition.
- Soft-hyphen removal at line break (logged as
  `soft-hyphen-removed at offset N`).
- Ligature decomposition for the closed set (`fi`, `fl`, etc.; logged
  as `ligature-decomposed at offset N`).
- Whitespace canonicalization (`\r\n` → `\n`; trailing spaces on
  lines preserved as the engine reported them; only `\r\n` is
  rewritten).
- Dehyphenation across line breaks **forbidden** at this phase
  (dehyphenation is a downstream concern; the skill records the
  raw verbatim and the normalization log).

The reversible-normalization log MUST round-trip: applying the log
in reverse against the normalized text MUST produce the engine's
exact output. The schema enforces this on write.

#### 4.2 Pairwise comparison

The skill computes pairwise similarity for each of the C(5,2) = 10
engine pairs, separately for each cell:

- **For COR and LOE cells:** **exact-string** comparison after
  normalization. The closed enums in `schemas/acc-aha-grading.yaml`
  are the authoritative value set (`AccAhaCOR ∈ {I, IIa, IIb, III-No-Benefit, III-Harm}`,
  `AccAhaLOE ∈ {A, B-R, B-NR, C-LD, C-EO}`). Any value outside the
  enum is auto-rejected (the engine output is treated as a
  recognition error).
- **For Recommendation, Supportive Text, and Citation cells:**
  character-level similarity (Levenshtein-based) after normalization.
  The threshold pins are recorded in
  `manifest.recbox_thresholds` (default 0.99 for Recommendation,
  0.97 for Supportive Text, 0.95 for Citations).

#### 4.3 Consensus state

The cell's consensus state is computed under the closed matrix
(`sair.yaml` `RecBoxConsensusState`):

| Pattern | State | Disposition |
|---|---|---|
| ≥ 4 of 5 engines agree exactly on COR or LOE | `agreed` | advance |
| 3 of 3 deterministic engines agree, but VLMs disagree on text | `agreed-A-anchored` | advance with anchor flag |
| ≥ 4 of 5 engines agree on Recommendation text within similarity threshold | `agreed` | advance |
| 3 of 5 agree, 2 dissent | `held` | route to queue |
| 2 of 5 agree, no majority | `held` | route to queue |
| Any engine reports text **insertion** (text not present in the raster) | `text-disputed` | route to queue; never auto-resolve |
| The cell is figure-only (figure caption or chart-derived) | `awaiting-corroboration` | hold; corroborate against P4 text spans or P7 OCR fallback |
| The cell's COR or LOE value falls outside the closed enum | `held` with `enum-violation` flag | route to queue |
| All 5 engines disagree | `held` with `engine-divergence` flag | route to queue |

The consensus state is recorded per cell on the SAIR's
`recommendation_boxes[*].rows[*].cells[*].consensus.state`. The
row-level consensus state is the most-restrictive of its constituent
cells (e.g., one `text-disputed` cell makes the row `text-disputed`).

#### 4.4 No-LLM-only path

The five-engine consensus is the **authoritative** read of the
recbox. The skill does **not** consult any LLM during P6;
language-model use is reserved for atomicity decomposition at P9
under the family-distinct rule. A row whose consensus is supported
only by VLM outputs (E4, E5 only, with E1-E3 silent) cannot reach
`agreed`; the schema requires at least two deterministic engines
in the agreement set.

### 5. Verbatim recommendation text capture

For every row whose consensus is `agreed` or `agreed-A-anchored`,
the skill captures the **verbatim recommendation text** under the
following rules:

1. The `text_verbatim` field is set to the consensus text exactly as
   normalized in §4.1; no further transformation.
2. The `normalization_log[]` is persisted on the SAIR cell, so that
   downstream phases can verify reversibility.
3. The cell's `bbox` and `page` are recorded; the citation anchor
   index is computed and stored for later footnote resolution.
4. The skill **never** dehyphenates across line breaks at this phase;
   downstream phases (P9) consume the raw verbatim plus the
   normalization log and may dehyphenate **only** under the closed
   `EditTarget` enum at Gate 1 (`text_verbatim_typo`).
5. The skill **never** paraphrases, summarizes, or interprets the
   recommendation. There is no `editorial_summary` produced at P6
   (`INV-04` of `recommendation-record-htn.yaml` is enforced
   downstream, but the skill avoids the field at this phase).

### 6. `awaiting_corroboration` flag and queue wiring

A row is set to `awaiting-corroboration` when, and only when, its
recommendation cell text is derived **only** from a figure or chart
region (e.g., a recommendation embedded in a flowchart figure rather
than a true recbox). This is detected by:

1. The candidate region's source-of-text indicator is the figure-class
   region from P5 (the region was extracted via VLM caption / chart
   parsing rather than by table engines).
2. No P4 text span overlaps the cell bbox with text density above
   the manifest-pinned threshold.

For such rows, the skill:

1. Sets `consensus.state = "awaiting-corroboration"`.
2. Persists the figure provenance (`figure_id`, `figure_caption_id`,
   `chart_data_table_id` if any) on the row.
3. Emits a queue entry at
   `work/<run_id>/queue/recbox/<row_id>.json` with kind
   `awaiting-corroboration`, the row's bbox / page, the engines'
   per-cell outputs, and the corroboration request: "Re-read this
   row's source region under P4's text-span pass or under P7's OCR
   fallback; if a text-derived consensus emerges that matches the
   figure-derived text within the manifest's threshold, advance the
   row to `agreed-A-anchored` with the corroboration audit event.
   Otherwise, hold."
4. The queue entry is consumed by `parse-reconcile-queue` at P8 (the
   shared queue UI). The orchestrator's two-person rule applies to
   the resolution: a single operator cannot dispose of an
   `awaiting-corroboration` row; one resolver plus a verifier are
   required.

When P8 resolves the row, the orchestrator signals this skill to
update the SAIR's `recommendation_boxes[*].rows[*].consensus` to the
resolved state (`agreed-A-anchored` if corroborated, `held` if not).
The skill is the only authorized writer of the consensus state on
the SAIR; the queue UI does not write directly.

### 7. Held / disputed routing

For every row whose consensus state is `held` or `text-disputed`,
the skill emits a queue entry at
`work/<run_id>/queue/recbox/<row_id>.json` with:

- `kind: held` or `kind: text-disputed`.
- The row's bbox / page on the conditioned PDF.
- Each engine's per-cell output (raw and normalized).
- The closed flag (`enum-violation`, `engine-divergence`,
  `numeric-fact-mismatch`, `text-insertion`, etc.).
- The remediation hint: which engine pin to investigate, which
  layout region to re-segment, which page to re-OCR.

The queue entry is consumed by `parse-reconcile-queue` at P8 under
the two-person rule. This skill **never** auto-resolves a `held` or
`text-disputed` row.

### 8. SAIR write-back

The skill writes the parsed boxes back into the SAIR document's
`recommendation_boxes[]` array atomically. Each box entry conforms
to `schemas/sair.yaml` `RecommendationBox`:

```yaml
- box_id: "rbx-<16hex>"        # deterministic from (page, bbox, conditioned_pdf_sha256)
  page: <int>
  bbox: { x0: ..., y0: ..., x1: ..., y1: ... }
  source_role: main-guideline | executive-summary | supplement | predecessor-2017
  rows:
    - row_id: "row-<16hex>"
      kind: recommendation | supportive-text-row | citation-row
      cells:
        - cell_id: "cel-<16hex>"
          kind: cor | loe | recommendation | supportive | citation
          text_verbatim: "..."
          normalization_log: [ ... ]
          bbox: { ... }
          consensus:
            state: agreed | agreed-A-anchored | held | text-disputed | awaiting-corroboration
            engines:
              - { engine_id: "camelot",     pin: "...", value: "..." }
              - { engine_id: "tabula",      pin: "...", value: "..." }
              - { engine_id: "pdfplumber",  pin: "...", value: "..." }
              - { engine_id: "tablemaster", pin: "...", value: "..." }
              - { engine_id: "donut-table", pin: "...", value: "..." }
            similarity_min_pairwise: <float>
            agreed_engines: [ ... ]
            dissenting_engines: [ ... ]
            flags: [ ... ]
      consensus:
        state: <row-level state, most-restrictive of cells>
        flags: [ ... ]
  consensus:
    state: <box-level state, most-restrictive of rows>
  provenance:
    detected_at: "<ISO-8601>"
    skill_version: "<this skill's version>"
    tools_lock_sha: "<from manifest>"
```

The `box_id`, `row_id`, and `cell_id` are **deterministic** —
truncated SHA-256 of `(page, bbox, conditioned_pdf_sha256, kind)` —
so re-runs against the same conditioned PDF produce the same ids
and re-runs of `extract-recommendation-cor-loe` at P9 reference the
same row by id without renumbering.

The skill recomputes the SAIR's `fixity.sair_sha256` after writes
and persists. On lock release, it appends a `recbox-parsed` event
to the SAIR's `audit_log[]` with:
- the run id,
- the page set,
- the engine roster,
- the count of admitted boxes / rows / cells,
- the count of advanced rows,
- the count of `held` / `text-disputed` / `awaiting-corroboration` rows,
- the SHA of the queue manifest emitted to
  `work/<run_id>/queue/recbox/`.

### 9. Determinism and reproducibility

- The five-engine consensus is deterministic given:
  - identical conditioned-PDF bytes;
  - identical engine pins (per the manifest's `tools_lock`);
  - identical layout-region inputs from P3;
  - identical text-span and figure inputs from P4 and P5.
- The deterministic engines (E1-E3) are byte-stable across runs.
- The VLMs (E4, E5) are non-deterministic in general; the consensus
  matrix tolerates VLM disagreement explicitly via the
  `agreed-A-anchored` and `held` states. A row whose `agreed` state
  depends solely on VLM agreement (E1-E3 silent) cannot reach
  `agreed`; the matrix in §4.3 enforces this.
- Re-running this skill on a sealed SAIR is a no-op.
- Re-running on an open SAIR with identical inputs and pinned tools
  produces identical `recommendation_boxes[]` (modulo VLM-only
  rows, which the matrix prevents from being decisive).
- The deterministic id derivation makes downstream consumers
  (P9, P10) re-runnable without renumbering.

## DQA Gates Enforced By This Skill

| Gate | Condition for advance |
|---|---|
| **G2.3-A** Engine pin integrity | All five (or the manifest-declared count of) engines respond at the pinned version; lock-sha matches. |
| **G2.3-B** Layout completeness | Every requested page has P3 `layout_regions[]`, P4 `text_spans[]`, P5 `figures[]`, and a recomputable `pdf_anchor`. |
| **G2.3-C** Cell shape compliance | Every admitted recbox segments cleanly into the canonical (COR, LOE, Recommendation, Supportive, Citations) shape. Non-canonical shapes route to held diagnostic; no row advances. |
| **G2.3-D** COR/LOE enum compliance | Every advanced cell of kind `cor` / `loe` has a value in the closed `AccAhaCOR` / `AccAhaLOE` enum from `acc-aha-grading.yaml`. Out-of-enum values force `held` with `enum-violation` flag. |
| **G2.3-E** Text-insertion detection | No advanced cell carries a VLM-introduced character not present in the raster; insertion forces `text-disputed`. |
| **G2.3-F** Reversible normalization | Every advanced cell's `normalization_log[]` round-trips against the engine output byte-for-byte. |
| **G2.3-G** Awaiting-corroboration accounting | Every figure-only or chart-derived row is flagged `awaiting-corroboration` and has a queue entry; no figure-only row advances to `agreed`. |
| **G2.3-H** Held/disputed routing | Every `held` and `text-disputed` row has a queue entry under `work/<run_id>/queue/recbox/`; the queue manifest's SHA is recorded in the audit log. |
| **G2.3-I** Deterministic id derivation | Every `box_id`, `row_id`, `cell_id` is reproducible from `(page, bbox, conditioned_pdf_sha256, kind)`. |
| **G2.3-J** SAIR write-back integrity | The SAIR's `fixity.sair_sha256` recomputes deterministically after the write; no concurrent writer touched `recommendation_boxes[]` during the run. |

Failure of any gate at any row → BLOCK; the row routes to the queue
with a specific gate diagnostic. There is **no override**.

## Outputs

- Updated SAIR document at `<sair-path>` with new
  `recommendation_boxes[]` entries, validated against
  `schemas/sair.yaml`.
- Per-row queue entries at `work/<run_id>/queue/recbox/<row_id>.json`
  for every `held`, `text-disputed`, and `awaiting-corroboration`
  row.
- Per-run report at `work/<run_id>/reports/recbox-<run_id>.md`
  summarizing pages processed, boxes admitted, rows advanced, rows
  routed to queue (by kind), engine-pair similarity histograms, and
  the closed-enum violation count.
- Build PROV bundle entries at
  `provenance/recbox-<run_id>.jsonld` recording per-engine
  Activity / Entity / Agent and the per-row consensus outcome.
- SAIR audit-log entry of kind `recbox-parsed`.
- Notifications to the orchestrator queue:
  - `recbox-parse-complete` on full success.
  - `recbox-rows-routed-to-queue` with the row count by kind.
  - `recbox-engine-divergence` if more than the manifest's threshold
    fraction of admitted rows route to `held` (advisory; an unusually
    high divergence rate is itself a remediation signal).

## Error Handling

- **Manifest not active.** BLOCK preflight.
- **SAIR sealed.** BLOCK preflight; await re-open or new run.
- **Engine pin mismatch.** BLOCK preflight; emit
  `engine-pin-mismatch`; require manifest amendment.
- **Conditioned PDF SHA mismatch.** BLOCK preflight; the SAIR's
  recorded `conditioned_pdf_sha256` differs from the manifest's pin;
  remediation is upstream (re-run P2).
- **Page missing P3 / P4 / P5 outputs.** BLOCK for that page; emit
  `upstream-incomplete`.
- **Box detection fails on a page.** Emit a `no-recbox-detected`
  advisory event; the page produces no `recommendation_boxes[]`
  entries; downstream phases may treat this as expected (some pages
  carry no recboxes).
- **Cell shape non-canonical.** Hold the entire row; route to queue
  with `cell-shape-noncanonical` flag; do not advance.
- **COR or LOE outside enum.** Hold the row; emit `enum-violation`
  flag; route to queue.
- **Text-insertion by a VLM.** Reject that VLM's contribution to
  the consensus; if a non-VLM consensus still reaches the threshold,
  advance with `agreed-A-anchored`; otherwise hold with
  `text-disputed`.
- **Engine divergence above threshold.** Hold the row; route to
  queue; emit advisory `engine-divergence` audit event at run end.
- **Awaiting-corroboration unresolvable.** Persist the
  `awaiting-corroboration` state; the queue holds the row until
  P4 / P7 corroborates or until the panel chair adjudicates.
- **SAIR write-back lock contention.** Wait up to a configured
  timeout; fail-closed if not acquired; concurrent writers on
  `recommendation_boxes[]` are not permitted.
- **Resume after SAIR hash change.** Reject; require a fresh run.
- **Direct edit attempt against `recommendation_boxes[]`.** Reject;
  emit `recbox-mutation-attempt`; investigate as adversarial input.

## Examples

```bash
# Default first-pass parse over all pages with recboxes
parse-acc-aha-recbox work/run-2026-04-30/sair.json

# Re-parse a specific page set after a queue resolution
parse-acc-aha-recbox work/run-2026-04-30/sair.json \
  --pages 14,15,16

# Targeted engine roster (for golden-set development only)
parse-acc-aha-recbox work/run-2026-04-30/sair.json \
  --engines camelot,tabula,pdfplumber,tablemaster,donut-table

# Dry-run plan emission for change-control review
parse-acc-aha-recbox work/run-2026-04-30/sair.json \
  --dry-run

# Resume after orchestrator reposted upstream layout updates
parse-acc-aha-recbox work/run-2026-04-30/sair.json \
  --resume
```

## Schema Reference

- `schemas/sair.yaml` — output target. Specifically, the
  `recommendation_boxes[]` sub-document and the
  `meta.write_back_lock_state` lifecycle are consumed by this skill;
  the schema's reversible-normalization log invariants and
  deterministic-id rules are enforced at write.
- `schemas/acc-aha-grading.yaml` — the closed `AccAhaCOR` and
  `AccAhaLOE` enums; the skill performs exact-string validation
  against these enums and refuses out-of-enum values.
- `schemas/recommendation-record-htn.yaml` — downstream consumer
  (P9). The skill does not write into this schema, but its outputs
  (verbatim text, COR, LOE, reversible-normalization log, anchors)
  are the inputs that enable `INV-06` (content-hash integrity) and
  `INV-08` (PICO precheck populated) at P9.
- `schemas/atomic-unit.yaml` — downstream consumer (P9). The skill's
  verbatim text and span integrity are the inputs that enable the
  family-distinct LLM atomicity decomposition.
- `schemas/guideline-manifest-hbp-2025.yaml` — pin source.
  Specifically:
  - `tools_lock.items[]` of kinds `table-engine`, `vlm`, `ocr` are
    the engine roster.
  - `recbox_thresholds` (when present in a future manifest revision)
    governs the per-cell similarity floors.
  - `GM-INV-08` (tools-lock SHA), `GM-INV-09` (family-distinct LLM,
    consulted at P9 — not at P6), `GM-INV-10` (≥3 OCR engines, used
    here for raster-only cell fallback), `GM-INV-21`
    (medical-director signoff verifies), `GM-INV-23` (active-state
    preconditions).

## Authority Boundaries

**Can do**
- Read the in-flight SAIR document and the conditioned PDFs whose
  SHAs are pinned by the active manifest.
- Detect candidate recboxes on layout regions classified by P3.
- Segment cells into the canonical (COR, LOE, Recommendation,
  Supportive, Citations) shape.
- Run the manifest-pinned five engines per cell and compute the
  consensus matrix.
- Apply Unicode NFC composition, soft-hyphen removal at line breaks,
  and ligature decomposition under the reversible-normalization log.
- Exact-string-validate COR and LOE values against the closed enums.
- Write the parsed boxes back into the SAIR's
  `recommendation_boxes[]` array atomically.
- Recompute the SAIR's `fixity.sair_sha256` after the write.
- Emit per-row queue entries for `held`, `text-disputed`, and
  `awaiting-corroboration` rows.
- Append `recbox-parsed` audit events to the SAIR's `audit_log[]`.
- Emit FHIR `Provenance` entries and PROV bundle updates per row.

**Requires approval (panel chair / new manifest version)**
- Any change to the engine roster (adding, removing, or replacing an
  engine).
- Any change to the per-cell similarity thresholds.
- Any change to the `acc-aha-recbox-style-matrix.md` document
  governing color-shading recognition.
- Any change to the consensus matrix thresholds (`agreed-A-anchored`
  rule, the `≥4 of 5` floor).
- Any decision to permit single-VLM consensus to reach `agreed`
  (the framework's default rejects this; the panel chair would have
  to authorize a manifest-level relaxation, which would itself
  require ADR-HTN-001 amendment).

**Never**
- Paraphrase, summarize, or interpret recommendation text.
- Coerce a COR or LOE value to fit the closed enum (e.g., rewrite
  "Class III" as `III-Harm`); out-of-enum values force `held` with
  `enum-violation` flag.
- Dehyphenate across line breaks at this phase.
- Run with fewer than the manifest-pinned engine count under
  `--strict false` in production.
- Allow a row to advance to `agreed` based on VLM agreement alone;
  at least two deterministic engines (E1-E3) must agree.
- Insert text not present in the raster (the rule applies to VLMs
  too; insertion forces `text-disputed`).
- Auto-resolve a `held`, `text-disputed`, or `awaiting-corroboration`
  row; resolution is the queue's responsibility under the
  two-person rule.
- Write into the SAIR while it is `sealed`.
- Substitute an engine pin without a new manifest version.
- Mutate a `recommendation_boxes[]` entry whose consensus state is
  `agreed` or `agreed-A-anchored` once written; corrections require
  the orchestrator to re-open the SAIR (which itself requires
  authorization) and a fresh re-parse against a fresh
  `tools_lock_sha`.
- Run with `--strict false` in production.

# safety-hbp

Phase-23 (P23) safety-analysis skill for the `cpg-htn-2025-acc-aha`
framework. The skill produces the **Safety Case** — the ISO 14971-shaped
hazard log + risk evaluation + residual-risk justification document
that becomes the `safe` member of the Gate-3 bundle hashed and signed
by `safety-case-attest`. The Safety Case covers the framework's ten
named hazards H-01 through H-10 (per framework spec §8 and ADR-HTN-001
D8 / D9 / D10 / D14 / D15), wires every hazard to one or more
mitigations referencing **CQL Libraries**, **CDS Hooks services**, or
**pipeline controls**, computes pre-mitigation and post-mitigation risk
under closed Severity × Likelihood matrices, and produces a per-hazard
residual-risk justification anchored to source evidence.

This skill does **not** produce clinical content, modify CQL Libraries,
edit CDS Hooks service descriptors, change recommendation records,
mutate atomic units, or alter terminology bindings. It is the
**safety-evaluation** surface over content already produced and gated
by upstream phases. Every mitigation reference is **verified** at sign
time: the referenced Library exists, has Gate-2-finalized signoff, and
the Library's hard-block invariant verifies; the referenced CDS Hooks
service exists with the manifest-required hook type and posture; the
referenced pipeline control is a real, machine-checkable behavior of
the orchestrator (e.g., the parser's reversible-normalization log, the
SAIR write-back lock, the gate1-register's append-only audit). Producer
claims are not trusted; the skill recomputes verifications.

Posture: **caution over velocity, fidelity over coverage, residual-risk
over claimed-risk.** The Safety Case may declare residual risks; it
may not declare them away. Pregnancy hard-block must remain
`order-select` hard refusal — no soft warning. PCE-legacy never
substitutes for PREVENT. Hazards without verified mitigations BLOCK
the build. Post-signoff Safety Case content is immutable; corrections
require a new Safety Case version with explicit predecessor chain.

This skill is the operational analogue of `safety-case-attest` at the
upstream end: where Gate 3 attests the build's published artifacts in
aggregate, P23 produces the safety-evaluation document that Gate 3
attests *to*.

## When to Use

Invoke this skill when:

- The orchestrator (`flow-hbp-2025-build`) reaches phase **P23** for a
  build whose Gate-1 cohort registers and Gate-2 cohort registers are
  in state `finalized`, whose CQL Libraries have all passed the 95%
  Synthea coverage floor, whose CDS Hooks services are packaged at P22,
  and whose `htn-pregnancy-denylist` service is wired as `order-select`
  with hard-refusal posture.
- A re-run is required after a Gate-2 reviewer recorded `reject-rework`
  on a Library that bears on a hazard's mitigation reference (the
  orchestrator regenerates the Library at P20–P21 and re-posts to
  Gate 2; on resume, this skill re-verifies the mitigation and
  re-emits the Safety Case).
- A regression run is needed against the framework's golden hazard
  set after a schema or skill change.
- A change-control review needs to verify that the Safety Case still
  references live, finalized artifacts (`--mode draft`).

Do **not** invoke this skill if:

- The active manifest is not in state `active` or has open errata
  blockers.
- Any Gate-1 or Gate-2 cohort referenced by mitigations is not in
  state `finalized`.
- Any CQL Library referenced by a mitigation has Synthea branch
  coverage below 95.0%.
- The CDS Hooks packaging at P22 has not produced the
  `htn-pregnancy-denylist` service with `order-select` hook type and
  hard-refusal posture.
- The orchestrator has not posted the Safety Case draft path to this
  skill's queue.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sair-path` | yes | — | Path to the sealed SAIR document at `work/<run_id>/sair.json` (read-only at this phase). The skill consults the SAIR for source-anchored basis pointers (e.g., the cor-iii-harm or cor-iii-no-benefit anchor that justifies a denylist mitigation). |
| `--records <list>` | no | `all-finalized` | Comma-separated list of recommendation record ids whose hazard implications are to be re-evaluated. Defaults to every record in `work/<run_id>/records.json` whose Gate-1 register state is `finalized`. |
| `--cohort <id>` | no | — | Restrict to records bound to the given Gate-1 cohort id. Useful for targeted re-runs after a single cohort's rework. |
| `--mode <draft\|sign>` | no | `draft` | `draft` produces the Safety Case content under a session-scoped `fixity` block, with no signature; `sign` opens an authenticated signing session for the medical director or hypertension specialist (the framework's default; institutional policy may pin a different signer role) and produces the signed Safety Case at `work/<run_id>/safety/safety-case.signed.jsonld`. |
| `--reviewer <id>` | no | — | The reviewer id (`rev-<16hex>`) for the current session. Required in `--mode sign`. The skill refuses to act on behalf of any other reviewer. |
| `--resume` | no | `false` | Resume an interrupted run from the last persisted hazard. The skill rejects resume if any underlying register's `register_sha256` has changed since session start. |
| `--strict` | no | `true` | Fail-closed on every gate. Setting `--strict false` is **never permitted** in production. |
| `--dry-run` | no | `false` | Run preflight + plan only; emit the planned hazard set, mitigation references, and the verification recompute outcomes; do not write the Safety Case or open a signing session. Permitted in production for change-control review. |

## Operation

### 1. Preflight

1. Validate `sair-path` against `schemas/sair.yaml`. Reject on any
   invariant failure.
2. Resolve `guideline_manifest_ref` from the SAIR; verify the active
   manifest's `medical_director_signoff` cryptographically per
   `GM-INV-21`; verify `state == "active"` and
   `errata_watch.blockers_open == []` per `GM-INV-23`.
3. Verify `tools_lock.lock_sha` against canonicalized
   `tools_lock.items[]` per `GM-INV-08`.
4. Verify upstream prerequisites (each is a release blocker if it
   fails):
   - `work/<run_id>/records.json` is sealed and validates against
     `schemas/recommendation-record-htn.yaml`.
   - `work/<run_id>/atomic-units.json` validates against
     `schemas/atomic-unit.yaml`.
   - Every Gate-1 cohort register file under
     `work/<run_id>/gate1/*.signed.jsonld` is in state `finalized`
     and validates against `schemas/gate1-register.yaml`.
   - Every Gate-2 cohort register file under
     `work/<run_id>/gate2/*.signed.jsonld` is in state `finalized`
     and validates against `schemas/gate2-register.yaml`.
   - Every CQL Library snapshot directory has Synthea branch coverage
     ≥ 95.0%.
   - Every CDS Hooks service descriptor under
     `work/<run_id>/cds-hooks/*.json` validates against the framework's
     CDS Hooks schema; `htn-pregnancy-denylist` MUST declare hook type
     `order-select` and hard-refusal posture.
5. Verify `tsa_list[]` in the manifest has at least one TSA whose
   `cert_valid_until` covers the wall-clock window. Otherwise BLOCK.
6. In `--mode sign`:
   - Resolve `--reviewer` to a `Reviewer` in any of the contributing
     Gate-1 / Gate-2 panels (the safety signer is institutional; the
     framework's default is the medical director who also signs the
     manifest, per ADR-HTN-001 D9, but a hypertension specialist
     designated by the panel chair is permitted).
   - Verify `identity_proof.ial >= "IAL2"` and `aal >= "AAL2"`; if
     the institutional policy pins a higher level for safety
     attestation, enforce that level.
   - Authenticate the reviewer via the institutional KMS bound to
     the reviewer's `key_id`.
7. Refuse to proceed if any precondition fails. **Fail-closed.**

### 2. Hazard set (closed)

The Safety Case covers the framework's ten named hazards exactly:

| Hazard id | Title | Category |
|---|---|---|
| H-01 | RAAS / MRA / direct-renin in pregnancy | drug-population (hard-block) |
| H-02 | Triple-whammy AKI (ACEi/ARB + diuretic + NSAID) | drug-drug-population |
| H-03 | Hyperkalemia on ACEi+ARB+MRA | drug-drug |
| H-04 | Older-adult orthostasis / falls | drug-population |
| H-05 | Beta-blocker rebound on abrupt discontinuation | drug-protocol |
| H-06 | Missed primary aldosteronism in resistant HTN | workup-omission |
| H-07 | In-office-only diagnosis (missed white-coat / masked HTN) | measurement-protocol |
| H-08 | LLM-hallucinated recommendation surfaces in published artifact | pipeline-integrity |
| H-09 | Terminology drift (RxNorm / SNOMED / LOINC editions move) | pipeline-integrity |
| H-10 | Source guideline updated / erratum published after build | pipeline-integrity |

The set is **closed** at the schema level; the skill refuses to add
or remove hazards without a manifest-version-level amendment under
panel-chair signoff. Adding an institution-specific hazard is
permitted only via a separate `safety-hbp-extensions` skill (out of
scope) whose output is concatenated to the canonical ten under a
clearly-marked `extensions` block; the canonical Gate-3 bundle hash
covers the union, and reviewers attest both blocks.

### 3. Per-hazard authoring

For each hazard H-01 through H-10, the skill produces a `Hazard`
entry per `schemas/safety-case-htn.yaml` (the dedicated Safety Case
schema; until that schema is formally drafted, the skill validates
against an inline shape that mirrors the YAML contract embedded in
this file's §6). The shape per hazard is:

```yaml
hazard_id: H-01
title: "..."
category: drug-population
intended_use_scope:
  age_min_inclusive: 18
  populations: [pregnant, postpartum]   # closed enum from schema
  out_of_scope_populations: [pediatric]
narrative:
  description_verbatim_anchored: true
  body: |
    Source-anchored description of the hazard, citing the
    `RecommendationRecord` ids and atomic-unit ids that bear on it.
basis:
  cor: III-Harm                          # closed enum
  loe: B-NR                              # closed enum
  source_anchors:
    - { record_id: rec-..., atomic_unit_id: au-..., anchor_kind: cor-iii-harm-anchor }
clinical_consequence:
  on_occurrence: "..."
pre_mitigation_risk:
  severity: serious                      # closed: minor | major | serious | catastrophic
  likelihood: occasional                 # closed: rare | occasional | probable | frequent
  combined: high                         # derived; see §4
mitigations:
  - mitigation_id: mit-...
    kind: cql-library | cds-hooks-service | pipeline-control | documentation
    target:
      cql_library:
        library_id: lib-hbp-pregnancy
        library_name: PregnancyHTN
        hard_block_invariant_kind: pregnancy-denylist-order-select-hard-refuse
      # OR
      cds_hooks_service:
        service_id: htn-pregnancy-denylist
        hook: order-select
        posture: hard-refuse
      # OR
      pipeline_control:
        control_kind: parse-acc-aha-recbox-cell-shape-compliance | gate1-register-immutability | manifest-no-auto-update | sair-write-back-lock
      # OR
      documentation:
        artifact: guideline-card | regulatory-traceability | retraction-notice
        section: "..."
    asserts_invariant_kind: pregnancy-denylist-order-select-hard-refuse
    verification:
      verifies: true                     # recomputed at sign time
      verified_by_reference_test_id: test-...
      verified_at: "<ISO-8601>"
    rationale: |
      ...
post_mitigation_risk:
  severity: serious                      # severity rarely changes; mitigations affect likelihood
  likelihood: rare
  combined: low
residual_risk_justification:
  is_acceptable_under_iso14971: true
  basis: |
    Source-anchored argument that residual risk is as low as
    reasonably practicable given the four sources, the manifest's
    intended-use scope, and the named mitigations.
  benefit_risk_summary: |
    Quantitative or semi-quantitative summary appropriate to the
    hazard.
  out_of_scope_assertion: |
    Explicit statement of what populations the framework does not
    address (e.g., pediatric is out of scope; the hazard does not
    propagate there because the age gate is enforced).
```

Per-hazard authoring rules:

#### 3.1 Source-anchored narrative
- The hazard's `narrative.body` MUST cite at least one
  `RecommendationRecord` and at least one `AtomicUnit` from the
  build's records and atomic units; for H-08, H-09, H-10
  (pipeline-integrity hazards), the narrative cites the relevant
  pipeline controls instead.
- The narrative MUST NOT paraphrase the verbatim source text; quoted
  spans use the manifest's quote envelope (the cumulative quote
  count is shared with `copyright-quote-check-acc-aha`).
- The narrative MUST include an explicit `out_of_scope_assertion` per
  the manifest's `intended_use.out_of_scope[]`.

#### 3.2 Closed grading inheritance
- `basis.cor` and `basis.loe` MUST be values from the closed enums
  in `acc-aha-grading.yaml`.
- For pipeline-integrity hazards (H-08, H-09, H-10) where ACC/AHA
  grading does not directly apply, the `basis.cor` is set to the
  most-restrictive grade among the records the hazard surfaces over;
  the skill records this explicitly and labels the inheritance as
  `derived-most-restrictive` to avoid confusion.

#### 3.3 Mitigation kind constraints (per hazard, mechanical)

The skill enforces per-hazard mitigation-kind constraints (any
violation BLOCKs the build):

| Hazard | Required mitigation kinds (at least one of each) |
|---|---|
| H-01 | (a) cql-library: `PregnancyHTN`, hard-block invariant `pregnancy-denylist-order-select-hard-refuse`; (b) cds-hooks-service: `htn-pregnancy-denylist`, hook `order-select`, posture `hard-refuse` |
| H-02 | (a) cql-library: at least one of `FirstLineSelection`, `SpecialPopulationModifiers`, asserting an AKI-triple-whammy warning invariant; (b) cds-hooks-service: `htn-pharm-first-line-check` |
| H-03 | (a) cql-library: `FirstLineSelection` and/or `SpecialPopulationModifiers`, asserting hyperkalemia-aceiarb-mra-warning invariant; (b) cds-hooks-service: `htn-pharm-first-line-check` |
| H-04 | (a) cql-library: `SpecialPopulationModifiers`, asserting older-adult-orthostasis-monitoring invariant; (b) cds-hooks-service: `htn-pharm-first-line-check` |
| H-05 | (a) cql-library: `SpecialPopulationModifiers`, asserting beta-blocker-no-abrupt-discontinuation invariant; (b) documentation: Guideline Card section on protocolized taper |
| H-06 | (a) cql-library: `ResistantHTN`, asserting aldosteronism-screen-resistant invariant; (b) cds-hooks-service: `htn-resistant-workup` |
| H-07 | (a) cql-library: `HBPStaging`, asserting bp-confirmation-out-of-office invariant; (b) cds-hooks-service: `htn-bp-stage-and-confirm`; (c) cds-hooks-service: `htn-hbpm-discharge` |
| H-08 | (a) pipeline-control: `gate1-register-immutability` (Gate-1 SME signoff with two-person rule); (b) pipeline-control: `parse-acc-aha-recbox-cell-shape-compliance` (cell-shape-compliance enforces no-text-insertion); (c) pipeline-control: `extract-recommendation-cor-loe-triple-modal` (triple-modal consensus); (d) pipeline-control: `safety-case-attest-bundle-hash` (Gate-3 bundle re-hash recompute) |
| H-09 | (a) pipeline-control: `manifest-terminology-edition-pin` (manifest pins terminology editions; bind-htn-vocab consults pinned editions); (b) pipeline-control: `manifest-no-auto-update`; (c) documentation: Retraction Notice template parameterized for terminology drift |
| H-10 | (a) pipeline-control: `acquire-hbp-2025-source-errata-watch`; (b) pipeline-control: `manifest-no-auto-update`; (c) pipeline-control: `gate3-attestation-decline-on-errata-blocker`; (d) documentation: Retraction Notice template parameterized for source-guideline update |

For each mitigation entry, the skill verifies the reference at sign
time:

- **cql-library**: the named Library exists in the build's
  `work/<run_id>/cql/`, its Gate-2 register entry is `accepted` or
  `accepted-with-comment` and `state == "finalized"` at the cohort
  level, the declared `hard_block_invariant_kind` is present in the
  Library's `hard_block_invariants[]`, and the verifying reference
  test passes (`reference_test_results[*].status == "pass"` for the
  test asserting that invariant).
- **cds-hooks-service**: the named service descriptor exists, its
  hook type matches the constraint, its posture matches the
  constraint, and (for H-01) the descriptor's hard-refusal semantics
  are verifiable mechanically (the service descriptor declares
  `suggestions[]` only — never `cards[]` with permissive override
  semantics — and the skill rejects any descriptor whose semantics
  permit attending override on the pregnancy denylist).
- **pipeline-control**: the named control kind is in the closed
  enum and the skill confirms the control is wired in the
  orchestrator's PROV bundle (e.g., a `gate1-register-immutability`
  control is satisfied iff the build PROV bundle records a
  `cohort-finalized` event with a chained-hash audit log).
- **documentation**: the named artifact exists in the build's
  `work/<run_id>/docs/` directory and the named section is
  non-empty.

A mitigation whose verification fails at sign time forces the
hazard's overall verification status to fail, which BLOCKs the
Safety Case from advancing to `--mode sign`.

#### 3.4 Pregnancy-specific reinforcements (mechanical)

For H-01 specifically:

- The skill verifies that the bound CDS Hooks service descriptor for
  `htn-pregnancy-denylist` declares hook type `order-select` (not
  `order-sign`, not `medication-prescribe`); any other hook type
  BLOCKs.
- The skill verifies the descriptor's posture is `hard-refuse` and
  that no `card.indicator` of `info` or `warning` is present on
  the denylist branch; any soft-warning indicator BLOCKs (the
  framework does not permit a soft warning on the pregnancy
  denylist under any circumstance).
- The skill verifies that the `PregnancyHTN` Library's denylist
  branch has no attending-override branch (no
  `permit_on_attending_override == true`); the schema enforces this
  at the Library level, but the skill re-checks at sign time.
- The skill records the two-person-rule attestation evidence: the
  Gate-1 cohort containing pregnancy records has at least one MFM
  signoff and one clinical pharmacology signoff; the Gate-2 cohort
  containing the `PregnancyHTN` Library has the same.

#### 3.5 PCE-legacy never substitutes for PREVENT (mechanical)

For every hazard whose mitigation references a CQL Library binding
a risk engine (notably H-02 / H-04 indirectly via PreventRisk):

- The skill verifies the Library's
  `snapshot.bound_risk_engine.name == "PREVENT"` and
  `bound_risk_engine.legacy_only == false`.
- Any binding to PCE-legacy BLOCKs the Safety Case at sign time
  (this is also enforced at Gate 2 by `cql-clinician-signoff`; the
  redundancy is intentional under ADR-HTN-001 D5).

### 4. Severity × Likelihood matrix (closed)

The skill computes pre-mitigation and post-mitigation risk per
hazard under the closed Severity × Likelihood matrix:

| Severity \ Likelihood | rare | occasional | probable | frequent |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **minor** | low | low | medium | medium |
| **major** | low | medium | high | high |
| **serious** | medium | high | high | extreme |
| **catastrophic** | high | high | extreme | extreme |

The matrix is **closed**; the skill does not permit operator
adjustment. Severity is rarely affected by mitigations (a
hyperkalemia event remains a serious clinical event whether
mitigated or not); mitigations primarily reduce likelihood. The
schema enforces this by requiring a non-trivial likelihood reduction
to claim a post-mitigation risk reduction, and by requiring a
narrative justification when severity changes between pre- and
post-mitigation.

For pipeline-integrity hazards (H-08, H-09, H-10), severity is
defined as the worst-case clinical severity of any record the
hazard would surface; for H-08 specifically, the worst-case is
`catastrophic` (a hallucinated recommendation in the pregnancy
denylist domain is a catastrophic safety event; the skill anchors
H-08's severity to `catastrophic` by default and the reviewer may
not lower it).

### 5. Residual-risk justification

Per hazard, the skill produces a `residual_risk_justification`
block:

- `is_acceptable_under_iso14971`: boolean. The reviewer's signature
  attests this; the skill records the value as a candidate and the
  signed Safety Case binds it.
- `basis`: free-text, source-anchored argument. The skill
  pre-populates a template citing the relevant
  `RecommendationRecord` ids and the relevant CQL / CDS-Hooks /
  pipeline-control mitigation ids; the reviewer completes the
  argument.
- `benefit_risk_summary`: free-text or quantitative summary.
- `out_of_scope_assertion`: required; verbatim from the manifest's
  `intended_use.out_of_scope[]` filtered to the hazard's domain.

The Safety Case **does not declare residual risk away**; if a hazard
has insufficient mitigations to reduce post-mitigation risk below
the manifest-pinned `acceptable_residual_risk_max` (the framework
default is `medium`), the skill records the residual risk as
**unacceptable** and BLOCKs the Safety Case from advancing to
`--mode sign`. The remediation is upstream: re-author the Library or
the CDS Hooks service to add the missing mitigation, then re-run
this skill.

### 6. Safety Case document shape (output contract)

The skill writes the Safety Case to
`work/<run_id>/safety/safety-case.signed.jsonld` in `--mode sign`
and to `work/<run_id>/safety/safety-case.draft.jsonld` in
`--mode draft`, under the following shape (mirroring the
forthcoming `schemas/safety-case-htn.yaml`):

```yaml
schema_version: "1.0.0"
safety_case_id: "sc-<16hex>"
safety_case_version: "1.0.0"
predecessor_safety_case_id: null
guideline_manifest_ref: "<manifest path>"
build:
  run_id: "<uuid>"
  build_version_label: "v1.0.0+ACC-AHA-2025+US+<date>"
  opened_at: "<ISO-8601>"
intended_use_scope:
  statement: "<verbatim from manifest.intended_use.statement>"
  age_min_inclusive: 18
  in_scope: [ ... ]
  out_of_scope: [ ... ]
  acceptable_residual_risk_max: medium
hazards:
  - <Hazard entry per §3>
  - ...
cohort_axis_attestations:
  iso14971_compliance_attested: true
  no_relax_of_hard_block_attested: true
  pce_legacy_never_propagates_attested: true
  pregnancy_order_select_hardrefuse_attested: true
  errata_watch_attested: true
  source_admission_attested: true
state: draft | signed | superseded | withdrawn
audit_log: [ <append-only AuditEvent entries> ]
fixity:
  safety_case_sha256: "<64hex>"
  computed_at: "<ISO-8601>"
  canonical_form: json-canonical-rfc8785
signature: <Signature; only present in `signed` state>
```

The deterministic id derivation: `safety_case_id` is the truncated
SHA-256 of `(build_run_id, manifest_sha256, hazards-set-sha256,
state)`, so identical inputs produce identical ids and the audit
chain is stable.

### 7. Sign cycle (`--mode sign`)

1. Lock the Safety Case file for write.
2. Re-run §3 verification for every hazard's every mitigation:
   - Re-resolve the CQL Library Gate-2 register entry; verify
     `state == "finalized"` and the hard-block invariant verifies.
   - Re-resolve the CDS Hooks service descriptor; verify hook type,
     posture, and (for H-01) the absence of attending-override.
   - Re-resolve the pipeline control's PROV-bundle evidence.
   - Re-resolve documentation artifacts and confirm sections are
     non-empty.
3. Re-run §4 risk-matrix computation; reject if the matrix outputs
   differ from the draft (this would indicate post-draft mutation
   of a Library or CDS Hooks descriptor, which is forbidden).
4. Verify every hazard's post-mitigation risk is at or below
   `acceptable_residual_risk_max`. Any violation BLOCKs.
5. Construct the `Signature` candidate over the JCS-canonical form
   of the Safety Case with `signature` field stripped; compute
   `payload_sha256`.
6. Issue a signature request to the reviewer's institutional KMS
   bound to `Reviewer.public_key.key_id`.
7. Request an RFC 3161 time-stamp from a TSA in
   `manifest.tsa_list[]` whose certificate validity covers
   `signed_at`. Persist the `TimeStampToken`.
8. Verify the signature locally before persisting:
   - Reconstruct the canonical payload.
   - Recompute `payload_sha256`.
   - Verify `signature_b64` against `Reviewer.public_key.key_pem`
     under `signature.algorithm`.
   - Confirm the time-stamp token's hash equals `payload_sha256`
     and the TSA cert chains to a trust anchor pinned in the
     manifest.
   - Set `signature.verifies = true` only after these checks
     succeed.
9. Persist the signed Safety Case at
   `work/<run_id>/safety/safety-case.signed.jsonld`.
10. Recompute `fixity.safety_case_sha256` (RFC 8785 with `fixity`
    excluded); persist.
11. Append an `audit_log[]` event of kind `safety-case-signed`.
12. Emit a FHIR `Provenance` resource update at
    `work/<run_id>/fhir/provenance/safety-case.json`, appending
    a `Provenance.signature` entry.
13. Signal the orchestrator: `safety-case-ready`. The Gate-3 bundle
    construction in `safety-case-attest` consumes this signed
    Safety Case as the `safe` bundle member.

### 8. Determinism and reproducibility

- The hazard set is closed; the skill cannot add or remove hazards.
- The mitigation-kind constraint matrix in §3.3 is closed; the
  skill enforces it mechanically.
- The Severity × Likelihood matrix in §4 is closed and produces
  identical outputs given identical inputs.
- The deterministic id derivation produces stable ids across
  re-runs.
- Re-running this skill on a `signed` Safety Case is a no-op (the
  skill refuses to mutate a signed Safety Case; corrections require
  a new Safety Case version with predecessor chain).
- Re-running on a `draft` Safety Case at the same input hashes
  produces identical content (modulo wall-clock-bearing fields like
  `opened_at`).

## DQA Gates Enforced By This Skill

| Gate | Condition for advance |
|---|---|
| **GS-A** Safety Case integrity | Safety Case validates against the schema's invariants at every write. |
| **GS-B** Closed hazard set | Exactly H-01 through H-10 present; no addition or removal at this skill's level. |
| **GS-C** Source-anchored basis | Every hazard cites at least one `RecommendationRecord` and one `AtomicUnit` (or, for pipeline-integrity hazards, at least one pipeline control with PROV evidence). |
| **GS-D** Closed grading inheritance | Every `basis.cor` and `basis.loe` is from the closed enums; pipeline-integrity hazards record `derived-most-restrictive`. |
| **GS-E** Mitigation kind constraints | Every hazard has at least the required mitigation kinds per §3.3. |
| **GS-F** Mitigation verification | Every mitigation reference verifies at sign time; producer claims of `verifies: true` are recomputed. |
| **GS-G** Pregnancy hard refuse | H-01 mitigations include `htn-pregnancy-denylist` with hook type `order-select` and posture `hard-refuse`; no soft-warning posture; no attending-override branch. |
| **GS-H** PCE-legacy excluded | No CQL Library cited in any mitigation has `bound_risk_engine.name == "PCE-legacy"` or `bound_risk_engine.legacy_only == true`. |
| **GS-I** Risk matrix closed | Pre- and post-mitigation risk per the closed matrix; reviewer cannot adjust the matrix outputs. |
| **GS-J** Acceptable residual risk | Every hazard's post-mitigation risk is at or below `acceptable_residual_risk_max`. |
| **GS-K** Signature integrity | Signature verifies under the reviewer's public key; TSA cert chains to a manifest-pinned trust anchor. |
| **GS-L** Append-only audit log | Audit log ordered by `occurred_at`; chained `payload_sha256` continuity verified at every write. |
| **GS-M** Predecessor chain | When a Safety Case supersedes a prior one, `predecessor_safety_case_id` is set and the predecessor's state is `superseded` or `withdrawn`. |

Failure of any gate at any hazard or sign step → BLOCK; the skill
rolls back the in-flight write, surfaces the specific gate, and
emits a diagnostic at
`work/<run_id>/reports/safety-<run_id>.md`. There is **no override**.

## Outputs

- Signed Safety Case at
  `work/<run_id>/safety/safety-case.signed.jsonld` (in `--mode sign`)
  or draft Safety Case at
  `work/<run_id>/safety/safety-case.draft.jsonld` (in `--mode draft`).
- Per-hazard mitigation-verification report at
  `work/<run_id>/reports/safety-mitigation-verification-<run_id>.md`.
- Per-run Safety Case report at
  `work/<run_id>/reports/safety-<run_id>.md` summarizing hazards,
  pre- and post-mitigation risk, mitigation references, residual
  risks, and any blockers.
- FHIR `Provenance` resource at
  `work/<run_id>/fhir/provenance/safety-case.json`, with
  `Provenance.signature` entries.
- PROV bundle update at `provenance/safety-<run_id>.jsonld`.
- Notifications to the orchestrator queue:
  - `safety-case-ready` on signed completion;
  - `safety-case-blocked` with the failing gate and remediation
    guidance on any failure.

## Error Handling

- **Manifest stale or not active.** BLOCK preflight; instruct
  operator to re-run `flow-hbp-2025-build` preflight.
- **Records or atomic units unsealed.** BLOCK; await P9 completion.
- **Gate-1 / Gate-2 cohort not finalized.** BLOCK; await sibling
  gates.
- **CQL Library coverage below 95%.** BLOCK; await `cql-test-synthea-htn`
  re-run.
- **Pregnancy denylist not order-select hard-refuse.** BLOCK
  unconditionally; emit `pregnancy-denylist-soft-warning-detected`
  audit event; require upstream remediation.
- **CDS Hooks service descriptor missing or malformed.** BLOCK;
  emit `cds-hooks-descriptor-missing`; await P22 re-run.
- **Mitigation reference unverifiable.** BLOCK the hazard; record
  the failure mode; do not advance to `--mode sign`.
- **Risk matrix output below acceptable residual.** BLOCK; require
  an upstream mitigation addition.
- **Hazard added or removed by direct API edit.** Reject; emit
  `hazard-set-tamper-attempt`; investigate as adversarial input.
- **PCE-legacy detected in any cited Library binding.** BLOCK
  unconditionally; emit `pce-legacy-binding-detected`; require
  upstream remediation under ADR-HTN-001 D5.
- **TSA unavailable.** Hold the in-flight signature; the candidate
  Safety Case is persisted with `signature: null` and state
  `awaiting-time-stamp`; the skill polls the next TSA. After
  exhausting the list, BLOCK.
- **KMS authentication failure.** Refuse signing; do not retry
  silently; emit `kms-auth-failure`.
- **Signature local verification failure.** Discard the candidate;
  emit `signature-verification-failed`; investigate KMS or
  canonicalization drift; never accept.
- **Lock contention.** Wait up to a configured timeout; fail-closed
  if not acquired; concurrent writers on the Safety Case file are
  not permitted.
- **Resume after register hash change.** Reject; require fresh run.
- **Direct edit attempt against a signed Safety Case.** Reject;
  emit `safety-case-mutation-attempt`; investigate as adversarial
  input.

## Examples

```bash
# Default first-pass draft against a build with finalized Gate-1 and Gate-2 cohorts
safety-hbp work/run-2026-04-30/sair.json

# Targeted draft restricted to a single Gate-1 cohort's records
safety-hbp work/run-2026-04-30/sair.json \
  --cohort cohort-7c2a8e91b3d4f561

# Signed Safety Case session by the medical director
safety-hbp work/run-2026-04-30/sair.json \
  --mode sign \
  --reviewer rev-c0a1b2c3d4e5f607

# Resume after orchestrator reposted updated Library snapshots
safety-hbp work/run-2026-04-30/sair.json \
  --mode sign \
  --reviewer rev-c0a1b2c3d4e5f607 \
  --resume

# Dry-run plan emission for change-control review
safety-hbp work/run-2026-04-30/sair.json \
  --dry-run
```

## Schema Reference

- `schemas/sair.yaml` — input source-of-truth for source-anchored
  basis pointers (e.g., `cor-iii-harm-anchor`).
- `schemas/recommendation-record-htn.yaml` — input. Specifically:
  - `INV-09` (denylist requires hard-block basis with source
    anchor).
  - `INV-10` (PCE-legacy never propagates).
- `schemas/atomic-unit.yaml` — input; the hazard narratives cite
  atomic-unit ids.
- `schemas/acc-aha-grading.yaml` — closed COR/LOE enums for
  `basis.cor` and `basis.loe`.
- `schemas/gate1-register.yaml` — input; finalization-state
  preconditions are consumed at preflight and at sign time.
- `schemas/gate2-register.yaml` — input; the hard-block invariants
  declared on each Library are the source of truth this skill cites
  for mitigations.
- `schemas/gate3-attestation.yaml` — downstream consumer; the signed
  Safety Case becomes the `safe` member of the Gate-3 bundle.
- `schemas/guideline-manifest-hbp-2025.yaml` — pin source for
  `intended_use`, `tsa_list`, `signature_policy`,
  `acceptable_residual_risk_max` (when present), `terminology[]`,
  `risk_engine`, and `errata_watch`.
- `schemas/safety-case-htn.yaml` — formal Safety Case schema (to be
  drafted as the next step at the same fidelity as
  `gate1-register.yaml` / `gate2-register.yaml` /
  `gate3-attestation.yaml`); until then, the inline shape in §6
  serves as the authoritative contract.

## Delegation

- Upstream phases (consumed read-only):
  - `cpg-htn-2025-acc-aha/skills/parse-acc-aha-recbox/SKILL.md` (P6).
  - `cpg-htn-2025-acc-aha/skills/extract-recommendation-cor-loe/SKILL.md` (P9).
  - `cpg-htn-2025-acc-aha/skills/bind-htn-vocab/SKILL.md` (P10).

  - KMS key rotation.

## Authority Boundaries

**Can do**
- Read finalized records, atomic units, Gate-1/Gate-2 registers,
  CQL Libraries, CDS Hooks service descriptors, and pipeline-control
  PROV evidence.
- Produce per-hazard `Hazard` entries citing source anchors.
- Compute pre- and post-mitigation risk under the closed
  Severity × Likelihood matrix.
- Verify mitigation references at sign time.
- Produce residual-risk justifications under reviewer attestation.
- Sign the Safety Case via the reviewer's institutional KMS,
  time-stamped against a manifest-pinned TSA.
- Persist the signed Safety Case atomically and emit FHIR
  `Provenance` updates.
- BLOCK the build on any unverified mitigation, soft-warning
  pregnancy posture, PCE-legacy binding, or residual-risk overage.

**Requires approval (panel chair / new manifest version)**
- Any change to the closed hazard set H-01..H-10.
- Any change to the mitigation-kind constraint matrix in §3.3.
- Any change to the Severity × Likelihood matrix in §4.
- Any change to `acceptable_residual_risk_max`.
- Any decision to advance a hazard whose post-mitigation risk
  exceeds `acceptable_residual_risk_max` (such a decision is forbidden
  at this skill; remediation is upstream re-author, not Safety Case
  override).

**Never**
- Add or remove hazards from the closed set H-01..H-10 at this
  skill's level (extensions go to a separate skill).
- Modify Library content, CDS Hooks service descriptors, or
  pipeline controls.
- Accept a soft-warning posture on `htn-pregnancy-denylist`.
- Accept an attending-override branch on the pregnancy denylist.
- Substitute PCE-legacy for PREVENT in any Library binding.
- Lower the age gate below 18.
- Declare a residual risk acceptable when post-mitigation risk
  exceeds `acceptable_residual_risk_max`.
- Mutate a signed Safety Case; corrections require a new Safety
  Case version with explicit predecessor chain.
- Sign the Safety Case via any path other than the reviewer's KMS
  with manifest-pinned TSA time-stamping.
- Run with `--strict false` in production.

## References

- **ADR-HTN-001** D5 (PREVENT canonical), D8 (pregnancy hard-block
  enforced at order-select), D9 (three non-overridable human
  gates; this skill produces the Safety Case that Gate 3 attests
  to), D10 (PHI fail-closed), D14 (predecessor 2017 advisory; H-10
  cites the supersession Communication resource), D15 (drift
  detection; H-09 and H-10 cite errata-watch and no-auto-update).
- **`flow-hbp-2025-build` §10 (Safety analysis P23)** — placement,
  DQA gates, exit conditions; this skill is the implementation
  invoked from P23.
- **Framework spec** §8 (hazards H-01..H-10; the canonical hazard
  list), §11 (Safety Case structure under ISO 14971).
- **`recommendation-record-htn.yaml`** invariants `INV-09`
  (denylist requires hard-block basis), `INV-10` (PCE-legacy never
  propagates).
- **`atomic-unit.yaml`** invariants — the hazard narratives cite
  atomic-unit ids.
- **`gate1-register.yaml`** policy and invariants — finalization
  preconditions consumed at preflight.
- **`gate2-register.yaml`** policy and invariants — hard-block
  invariants per Library are the source of truth for mitigations.
- **`gate3-attestation.yaml`** — downstream consumer; the Safety
  Case is the `safe` bundle member.
- **`guideline-manifest-hbp-2025.yaml`** invariants `GM-INV-08`
  (tools-lock SHA), `GM-INV-12` (PREVENT canonical), `GM-INV-21`
  (medical-director signoff), `GM-INV-23` (active-state
  preconditions).
- **ISO 14971** — informs the Safety Case structure
  (pre-mitigation risk, mitigations, residual risk, residual-risk
  justification, Severity × Likelihood matrix).
- **NAM CGAT** — informs the safety-and-risk-evaluation standards
  consumed by the downstream `guideline-docs` skill.
- **AGREE II** — informs the safety-related items of the Guideline
  Card.
- **REF-475** ML Reproducibility Checklist — informs determinism
  rules applied to the Safety Case.
- **REF-062** W3C PROV-O — informs the per-hazard
  Activity/Entity/Agent emission and the Safety Case-level FHIR
  `Provenance` mapping.
- **NIST SP 800-63** (IAL/AAL) — informs the reviewer assurance
  level applied at sign time.
- **RFC 3161 / RFC 8785** — time-stamp protocol and JSON
  canonicalization scheme used in the signature envelope.
- **Parent framework** `aiwg-training` rules: `god-session` (≤7
  responsibilities per skill; this skill's responsibilities are
  bounded to: preflight, hazard authoring, mitigation verification,
  risk-matrix computation, residual-risk justification, sign cycle,
  and Safety Case write-back), `human-authorization` (the Safety
  Case is signed by the medical director or designate; Gate 3
  re-attests it), `native-ux-tools` (the queue UI invocation
  pattern; the Safety Case interacts with the orchestrator via the
  same notification surface used by other gate skills).
```

Saved as `skills/safety-hbp/SKILL.md`. The skill is the only authorized P23 producer of the Safety Case (`safe` member of the Gate-3 bundle), mirrors the parent repo's frontmatter and section discipline established by `acquire-training-source`, `dataset-docs`, `parse-acc-aha-recbox`, `extract-recommendation-cor-loe`, `flow-hbp-2025-build`, `gate1-sme-review`, `cql-clinician-signoff`, `safety-case-attest`, and `acquire-hbp-2025-source`, and is fully aligned to ADR-HTN-001 D5/D8/D9/D10/D14/D15 and to the framework spec §8/§11.

The hazard set is closed at H-01..H-10 and explicitly enumerated in §2. The mitigation-kind constraint matrix in §3.3 binds every hazard to one or more mitigations referencing CQL Libraries, CDS Hooks services, pipeline controls, or documentation artifacts; H-01 specifically requires both `PregnancyHTN` Library with the `pregnancy-denylist-order-select-hard-refuse` invariant *and* the `htn-pregnancy-denylist` CDS Hooks service with hook type `order-select` and posture `hard-refuse`. Pregnancy-specific reinforcements in §3.4 mechanically reject soft-warning postures, attending-override branches, and any hook type other than `order-select`. PCE-legacy never substitutes for PREVENT in §3.5 with redundant enforcement against `cql-clinician-signoff`'s Gate-2 enforcement, per ADR-HTN-001 D5. The closed Severity × Likelihood matrix in §4 is enforced mechanically; reviewer cannot adjust matrix outputs. The residual-risk justification block in §5 forbids declaring residual risk away when post-mitigation risk exceeds `acceptable_residual_risk_max`; remediation is upstream re-author. The signed Safety Case shape in §6 is the inline contract until `schemas/safety-case-htn.yaml` is formally drafted. The sign cycle in §7 re-runs verification at sign time, never trusts the draft's verifications, and binds the signature to a manifest-pinned TSA time-stamp. Thirteen DQA gates (`GS-A` … `GS-M`) are fail-closed at every hazard and write step.

If you want the next concrete step at the same fidelity (one at a time):

1. `schemas/safety-case-htn.yaml` — the formal Safety Case schema this skill writes against, drafted at the same fidelity as `gate1-register.yaml` / `gate2-register.yaml` / `gate3-attestation.yaml`, with closed hazard ids H-01..H-10, the closed mitigation-kind constraint matrix, the closed Severity × Likelihood matrix, the closed `acceptable_residual_risk_max` enum, the predecessor-Safety-Case chain, and post-signoff immutability rules.
2. `copyright-quote-check-acc-aha` `SKILL.md` — the per-page and document-wide envelope checker that emits the `cpr` member of the Gate-3 bundle, with publisher-contract-window awareness and figures/tables-quotable gating.
3. `phi-scrub` `SKILL.md` — the PHI scrub skill that emits the `phi` member of the Gate-3 bundle, fail-closed at zero hits, no override, with closed detector set and institutional hazard handler runbook integration.
4. `cds-hooks-package-htn` `SKILL.md` — the P22 CDS Hooks packaging skill, including the `htn-pregnancy-denylist` `order-select` hard-refuse construction and the seven-service service set.

# =============================================================================
# safety-case-htn.yaml
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Standalone schema for the Safety Case — the ISO 14971-shaped hazard log,
# risk evaluation, and residual-risk justification document produced by
# `safety-hbp` at Phase 23 (P23) and consumed as the `safe` member of the
# Gate-3 bundle by `safety-case-attest`.
#
# This file is the contract for:
#   - Safety Case identity (id, version, predecessor chain, build binding,
#     manifest binding).
#   - Intended-use scope (verbatim from manifest; age gate; in-scope and
#     out-of-scope populations; acceptable residual-risk ceiling).
#   - The closed hazard set H-01..H-10 (per framework spec §8 and ADR-HTN-001
#     D8/D9/D10/D14/D15) with per-hazard:
#       * source-anchored basis (RecommendationRecord ids + AtomicUnit ids,
#         or pipeline-control PROV evidence for pipeline-integrity hazards),
#       * closed COR/LOE inheritance (from acc-aha-grading.yaml),
#       * pre-mitigation risk under the closed Severity × Likelihood matrix,
#       * mitigations under the closed mitigation-kind constraint matrix
#         (CQL Library / CDS Hooks service / pipeline control / documentation),
#       * post-mitigation risk under the same closed matrix,
#       * residual-risk justification with explicit out-of-scope assertions.
#   - Cohort-axis attestations (no-relax-of-hard-block, PCE-legacy-never-
#     propagates, pregnancy-order-select-hard-refuse, errata-watch,
#     source-admission, ISO-14971 compliance).
#   - Cryptographic signature envelope (Ed25519 / ECDSA-P256-SHA256 over
#     RFC 8785 JCS canonical payload, RFC 3161 time-stamp).
#   - Audit log (append-only).
#   - Fixity (RFC 8785 SHA-256 of the canonical document with `fixity`
#     and `signature` excluded).
#
# Posture: caution over velocity, fidelity over coverage, residual-risk
# over claimed-risk. The closed hazard set is mechanically closed; the
# closed mitigation-kind constraint matrix mechanically binds every hazard
# to one or more verifiable mitigations; the closed Severity × Likelihood
# matrix is non-negotiable; the closed `acceptable_residual_risk_max` enum
# pins the framework's risk-acceptability ceiling at `medium` by default.
# Pregnancy hard-block must remain `order-select` hard refusal — no soft
# warning. PCE-legacy never substitutes for PREVENT.
#
# This file does NOT contain mitigation source code, CQL Library bytes,
# or CDS Hooks service descriptors. It records WHO authored WHICH safety
# evaluation at WHAT bundle hash and WHEN, with explicit verification
# pointers to upstream artifacts. Verification is performed by `safety-hbp`
# at sign time and re-verified by `safety-case-attest` as part of the
# Gate-3 bundle integrity check.
#
# Authority:
#   - ADR-HTN-001 D5 (PREVENT canonical risk function)
#   - ADR-HTN-001 D8 (pregnancy hard-block enforced at order-select)
#   - ADR-HTN-001 D9 (three non-overridable human gates; the Safety Case
#     is the safety-attestation surface that Gate 3 inherits)
#   - ADR-HTN-001 D10 (PHI fail-closed; H-08 mitigations include the PHI
#     scrub control; H-08 is the LLM-hallucinated-recommendation hazard,
#     mitigated by triple-modal consensus + Gate 1 SME signoff +
#     citation-anchor preservation)
#   - ADR-HTN-001 D14 (supersession of 2017; H-10 mitigations cite the
#     errata-watch and the no-auto-update rule)
#   - ADR-HTN-001 D15 (drift detection; H-09 / H-10 cite errata-watch)
#   - Framework spec §8 (hazards H-01..H-10)
#   - Framework spec §11 (Safety Case structure under ISO 14971)
#   - `safety-hbp` SKILL.md (the only authorized writer)
#   - Parent framework rules: `god-session`, `human-authorization`,
#     `native-ux-tools`
#
# Relationship to neighboring schemas (separate files, referenced by $ref
# or by content-hash pointer):
#   - schemas/recommendation-record-htn.yaml  (per-hazard `basis.source_anchors[]`
#                                              cite RecommendationRecord ids)
#   - schemas/atomic-unit.yaml                (per-hazard `basis.source_anchors[]`
#                                              cite AtomicUnit ids)
#   - schemas/sair.yaml                       (referenced for source anchors
#                                              the reviewer may navigate to as
#                                              context)
#   - schemas/acc-aha-grading.yaml            (closed COR/LOE enums for
#                                              `basis.cor` and `basis.loe`)
#   - schemas/gate1-register.yaml             (Gate 1 finalization is a
#                                              precondition for Safety Case
#                                              authoring; the Safety Case
#                                              cites the relevant cohort ids)
#   - schemas/gate2-register.yaml             (Gate 2 finalization is a
#                                              precondition; the Safety Case
#                                              cites Library hard-block
#                                              invariant kinds and verifying
#                                              reference test ids)
#   - schemas/gate3-attestation.yaml          (downstream consumer; the
#                                              signed Safety Case is the `safe`
