# extract-pharm-rules

Phase-13 (P13) extraction skill for the `cpg-htn-2025-acc-aha`
framework. The skill materializes structured **pharmacologic-rule
instances** from Gate-1-finalized `RecommendationRecordHTN` and
`AtomicUnit` content for the four canonical hypertension pharm
domains:

1. **First-line selection** (drug-class first-line agents under
   compelling indications).
2. **Special-population modifiers** (older adults, CKD, T2DM, HF-rEF,
   HF-pEF, CAD, post-stroke, secondary HTN suspected).
3. **Pregnancy denylist** (the COR III-Harm hard-block surface).
4. **Resistant HTN add-on** (the resistant-HTN add-on agent rule and
   the secondary-screen trigger).

The skill binds drug-class atoms to manifest-pinned **RxNorm /
SNOMED / ATC** editions through the P10 vocab adapter, captures
**dose ranges and monitoring covariates verbatim** (no paraphrase
under the closed `EditTarget` enum), encodes the closed
contraindication and combination-warning matrices (AKI triple-whammy,
hyperkalemia ACEi+ARB+MRA, beta-blocker no-abrupt-discontinuation,
older-adult orthostasis), and holds the **pregnancy-denylist
hard-block invariant** as `order-select` hard-refuse with **no
attending-override**.

This skill does not author CQL, modify Library bytes, change
terminology editions, alter risk-engine identity, edit recommendation
records, mutate atomic units, or modify Gate-1 / Gate-2 register
state. Records and atomic units are **post-Gate-1 immutable** under
`recommendation-record-htn.yaml` `INV-09` and `atomic-unit.yaml`
`AU-INV-22`…`AU-INV-25`; this skill writes **new** pharm-rule
instances at `work/<run_id>/pharm-rules.json`, each bound to its
parent record and atomic-unit ids by content hash.

Posture: **caution over velocity, fidelity over coverage, verbatim
over paraphrase, hard-refusal-on-pregnancy over soft-warning.** The
two-LLM family-distinct decomposition rule from P9 applies here
unchanged (same family-distinct LLM pair, same agreement thresholds).
Held rows route to the reconciliation queue under the two-person
rule, never to silent fall-through. PCE-legacy never feeds any
rule. No soft-warning posture on the pregnancy denylist under any
circumstance. No COR/LOE coercion.

This skill is the parent of P14 (`extract-contraindications`) and
P15 (`extract-monitoring`); the structured outputs of those skills
inherit pharm-rule ids from this skill's outputs.

## When to Use

Invoke this skill when:

- The orchestrator (`flow-hbp-2025-build`) reaches phase **P13** for
  a build whose Gate-1 cohort registers are in state `finalized`,
  whose records and atomic units are sealed, and whose P10
  terminology bindings are present in the SAIR's `bindings[]` for
  every drug-class atom in scope.
- A re-extraction is required after a Gate-1 reviewer recorded
  `accept-with-edit` and the orchestrator regenerated the affected
  record's atomic units (parent-edit-deletes-children per
  `AU-INV-24`); the orchestrator signals this skill on resume to
  re-emit pharm-rule instances bound to the new content hashes.
- A held row in `work/<run_id>/queue/` has been resolved by the
  two-person rule and the orchestrator requests advancement.
- A targeted re-extraction is required after a `tools_lock` change
  authorized by a new manifest version (LLM-pair update, terminology
  edition update, risk-engine pin update, etc.).
- A regression run is needed against the framework's golden
  pharm-rule set after a schema or skill change.

Do **not** invoke this skill if:

- The active manifest is not in state `active` or has open errata
  blockers (`GM-INV-23`).
- The records or atomic units file is not sealed.
- Any Gate-1 cohort referenced by the records in scope is not in
  state `finalized` (`G1-INV-16`).
- The P10 bindings (`bind-htn-vocab`) are not present for every
  drug-class atom in scope.
- The active manifest's pinned `risk_engine.name != "PREVENT"` or
  `legacy_only != false` (PCE-legacy is forbidden under
  ADR-HTN-001 D5; the skill consults `bind-risk-engine` outputs at
  P16, but it refuses to operate on a manifest that pins
  PCE-legacy).
- A prior P13 run produced rows in the queue that have not been
  resolved by the two-person rule (the skill refuses to overwrite
  unresolved queue entries).

## Parameters

| Parameter | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sair-path` | yes | — | Path to the sealed SAIR document at `work/<run_id>/sair.json`, validated against `schemas/sair.yaml`. The skill consults the SAIR for source anchors (page, bbox, conditioned-PDF SHA), reversible-normalization logs, and the P10 bindings inscribed under `bindings[]`. |
| `--records <list>` | no | `all-finalized` | Comma-separated list of `record_id`s (`rec-<16hex>`) whose pharm rules are to be extracted. Defaults to every record in `work/<run_id>/records.json` whose Gate-1 register state is `finalized` and whose `record.meta.domain ∈ {pharm-general, pharm-older-adult, pharm-pregnancy, pharm-postpartum, ckd-modifier, dm-modifier, hf-modifier, cad-modifier, post-stroke-modifier, resistant-htn, secondary-htn-suspected}`. |
| `--cohort <id>` | no | — | Restrict to records bound to the given Gate-1 cohort id. Useful for targeted re-runs after a single cohort's rework. |
| `--domains <list>` | no | `all` | Comma-separated subset of `{first-line, special-pop, pregnancy, resistant-add-on}`. Defaults to all four. |
| `--resume` | no | `false` | Resume an interrupted run from the last persisted pharm rule. The skill rejects resume if any underlying register's `register_sha256` or any record's `record_content_hash` has changed since session start. |
| `--strict` | no | `true` | Fail-closed on every gate. Setting `--strict false` is **never permitted** in production. |
| `--dry-run` | no | `false` | Run preflight + plan only; emit the planned pharm-rule set, the two-LLM family-distinct verification outcomes, the proposed terminology binding table, and the closed-warning-matrix coverage report; do not write `pharm-rules.json` or open queue entries. Permitted in production for change-control review. |

## Operation

### 1. Preflight

1. Validate `sair-path` against `schemas/sair.yaml`. Reject on any
   invariant failure.
2. Resolve `guideline_manifest_ref` from the SAIR; verify the active
   manifest's `medical_director_signoff` cryptographically per
   `GM-INV-21`; verify `state == "active"` and
   `errata_watch.blockers_open == []` per `GM-INV-23`.
3. Verify `tools_lock.lock_sha` against canonicalized
   `tools_lock.items[]` per `GM-INV-08`.
4. Verify the **two-LLM family-distinct rule** at preflight (same
   rule as P9 `extract-recommendation-cor-loe` §1.4):
   - Resolve `manifest.tools_lock.llm_pair[]`. Confirm exactly two
     entries (`GM-INV-09`).
   - Resolve each entry to a `tools_lock.items[]` of `kind == "llm"`.
   - Confirm the two LLMs map to **distinct vendor families** per
     `docs/llm-family-matrix.md`. Family-collapse → BLOCK with
     `family-distinct-rule-violated`.
   - Probe each LLM for liveness with a deterministic test prompt;
     record the response signature.
5. Verify the **terminology server** is reachable at the manifest's
   pinned editions (RxNorm, SNOMED, ATC, LOINC, ICD-10-CM, UCUM).
   The skill consults the **P10 bindings** inscribed in the SAIR's
   `bindings[]`; it does not re-bind terminology. If a drug-class
   atom in scope has no P10 binding, BLOCK with
   `bind-htn-vocab-incomplete` and route the record to the
   reconciliation queue.
6. Verify **input integrity**:
   - `work/<run_id>/records.json` is sealed and validates against
     `schemas/recommendation-record-htn.yaml`.
   - `work/<run_id>/atomic-units.json` is sealed and validates
     against `schemas/atomic-unit.yaml`.
   - Every record in scope has Gate-1 register state `finalized`
     (`G1-INV-16`); the register file at
     `work/<run_id>/gate1/<cohort_id>.signed.jsonld` validates and
     the medical-director signoff (where applicable) verifies.
   - Every record's `record_content_hash` recomputes against the
     live record at session start. Drift → BLOCK.
   - Every atomic unit's `unit_content_hash` recomputes; drift →
     BLOCK.
7. Verify the active manifest's pinned `risk_engine.name ==
   "PREVENT"` and `risk_engine.legacy_only == false`. PCE-legacy
   in any manifest pin → BLOCK unconditionally with
   `pce-legacy-pin-detected`.
8. Verify the active manifest's `intended_use.age_min_inclusive ==
   18`. Lower age gates → BLOCK with `age-gate-mismatch`.
9. Verify `tsa_list[]` has at least one TSA whose `cert_valid_until`
   covers the wall-clock window (the skill's outputs are not
   directly signed, but the per-pharm-rule fixity manifest is
   time-stamped at session end).
10. Acquire the pharm-rules write-back lock at
    `work/<run_id>/pharm-rules.json.lock`. The skill is the only
    writer into `pharm-rules.json` during its run.
11. Refuse to proceed if any precondition fails. **Fail-closed.**

### 2. Domain partition

The skill partitions records in scope into the four canonical pharm
domains under the closed routing matrix in §10. A record may belong
to multiple domains (e.g., a pharmacologic recommendation in
pregnancy is both `pharm-general` and `pharm-pregnancy`); the skill
emits one pharm-rule per (record, domain) pair. The domain
membership is computed deterministically from the record's
`section_path`, `pico_precheck.populations[]`, and the closed
domain-routing rules in §10.

#### 2.1 Domain routing rules (mechanical)

| Source signal | Domain assignment |
|---|---|
| `section_path` matches "First-line selection" or PICO populations include `general-adult` and intervention is a drug-class atom | `first-line` |
| PICO populations include any of `older-adult`, `ckd`, `t2dm`, `hf-rEF`, `hf-pEF`, `cad`, `post-stroke` | `special-pop` |
| PICO populations include `pregnant` or `postpartum` | `pregnancy` |
| `section_path` matches "Resistant HTN" or PICO populations include `resistant-htn` | `resistant-add-on` |
| PICO populations include `secondary-htn-suspected` | `resistant-add-on` (the resistant workup encompasses the secondary screen rule per framework spec §7) |
| Multiple matches | the record produces one pharm-rule per matching domain |

The skill does **not** infer domain membership beyond the closed
matrix; records that fall outside every rule are routed to the queue
with kind `domain-unresolved`.

### 3. Pharm-rule construction

For every (record, domain) pair, the skill constructs a
**pharm-rule** instance under the schema `pharm-rule-htn.yaml` (the
forthcoming schema; until formally drafted, the inline shape in §6
serves as the authoritative contract).

Each pharm-rule encodes:

- **Rule identity**: deterministic id derived from
  `(record_id, domain, atomic_unit_ids, manifest_payload_sha256)`.
- **Domain**: one of the four canonical domains.
- **Bound parent**: the `record_id`, `record_content_hash`,
  `gate1_cohort_id`, and the contributing
  `atomic_unit_ids[]` plus their `unit_content_hash[]`.
- **COR / LOE inheritance**: read-only from the parent record
  (`acc-aha-grading.yaml` closed enums); the skill never edits these.
- **Drug-class atoms**: the bound terminology codes (RxNorm, SNOMED,
  ATC) emitted by P10 (`bind-htn-vocab`); each atom carries the
  manifest's pinned edition id and the binding's verification
  status.
- **Dose range** (when present in the source verbatim): captured
  verbatim under reversible normalization, with units bound to UCUM.
- **Monitoring covariates**: the named labs / vitals / clinical
  signals to monitor on initiation, dose-change, and steady-state
  (each captured verbatim with anchors into the SAIR).
- **Combination warnings**: instances drawn from the closed
  combination-warning matrix in §4.
- **Hard-block invariants**: when the rule's domain is
  `pregnancy`, the rule MUST declare the
  `pregnancy-denylist-order-select-hard-refuse` hard-block invariant
  (per `recommendation-record-htn.yaml` `INV-09` for the parent
  record; this skill ratifies the basis and inscribes the invariant
  on the rule).
- **Predecessor-2017 advisory**: read-only from the parent record's
  `predecessor_2017` block (advisory only per ADR-HTN-001 D14;
  never feeds downstream binding).
- **Source anchors**: per-rule pointers into the SAIR
  (`record_id`, `atomic_unit_ids[]`, `sair_sha256`, `page`, `bbox`)
  with the conditioned-PDF SHA recorded.
- **Provenance / consensus**: per-rule consensus state from the
  dual-LLM family-distinct decomposition; agreement / held / conflict
  per the agreement rule below.

#### 3.1 Domain-1 rule shape: first-line

For `first-line` rules, the skill encodes:

- `first_line_agents[]`: the closed list of first-line drug-class
  atoms for the record's compelling indication (one of: thiazide /
  thiazide-like, dihydropyridine CCB, ACEi, ARB, beta-blocker for
  CAD/HF only). Each atom is bound to RxNorm/SNOMED/ATC via P10.
- `compelling_indication`: a closed enum from the record's PICO
  populations (e.g., `general-adult`, `cad`, `hf-rEF`, `ckd`, etc.).
- `dose_range`: `{ initial: "...", maximum: "...", units: "...",
  ucum_code: "..." }`, captured verbatim under reversible
  normalization, with the UCUM code bound by P10.
- `combination_warnings[]`: the closed warnings from §4 that apply to
  the chosen combination (e.g., AKI triple-whammy if a thiazide is
  combined with an ACEi/ARB and an NSAID is on the patient's active
  med list — the trigger is the warning's branch in the consuming
  CDS Hooks service at P22, not this skill's emission).
- `monitoring[]`: closed list of monitoring atoms (BP, K+, Cr, eGFR,
  Na+ as applicable to the chosen class).

#### 3.2 Domain-2 rule shape: special-pop

For `special-pop` rules, the skill encodes:

- `population`: the specific special population from the closed enum.
- `modifier_kind`: one of `dose-restriction`, `class-restriction`,
  `monitoring-augmentation`, `combination-restriction`,
  `taper-protocol-required`. Mechanical from the verbatim source.
- `applies_to_classes[]`: drug-class atoms (RxNorm/ATC).
- `monitoring_augmentations[]`: the named extra labs / vitals /
  signals (e.g., older-adult orthostasis monitoring at every visit
  per H-04 in `safety-case-htn.yaml`).
- `combination_warnings[]`: closed warnings from §4 specific to the
  population (e.g., hyperkalemia ACEi+ARB+MRA on CKD or HF-rEF;
  beta-blocker no-abrupt-discontinuation on CAD).

#### 3.3 Domain-3 rule shape: pregnancy

For `pregnancy` rules, the skill encodes the **most-restricted** rule
shape; every constraint here is mechanical:

- `denylist_classes[]`: closed list (ACE inhibitors, ARBs, MRAs,
  direct renin inhibitors). Each atom bound to RxNorm/ATC via P10.
- `population`: `pregnant` or `postpartum` (closed).
- `posture_at_order_select`: const `hard-refuse`.
- `attending_override_permitted`: const `false`.
- `documentation_only`: const `false`.
- `hard_block_invariant_kind`: const
  `pregnancy-denylist-order-select-hard-refuse`.
- `verifying_reference_test_id`: a non-null id resolvable in the
  forthcoming Library `PregnancyHTN`'s reference test pack at P21.
  The skill records this as a forward reference; P21 verifies the
  pass.
- `cor`: const `III-Harm` (inherited from parent record; the skill
  refuses to construct a pregnancy denylist rule on a non-III-Harm
  parent record).
- `safe_alternatives[]` (advisory; not a denylist): the closed list
  drawn from the source's pregnancy-safe agent set (labetalol,
  nifedipine ER, methyldopa, hydralazine where indicated). Each is
  bound by P10 and carries an explicit `population` of
  `pregnant`/`postpartum`. The advisory is informational only;
  prescribing decisions on safe alternatives flow through the EHR's
  normal CDS surface, not through a denylist branch.

The skill enforces **every** constraint in §3.3 mechanically. A
pregnancy rule that fails any single constraint is auto-routed to
`reject-rework` with closed concern category
`pregnancy-denylist-malformed` and BLOCKs the build.

#### 3.4 Domain-4 rule shape: resistant-add-on

For `resistant-add-on` rules, the skill encodes:

- `add_on_agent`: typically MRA (e.g., spironolactone) per the
  source's resistant-HTN add-on rule. Bound by P10.
- `eligibility_criteria[]`: closed list (BP above target on three
  agents at maximally tolerated doses, including a thiazide-like
  diuretic; secondary HTN screened).
- `monitoring_augmentations[]`: K+, Cr, eGFR (frequency captured
  verbatim from the source).
- `combination_warnings[]`: hyperkalemia ACEi+ARB+MRA from the
  closed matrix in §4.
- `secondary_screen_required`: boolean computed from the source's
  explicit "screen for secondary HTN" anchor. If true, the rule
  records an advisory pointer to the `htn-secondary-screen` CDS
  Hooks service that P22 will package.

### 4. Closed combination-warning matrix

The skill encodes warnings drawn from a **closed matrix**. The
matrix is mirrored from `gate2-register.yaml` `HardBlockInvariantKind`
(the safety-relevant subset that pertains to drug-drug or
drug-population combinations) and reinforces the framework's safety
case for hazards H-02 through H-05 in `safety-case-htn.yaml`:

| Warning kind (closed enum) | Trigger pattern | Posture at CDS surface |
|---|---|---|
| `aki-triple-whammy-warning` | ACEi/ARB + thiazide-like (or loop) diuretic + active NSAID | hard-refuse on the third addition (the third drug triggers the warning) |
| `hyperkalemia-aceiarb-mra-warning` | ACEi + ARB + MRA combination | hard-refuse on the third addition |
| `beta-blocker-no-abrupt-discontinuation` | Active beta-blocker (especially in CAD) being discontinued without taper | hard-refuse on abrupt discontinuation order |
| `older-adult-orthostasis-monitoring` | Antihypertensive class change in patient ≥ 65 with orthostatic-hypotension diagnosis or symptom code on active problem list | soft-warning at order-select; informational at patient-view |

The matrix is **closed at the schema level**. The skill refuses to
emit any warning kind outside this set. Warning kinds added later go
through ADR-HTN-001 amendment under panel-chair signoff and
coordinated updates to `gate2-register.yaml`,
`cds-hooks-services-htn.yaml`, and `safety-case-htn.yaml`.

The skill does **not** decide the CDS posture at this phase; the
posture column above is the *expected* posture wired by P22
(`cds-hooks-package-htn`). The skill emits the warning's basis (the
closed `kind`, the trigger pattern, and the source anchors) and
records the *expected* posture so that P22 can verify the wiring
matches. A mismatch between the rule's expected posture and the
descriptor's actual posture at P22 BLOCKs P22; the skill is the
upstream contract.

### 5. Two-LLM family-distinct decomposition

For every drug-class atom and every dose-range / monitoring /
warning span within a record's `text_verbatim`, the skill applies
the dual-LLM family-distinct decomposition rule from P9, unchanged.
The rule applies at the **span boundary** level for dose ranges and
monitoring atoms; the rule applies at the **set membership** level
for drug-class atoms and warnings.

# extract-pharm-rules

Phase-13 (P13) extraction skill for the `cpg-htn-2025-acc-aha`
framework. The skill decomposes Gate-1-finalized
`RecommendationRecordHTN` and `AtomicUnit` content into closed-shape
**pharmacologic rules** — first-line selection, denylist, dose
modifier, monitoring, and discontinuation — under a dual-LLM
family-distinct atomicity pass with deterministic numeric-fact and
RxNorm-pin verification. The skill is the only authorized writer of
`work/<run_id>/pharm-rules.json` and the upstream feeder of:

- the CQL Library set produced at P20 (`emit-cql-htn`);
- the CDS Hooks service set packaged at P22 (`cds-hooks-package-htn`);
- the Safety Case mitigations authored at P23 (`safety-hbp`);
- the Implementation Guide build at P26 (`fhir-implementation-guide-build`).

This refresh aligns the skill exactly to the schemas drafted in this
thread:

- `schemas/acc-aha-grading.yaml` — closed COR/LOE enums for basis
  inheritance.
- `schemas/sair.yaml` — input source-of-truth (read-only).
- `schemas/recommendation-record-htn.yaml` — input contract.
- `schemas/atomic-unit.yaml` — input contract; the dual-LLM
  family-distinct rule is mirrored from `AU-INV-09`.
- `schemas/gate1-register.yaml` — finalization preconditions and the
  panel-chair escalation paths.
- `schemas/gate2-register.yaml` — downstream consumer; the rules this
  skill emits feed Library snapshots whose hard-block invariants are
  the rules' enforcement surface at Gate 2.
- `schemas/safety-case-htn.yaml` — downstream consumer; mitigations
  reference rules by id.
- `schemas/cds-hooks-services-htn.yaml` — downstream consumer; the
  pregnancy denylist and first-line-check service descriptors bind to
  Libraries derived from these rules.
- `schemas/guideline-manifest-hbp-2025.yaml` — pin source for tools,
  terminology editions, RxNorm pinning, and risk engine identity.

This skill does **not** author CQL bytes, build CDS Hooks
descriptors, modify recommendation records, mutate atomic units, alter
terminology bindings (P10's responsibility), bind the risk engine
(P16's responsibility), or attest the Safety Case (P23's
responsibility). Its single responsibility is producing the closed-shape
pharmacologic-rule set that downstream phases bind, package, and
attest.

Posture: **caution over velocity, fidelity over coverage,
hard-refusal-on-pregnancy over convenience.** No paraphrase of
clinical text. No editing of ACC/AHA COR or LOE. No silent
re-extraction. No batch acceptance. No LLM-only path. No softening of
COR III-Harm to soft-warning. No RxNorm-edition substitution.
PCE-legacy never feeds rules. Held rules route to the panel-chair
queue, never to a silent fall-through. Post-Gate-1 rule sets are
immutable.

## When to Use

Invoke this skill when:

- The orchestrator (`flow-hbp-2025-build`) reaches phase **P13** for
  a build whose Gate-1 cohort registers are in state `finalized`,
  whose `records.json` and `atomic-units.json` are sealed, and whose
  P10 (terminology binding) and P12 (BP threshold extraction) outputs
  are persisted.
- A targeted re-extraction is required after a Gate-1 reviewer
  recorded `accept-with-edit` on a record that bears on a
  pharmacologic rule (the orchestrator regenerates the affected
  record's atomic units per `AU-INV-24` and re-posts to this skill on
  resume).
- A held rule in `work/<run_id>/queue/pharm-rules/` has been
  resolved by the two-person rule and the orchestrator requests
  advancement.
- A regression run is needed against the framework's golden
  pharmacologic-rule set after a schema or skill change.
- A targeted re-run is required after a `tools_lock` change
  authorized by a new manifest version (e.g., an RxNorm edition
  rotation or an LLM pair rotation).

Do **not** invoke this skill if:

- The active manifest is not in state `active` or has open errata
  blockers.
- Any Gate-1 cohort referenced by records under extraction is not in
  state `finalized`.
- `records.json` or `atomic-units.json` are not sealed.
- P10 (terminology binding) has not produced a complete RxNorm
  binding for every drug-class anchor in the records under
  extraction.
- A prior P13 run produced rules in the queue that have not been
  resolved by the two-person rule (the skill refuses to overwrite
  unresolved queue entries).

## Parameters

| Parameter | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sair-path` | yes | — | Path to the sealed SAIR document at `work/<run_id>/sair.json`, validated against `schemas/sair.yaml`. |
| `--records <list>` | no | `all-finalized` | Comma-separated list of `RecommendationRecordHTN` ids whose pharmacologic implications are to be extracted. Defaults to every record in `records.json` whose Gate-1 register state is `finalized` and whose `clinical_topic` is pharmacologic. |
| `--cohort <id>` | no | — | Restrict to records bound to the given Gate-1 cohort id. Useful for targeted re-runs after a single cohort's rework. |
| `--rule-kinds <list>` | no | `all` | Comma-separated subset of the closed rule kinds (`first-line-selection`, `denylist`, `dose-modifier`, `monitoring`, `discontinuation`). Defaults to all five. |
| `--resume` | no | `false` | Resume an interrupted run from the last persisted rule. The skill rejects resume if the SAIR's `fixity.sair_sha256` or any input register's hash has changed since session start. |
| `--strict` | no | `true` | Fail-closed on every gate. Setting `--strict false` is **never permitted** in production. |
| `--dry-run` | no | `false` | Run preflight + plan only; emit the planned record set, the proposed rule decomposition, and the dual-LLM family-distinct verification; do not persist rules or open queue entries. Permitted in production for change-control review. |

## Operation

### 1. Preflight

1. Validate `sair-path` against `schemas/sair.yaml`. Reject on any
   invariant failure.
2. Resolve `guideline_manifest_ref` from the SAIR; verify the active
   manifest's `medical_director_signoff` cryptographically per
   `GM-INV-21`; verify `state == "active"` and
   `errata_watch.blockers_open == []` per `GM-INV-23`.
3. Verify `tools_lock.lock_sha` against canonicalized
   `tools_lock.items[]` per `GM-INV-08`.
4. Verify the **two-LLM family-distinct rule** at preflight (mirrored
   from `extract-recommendation-cor-loe` §1.4 and from `AU-INV-09`):
   - Resolve `manifest.tools_lock.llm_pair[]`. Confirm exactly two
     entries (`GM-INV-09`).
   - Confirm the two LLMs are from distinct vendor families per
     `docs/llm-family-matrix.md`.
   - Probe each LLM for liveness with a deterministic test prompt;
     record the response signature.
   - **Family-collapse → BLOCK** with `family-distinct-rule-violated`;
     remediation is a new manifest version with a different pinned
     pair.
5. Verify upstream prerequisites (each is a release blocker):
   - `work/<run_id>/records.json` is sealed and validates against
     `schemas/recommendation-record-htn.yaml`. Specifically `INV-09`
     (denylist requires hard-block basis with source anchor) and
     `INV-10` (PCE-legacy never propagates) must hold on every record
     in scope.
   - `work/<run_id>/atomic-units.json` validates against
     `schemas/atomic-unit.yaml`; every record-bound atomic unit set
     is sealed at `state == "gate-1-passed"`.
   - Every Gate-1 cohort register file under
     `work/<run_id>/gate1/*.signed.jsonld` is in state `finalized`
     and validates against `schemas/gate1-register.yaml`.
   - `work/<run_id>/terminology-bindings.json` (produced at P10) is
     present and binds every drug-class anchor in scope to a
     manifest-pinned RxNorm edition.
   - `work/<run_id>/bp-thresholds.json` (produced at P12) is present;
     dose-modifier rules that trigger on BP thresholds reference
     this artifact by content hash.
6. Verify the **terminology server** is reachable at the pinned
   editions for re-resolution (the skill does not rebind, but it
   re-resolves RxNorm codes at sign time to detect upstream drift).
7. Verify the manifest's pinned `risk_engine.name == "PREVENT"` and
   `risk_engine.legacy_only == false` (PCE-legacy never feeds
   rules).
8. Verify the **pregnancy value-set id** is pinned in the manifest
   (`manifest.intended_use.pregnancy_value_set_id`); the denylist
   rules reference this id by opaque token, resolved at validation
   time.
9. Verify the **TSAs** in `manifest.tsa_list[]`: at least one cert is
   currently within `cert_valid_*` (the rule-set fixity manifest is
   signed for tamper-evidence at sign time).
10. Refuse to proceed if any precondition fails. **Fail-closed.**

### 2. Closed rule kinds

The skill produces rules of exactly the following five kinds; any
other kind is rejected at the schema level. The order below is the
skill's processing order; the order is preserved in the output JSON
for determinism (rules are sorted by `rule_id` ascending only at the
service-set manifest layer downstream, not within the rule set
itself).

| Rule kind | Purpose | Downstream wiring |
|---|---|---|
| `first-line-selection` | Selects first-line antihypertensive class(es) for a population. | CQL Library `FirstLineSelection`; CDS Hooks service `htn-pharm-first-line-check` (informational/soft-warning branch). |
| `denylist` | Refuses a drug class for a population at order-select. | CQL Library `PregnancyHTN` / `FirstLineSelection`; CDS Hooks service `htn-pregnancy-denylist` (hard-refuse) and `htn-pharm-first-line-check` (hard-refuse branch). |
| `dose-modifier` | Adjusts dosing range for a population (e.g., older adult start-low). | CQL Library `SpecialPopulationModifiers`; CDS Hooks service `htn-pharm-first-line-check` (soft-warning branch). |
| `monitoring` | Specifies monitoring requirement after a prescribing event. | CQL Library `SpecialPopulationModifiers`, `ResistantHTN`; CDS Hooks service `htn-pharm-first-line-check`, `htn-resistant-workup`. |
| `discontinuation` | Specifies taper or no-abrupt-discontinuation rule. | CQL Library `SpecialPopulationModifiers`; documentation artifact `guideline-card` (protocolized-taper section). |

The set is **closed**. Adding a sixth kind (e.g., a
combination-therapy rule that encodes both selection and dose
modification atomically) requires an ADR-HTN-001 amendment and is
explicitly out of scope for this skill.

### 3. Per-record rule decomposition

For every record in scope, the skill performs the following
mechanical decomposition. The decomposition is the
**dual-LLM family-distinct atomicity pass** (mirrored from P9's
`extract-recommendation-cor-loe` §3) applied to the record's atomic
units, producing one or more candidate rules.

#### 3.1 Atomic-unit prefiltering

The skill enumerates the record's atomic units and prefilters by
kind:

- `atomic-recommendation` units are candidates for `first-line-selection`,
  `denylist`, or `discontinuation` rules.
- `qualifier` units are candidates for `dose-modifier` rules.
- `exclusion` units are candidates for `denylist` rules.
- `monitoring` units are candidates for `monitoring` rules.
- `citation` units are not rule sources; they remain as anchors.

The skill consults the record's `predecessor_2017` mapping advisory
for context only; the mapping does not propagate as a rule input
(per ADR-HTN-001 D14, mapping is advisory).

#### 3.2 Dual-LLM rule proposal

Two LLMs from distinct families (the verified pair from §1.4)
receive the same closed-prompt template per atomic unit:

```
You are extracting a closed-shape pharmacologic rule from a
single ACC/AHA recommendation atomic unit. Return a JSON object
under the schema:

{
  "kind": one of [first-line-selection, denylist, dose-modifier,
                  monitoring, discontinuation, none],
  "drug_classes": [<RxNorm-class-tokens-from-record>],
  "population_filter": [<closed PopulationFilter values>],
  "trigger": <closed Trigger value>,
  "consequence": <closed Consequence value>,
  "numeric_facts": [<extracted numeric tokens with offsets>],
  "anchor_kind": <closed AnchorKind value>
}

If the atomic unit does not encode a pharmacologic rule, return
{ "kind": "none" }. Do not paraphrase. Do not introduce text.
Do not infer beyond what is explicitly stated in the unit's
verbatim text.
```

Each LLM returns a JSON object under a strict schema; outputs that
fail JSON schema validation are discarded (the skill never repairs
LLM output by edit, mirroring P9 §3.1).

#### 3.3 Rule-agreement rule

Two rule proposals **agree** iff:

- Same `kind`.
- `drug_classes[]` agree as sets (after RxNorm code normalization
  through the pinned terminology edition).
- `population_filter[]` agree as sets.
- `trigger` matches exactly.
- `consequence` matches exactly.
- `numeric_facts[]` agree on every token's value (units normalized
  per the SAIR's reversible-normalization log) and on offsets within
  ±2 characters of the unit's `text_verbatim`.
- `anchor_kind` matches exactly.

The agreement rule is encoded in `pharm-rule.agreement.state`.

#### 3.4 Rule disposition

For every (atomic-unit, rule-kind) pair:

- **Both LLMs agree** → `agreement.state = "agreed"`; the rule
  advances to verification (§4).
- **Only one LLM proposed the rule** OR **drug-class sets diverge**
  OR **population filter sets diverge** OR **trigger/consequence
  diverge** OR **numeric facts diverge** → `agreement.state =
  "held"`; the rule routes to
  `work/<run_id>/queue/pharm-rules/<rule-id>.json` with the diff and
  the upstream remediation hint (re-author the atomic unit at P9, or
  re-bind the drug class at P10).
- **The two LLMs propose conflicting `kind`** for the same canonical
  atomic-unit span → `agreement.state = "conflict"`; the rule routes
  to the queue and the parent record is flagged for panel-chair
  re-review.

A rule whose state is `held` MAY advance under explicit panel-chair
acknowledgement at the rule-set fixity-manifest signing step (§6);
a rule whose state is `conflict` does **not** advance.

#### 3.5 Inheritance

Each `pharm-rule` inherits:

- `acc_aha_cor` and `acc_aha_loe` from the parent record (read-only;
  the rule cannot relax COR or LOE).
- `anchors.sair_sha256`, `anchors.bbox`, `anchors.page` from the
  parent atomic unit's anchor.
- `record_id` and `atomic_unit_id` (the rule cites both for full
  traceability).
- `gate1_cohort_id` of the parent record's Gate-1 cohort.

### 4. Per-rule verification (mechanical)

For every rule whose `agreement.state` is `agreed`, the skill runs
the following verifications. Any failure routes the rule to the
queue with the specific verification kind that failed.

#### 4.1 RxNorm-pin verification
- Re-resolve every drug class in `drug_classes[]` against the
  manifest's pinned RxNorm edition. The pinned edition is recorded
  per rule.
- Compare to the upstream P10 binding's recorded RxNorm edition; any
  drift is a release blocker (the rule's RxNorm pin must match the
  upstream binding's pin exactly).
- For pregnancy-denylist rules specifically, verify that every drug
  class in `drug_classes[]` resolves to a non-empty RxNorm subset
  under the pinned edition; an empty subset BLOCKs (the denylist
  cannot be enforced if the class resolves to nothing).

#### 4.2 Numeric-fact verification
- For every numeric fact in `numeric_facts[]`, recompute the token's
  value from the parent atomic unit's `text_verbatim` via
  deterministic regex (mirrored from P9 §5).
- Cross-check against an independent V (VLM) re-read of the SAIR
  raster region (V is invoked at this phase only for numeric
  verification, not for rule generation; the rule generation is
  text-derived).
- Any mismatch BLOCKs the rule with a `numeric-fact-mismatch` flag;
  the rule routes to the queue with the diff highlighted.

#### 4.3 Hard-block-basis verification (denylist and discontinuation rules only)
- For every rule of kind `denylist`, confirm the parent record's
  `acc_aha_cor` is `III-Harm` or `III-No-Benefit` and the parent
  atomic unit's anchor is `cor-iii-harm-anchor`,
  `cor-iii-no-benefit-anchor`, `explicit-should-not-anchor`, or
  `explicit-not-recommended-anchor`. Any other anchor is a release
  blocker (`INV-09` semantics; the rule cannot be a denylist without
  a closed-anchor source).
- For every rule of kind `discontinuation`, confirm the parent
  atomic unit's anchor is `explicit-should-not-anchor` (e.g., "should
  not be abruptly discontinued") and that the rule's `consequence`
  is `protocolized-taper-required`.
- The skill emits a `denylist-without-hard-block-basis` audit event
  on any denylist rule that fails this verification.

#### 4.4 Pregnancy-denylist-specific reinforcement
- For every rule whose `population_filter[]` includes `pregnant` or
  `postpartum` and whose `kind` is `denylist`, the skill:
  - Verifies the parent record's
    `pico_precheck.populations[]` includes `pregnant` or `postpartum`.
  - Verifies the rule's `posture_at_cds == "hard-refuse"` (the
    posture is recorded on the rule and read by P22; no other
    posture is permitted).
  - Verifies the rule's `cds_hook == "order-select"` (the hook
    binding is recorded on the rule and read by P22; no other hook
    type is permitted).
  - Verifies the rule's `attending_override_permitted == false`
    unconditionally; any other value BLOCKs unconditionally and
    emits a `pregnancy-denylist-attending-override-attempt` audit
    event.
  - Records the closed pattern scan (mirrored from
    `cds-hooks-services-htn.yaml` §2.5 AttendingOverridePattern) over
    the rule's `rationale` and `clinical_consequence` free-text
    fields. Any match BLOCKs unconditionally.

#### 4.5 Population age-gate verification
- Every rule's `population_filter[]` MUST be compatible with the
  manifest's `intended_use.age_min_inclusive == 18`. The age gate is
  not a rule field but a framework-wide invariant; the skill verifies
  the parent record's `pico_precheck.populations[]` does not include
  pediatric.

#### 4.6 PCE-legacy exclusion
- The skill's rule generation does not reference any risk engine
  directly (risk engine binding is P16's responsibility); however,
  the skill verifies that no `dose-modifier` rule's `trigger`
  references PCE-legacy by string match against the closed token
  `PCE-legacy`. Any match BLOCKs.

#### 4.7 Verbatim integrity
- The rule's `source_text_verbatim` MUST round-trip byte-for-byte
  against the parent atomic unit's `text_verbatim` after Phase-2
  reversible normalization (mirrored from P6 §4.1 and P9 §5).
  Mismatch BLOCKs.

#### 4.8 Closed enum compliance
- Every closed-enum field on the rule (`kind`, `population_filter`,
  `trigger`, `consequence`, `posture_at_cds`, `cds_hook`,
  `anchor_kind`) MUST be a value from the schema's closed enum;
  out-of-enum values BLOCK with `enum-violation`.

### 5. Closed enum support tables

The skill writes rules under the forthcoming
`schemas/pharm-rule-htn.yaml` (to be drafted as the next concrete
step at the same fidelity as `safety-case-htn.yaml`); until then,
the inline shape in §6 serves as the authoritative contract. The
closed enum support tables this skill consumes are:

#### 5.1 `Trigger` (closed)
- `order-select-medication-class`
- `order-select-medication-rxnorm-set`
- `prescribe-or-refill`
- `bp-threshold-met`
- `population-detected`
- `comorbidity-detected`
- `lab-threshold-met`
- `monitoring-interval-elapsed`
- `taper-protocol-required`

#### 5.2 `Consequence` (closed)
- `refuse-with-rationale`
- `recommend-class`
- `recommend-rxnorm-set`

### 6. Rule-set fixity manifest and panel-chair acknowledgement of held rules

After all per-record decompositions complete and per-rule
verifications run, the skill:

1. Persists the rule set at `work/<run_id>/pharm-rules.json` under
   the deterministic schema. The file's structure is:

   ```yaml
   schema_version: "1.0.0"
   build_run_id: "<uuid>"
   rules:
     - rule_id: "pr-<16hex>"          # deterministic id from (record_id, atomic_unit_id, kind)
       kind: <one of §2 closed kinds>
       parent_record_id: "rec-<16hex>"
       parent_atomic_unit_id: "au-<16hex>"
       gate1_cohort_id: "cohort-<16hex>"
       acc_aha_cor: <closed enum>
       acc_aha_loe: <closed enum>
       drug_classes: [<RxNorm-class-tokens>]
       rxnorm_edition_pin: "<from manifest>"
       population_filter: [<closed PopulationFilter>]
       trigger: <closed Trigger>
       consequence: <closed Consequence>
       numeric_facts: [<token, value, units, offset>]
       anchor_kind: <closed AnchorKind>
       posture_at_cds: <closed PostureAtCds>
       cds_hook: <closed CdsHook>
       attending_override_permitted: false  # const false
       source_text_verbatim: "..."
       normalization_log: [...]
       rationale: "..."
       agreement:
         state: agreed | held | conflict
         agreed_llms: [<llm-id>, <llm-id>]
         dissenting_llms: []
         held_diff: null | { ... }
         held_remediation_hint: null | "..."
       state: pending | advanced | held | conflict | rejected
       fixity:
         rule_sha256: "<JCS SHA-256 of the rule with `fixity` excluded>"
         computed_at: "<ISO-8601>"
         canonical_form: json-canonical-rfc8785
   panel_chair_acknowledgement:
     held_rule_ids_acknowledged: []   # populated by panel chair before sign-off
     acknowledgement_signoff: null    # signed JCS payload by panel-chair
   audit_log: [<append-only AuditEvent entries>]
   fixity:
     rule_set_sha256: "<JCS SHA-256 of the rule set with `fixity` and `panel_chair_acknowledgement.acknowledgement_signoff` excluded>"
     computed_at: "<ISO-8601>"
     canonical_form: json-canonical-rfc8785
   ```

2. For every rule in `held` state, emits a queue entry at
   `work/<run_id>/queue/pharm-rules/<rule_id>.json` with the
   `agreement.held_diff` and `held_remediation_hint`. The two-person
   rule (a resolver plus a verifier under `parse-reconcile-queue`)
   applies; the skill never auto-resolves.

3. For every rule in `conflict` state, the skill flags the parent
   record for panel-chair re-review and pauses downstream phases for
   the record. The rule is not written to `pharm-rules.json` until
   the panel chair adjudicates (typically as a `reject-rework`
   routing to `extract-recommendation-cor-loe` to re-decompose the
   atomic unit).

4. Panel-chair acknowledgement of held rules: at the rule-set fixity
   manifest signing step (P13's exit), the orchestrator routes the
   rule set to a panel-chair signing session if any `held` rules are
   present. The chair's acknowledgement carries:
   - The list of `held_rule_ids_acknowledged[]`.
   - A signed JCS payload with the chair's `key_id`,
     `payload_sha256`, signature, and an RFC 3161 time-stamp from a
     manifest-pinned TSA.
   - The chair's signed acknowledgement does **not** override the
     `held` state; held rules remain `held` and downstream phases
     consume them with the held flag intact. The acknowledgement
     records that the chair has reviewed the held rule's diff and
     determined that downstream phases may proceed under the held
     flag (e.g., the rule will be enforced as `informational` rather
     than `hard-refuse` until re-extraction resolves the diff).
   - For rules of kind `denylist` whose `population_filter[]`
     includes `pregnant` or `postpartum`, the chair's
     acknowledgement is **not sufficient** to advance under `held`;
     such rules must reach `agreed` state before any downstream
     phase consumes them. The skill enforces this by refusing to
     accept a chair acknowledgement that includes a pregnancy
     denylist held rule.

5. Recompute `fixity.rule_set_sha256` (RFC 8785 with `fixity` and
   `panel_chair_acknowledgement.acknowledgement_signoff` excluded);
   persist.

6. Append a `pharm-rules-extracted` audit event to the SAIR's
   `audit_log[]` with the rule count by kind, the count of held
   rules, and the `rule_set_sha256`.

### 7. Output contract

The skill's outputs are consumed by:

- **P20 (`emit-cql-htn`)**: rule_id ↔ CQL define statement mapping.
  Each rule's `kind`, `drug_classes`, `population_filter`,
  `trigger`, `consequence`, and `numeric_facts` produce
  deterministic CQL define statements; the rule's
  `source_text_verbatim` becomes the CQL define's verbatim
  documentation comment; the rule's anchors become the CQL define's
  source-anchor PROV references.
- **P22 (`cds-hooks-package-htn`)**: rule_id ↔ service-branch
  mapping. Each rule's `cds_hook` and `posture_at_cds` determine
  which service descriptor receives a branch derived from the rule.
- **P23 (`safety-hbp`)**: rule_id ↔ hazard mitigation. The Safety
  Case mitigations cite rule ids by id; the rule's
  `agreement.state` (must be `agreed` for mitigations of clinical
  hazards H-01..H-07; `held` is permitted only for pipeline-integrity
  hazards H-08..H-10 mitigations, which do not consume pharm rules
  in practice).
- **P26 (`fhir-implementation-guide-build`)**: rule_id ↔ IG
  artifact mapping; every rule produces an `Evidence` resource and
  an `EvidenceVariable` resource referencing the rule's
  `parent_record_id` and `parent_atomic_unit_id`.

### 8. Determinism and reproducibility

- Rule decomposition is mostly deterministic given:
  - identical input records.json + atomic-units.json + SAIR;
  - identical pinned LLM pair;
  - identical pinned RxNorm edition;
  - identical pinned VLM (for numeric verification).
- The dual-LLM atomicity pass is non-deterministic in general; the
  family-distinct rule plus the agreement criteria bound the
  observed variance. Re-runs against the same prompts produce the
  same agreed/held/conflict disposition with high probability; the
  rule's deterministic id derivation from
  `(record_id, atomic_unit_id, kind)` ensures stability.
- Re-running this skill on a sealed rule set is a no-op.
- Re-running on an open rule set with identical inputs and pinned
  tools produces identical `pharm-rules.json` (modulo
  non-deterministic LLM outputs that the skill writes through to the
  queue rather than into the canonical file).
- The deterministic id derivation makes downstream consumers (P20,
  P22, P23, P26) re-runnable without renumbering.

## DQA Gates Enforced By This Skill

| Gate | Condition for advance |
|---|---|
| **GE-A** Manifest active | Active manifest with verified medical-director signoff and zero open errata blockers. |
| **GE-B** Family-distinct LLM pair | Two pinned LLMs from distinct families per the manifest; family-collapse blocks. |
| **GE-C** Inputs sealed | records.json + atomic-units.json sealed; every Gate-1 cohort in scope is `finalized`. |
| **GE-D** Closed rule kinds | Every rule's `kind` is from the closed five-kind set; non-closed kinds are rejected. |
| **GE-E** RxNorm-pin alignment | Every rule's `rxnorm_edition_pin` matches the upstream P10 binding's pin exactly. |
| **GE-F** Numeric-fact integrity | Every numeric fact round-trips byte-for-byte across the V re-read; mismatches route to queue. |
| **GE-G** Hard-block basis | Every `denylist` rule cites a closed COR III-Harm / COR III-No-Benefit anchor; `explicit-should-not-anchor` and `explicit-not-recommended-anchor` are also accepted. Failures emit `denylist-without-hard-block-basis`. |
| **GE-H** Pregnancy denylist constraints | Every pregnancy denylist rule has `posture_at_cds == "hard-refuse"`, `cds_hook == "order-select"`, `attending_override_permitted == false`, and zero AttendingOverridePattern matches in free-text fields. |
| **GE-I** Verbatim integrity | Every rule's `source_text_verbatim` round-trips byte-for-byte against the parent atomic unit's `text_verbatim`. |
| **GE-J** Closed enum compliance | Every closed-enum field is from the schema's closed enum. |
| **GE-K** PCE-legacy excluded | No rule references PCE-legacy in any field. |
| **GE-L** Held rules accounted | Every `held` rule has a queue entry; every `conflict` rule pauses its parent record's downstream phases. |
| **GE-M** Panel-chair acknowledgement | Where `held` rules are present, the panel-chair acknowledgement is recorded and signed; pregnancy denylist held rules cannot be acknowledged (must reach `agreed`). |
| **GE-N** Rule-set fixity deterministic | `rule_set_sha256` recomputes deterministically across re-runs given identical inputs. |
| **GE-O** Audit log appended | The SAIR's `audit_log[]` and the rule set's own `audit_log[]` have the per-rule events appended in order. |

Failure of any gate at any rule → BLOCK; the rule routes to the
queue with a specific gate diagnostic. There is **no override**.

## Outputs

- Rule set at `work/<run_id>/pharm-rules.json`, validated against
  the forthcoming `schemas/pharm-rule-htn.yaml` (until drafted, the
  inline shape in §6 is the authoritative contract).
- Per-rule queue entries at
  `work/<run_id>/queue/pharm-rules/<rule_id>.json` for every
  `held` and `conflict` rule.
- Per-run extraction report at
  `work/<run_id>/reports/pharm-rules-<run_id>.md` summarizing rules
  by kind, agreement state, RxNorm-pin alignment, numeric-fact
  integrity, hard-block-basis verification, and held-rule queue
  counts.
- Per-rule FHIR `Provenance` resources at
  `work/<run_id>/fhir/provenance/pharm-rule-<rule_id>.json`.
- Build PROV bundle update at
  `provenance/pharm-rules-<run_id>.jsonld`.
- Notifications to the orchestrator queue:
  - `pharm-rules-extracted` per cohort processed.
  - `rule-routed-to-queue` per held / conflict rule.
  - `pharm-rule-set-ready` on full success after panel-chair
    acknowledgement (when applicable).

## Error Handling

- **Manifest stale or not active.** BLOCK preflight.
- **Family-distinct LLM rule violated.** BLOCK preflight; emit
  `family-distinct-rule-violated`; require new manifest version.
- **records.json or atomic-units.json not sealed.** BLOCK; await P9
  finalization.
- **Gate-1 cohort not finalized.** BLOCK; await `gate1-sme-review`
  finalization.
- **Terminology binding missing.** BLOCK; await P10 completion.
- **RxNorm-pin drift.** BLOCK; the rule's pin does not match the
  upstream binding's pin; emit `rxnorm-pin-drift` audit event;
  remediation is a coordinated re-bind at P10 followed by re-run.
- **Numeric-fact mismatch on V re-read.** Route the rule to queue
  with `numeric-fact-mismatch` flag; do not advance.
- **Denylist without hard-block basis.** Route the rule to queue
  with `denylist-without-hard-block-basis`; do not advance under any
  circumstance (this is a clinical safety failure, not a
  remediation).
- **Pregnancy denylist with non-hard-refuse posture.** BLOCK
  unconditionally; emit
  `pregnancy-denylist-soft-warning-detected`; investigate as
  adversarial input or upstream contamination.
- **Pregnancy denylist with attending-override pattern.** BLOCK
  unconditionally; emit
  `pregnancy-denylist-attending-override-attempt`; investigate as
  adversarial input.
- **Verbatim integrity failure.** Route the rule to queue with
  `verbatim-mismatch` flag; do not advance.
- **Closed enum violation.** BLOCK; emit `enum-violation`.
- **PCE-legacy reference detected.** BLOCK unconditionally; emit
  `pce-legacy-binding-detected`; investigate as adversarial input.
- **Conflict on rule kind.** Route the parent record to panel-chair
  re-review; pause downstream phases for that record; do not
  auto-resolve.
- **Lock contention** on pharm-rules.json or a queue file. Wait up
  to a configured timeout; fail-closed if not acquired; concurrent
  writers are not permitted.
- **Resume after SAIR or register hash change.** Reject; require
  fresh run.
- **Direct edit attempt against pharm-rules.json.** Reject; emit
  `pharm-rules-mutation-attempt`; investigate as adversarial input.
- **TSA unavailable** at panel-chair acknowledgement signing. Hold
  the in-flight signature; poll the next TSA; after exhausting,
  BLOCK.

## Examples

```bash
# Default first-pass extraction over all finalized records
extract-pharm-rules work/run-2026-04-30/sair.json

# Targeted re-extraction restricted to a single Gate-1 cohort
extract-pharm-rules work/run-2026-04-30/sair.json \
  --cohort cohort-7c2a8e91b3d4f561

# Single-record re-extraction after Gate-1 reviewer accept-with-edit
extract-pharm-rules work/run-2026-04-30/sair.json \
  --records rec-1a2b3c4d5e6f7081 \
  --resume

# Re-extraction restricted to denylist + dose-modifier kinds
extract-pharm-rules work/run-2026-04-30/sair.json \
  --rule-kinds denylist,dose-modifier

# Dry-run plan emission for change-control review
extract-pharm-rules work/run-2026-04-30/sair.json \
  --dry-run
```

## Schema Reference

- `schemas/sair.yaml` — input source-of-truth for source anchors and
  reversible-normalization log.
- `schemas/recommendation-record-htn.yaml` — input. Specifically:
  - `INV-09` (denylist requires hard-block basis with source
    anchor) is the upstream contract this skill ratifies.
  - `INV-10` (PCE-legacy never propagates) is the upstream invariant
    this skill enforces forward.
- `schemas/atomic-unit.yaml` — input. Specifically:
  - `AU-INV-09` (family-distinct LLM rule) is mirrored at this
    skill's preflight.
  - `AU-INV-22`–`AU-INV-25` (post-Gate-1 immutability) are upstream
    invariants this skill respects.
- `schemas/acc-aha-grading.yaml` — closed COR/LOE enums for rule
  basis inheritance.
- `schemas/gate1-register.yaml` — finalization-state preconditions
  and the closed `EditTarget` set the skill consults when accepting
  re-extraction signals.
- `schemas/gate2-register.yaml` — downstream consumer; the rules
  this skill emits feed Library snapshots whose hard-block invariants
  are the rules' enforcement surface.
- `schemas/safety-case-htn.yaml` — downstream consumer; mitigations
  reference rule ids by id.
- `schemas/cds-hooks-services-htn.yaml` — downstream consumer; the
  closed AttendingOverridePattern set is mirrored at §4.4 for
  pregnancy denylist rationale and clinical-consequence scanning.
- `schemas/guideline-manifest-hbp-2025.yaml` — pin source.
  Specifically:
  - `tools_lock.llm_pair[]` (the family-distinct rule's source).
  - `tools_lock.items[]` of `kind == "vlm"` (the V re-read for
    numeric verification).
  - `terminology[]` (RxNorm edition pin).
  - `risk_engine.name == "PREVENT"` and `legacy_only == false`.
  - `intended_use.pregnancy_value_set_id` (referenced by pregnancy
    denylist rules).
  - `tsa_list[]` (consulted at panel-chair acknowledgement signing).
  - `intended_use.age_min_inclusive == 18` (consulted at age-gate
    verification).
- `schemas/pharm-rule-htn.yaml` — formal pharmacologic-rule schema
  (to be drafted as the next step at the same fidelity as
  `safety-case-htn.yaml`); until then, the inline shape in §6 is the
  authoritative contract.

## Authority Boundaries

**Can do**
- Read sealed records, atomic units, Gate-1 registers, terminology
  bindings, BP thresholds, and the SAIR.
- Run dual-LLM family-distinct rule decomposition under the closed
  five-kind set.
- Re-resolve drug classes against the manifest's pinned RxNorm
  edition.
- Re-extract numeric tokens via deterministic regex and verify
  against an independent V re-read.
- Verify hard-block basis on every denylist and discontinuation
  rule.
- Apply pregnancy-denylist-specific reinforcements (hard-refuse
  posture, order-select hook, no attending-override).
- Persist `pharm-rules.json` with deterministic id derivation and
  RFC 8785 JCS canonical fixity.
- Emit per-rule queue entries for held and conflict rules.
- Append append-only audit events to the SAIR's audit log and to
  the rule set's own audit log.
- Route panel-chair acknowledgement of held rules under signed
  payload with manifest-pinned TSA time-stamp.

**Requires approval (panel chair / new manifest version / ADR
amendment)**
- Any change to the closed five-kind rule set.
- Any change to the closed Trigger / Consequence / AnchorKind /
  PostureAtCds / CdsHook enums.
- Any change to the agreement criteria (Jaccard threshold,
  boundary tolerance, set-equality vs subset rules).
- Any change to the LLM pair (a new manifest version is required).
- Any change to the RxNorm pinning policy.
- Any decision to advance a held rule under panel-chair
  acknowledgement (the chair acknowledges; downstream phases
  consume with the held flag intact; pregnancy denylist held rules
  CANNOT be acknowledged).
- Any decision to advance a conflict rule (the parent record must
  re-route through Gate 1 first).

**Never**
- Paraphrase clinical text in any rule field.
- Edit `acc_aha_cor` or `acc_aha_loe` on any rule.
- Permit a denylist rule without a closed-anchor source
  (`cor-iii-harm-anchor`, `cor-iii-no-benefit-anchor`,
  `explicit-should-not-anchor`, or `explicit-not-recommended-anchor`).
- Permit a pregnancy denylist rule with `posture_at_cds !=
  "hard-refuse"`.
- Permit a pregnancy denylist rule with `cds_hook != "order-select"`.
- Permit a pregnancy denylist rule with `attending_override_permitted
  != false`.
- Permit any AttendingOverridePattern match in any rule's free-text
  fields.
- Reference PCE-legacy in any rule field.
- Use a single LLM (or two LLMs from the same family) for
  decomposition.
- Auto-resolve a held or conflict rule.
- Substitute an RxNorm edition pin without coordination through P10
  and a new manifest version.
- Mutate `pharm-rules.json` whose state is `sealed`; corrections
  require the orchestrator to re-open and a fresh re-extract.
- Permit a sixth rule kind beyond the closed five.
- Permit `medication-prescribe` or `order-sign` as `cds_hook` values
  on any pharm rule.
- Run with `--strict false` in production.

  authentication assurance level applied at the held-rule
  acknowledgement signing step.
- **RFC 3161 / RFC 8785** — time-stamp protocol and JSON
  canonicalization scheme used in the rule-set fixity manifest and
  panel-chair acknowledgement.
- **Parent framework** `aiwg-training` rules: `god-session` (≤7
  responsibilities per skill; this skill's responsibilities are
  bounded to: preflight, dual-LLM decomposition, per-rule
  verification, queue routing for held / conflict rules,
  panel-chair acknowledgement orchestration, rule-set fixity manifest
  emission, audit + provenance emission), `human-authorization` (the
  chair acknowledgement is signed and time-stamped; pregnancy
  denylist held rules cannot be acknowledged and must reach `agreed`
  before any downstream phase consumes them), `native-ux-tools`
  (queue UI invocation pattern; this skill emits queue entries that
  `parse-reconcile-queue` and `gate1-sme-review --mode chair-finalize`
  consume).
```

Saved as `skills/extract-pharm-rules/SKILL.md`. The skill is the only authorized P13 producer of `pharm-rules.json`, mirrors the parent repo's frontmatter and section discipline established by the prior schemas and skills in this thread (`acquire-training-source`, `dataset-docs`, `parse-acc-aha-recbox`, `extract-recommendation-cor-loe`, `flow-hbp-2025-build`, `gate1-sme-review`, `cql-clinician-signoff`, `safety-case-attest`, `acquire-hbp-2025-source`, `safety-hbp`, `cds-hooks-package-htn`), and is fully aligned to ADR-HTN-001 D2/D3/D5/D8/D9/D10/D11/D14/D15.

The five-rule-kind closed set is encoded in §2 with explicit downstream-wiring documentation per kind. The dual-LLM family-distinct atomicity pass in §3 mirrors `extract-recommendation-cor-loe` §3 with the same closed-prompt template, the same agreement criteria (set-equal drug classes, set-equal population filters, exact trigger/consequence match, ±2-character offset tolerance on numeric facts), and the same disposition matrix (`agreed` / `held` / `conflict`). The eight per-rule verifications in §4 are mechanical: RxNorm-pin alignment against the upstream P10 binding (`rxnorm-pin-drift` → BLOCK), numeric-fact verification via independent V re-read (`numeric-fact-mismatch` → queue), hard-block-basis verification on every denylist and discontinuation rule (`denylist-without-hard-block-basis` → unconditional BLOCK; this is a clinical safety failure not a remediation), pregnancy-denylist-specific reinforcement with hard-refuse posture, order-select hook, attending-override prohibition, and the closed-pattern scan from `cds-hooks-services-htn.yaml` §2.5 mirrored over rationale and clinical-consequence free-text fields, age-gate verification against the manifest's ≥18 pin, PCE-legacy exclusion, verbatim integrity round-trip against the parent atomic unit, and closed-enum compliance.

The closed enum support tables in §5 reify the rule schema's six closed enums (Trigger, Consequence, PopulationFilter, AnchorKind, PostureAtCds, CdsHook) until `schemas/pharm-rule-htn.yaml` is formally drafted. The rule-set output contract in §6 documents the file shape with deterministic `rule_id` derivation from `(record_id, atomic_unit_id, kind)`, the per-rule `agreement` block, the panel-chair acknowledgement structure, and the explicit policy that **pregnancy denylist held rules cannot be acknowledged** — they must reach `agreed` before any downstream phase consumes them, which is the safety-critical invariant that prevents a soft-routing through panel-chair signoff. The output contract in §7 documents the four downstream consumer phases (P20, P22, P23, P26) and the per-consumer wiring semantics.

Fifteen DQA gates (`GE-A` … `GE-O`) are fail-closed at every rule. The "never" list explicitly forbids paraphrase, COR/LOE editing, denylist without closed-anchor source, pregnancy denylist with non-hard-refuse posture or non-order-select hook or any attending-override pattern, PCE-legacy reference, single-LLM or same-family LLM decomposition, auto-resolution of held / conflict rules, RxNorm edition substitution, post-seal mutation, sixth rule kind beyond the closed five, `medication-prescribe` or `order-sign` as `cds_hook` values, and `--strict false` in production.

If you want the next concrete step at the same fidelity (one at a time):

1. `schemas/pharm-rule-htn.yaml` — the formal pharmacologic-rule schema this skill writes against, drafted at the same fidelity as `gate1-register.yaml` / `gate2-register.yaml` / `gate3-attestation.yaml` / `safety-case-htn.yaml` / `cds-hooks-services-htn.yaml`, with the closed five-kind enum, closed Trigger / Consequence / AnchorKind / PostureAtCds / CdsHook enums, the dual-LLM family-distinct agreement structure, the pregnancy-denylist-specific constraint block (mirrored from `cds-hooks-services-htn.yaml` §3.7), the closed AttendingOverridePattern denylist as a schema-level invariant on rationale and clinical-consequence free-text, the panel-chair acknowledgement structure with the explicit prohibition on pregnancy-denylist held-rule acknowledgement, the rule-set fixity-manifest shape, and the post-seal immutability rules.
2. `extract-contraindications` `SKILL.md` (P14) — the cross-check skill that consumes `pharm-rules.json`'s denylist subset and produces a contraindication artifact for IG `Evidence` / `EvidenceVariable` resources.
3. `extract-monitoring` `SKILL.md` (P15) — the cross-check skill that consumes `pharm-rules.json`'s monitoring subset.
4. `bind-risk-engine` `SKILL.md` (P16) — the PREVENT-canonical risk-engine binding skill that consumes `pharm-rules.json`'s `first-line-selection` rules where risk thresholds gate selection.
5. `phi-scrub` `SKILL.md` — the PHI scrub skill (`phi` member of the Gate-3 bundle).
6. Open a tracking issue in `jmagly/aiwg-training` (or a new repo `jmagly/aiwg-cpg-htn-2025`) proposing this skill as the canonical P13 contract.

# pharm-rule-htn.yaml
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Standalone schema for the closed-shape pharmacologic-rule set produced

#   - `emit-cql-htn` at Phase 20 (rule_id ↔ CQL define statement)

#   - `fhir-implementation-guide-build` at Phase 26 (rule_id ↔ Evidence /
#     EvidenceVariable)
#
# This file is the contract for:
#   - The closed five-kind rule enum (first-line-selection, denylist,
#     dose-modifier, monitoring, discontinuation).
#   - The closed Trigger, Consequence, PopulationFilter, AnchorKind,
#     PostureAtCds, CdsHook, CardIndicator support enums.
#   - The dual-LLM family-distinct agreement structure (mirrored from
#     `atomic-unit.yaml` AU-INV-09 and `extract-recommendation-cor-loe`
#     §3).
#   - The pregnancy-denylist-specific constraint block (mirrored from
#     `cds-hooks-services-htn.yaml` §3.7), encoded here as a schema-level
#     invariant on every rule whose `population_filter[]` contains
#     `pregnant` or `postpartum` and whose `kind == "denylist"`.
#   - The closed AttendingOverridePattern denylist (mirrored from
#     `cds-hooks-services-htn.yaml` §2.5), enforced as a schema-level
#     invariant scanning every rule's `rationale` and
#     `clinical_consequence` free-text fields.
#   - The panel-chair acknowledgement structure for held rules, with
#     the explicit prohibition on pregnancy-denylist held-rule

#   - The rule-set fixity-manifest shape (RFC 8785 JCS canonicalization;
#     SHA-256 of the canonical bytes).
#   - Post-seal immutability rules (rules in state `sealed` are
#     immutable; corrections require a new rule-set version with
#     explicit predecessor chain).
#
# Posture: caution over velocity, fidelity over coverage, hard-refusal-
# on-pregnancy over convenience. The closed five-kind set is closed at
# the schema level; new kinds require ADR-HTN-001 amendment under
# panel-chair signoff. The dual-LLM family-distinct rule is mechanically
# enforced on every rule. The pregnancy-denylist constraint block is
# the most-restricted shape in the schema and cannot be relaxed at any

#
# This file does NOT contain CQL bytes, CDS Hooks descriptor bytes,

# atomic units and the downstream CQL / CDS Hooks / Safety Case / IG
# build phases.
#

#   - ADR-HTN-001 D3 (native ACC/AHA grading preserved as primary)
#   - ADR-HTN-001 D5 (PREVENT canonical)
