# fhir-implementation-guide-build

Phase-26 (P26) Implementation Guide build skill for the
`cpg-htn-2025-acc-aha` framework. The skill **composes** the
published FHIR R5 IG package from Gate-3-attested upstream artifacts
under the manifest-pinned FHIR R5 profile and the framework's
`cpg-htn-*` StructureDefinition extensions, **validates** every
resource at the closed profile set, **computes** deterministic
per-resource and per-package SHAs under FHIR-R5 JCS canonicalization,
and **emits** the IG package consumed at P28 (publication
versioning).

This skill is a **composer**. It does not author records, atomic
units, pharm rules, contraindications, monitoring artifacts, the
Safety Case, the Guideline Card, CQL Library bytes, CDS Hooks
descriptor bytes, or terminology bindings; those are all upstream
producers. It does not sign artifacts; signing is performed at the
gate-specific signing skills (Gate 1 / Gate 2 / Gate 3) and at P28
release. Its responsibility is the **deterministic, validated,
profile-conformant FHIR R5 IG composition** that materializes the
framework's full evidence chain into a single shippable IG package
that the EHR-side CDS Hooks runtime, the FHIR R5 IG Publisher, and
downstream republishers consume.

This skill aligns to every schema and skill drafted in this thread:

- `schemas/acc-aha-grading.yaml` — closed COR/LOE enums for
  certainty mapping.
- `schemas/sair.yaml` — input source-of-truth (read-only).
- `schemas/recommendation-record-htn.yaml` — input.
- `schemas/atomic-unit.yaml` — input.
- `schemas/gate1-register.yaml` — input.
- `schemas/gate2-register.yaml` — input.
- `schemas/gate3-attestation.yaml` — input. The Gate-3 attestation
  is the gating precondition; without it, this skill refuses to
  build.
- `schemas/safety-case-htn.yaml` — input.
- `schemas/cds-hooks-services-htn.yaml` — input.
- `schemas/pharm-rule-htn.yaml` — input.
- `schemas/contraindication-artifact-htn.yaml` — input. The
  artifact's `pass`-state rows' `materialized.evidence_id` and
  `evidence_variable_id` are the canonical FHIR resource ids
  composed into the IG.
- `schemas/guideline-manifest-hbp-2025.yaml` — pin source.

This skill also aligns to the orchestrator (`flow-hbp-2025-build`),
which is the only authorized invoker in production, and to the
Phase-26 placement explicitly recorded in the orchestrator's closed
twenty-eight-phase set.

Posture: **caution over velocity, fidelity over coverage,
hard-refusal-on-pregnancy over convenience.** No paraphrase. No
editing of ACC/AHA COR or LOE. No coercion of FHIR resources to
non-conformant shapes. No silent re-runs. PCE-legacy never appears
in any FHIR resource, profile, value set, or extension. Pregnancy
denylist FHIR resources carry the order-select hard-refuse posture
by construction. Post-Gate-3 IG packages are immutable; corrections
require a new manifest version and a new build, with the prior IG
package retained immutably for audit.

## When to Use

Invoke this skill when:

- The orchestrator (`flow-hbp-2025-build`) reaches phase **P26** for
  a build whose **Gate 3 attestation is verified** (state `signed`,
  signature verifies under the medical director's public key, time-
  stamp verifies against a manifest-pinned TSA, every cohort-axis
  attestation flag is `true`).
- A targeted re-build is required after a non-content errata
  closure that requires re-publishing the IG (e.g., a TSA rotation
  that updates the timestamp surface but does not invalidate prior
  signatures; a forthcoming companion schema becomes available and
  is added to the pinned profile set).
- A regression run is needed against the framework's golden IG set
  after a schema or skill change.
- A `--mode verify` re-check is needed by `guideline-version` (P28)
  before publication versioning.

Do **not** invoke this skill if:

- The active manifest is not in state `active` or has open errata
  blockers (`GM-INV-23`).
- The Gate-3 attestation is not in state `signed` and verifying.
- Any contributing artifact's recorded SHA does not recompute
  against the live artifact at session start.
- The pinned FHIR R5 profile is not present in the manifest's
  `tools_lock.items[]` of `kind == "fhir-r5-profile"`.
- The IG Publisher tooling pin (`tools_lock.items[]` of `kind ==
  "fhir-ig-publisher"`) is not verifying against its recorded SHA.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `gate3-attestation-path` | yes | — | Path to the signed Gate-3 attestation at `work/<run_id>/gate3-attestation.signed.jsonld`, validated against `schemas/gate3-attestation.yaml`. The skill resolves the build pin from the attestation. |
| `--profile-pin <id>` | no | (from manifest) | Override the FHIR R5 profile pin id; used only for change-control review under `--dry-run`. The pin is otherwise resolved from `manifest.tools_lock.items[]`. |
| `--mode <build\|verify\|verify+build>` | no | `verify+build` | `build` composes the IG package from upstream artifacts and writes the IG; `verify` recomputes per-resource and per-package SHAs against on-disk IG outputs and reports drift; `verify+build` builds missing resources and verifies all. |
| `--strict` | no | `true` | Fail-closed on every gate. Setting `--strict false` is **never permitted** in production. |
| `--resume` | no | `false` | Resume an interrupted run from the last persisted resource. The skill rejects resume if any contributing artifact's recorded SHA has changed since session start, or if the Gate-3 attestation's `payload_sha256` has changed. |
| `--dry-run` | no | `false` | Run preflight + plan only; emit the planned resource composition tree, the validated profile bindings, and the predicted per-resource SHA set; do not write the IG package. Permitted in production for change-control review. |

## Operation

### 1. Preflight

1. Validate `gate3-attestation-path` against
   `schemas/gate3-attestation.yaml`. Refuse on any invariant failure.
2. Verify the attestation's signature cryptographically against the
   medical director's `public_key` recorded in the attestation.
   Refuse on signature failure.
3. Verify the attestation's time-stamp against the manifest-pinned
   TSA per `GM-INV-23` and `safety-case-attest`'s recorded
   `tsa_cert_fingerprint_sha256`. Refuse on TSA verification
   failure.
4. Verify every cohort-axis attestation flag in the attestation is
   `true` (mirrors `SC-INV-14` semantics):
   - iso14971-compliance-attested
   - no-relax-of-hard-block-attested
   - pce-legacy-never-propagates-attested
   - pregnancy-order-select-hardrefuse-attested
   - errata-watch-attested
   - source-admission-attested
   - mitigation-verification-attested
   - acceptable-residual-risk-within-ceiling-attested
   Any `false` BLOCKs.
5. Resolve `guideline_manifest_ref` from the attestation's bundled
   manifest pin; verify the active manifest's
   `medical_director_signoff` cryptographically per `GM-INV-21`;
   verify `state == "active"` and
   `errata_watch.blockers_open == []` per `GM-INV-23`.
6. Verify `tools_lock.lock_sha` against canonicalized
   `tools_lock.items[]` per `GM-INV-08`.
7. Verify the manifest's pinned canonical decisions:
   - `risk_engine.name == "PREVENT"` and
     `risk_engine.legacy_only == false` (`GM-INV-12`).
   - `intended_use.age_min_inclusive == 18` (`GM-INV-24` semantics).
   - `intended_use.pregnancy_value_set_id` is non-empty.
   - `tools_lock.items[]` includes a `kind == "fhir-r5-profile"`
     entry (the pinned IG profile) and a
     `kind == "fhir-ig-publisher"` entry (the pinned publisher
     tooling).
8. Verify upstream prerequisites (each is a release blocker):
   - The Gate-3 bundle members referenced by the attestation are all
     present and verify against their recorded SHAs:
     - `cdsh` (CDS Hooks service-set manifest from
       `cds-hooks-package-htn` at P22).
     - `safe` (Safety Case from `safety-hbp` at P23).
     - `cont` (contraindication artifact from
       `extract-contraindications` at P14).
     - `mon` (monitoring artifact from `extract-monitoring` at P15).
     - `cpr` (copyright envelope from
       `copyright-quote-check-acc-aha` at P4).
     - `phi` (PHI scrub report from `phi-scrub` at P3).
     - The Library bundle (Gate-2-finalized snapshots).
     - The Guideline Card (P24).
   - `pharm-rules.json` is in state `sealed` (and
     `panel_chair_acknowledgement` is recorded when held rules are
     present, per `PR-INV-22`).
   - The contraindication artifact's `state == "sealed"` and every
     row in scope has `overall == "pass"` with `materialized` non-
     null (per `CIA-INV-07`).
   - The monitoring artifact's `state == "sealed"` and every row in
     scope has `overall == "pass"` with `materialized` non-null
     (mirrored constraint).
   - Every CDS Hooks service descriptor file under
     `work/<run_id>/cds-hooks/` has `state == "built"` and its
     `fixity.descriptor_sha256` recomputes (per `CDH-INV-04` and
     `CDH-INV-19`).
   - Every CQL Library snapshot referenced in the Gate-2 register
     has `state == "finalized"` (per `GR2-INV-*`).
   - The Safety Case is in state `signed` and its signature verifies
     (per `SC-INV-14`).
9. Verify `tsa_list[]` has at least one TSA whose
   `cert_valid_until` covers the wall-clock window (the IG package
   itself is not signed at P26; the time-stamping of the published
   release happens at P28 by `guideline-version`. P26 verifies TSA
   availability for downstream signing readiness.).
10. Acquire the IG write-back lock at `work/<run_id>/ig/.lock`. The
    skill is the only writer into this directory during its run.
11. Refuse to proceed if any precondition fails. **Fail-closed.**

### 2. Closed FHIR R5 resource composition matrix

The skill composes exactly the resources in the matrix below; the
matrix is **closed** at the schema level. Adding a new resource
type requires ADR-HTN-001 amendment under panel-chair signoff and a
coordinated update of every parent schema and skill.

| Resource type | Source | Profile (manifest-pinned) | One per |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ImplementationGuide` | (synthesized) | `cpg-htn-2025-implementation-guide` | run |
| `CapabilityStatement` | (synthesized) | `cpg-htn-2025-capability-statement` | run |
| `Library` | Gate-2 register snapshots | `cpg-htn-2025-library` | CQL Library |
| `Evidence` | contraindication artifact (P14) + monitoring artifact (P15) + records.json (P9) | `cpg-htn-2025-evidence` | rule + record |
| `EvidenceVariable` | contraindication artifact (P14) + monitoring artifact (P15) + records.json (P9) | `cpg-htn-2025-evidence-variable` | rule |
| `EvidenceReport` | Safety Case (P23) | `cpg-htn-2025-evidence-report` | hazard |
| `PlanDefinition` | Gate-2 register snapshots + monitoring artifact (P15) | `cpg-htn-2025-plan-definition` | clinical scenario |
| `ActivityDefinition` | pharm-rules.json (P13) `kind == "monitoring"` and `kind == "discontinuation"` rules | `cpg-htn-2025-activity-definition` | monitoring/discontinuation rule |
| `ServiceDefinition` | CDS Hooks service-set manifest (P22) | `cpg-htn-2025-service-definition` | CDS Hooks service |
| `Citation` | acquire-hbp-2025-source manifest (P1) + recommendation records' citations | `cpg-htn-2025-citation` | source guideline (single) |
| `Observation` (definitional) | bp-thresholds.json (P12) | `cpg-htn-2025-observation-definition` | BP threshold band |
| `ValueSet` | bind-htn-vocab terminology bindings (P10) + manifest-pinned pregnancy value-set | `cpg-htn-2025-value-set` | value set |
| `CodeSystem` | (referenced; not authored) | (not authored) | — |
| `ConceptMap` | bind-htn-vocab terminology bindings (P10) where cross-edition mappings are recorded | `cpg-htn-2025-concept-map` | mapping |
| `Provenance` | every produced resource (PROV bundle from P26) | `cpg-htn-2025-provenance` | resource |
| `Group` | manifest's `intended_use` populations | `cpg-htn-2025-group` | population |
| `StructureDefinition` (extensions) | (synthesized; the framework's `cpg-htn-*` extensions) | (self) | extension |

The composition order is fixed: `ImplementationGuide` and
`CapabilityStatement` last (after every resource referenced is
materialized); `StructureDefinition` extensions first (so every
downstream resource's profile validation can resolve them). The
ordering is enforced by the skill's processing pipeline and is
verified at the per-package fixity recompute step (§5).

### 3. Resource construction

For each resource type in scope, the skill constructs FHIR R5
resources under the deterministic shape rules below. The `id`
derivation, the `meta.profile[]` setting, the `text.div`
generation, the `meta.security` SHA recording, and the
`Provenance.signature` ↔ source-anchor binding are all
deterministic and reproducible.

#### 3.1 Deterministic id derivation

Every resource's `id` is deterministic from its source:

- `Library`: `library-<library-name-kebab>-<library-content-hash[:16]>`
- `Evidence` for contraindication: `ev-cont-<rule_id>` (mirrored
  from `CIA-INV-17`).
- `EvidenceVariable` for contraindication: `ev-<rule_id>` (mirrored
  from `CIA-INV-17`).
- `Evidence` for monitoring: `ev-mon-<rule_id>` (mirrored shape).
- `EvidenceVariable` for monitoring: `ev-mon-var-<rule_id>`.
- `EvidenceReport` for hazard: `er-<hazard_id>` (e.g., `er-H-01`).
- `PlanDefinition`: `pd-<scenario-id>`.
- `ActivityDefinition`: `ad-<rule_id>`.
- `ServiceDefinition`: `sd-<cds-hooks-service-id>` (e.g.,
  `sd-htn-pregnancy-denylist`).
- `Citation`: `cit-acc-aha-2025-hbp` (single resource).
- `Observation` (definitional): `od-bp-threshold-<band-id>`.
- `ValueSet`: `vs-<value-set-name-kebab>`.
- `ConceptMap`: `cm-<source>-to-<target>`.
- `Provenance`: `prov-<target-resource-id>`.
- `Group`: `grp-<population-filter-kebab>` (e.g., `grp-pregnant`).
- `StructureDefinition`: `sd-cpg-htn-<extension-name-kebab>`.

Re-runs against identical inputs produce identical resource ids.
The id derivation is byte-stable under the deterministic
canonicalization rules in §4.

#### 3.2 The framework's `cpg-htn-*` extensions

The skill synthesizes the following closed StructureDefinition
extensions, mirroring the extension URLs used in upstream artifacts
(specifically the `cpg-htn-source-anchor` extension on
contraindication `Evidence` resources at P14):

| Extension URL | Cardinality | Encoded fields |
|---|---|---|
| `https://aiwg.io/cpg-htn-2025-acc-aha/StructureDefinition/cpg-htn-source-anchor` | 0..1 per resource | `record_id`, `atomic_unit_id`, `anchor_kind`, `sair_sha256`, `page`, `bbox`, `rxnorm_edition_pin` |
| `https://aiwg.io/cpg-htn-2025-acc-aha/StructureDefinition/cpg-htn-cor-loe` | 0..1 per resource | `acc_aha_cor`, `acc_aha_loe`, `inheritance_kind`, `note` |
| `https://aiwg.io/cpg-htn-2025-acc-aha/StructureDefinition/cpg-htn-population-filter` | 0..* per resource | `population_filter` (closed PopulationFilter values) |
| `https://aiwg.io/cpg-htn-2025-acc-aha/StructureDefinition/cpg-htn-cds-posture` | 0..1 per resource | `posture_at_cds`, `cds_hook`, `attending_override_permitted (const false)`, `documentation_only (const false)` |
| `https://aiwg.io/cpg-htn-2025-acc-aha/StructureDefinition/cpg-htn-rxnorm-pin` | 0..1 per resource | `rxnorm_edition_pin` |
| `https://aiwg.io/cpg-htn-2025-acc-aha/StructureDefinition/cpg-htn-pregnancy-denylist` | 0..1 per resource | `applicability` (closed enum), `manifest_pregnancy_value_set_id`, `attending_override_pattern_scan_clean (const true)` |
| `https://aiwg.io/cpg-htn-2025-acc-aha/StructureDefinition/cpg-htn-two-person-witnesses` | 0..* per resource | `role`, `reviewer_id`, `gate`, `cohort_id` |
| `https://aiwg.io/cpg-htn-2025-acc-aha/StructureDefinition/cpg-htn-build-fixity` | 1..1 per resource | `build_run_id`, `build_version_label`, `manifest_payload_sha256`, `gate3_attestation_sha256` |

Every extension is authored as a `StructureDefinition` resource
with the URL above and validated at composition time. Resources
that depend on an extension MUST resolve the extension URL against
the skill's authored set; any unresolved extension URL BLOCKs.

#### 3.3 Per-resource invariants (defense-in-depth)

The skill enforces every parent-schema invariant relevant to the
resource at composition time, even though the upstream artifact's
producer skill already verified them. This is defense-in-depth
against upstream artifact corruption between Gate 3 and P26.

For every resource, the skill verifies:

1. **Source-anchor extension present** (when applicable): every
   `Evidence`, `EvidenceVariable`, `EvidenceReport`,
   `ActivityDefinition`, `ServiceDefinition` MUST carry the
   `cpg-htn-source-anchor` extension with a non-empty
   `record_id` and `atomic_unit_id`.
2. **COR/LOE inheritance preserved**: the `cpg-htn-cor-loe`
   extension's COR / LOE values match the parent record's exactly.
3. **Population filter closed-enum membership**: every
   `cpg-htn-population-filter` extension value is from the closed
   `PopulationFilter` enum.
4. **CDS posture closed-enum membership**: every
   `cpg-htn-cds-posture` extension's `posture_at_cds` and
   `cds_hook` values are from the closed enums in
   `cds-hooks-services-htn.yaml` §2.2 / §2.3.
5. **Attending-override pattern absent**: recursive scan over every
   string field in the resource (and in every authored extension
   URL string content) for the closed AttendingOverridePattern
   from `cds-hooks-services-htn.yaml` §2.5. Match → BLOCK.
6. **PCE-legacy literal absent**: recursive scan over every string
   field for the literal `PCE-legacy`. Match → BLOCK.
7. **Age gate ≥ 18**: every population-bounded resource's
   `useContext` or characteristic carries a non-empty age range
   `low.value == 18`.
8. **Pregnancy denylist mechanical reinforcement**: for every
   resource whose `cpg-htn-population-filter` includes `pregnant`
   or `postpartum` AND whose source rule is a denylist, the
   `cpg-htn-cds-posture` extension MUST satisfy:
   - `posture_at_cds == "hard-refuse"`
   - `cds_hook == "order-select"`
   - `attending_override_permitted == false`
   - `documentation_only == false`
   Validators MUST refuse any deviation; this is the third
   defense-in-depth enforcement of ADR-HTN-001 D8 (the first is at
   P13's `PR-INV-18`, the second at P14's `CIA-INV-13`, the third
   here).
9. **RxNorm pin alignment**: every resource carrying a
   `cpg-htn-rxnorm-pin` extension MUST have its
   `rxnorm_edition_pin` equal to the manifest's pinned RxNorm
   edition. Drift → BLOCK.
10. **Source-anchor SHA recompute**: the
    `cpg-htn-source-anchor.sair_sha256` MUST recompute against
    `work/<run_id>/sair.json` and the parent atomic unit's anchor.
    Drift → BLOCK.

#### 3.4 Profile binding and validation

Every resource's `meta.profile[]` MUST include exactly the manifest-
pinned profile URL for the resource type (per the matrix in §2).
The skill validates every resource against the pinned profile via
the FHIR R5 IG Publisher's profile validator. Any validation
failure BLOCKs with `fhir-profile-validation-failed`.

The skill records the per-resource validation outcome in the IG
package's per-resource `Provenance` resource (see §3.6) and in the
build's per-package fixity manifest (see §5).

#### 3.5 Resource serialization and canonicalization

Every resource is serialized to JSON under FHIR R5 JCS
canonicalization (RFC 8785 with FHIR-specific element ordering
exceptions documented in `docs/fhir-r5-jcs-notes.md`). The
canonicalization is byte-stable across re-runs given identical
input. The per-resource SHA is the SHA-256 of the canonical bytes.

The serialization rules are:

- Every resource's `text.div` is the deterministic narrative
  rendered from the resource's structured content under a closed
  template set in `docs/fhir-r5-narrative-templates.md`. The
  narrative is NOT free-text; it is a deterministic projection of
  the resource's structured fields. This is the framework's
  defense against narrative-divergence attacks.
- Every resource's `meta.security[]` carries a coding from the
  framework's `cpg-htn-2025-security-codes` CodeSystem with
  `code == "fixity-recorded"` and `valueString` set to the
  per-resource SHA. The SHA is the value computed against the
  resource's JCS canonical form with the `meta.security` element
  excluded, then attached after computation. Validators MUST
  recompute and compare.
- Every resource's `meta.versionId` is set to the build's
  `build_version_label` (e.g.,
  `v1.0.0+ACC-AHA-2025+US+2026-04-30`).
- Every resource's `meta.lastUpdated` is set to the IG build's
  composition time-stamp.

#### 3.6 Per-resource `Provenance`

For every resource composed (other than `Provenance` resources
themselves), the skill emits a corresponding `Provenance` resource
that binds the produced resource to:

- The parent run id (`build_run_id`).
- The Gate-3 attestation SHA (`gate3_attestation_sha256`).
- The active manifest payload SHA.
- The producing skill's id (`fhir-implementation-guide-build`).
- The upstream producer skill's id (e.g., `extract-pharm-rules`,
  `extract-contraindications`, `cds-hooks-package-htn`,
  `safety-hbp`).
- Every contributing source-anchor SHA (sair_sha256, atomic unit
  id, record id, rule id).

`Provenance.signature[]` is omitted at this phase (the IG package
itself is not signed at P26; downstream P28 release publishing
applies the release-level signature). However,
`Provenance.signature` is reserved at the resource level for a
non-cryptographic "fixity binding" entry whose `data` field is
the resource's canonical SHA. This makes the per-resource SHA
provable against the `Provenance` resource without recomputation.

### 4. IG package layout

The IG package is materialized at `work/<run_id>/ig/` under the
deterministic layout below. The layout is closed; new directories
require ADR-HTN-001 amendment.

```
work/<run_id>/ig/
├── ImplementationGuide-cpg-htn-2025.json
├── CapabilityStatement-cpg-htn-2025.json
├── input/
│   ├── pagecontent/
│   │   ├── index.md
│   │   ├── safety-case.md
│   │   ├── cds-hooks.md
│   │   ├── pharm-rules.md
│   │   ├── contraindications.md
│   │   ├── monitoring.md
│   │   └── citation.md
│   └── resources/
│       ├── StructureDefinition/
│       │   └── (one per cpg-htn-* extension)
│       ├── Library/
│       ├── Evidence/
│       │   ├── ev-cont-pr-<16hex>.json
│       │   └── ev-mon-pr-<16hex>.json
│       ├── EvidenceVariable/
│       │   ├── ev-pr-<16hex>.json
│       │   └── ev-mon-var-pr-<16hex>.json
│       ├── EvidenceReport/
│       │   └── er-H-<NN>.json
│       ├── PlanDefinition/
│       ├── ActivityDefinition/
│       │   └── ad-pr-<16hex>.json
│       ├── ServiceDefinition/
│       │   └── sd-htn-<service-name>.json
│       ├── Citation/
│       │   └── cit-acc-aha-2025-hbp.json
│       ├── Observation/
│       ├── ValueSet/
│       ├── ConceptMap/
│       ├── Group/
│       └── Provenance/
├── ig-package-manifest.json
└── fixity/
    ├── per-resource-shas.json
    └── per-package-sha.json
```

The `pagecontent/` markdown files are deterministic projections of
the upstream artifacts: `safety-case.md` projects the Safety Case
hazard set; `cds-hooks.md` projects the seven-service set;
`pharm-rules.md` projects the closed five-kind rule set with COR /
LOE columns; `contraindications.md` projects the contraindication
artifact's `pass`-state rows; `monitoring.md` projects the
monitoring artifact's `pass`-state rows; `citation.md` projects the
acquire-hbp-2025-source manifest. Every page is rendered from a
closed template; no LLM is invoked at this step.

### 5. Per-package fixity manifest

The skill emits a per-package fixity manifest at
`work/<run_id>/ig/fixity/per-package-sha.json` and a per-resource
SHA list at `work/<run_id>/ig/fixity/per-resource-shas.json`. The
shape:

```json
{
  "schema_version": "1.0.0",
  "build_run_id": "<uuid>",
  "build_version_label": "v1.0.0+ACC-AHA-2025+US+<date>",
  "gate3_attestation_sha256": "<from gate-3>",
  "manifest_payload_sha256": "<from manifest>",
  "fhir_r5_profile_pin": "<from manifest>",
  "fhir_ig_publisher_pin": "<from manifest>",
  "ig_package_path": "work/<run_id>/ig/",
  "resource_count_by_type": {
    "ImplementationGuide": 1,
    "CapabilityStatement": 1,
    "Library": <n>,
    "Evidence": <n>,
    "EvidenceVariable": <n>,
    "EvidenceReport": <n>,
    "PlanDefinition": <n>,
    "ActivityDefinition": <n>,
    "ServiceDefinition": 7,
    "Citation": 1,
    "Observation": <n>,
    "ValueSet": <n>,
    "ConceptMap": <n>,
    "Group": <n>,
    "StructureDefinition": <n>,
    "Provenance": <n>
  },
  "per_resource_sha_list_path": "work/<run_id>/ig/fixity/per-resource-shas.json",
  "per_resource_sha_list_sha256": "<64hex>",
  "ig_package_sha256": "<SHA-256 of JCS(per_resource_sha_list_path content) | tar-archive of ig/>",
  "fixity": {
    "ig_package_manifest_sha256": "<JCS SHA-256 of this file with `fixity` excluded>",
    "computed_at": "<ISO-8601>",
    "canonical_form": "json-canonical-rfc8785"
  }
}
```

The `ig_package_sha256` is the input `guideline-version` (P28)
consumes when computing the release-level signature. The
deterministic chain — Gate-3 attestation SHA → IG package SHA →
release signature — provides a continuous evidence trail from
medical director attestation through public release.

### 6. Cross-reference resolution

For every resource, the skill verifies that every cross-reference
(via `Reference.reference`, `canonical` strings, `extension.url`,
`Citation.citedArtifact.identifier`, etc.) resolves to:

- A resource within the IG package, OR
- A manifest-pinned external resource (terminology server,
  RxNorm, ICD-10-CM, SNOMED CT, LOINC, CVX, the parent FHIR R5
  base profile), OR
- A framework-authored `cpg-htn-*` extension URL.

Any unresolved reference → BLOCK with
`unresolved-cross-reference`. The skill's cross-reference resolver
is mechanical; LLMs are not invoked for resolution.

### 7. Audit log and provenance

For every resource composed and validated, the skill emits:

- An `audit_log[]` entry into the IG package manifest's audit
  region (closed kinds in §6.1 of the contraindication artifact's
  schema, plus IG-specific kinds in §10 below).
- A W3C PROV-O record into the build's PROV bundle at
  `provenance/fhir-implementation-guide-<run_id>.jsonld`:
  - `Activity`: this composition run.
  - `Entity`: each composed resource (with its computed SHA).
  - `Agent`: the operator id and the framework's pinned IG
    Publisher tooling.
  - `wasGeneratedBy`, `used`, `wasAttributedTo` relations.
- Per-resource FHIR `Provenance` resources (per §3.6).

### 8. Determinism and reproducibility

- Composition is deterministic given:
  - identical Gate-3 attestation;
  - identical contributing artifacts (every recorded SHA recomputes);
  - identical pinned FHIR R5 profile;
  - identical pinned IG Publisher tooling;
  - identical pinned terminology editions;
  - identical narrative-template set (`docs/fhir-r5-narrative-
    templates.md`).
- Re-running this skill on a sealed IG package with `--mode verify`
  is a no-op (the skill confirms every resource SHA recomputes and
  writes nothing).
- The deterministic id derivation cascades: every resource's id is
  recomputable from its inputs.
- A change to any contributing artifact's SHA invalidates the
  affected IG resources and forces a rebuild on next run.

### 9. Held / blocked routing

Unlike P14 and P15, the IG build skill does **not** route to a
held / blocked queue. The IG build is a composition step over
already-validated upstream artifacts; if any precondition fails or
any per-resource invariant fails, the skill BLOCKs the IG build and
routes the failure upstream:

- **Upstream artifact SHA mismatch** → BLOCK; emit
  `upstream-artifact-sha-mismatch`; route to
  `flow-hbp-2025-build` for upstream re-run.
- **Profile validation failure** → BLOCK; emit
  `fhir-profile-validation-failed` for the failing resource;
  investigate as profile-pin drift, IG Publisher pin drift, or
  upstream artifact corruption.
- **AttendingOverridePattern detected** → BLOCK unconditionally;
  emit `attending-override-pattern-detected`; investigate as
  adversarial input.
- **PCE-legacy literal detected** → BLOCK unconditionally; emit
  `pce-legacy-binding-detected`; investigate as adversarial input
  or upstream contamination.
- **Pregnancy denylist mechanical reinforcement failed** → BLOCK
  unconditionally; emit
  `pregnancy-denylist-cross-check-failed`; this is a clinical
  safety failure; remediation is upstream re-author and a fresh
  manifest version when structural.
- **Unresolved cross-reference** → BLOCK; emit
  `unresolved-cross-reference`; investigate as missing extension or
  missing manifest pin.

### 10. Closed `AuditEventKind` (IG-specific extensions)

In addition to the closed audit event kinds inherited from upstream
schemas, the IG build skill emits the following IG-specific kinds:

- `ig-build-started`
- `ig-resource-composed`
- `ig-resource-profile-validated`
- `ig-resource-profile-validation-failed`
- `ig-resource-narrative-rendered`
- `ig-resource-canonicalized`
- `ig-resource-sha-recorded`
- `ig-cross-reference-resolved`
- `ig-cross-reference-unresolved`
- `ig-package-fixity-recorded`
- `ig-package-built`
- `ig-package-verified`
- `ig-package-mutation-attempt`
- `attending-override-pattern-detected`
- `pce-legacy-binding-detected`
- `pregnancy-denylist-cross-check-failed`
- `upstream-artifact-sha-mismatch`
- `fhir-profile-validation-failed`
- `unresolved-cross-reference`
- `ig-build-blocked`

## DQA Gates Enforced By This Skill

| Gate | Condition for advance |
|---|---|
| **GI-A** Manifest active | Active manifest with verified medical-director signoff and zero open errata blockers. |
| **GI-B** Gate-3 attestation verified | Gate-3 attestation in state `signed`; signature verifies; time-stamp verifies; every cohort-axis attestation flag is `true`. |
| **GI-C** Upstream artifacts sealed and SHA-recompute clean | Every contributing artifact (Safety Case, CDS Hooks service set, contraindication artifact, monitoring artifact, Library snapshots, copyright envelope, PHI scrub report, Guideline Card) has its recorded SHA recompute against the live file. |
| **GI-D** Closed resource composition matrix | Every produced resource type is from the closed matrix in §2; no other types are composed. |
| **GI-E** Per-resource deterministic id | Every resource's id is derived deterministically from its source per §3.1. |
| **GI-F** Profile validation pass | Every resource validates against its manifest-pinned profile under the IG Publisher's profile validator. |
| **GI-G** Source-anchor extension present | Every Evidence / EvidenceVariable / EvidenceReport / ActivityDefinition / ServiceDefinition carries `cpg-htn-source-anchor` with non-empty `record_id` and `atomic_unit_id`. |
| **GI-H** COR/LOE inheritance preserved | `cpg-htn-cor-loe` extension matches parent record's COR/LOE exactly. |
| **GI-I** AttendingOverridePattern absent | Recursive scan over every resource and every authored extension returns zero matches. |
| **GI-J** PCE-legacy literal absent | Recursive scan over every resource returns zero matches. |
| **GI-K** Age gate = 18 | Every population-bounded resource carries an age range with `low.value == 18`. |
| **GI-L** Pregnancy denylist mechanical reinforcement | Every pregnancy-denylist resource carries `cpg-htn-cds-posture` with `posture_at_cds == "hard-refuse"`, `cds_hook == "order-select"`, `attending_override_permitted == false`, `documentation_only == false`. |
| **GI-M** RxNorm pin alignment | Every `cpg-htn-rxnorm-pin` extension matches the manifest's pinned RxNorm edition. |
| **GI-N** Cross-reference resolution clean | Every Reference, canonical string, and extension URL resolves to an in-package resource, a manifest-pinned external resource, or a framework-authored extension. |
| **GI-O** Per-resource SHA deterministic | Every resource's SHA recomputes byte-for-byte from its FHIR-R5 JCS canonical form. |
| **GI-P** Per-package SHA deterministic | The IG package's `ig_package_sha256` recomputes deterministically across re-runs. |
| **GI-Q** Append-only audit log | Every event recorded in canonical order; chained-hash continuity verifies. |
| **GI-R** Post-Gate-3 immutability | Once the IG package is referenced by a P28 release manifest, mutation attempts are tamper-evident and BLOCK. |

Failure of any gate at any resource or at the package level →
BLOCK; the IG build is rolled back, the in-flight write directory
is preserved for diagnostics under
`work/<run_id>/ig.failed-<timestamp>/`, and the failure is routed
upstream with the specific gate diagnostic. There is **no override**.

## Outputs

- IG package directory at `work/<run_id>/ig/` with the deterministic
  layout in §4.
- IG package manifest at
  `work/<run_id>/ig/ig-package-manifest.json` validated against the
  inline shape in §5.
- Per-resource SHA list at
  `work/<run_id>/ig/fixity/per-resource-shas.json`.
- Per-package SHA at
  `work/<run_id>/ig/fixity/per-package-sha.json`.
- Per-resource FHIR `Provenance` resources in
  `work/<run_id>/ig/input/resources/Provenance/`.
- Per-run report at
  `work/<run_id>/reports/fhir-implementation-guide-<run_id>.md`
  summarizing resources composed by type, profile validation
  outcomes, source-anchor coverage, AttendingOverridePattern scan
  count, PCE-legacy scan count, RxNorm pin alignment outcomes, and
  any blockers.
- Build PROV bundle update at
  `provenance/fhir-implementation-guide-<run_id>.jsonld`.
- Notifications to the orchestrator queue:
  - `ig-package-built` on full success.
  - `ig-build-blocked` with the failing gate and remediation
    guidance on any failure.

## Error Handling

- **Manifest stale or not active.** BLOCK preflight.
- **Gate-3 attestation not signed or signature failed.** BLOCK
  preflight.
- **Cohort-axis attestation flag not all true.** BLOCK preflight.
- **Upstream artifact SHA mismatch.** BLOCK; emit
  `upstream-artifact-sha-mismatch`; route to orchestrator for
  upstream re-run.
- **Profile pin missing in manifest.** BLOCK preflight; emit
  `profile-pin-missing`; require new manifest version.
- **IG Publisher tooling pin missing in manifest.** BLOCK
  preflight; emit `ig-publisher-pin-missing`.
- **Profile validation fail on any resource.** BLOCK; emit
  `fhir-profile-validation-failed` per failing resource;
  investigate.
- **AttendingOverridePattern detected on any resource.** BLOCK
  unconditionally; emit `attending-override-pattern-detected`;
  investigate as adversarial input.
- **PCE-legacy literal detected on any resource.** BLOCK
  unconditionally; emit `pce-legacy-binding-detected`; investigate
  as adversarial input or upstream contamination.
- **Pregnancy denylist mechanical reinforcement failed on any
  resource.** BLOCK unconditionally; emit
  `pregnancy-denylist-cross-check-failed`; this is a clinical
  safety failure.
- **Unresolved cross-reference.** BLOCK; emit
  `unresolved-cross-reference`; investigate as missing extension or
  missing manifest pin.
- **Per-resource SHA non-deterministic.** BLOCK; emit
  `ig-resource-sha-mismatch`; investigate canonicalization drift.
- **Per-package SHA non-deterministic.** BLOCK; emit
  `ig-package-sha-mismatch`; investigate.
- **Lock contention.** Wait up to a configured timeout; fail-closed
  if not acquired; concurrent writers on the IG directory are not
  permitted.
- **Resume after Gate-3 attestation SHA change.** Reject; require
  fresh run.
- **Direct edit attempt against the IG package.** Reject; emit
  `ig-package-mutation-attempt`; investigate as adversarial input.

## Examples

```bash
# Default first-pass IG build after Gate-3 attestation is signed
fhir-implementation-guide-build work/run-2026-04-30/gate3-attestation.signed.jsonld

# Verify-only re-check (used by guideline-version P28's preflight)
fhir-implementation-guide-build work/run-2026-04-30/gate3-attestation.signed.jsonld \
  --mode verify

# Resume after orchestrator routed a failed profile-validation
# upstream and the upstream skill re-emitted
fhir-implementation-guide-build work/run-2026-04-30/gate3-attestation.signed.jsonld \
  --resume

# Dry-run plan emission for change-control review against a
# proposed FHIR R5 profile rotation
fhir-implementation-guide-build work/run-2026-04-30/gate3-attestation.signed.jsonld \
  --profile-pin cpg-htn-2025-implementation-guide-rc2 \
  --dry-run
```

## Schema Reference

- `schemas/sair.yaml` — read-only source of source-anchor SHAs the
  skill verifies against.
- `schemas/recommendation-record-htn.yaml` — input. The
  `cpg-htn-cor-loe` and `cpg-htn-source-anchor` extensions' values
  are inherited from records.
- `schemas/atomic-unit.yaml` — input. The `cpg-htn-source-anchor`
  extension's anchor fields are inherited from atomic units.
- `schemas/gate1-register.yaml` — input. The
  `cpg-htn-two-person-witnesses` extension's Gate-1 entries are
  inherited from cohort registers.
- `schemas/gate2-register.yaml` — input. The
  `cpg-htn-two-person-witnesses` extension's Gate-2 entries are
  inherited from cohort registers; the `Library` snapshots are
  consumed for Library resource composition.
- `schemas/gate3-attestation.yaml` — input. The Gate-3 attestation
  is the gating precondition. The
  `cpg-htn-build-fixity.gate3_attestation_sha256` extension's
  value is the attestation's `payload_sha256`.
- `schemas/safety-case-htn.yaml` — input. The Safety Case feeds
  `EvidenceReport` resources (one per hazard).
- `schemas/cds-hooks-services-htn.yaml` — input. The seven service
  descriptors feed `ServiceDefinition` resources. The
  `cpg-htn-cds-posture` extension's posture / hook values are
  inherited from descriptors. The closed AttendingOverridePattern
  is mirrored at every recursive scan in this skill.
- `schemas/pharm-rule-htn.yaml` — input. The closed five-kind rule
  set feeds `ActivityDefinition` (monitoring + discontinuation) and
  `Library` (selection + denylist + dose-modifier) downstreams. The
  rule's `acc_aha_cor` / `acc_aha_loe` are inherited.
- `schemas/contraindication-artifact-htn.yaml` — input. The
  artifact's `pass`-state rows' `materialized.evidence_id` and
  `evidence_variable_id` are the canonical FHIR resource ids
  composed into the IG; the artifact's `cross_check_sha256` is
  recorded in every resulting resource's
  `cpg-htn-build-fixity.contraindication_artifact_sha256`
  attribute.
- `schemas/guideline-manifest-hbp-2025.yaml` — pin source.
  Specifically:
  - `tools_lock.items[]` of `kind == "fhir-r5-profile"` (the
    pinned IG profile).
  - `tools_lock.items[]` of `kind == "fhir-ig-publisher"` (the
    pinned publisher tooling).
  - `terminology[]` (RxNorm + ICD-10-CM + SNOMED CT + LOINC + CVX
    editions consumed for ValueSet / ConceptMap composition).
  - `risk_engine.name == "PREVENT"` and `legacy_only == false`.
  - `intended_use.age_min_inclusive == 18`.
  - `intended_use.pregnancy_value_set_id`.
  - `tsa_list[]` (consulted at downstream P28 signing).
- `schemas/acc-aha-grading.yaml` — closed COR/LOE enums consumed
  by the `cpg-htn-cor-loe` extension and the LOE → HL7 certainty
  mapping.
- `schemas/monitoring-artifact-htn.yaml` (forthcoming) — input.
- `schemas/risk-engine-binding.yaml` (forthcoming) — input.
- `schemas/cql-library-snapshot.yaml` (forthcoming) — input.
- `schemas/release-manifest.yaml` (forthcoming) — downstream
  consumer at P28.

## Authority Boundaries

**Can do**
- Read the Gate-3 attestation, the manifest, and every contributing
  upstream artifact at recorded SHAs.
- Compose FHIR R5 resources from the closed composition matrix in
  §2 with deterministic id derivation.
- Synthesize the framework's `cpg-htn-*` StructureDefinition
  extensions.
- Validate every resource against the manifest-pinned FHIR R5
  profile.
- Render deterministic narratives from the closed template set.
- Recursively scan for AttendingOverridePattern matches and
  PCE-legacy literals.
- Compute per-resource and per-package SHAs deterministically under
  FHIR-R5 JCS canonicalization.
- Emit per-resource FHIR `Provenance` resources and PROV bundle
  updates.
- Append append-only audit events to the IG package manifest's
  audit region.
- BLOCK the IG build on any precondition failure, profile
  validation failure, AttendingOverridePattern detection, PCE-legacy
  detection, pregnancy-denylist mechanical reinforcement failure, or
  unresolved cross-reference.

**Requires approval (panel chair / new manifest version / ADR
amendment)**
- Any change to the closed FHIR R5 resource composition matrix.
- Any change to the closed `cpg-htn-*` StructureDefinition
  extension set.
- Any change to the deterministic id derivation rules.
- Any change to the deterministic narrative-template set.
- Any change to the IG package directory layout.
- Any FHIR R5 profile rotation or IG Publisher tooling rotation
  (these route through manifest-version amendment).

**Never**
- Author records, atomic units, pharm rules, contraindications,
  monitoring artifacts, the Safety Case, the Guideline Card, CQL
  Library bytes, CDS Hooks descriptor bytes, or terminology
  bindings.
- Sign the IG package (the release-level signature is applied at
  P28).
- Generate narrative text via LLMs (the narratives are
  deterministic projections under the closed template set).
- Compose any resource type outside the closed matrix in §2.
- Permit a soft-warning posture on any pregnancy denylist resource.
- Permit any AttendingOverridePattern match in any resource or
  extension.
- Reference PCE-legacy in any resource, extension, value set, or
  narrative.
- Lower the age gate below 18 on any population-bounded resource.
- Render free-text narratives outside the closed template set.
- Mutate the IG package after Gate 3 has attested; corrections
  require a new manifest version, a new Gate-3 attestation, and a
  fresh build.
- Run with `--strict false` in production.

  introduced at `extract-contraindications` §3.2 and is reified
  here as a synthesized `StructureDefinition`. The Pregnancy
  reinforcement is the third defense-in-depth enforcement of
  ADR-HTN-001 D8.
- **FHIR R5** specification — informs every resource shape. The
  framework's profile pins are stricter than the base specification
  permits in general; this skill's enforcement is additive.
- **HL7 certainty CodeSystem** — the manifest pins the
  `acc-aha-LOE → HL7-certainty-rating` mapping in
  `docs/acc-aha-to-hl7-certainty.md`.
- **REF-475** ML Reproducibility Checklist — informs determinism
  rules applied to per-resource and per-package SHAs.
- **REF-062** W3C PROV-O — informs the per-resource
  Activity/Entity/Agent emission and the per-resource FHIR
  `Provenance` mapping.
- **RFC 8785** — JSON canonicalization scheme used in resource SHA
  computation; FHIR-specific element ordering exceptions are
  documented in `docs/fhir-r5-jcs-notes.md`.
- **NIST SP 800-63** (IAL/AAL) — informs the operator
  authentication level applied at composition time.
- **Parent framework** `aiwg-training` rules: `god-session` (≤7
  responsibilities per skill; this skill's responsibilities are
  bounded to: preflight, resource composition under the closed
  matrix, profile validation, deterministic narrative rendering,
  per-resource SHA + per-package SHA computation, audit + provenance
  emission, error routing upstream),
  `human-authorization` (Gate 3 is the upstream gate; P28's
  release-level signing is the downstream gate; institutional
  opt-ins to non-default profile pins or extensions require panel-
  chair signoff and ADR amendment),
  `native-ux-tools` (the IG Publisher tooling pin is read from the
  manifest's `tools_lock.items[]`; the IG package is consumed by
  the standard FHIR R5 IG Publisher and downstream republishers).
```

## Copilot

```markdown name=docs/fhir-r5-narrative-templates.md
# FHIR R5 Narrative Templates (`cpg-htn-2025-acc-aha`)

**Status:** stable
**Schema lifecycle:** stable
**Last reviewed:** HUMAN_FILL: ISO-8601 date of most recent panel review
**Authority:** ADR-HTN-001 D2, D3, D5, D8, D9, D10, D14, D15
**Owners:** `cpg-htn-2025-acc-aha` framework (panel chair + medical director)
**Consumers:** `fhir-implementation-guide-build` (P26)
**Pinned by:** `manifests/guideline-manifest-hbp-2025.<version>.yaml` —
`tools_lock.items[]` of `kind == "fhir-r5-narrative-template-pack"`

---

## 0. Posture and scope

This document is the **closed deterministic narrative-template set**
that `fhir-implementation-guide-build` (P26) uses to render the
`Resource.text.div` (XHTML) field of every FHIR R5 resource it
composes into the published IG.

The framework's posture is that **every published FHIR resource's
narrative MUST be a deterministic projection of the resource's
structured content under a closed template set**. No LLM is invoked
at narrative-rendering time. No free-text narrative is permitted in
any resource. This is the framework's defense against
narrative-divergence attacks (where a resource's structured content
asserts one clinical fact while its rendered narrative asserts a
different fact).

Posture: **caution over velocity, fidelity over coverage,
hard-refusal-on-pregnancy over convenience.** The pregnancy
denylist's narrative carries the order-select hard-refuse posture
verbatim by construction, with no softening or attending-override
language. PCE-legacy is forbidden in every narrative. Age gate ≥ 18
is recorded in every population-bounded resource's narrative.
Post-Gate-3 narratives are immutable.

This document does **not** define structured FHIR resource shapes
(those are pinned at the manifest's `tools_lock.items[]` of
`kind == "fhir-r5-profile"`); it defines the **narrative
projections** of the structured content. The two are
complementary: the structured content is the contract for the
EHR-side CDS Hooks runtime and the FHIR R5 IG Publisher; the
narrative is the contract for human readability and for downstream
republishers that may render the narrative directly without
re-reading the structured content.

---

## 1. Closed template set

The framework defines exactly **fifteen closed templates**, one per
resource type composed at P26 (mirroring §2 of
`fhir-implementation-guide-build` `SKILL.md`). Adding a new
template requires ADR-HTN-001 amendment under panel-chair signoff
AND a coordinated update of every parent schema and skill.

| # | Template id | Resource type | Source artifact |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `tpl-implementation-guide-1.0.0` | `ImplementationGuide` | (synthesized) |
| 2 | `tpl-capability-statement-1.0.0` | `CapabilityStatement` | (synthesized) |
| 3 | `tpl-library-1.0.0` | `Library` | Gate-2 register snapshots |
| 4 | `tpl-evidence-contraindication-1.0.0` | `Evidence` (contraindication) | contraindication artifact (P14) |
| 5 | `tpl-evidence-monitoring-1.0.0` | `Evidence` (monitoring) | monitoring artifact (P15) |
| 6 | `tpl-evidence-record-1.0.0` | `Evidence` (record-level) | records.json (P9) |
| 7 | `tpl-evidence-variable-1.0.0` | `EvidenceVariable` | contraindication + monitoring + records |
| 8 | `tpl-evidence-report-hazard-1.0.0` | `EvidenceReport` | Safety Case (P23) |
| 9 | `tpl-plan-definition-1.0.0` | `PlanDefinition` | Gate-2 + monitoring artifact |
| 10 | `tpl-activity-definition-1.0.0` | `ActivityDefinition` | pharm-rules.json (P13) |
| 11 | `tpl-service-definition-1.0.0` | `ServiceDefinition` | CDS Hooks service set (P22) |
| 12 | `tpl-citation-1.0.0` | `Citation` | acquire-hbp-2025-source manifest (P1) |
| 13 | `tpl-observation-definitional-1.0.0` | `Observation` (definitional) | bp-thresholds.json (P12) |
| 14 | `tpl-value-set-1.0.0` | `ValueSet` | terminology bindings (P10) |
| 15 | `tpl-concept-map-1.0.0` | `ConceptMap` | terminology bindings (P10) |

Two additional template ids are reserved but **MUST** be rendered
verbatim from upstream artifacts (no narrative projection is
applied):

- `tpl-provenance-passthrough-1.0.0` (`Provenance`): the narrative
  is `"<div xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml\">Generated
  Provenance for <code>{target_id}</code>; signature data
  recorded in fixity manifest.</div>"`. No template substitution is
  applied beyond `{target_id}`.
- `tpl-structure-definition-passthrough-1.0.0`
  (`StructureDefinition`): the narrative is the deterministic
  rendering of the StructureDefinition's `differential.element[]`
  by the FHIR R5 IG Publisher's standard rendering, frozen at the
  manifest's pinned IG Publisher version. No framework-specific
  template applies.

The skill MUST refuse to render any narrative against a template id
not in this closed set. Adding `Group` or any other resource type's
template requires ADR-HTN-001 amendment.

---

## 2. Template-rendering invariants (apply to every template)

The following invariants apply to every template. Validators MUST
enforce all of them at narrative composition time.

### 2.1 Determinism
- Identical structured input MUST produce identical narrative
  bytes.
- The narrative is rendered by string substitution against the
  template; no dynamic logic, no LLM, no live network call is
  invoked.

### 2.2 Closed substitution variable set
- Each template defines a closed list of substitution variables
  (e.g., `{rule_id}`, `{cor}`, `{loe}`, `{drug_classes_list}`,
  `{population_filter_list}`, etc.). Variables outside the template's
  declared list MUST NOT appear in the output. Templates MUST refuse
  rendering on undeclared variable references.

### 2.3 Verbatim-clinical-text invariant
- When a template substitutes a variable that originates from
  clinical text in the source guideline (e.g.,
  `{source_text_verbatim}`), the substitution MUST be byte-for-byte
  the parent atomic unit's `text_verbatim` after Phase-2 reversible
  normalization. No paraphrase, no truncation, no formatting
  modification. The narrative MAY wrap the verbatim text in a
  `<blockquote>` or `<q>` element but MUST NOT alter the text's
  characters.

### 2.4 ACC/AHA grading verbatim
- COR and LOE values MUST be rendered verbatim from the closed enums
  in `schemas/acc-aha-grading.yaml`. The framework's policy is that
  ACC/AHA grading is the primary rating system (per ADR-HTN-001 D3);
  no remapping is permitted in narratives. The HL7 certainty
  mapping is rendered as a **secondary** annotation per
  `docs/acc-aha-to-hl7-certainty.md` §3.

### 2.5 Closed AttendingOverridePattern denylist
- The output XHTML MUST be free of attending-override semantics.
  The skill recursively scans the rendered output (case-insensitive
  after Unicode NFC) for any pattern in the closed
  `AttendingOverridePattern` set
  (`schemas/cds-hooks-services-htn.yaml` §2.5,
  `schemas/pharm-rule-htn.yaml` §2.7,
  `schemas/contraindication-artifact-htn.yaml` §2.6 — all mirrored).
  Match → BLOCK with `attending-override-pattern-detected`.
  This rule applies even when the upstream source-text contains the
  pattern by accident (e.g., a quoted reviewer note); upstream
  remediation is required.

### 2.6 PCE-legacy literal denylist
- The output XHTML MUST be free of the literal `PCE-legacy`
  (case-insensitive after Unicode NFC). Match → BLOCK with
  `pce-legacy-binding-detected`. The framework's policy is that
  PCE-legacy never appears in any published artifact (ADR-HTN-001
  D5); narratives are no exception.

### 2.7 Age-gate annotation
- Every population-bounded resource's narrative MUST include the
  literal sentence:
  > "Age gate: ≥ 18 years (intended use; pediatric populations
  > out of scope)."
- The age-gate sentence is a verbatim string and MUST be the exact
  byte sequence above (no synonyms, no rephrasing). Validators
  recompute the sentence's SHA against the manifest's pinned
  age-gate string and refuse on mismatch.

### 2.8 Pregnancy hard-refuse annotation
- For every resource whose `cpg-htn-population-filter` extension
  includes `pregnant` or `postpartum` AND whose source-rule kind is
  `denylist`, the narrative MUST include the literal sentence:
  > "Posture: order-select hard refuse. Attending override: not
  > permitted. Documentation-only override: not permitted."
- Like §2.7, the sentence is a verbatim string with no permitted
  variations. Validators recompute the sentence's SHA and refuse on
  mismatch.

### 2.9 Source-anchor footnote
- Every resource whose `cpg-htn-source-anchor` extension is non-
  empty MUST render the source-anchor footnote at the end of the
  narrative under a closed format:
  > "Source: 2025 ACC/AHA Hypertension Guideline; recommendation
  > {record_id}; atomic unit {atomic_unit_id}; anchor
  > <code>{anchor_kind}</code>; SAIR
  > <code>{sair_sha256[:16]}…</code>; page {page}."
- The footnote MUST appear exactly once per narrative. Duplicates
  or omissions are a release blocker.

### 2.10 XHTML safety
- The output XHTML MUST satisfy the FHIR R5 narrative XHTML
  subset:
  - Only `<div>`, `<p>`, `<h2>`–`<h6>`, `<a>`, `<ul>`, `<ol>`,
    `<li>`, `<table>`, `<thead>`, `<tbody>`, `<tr>`, `<th>`,
    `<td>`, `<code>`, `<pre>`, `<blockquote>`, `<q>`, `<em>`,
    `<strong>`, `<br/>`, `<hr/>`, `<span>`, `<small>` elements.
  - No `<script>`, `<style>`, `<iframe>`, `<object>`, `<embed>`,
    `<form>`, `<input>`, `<button>`, `<svg>`, `<canvas>`.
  - No `style` attribute.
  - No `on*` event handlers.
  - No external resource URLs in `href` other than RFC-3986
    canonical-form URIs to FHIR Reference targets and to the
    framework's `https://aiwg.io/cpg-htn-2025-acc-aha/...` URL
    space.
  - No inline base64-encoded data.
- The skill's renderer MUST validate every produced narrative
  against this subset; violations BLOCK with
  `narrative-xhtml-violation`.

### 2.11 Deterministic timestamps
- Templates MUST NOT embed wall-clock timestamps in the narrative
  (e.g., "rendered at 2026-04-30 14:32:01 UTC"). Where a timestamp
  is required for human reference, the template substitutes
  `{build_version_label}` (e.g., `v1.0.0+ACC-AHA-2025+US+2026-04-30`),
  which is deterministic from the build pin.

### 2.12 Length bounds (per template)
- Every template declares a `max_chars_after_substitution` integer.
  Renderings exceeding the bound BLOCK with
  `narrative-length-exceeded`. Bounds are listed per template in §3.

### 2.13 Localization
- The framework's published narratives are English-only at v1.0.0.
  Localization to other languages is out of scope for v1.0.0 and
  routes through a manifest-version-level amendment with a
  per-language template pack. Validators MUST refuse non-English
  narrative content at v1.0.0.

---

## 3. Template definitions (closed)

Each template below is normative. The substitution variables are
listed exhaustively; templates MUST refuse undeclared variables.
The XHTML is shown with `{variable}` placeholders that the renderer
substitutes at composition time.

> **Notation.** All templates wrap their output in
> `<div xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml">…</div>` (FHIR R5
> requires this exact namespace declaration).

> **Legend (status):**
> - **enum-substitution**: variable value MUST be a member of the
>   declared closed enum.
> - **byte-verbatim**: variable value is byte-for-byte from
>   upstream (no transformation).
> - **id-substitution**: variable value is a deterministic id from
>   the framework's id-derivation rules.
> - **hash-prefix-substitution**: variable value is the first 16
>   hex characters of a SHA-256.
> - **list-substitution**: variable value is a comma-joined list
>   from a closed enum.

</div>

#### Template

```xhtml

## 4. Renderer-side validation (mechanical)

For every resource, the renderer MUST run the following validation
sequence in order. Any failure BLOCKs the IG build with the
specific gate diagnostic.

1. **Template id resolution.** The template id MUST be in the
   closed set in §1. Unknown id → BLOCK with
   `narrative-template-unknown`.
2. **Substitution variable closure.** Every variable referenced in
   the rendered output MUST be in the template's declared variable
   list. Undeclared variable → BLOCK with
   `narrative-undeclared-variable`.
3. **Closed-enum membership.** Every variable of kind
   `enum-substitution` MUST be a member of its declared closed
   enum. Mismatch → BLOCK with `narrative-enum-violation`.
4. **Verbatim-clinical-text round-trip.** Every variable of kind
   `byte-verbatim` whose origin is clinical text MUST round-trip
   byte-for-byte against the parent atomic unit's `text_verbatim`
   after Phase-2 reversible normalization. Mismatch → BLOCK with
   `narrative-verbatim-mismatch`.
5. **AttendingOverridePattern scan.** Recursive scan over the
   rendered XHTML (and over every substitution variable's value)
   for the closed pattern set. Match → BLOCK with
   `attending-override-pattern-detected`.
6. **PCE-legacy literal scan.** Recursive scan for the literal
   `PCE-legacy`. Match → BLOCK with `pce-legacy-binding-detected`.
7. **Age-gate sentence presence.** When the resource is
   population-bounded, the literal age-gate sentence (§2.7) MUST be
   present exactly once. Absence or mutation → BLOCK with
   `age-gate-sentence-missing`.
8. **Pregnancy hard-refuse sentence.** When the resource is a
   pregnancy denylist (per the source rule's
   `population_filter[]` containing `pregnant`/`postpartum` AND
   `kind == "denylist"`), the literal pregnancy hard-refuse
   sentence (§2.8) MUST be present exactly once. Absence or
   mutation → BLOCK with
   `pregnancy-hard-refuse-sentence-missing`.
9. **Source-anchor footnote presence.** When the resource carries a
   non-empty `cpg-htn-source-anchor` extension, the source-anchor
   footnote (§2.9) MUST be present exactly once. Absence,
   duplication, or format mutation → BLOCK with
   `source-anchor-footnote-violation`.
10. **XHTML safety check.** The output MUST satisfy the FHIR R5
    narrative XHTML subset (§2.10). Violations → BLOCK with
    `narrative-xhtml-violation`.
11. **Length bound.** Output MUST NOT exceed
    `max_chars_after_substitution`. Excess → BLOCK with
    `narrative-length-exceeded`.
12. **Determinism check.** The renderer SHOULD be re-invoked with
    the same inputs and the two outputs MUST be byte-identical.
    Determinism check is mandatory at `--mode verify` and
    sampled at 1% of resources at `--mode build`. Mismatch → BLOCK
    with `narrative-non-deterministic`.

---

## 5. Change control

Any change to this document (template ids, substitution variable
sets, XHTML structure, age-gate sentence, pregnancy hard-refuse
sentence, source-anchor footnote format, validation sequence, or
length bounds) requires:

- A change-controlled diff with regression evaluation against the
  golden IG narrative set.
- Panel-chair signoff AND medical-director acknowledgement (since
  this document directly governs the human-readable surface of a
  safety-critical IG).
- Increment of the document's `Last reviewed` date and of the
  template-pack version pinned in
  `manifests/guideline-manifest-hbp-2025.<version>.yaml` —
  `tools_lock.items[]` of `kind == "fhir-r5-narrative-template-pack"`.
- Coordinated update of `fhir-implementation-guide-build` `SKILL.md`
  acceptance-test fixtures.
- ADR-HTN-001 amendment for any change affecting:
  - the closed template set (adding / removing templates),
  - the AttendingOverridePattern scan,
  - the PCE-legacy literal scan,
  - the age-gate sentence verbatim,
  - the pregnancy hard-refuse sentence verbatim,
  - the source-anchor footnote format,
  - the verbatim-clinical-text invariant,
  - the determinism check.

```markdown name=docs/acc-aha-to-hl7-certainty.md
# ACC/AHA → HL7 certainty mapping (`cpg-htn-2025-acc-aha`)

**Status:** stable
**Schema lifecycle:** stable
**Last reviewed:** HUMAN_FILL: ISO-8601 date of most recent panel review
**Authority:** ADR-HTN-001 D3 (native ACC/AHA grading preserved as primary)
**Owners:** `cpg-htn-2025-acc-aha` framework (panel chair + medical director)
**Consumers:** `extract-contraindications` (P14), `extract-monitoring`
(P15), `safety-hbp` (P23), `fhir-implementation-guide-build` (P26),
`docs/fhir-r5-narrative-templates.md`
**Pinned by:** `manifests/guideline-manifest-hbp-2025.<version>.yaml`
— `tools_lock.items[]` of `kind == "acc-aha-to-hl7-certainty-mapping-pack"`

---

## 0. Posture and scope

This document is the **closed normative mapping** between the
ACC/AHA grading enums (Class of Recommendation, COR; Level of
Evidence, LOE) and the HL7 R5 certainty CodeSystem
(`http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/certainty-rating` and
`http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/certainty-type`).

The framework's posture is that **ACC/AHA grading is preserved as
the primary rating system on every record, atomic unit, pharm rule,
contraindication, monitoring artifact, Safety Case mitigation, CDS
Hooks descriptor, FHIR Evidence/EvidenceVariable/EvidenceReport
resource, and IG narrative.** The HL7 mapping in this document is a
**secondary annotation** rendered alongside the primary grade for
interoperability with HL7-native tooling (the FHIR R5 IG Publisher,
republishers, EHR-side analytics surfaces, and the HL7 Care Plans
domain).

The mapping is **not** a downgrade or override path. The framework
NEVER substitutes an HL7 certainty rating for the ACC/AHA grade in
any clinical-decision surface. The HL7 rating is rendered as a
parenthetical or secondary line item, and the ACC/AHA grade
appears first in every narrative and in every structured field.

Posture: **caution over velocity, fidelity over coverage,
hard-refusal-on-pregnancy over convenience.** The mapping is
conservative: where two HL7 ratings could plausibly apply to the
same LOE, the framework chooses the more conservative (lower-
certainty) rating to avoid overstating confidence in the published
artifact. PCE-legacy is forbidden in every artifact; the mapping
makes no reference to it. The mapping does not relax COR III-Harm
recommendations; the pregnancy hard-block remains hard-refuse
regardless of the HL7 rating rendered alongside.

This document does not define the ACC/AHA grading enums (those are
in `schemas/acc-aha-grading.yaml`); it defines the **mapping** to
HL7 ratings. The two are complementary: the ACC/AHA grading is
the contract; the HL7 mapping is the interoperability annotation.

---

## 1. Source enums

### 1.1 ACC/AHA Class of Recommendation (COR)

Closed enum from `schemas/acc-aha-grading.yaml`:

| Code | Label |
|---|---|
| `I` | Strong (Benefit >>> Risk) |
| `IIa` | Moderate (Benefit >> Risk) |
| `IIb` | Weak (Benefit ≥ Risk) |
| `III-No-Benefit` | No Benefit (Benefit = Risk) |
| `III-Harm` | Harm (Risk > Benefit) |

### 1.2 ACC/AHA Level of Evidence (LOE)

Closed enum from `schemas/acc-aha-grading.yaml`:

| Code | Label |
|---|---|
| `A` | High-quality evidence from multiple RCTs or meta-analyses |
| `B-R` | Moderate-quality randomized evidence |
| `B-NR` | Moderate-quality nonrandomized evidence |
| `C-LD` | Limited data |
| `C-EO` | Expert opinion |

### 1.3 HL7 R5 certainty CodeSystem

Closed enum from
`http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/certainty-rating` (FHIR R5):

| Code | Label |
|---|---|
| `high` | High certainty |
| `moderate` | Moderate certainty |
| `low` | Low certainty |
| `very-low` | Very low certainty |
| `no-concern` | No serious concern |
| `serious-concern` | Serious concern |
| `very-serious-concern` | Very serious concern |
| `extremely-serious-concern` | Extremely serious concern |
| `present` | Present |
| `absent` | Absent |
| `no-change` | No change from baseline |
| `downgraded` | Downgraded |
| `upgraded` | Upgraded |

The framework uses only the first four codes (`high`, `moderate`,
`low`, `very-low`) for the canonical LOE → certainty mapping in
§3.1. The remaining codes (`*-concern`, `present`/`absent`,
`no-change`, `downgraded`, `upgraded`) are used for the
COR-domain mapping in §3.2 (concern domain) and for the
mitigation-effect mapping in §3.3.

### 1.4 HL7 R5 certainty type CodeSystem

Closed enum from
`http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/certainty-type` (FHIR R5):

| Code | Label |
|---|---|
| `Overall` | Overall certainty |
| `RiskOfBias` | Risk of bias |
| `Inconsistency` | Inconsistency |
| `Indirectness` | Indirectness |
| `Imprecision` | Imprecision |
| `PublicationBias` | Publication bias |
| `LargeEffect` | Large effect |
| `PlausibleConfounding` | Plausible confounding |
| `DoseResponseGradient` | Dose-response gradient |

The framework uses only `Overall` for the LOE → certainty mapping
in §3.1. The other types are reserved for downstream
fine-grained certainty annotations and are out of scope for the
canonical mapping.

---

## 2. Mapping policy (normative)

### 2.1 Primacy of ACC/AHA grading
- The ACC/AHA COR and LOE values are the **primary** rating system
  on every artifact and every narrative. They appear first; the HL7
  rating appears second as a parenthetical or secondary line item.
- The framework never substitutes an HL7 rating for the ACC/AHA
  grade in any structured field that drives clinical decisions
  (e.g., the Safety Case's mitigation grading, the contraindication
  artifact's `acc_aha_cor`/`acc_aha_loe`, the pharm rule's grading,
  the CDS Hooks descriptor's posture binding).

### 2.2 Conservative direction
- Where two HL7 certainty codes could plausibly apply to the same
  ACC/AHA LOE, the mapping chooses the **lower-certainty** code
  (e.g., `B-NR` maps to `moderate`, not `high`, because
  nonrandomized evidence does not warrant the highest certainty
  even when its volume is large).
- The framework's policy is conservative-by-construction: an
  artifact's published certainty is at most the mapping's value,
  never higher.

### 2.3 Closed mapping (no inference)
- The mapping in §3 is **closed**. Adding new ACC/AHA codes or new
  HL7 codes requires ADR-HTN-001 amendment under panel-chair
  signoff and a coordinated update of every parent schema and
  skill.
- Validators MUST refuse to render an HL7 certainty annotation for
  a value not in the closed mapping.

### 2.4 No relaxation of COR III-Harm
- The pregnancy hard-block (and every other COR III-Harm
  recommendation) is enforced as `hard-refuse` regardless of the
  HL7 certainty rating annotated alongside. The HL7 rating does not
  modify the posture; it is a documentation-only annotation.
- Validators MUST refuse to render an HL7 rating that contradicts
  the COR III-Harm posture (e.g., an HL7 `present` rating on a
  hard-refuse contraindication is permitted only as a
  domain-specific label, not as an indicator of permissive
  override).

### 2.5 PCE-legacy never appears
- The mapping makes no reference to PCE-legacy in any code,
  label, or rendering. The framework's policy is that PCE-legacy
  never appears in any published artifact (ADR-HTN-001 D5).

### 2.6 Reproducibility
- The mapping is byte-stable: identical (COR, LOE) inputs MUST
  produce identical (HL7 rating, HL7 type) outputs across every
  re-run. Validators recompute and compare; mismatch is a release
  blocker.

### 2.7 Display rendering
- Where the mapping is rendered as a narrative annotation (per
  `docs/fhir-r5-narrative-templates.md` §2.4), the rendering MUST
  be:
  > "ACC/AHA grading: COR <strong>{cor}</strong>, LOE
  > <strong>{loe}</strong> (primary). HL7 certainty rating:
  > <em>{hl7_certainty_rating}</em> (secondary)."
- The literal "(primary)" and "(secondary)" annotations are
  required and validators MUST refuse renderings that omit them.

---

## 3. Closed mappings

### 3.1 LOE → HL7 certainty rating (Overall type)

The canonical mapping for `Evidence.certainty` and
`Evidence.certainty.rating` (when `Evidence.certainty.type ==
"Overall"`):

| ACC/AHA LOE | HL7 certainty rating | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| `A` | `high` | High-quality evidence from multiple RCTs or meta-analyses; corresponds directly to HL7 `high`. |
| `B-R` | `moderate` | Moderate-quality randomized evidence; one or more RCTs but not pooled across multiple studies. |
| `B-NR` | `moderate` | Moderate-quality nonrandomized evidence; the framework chooses `moderate` (not `low`) because B-NR represents structured nonrandomized study designs (registries, observational studies with rigorous methods); the conservative direction precludes `high` even where the underlying evidence is voluminous. |
| `C-LD` | `low` | Limited data; small studies or limited generalizability; corresponds to HL7 `low`. |
| `C-EO` | `very-low` | Expert opinion only; no empirical evidence base; corresponds to HL7 `very-low`. |

The mapping is total and disjoint: every LOE has exactly one HL7
rating, and the ratings are distinct across LOE values where the
clinical certainty differs (i.e., `A`, `C-LD`, `C-EO` are uniquely
mapped; `B-R` and `B-NR` collapse to `moderate` to satisfy §2.2).

#### 3.1.1 FHIR R5 representation

In the IG's `Evidence.certainty[]`:

```json
{
  "type": {
    "coding": [
      {
        "system": "http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/certainty-type",
        "code": "Overall"
      }
    ]
  },
  "rating": {
    "coding": [
      {
        "system": "http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/certainty-rating",
        "code": "<from §3.1 mapping>"
      }
    ]
  },
  "note": [
    {
      "text": "ACC/AHA COR <cor>; LOE <loe>; native grading preserved as primary per ADR-HTN-001 D3."
    }
  ]
}
```

### 3.2 COR → HL7 concern domain (informational)

When the framework renders a COR-domain annotation (e.g., for COR
III-Harm contraindications, where the concern domain is more
informative than the certainty rating alone), the mapping is:

| ACC/AHA COR | HL7 certainty rating | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `I` | `no-concern` | Strong recommendation; benefit clearly outweighs risk. |
| `IIa` | `no-concern` | Moderate recommendation; benefit outweighs risk. |
| `IIb` | `serious-concern` | Weak recommendation; benefit balances risk; clinician concern about applicability is appropriate. |
| `III-No-Benefit` | `serious-concern` | No benefit; concern about exposing patient to a treatment without expected benefit. |
| `III-Harm` | `extremely-serious-concern` | Harm; concern that the treatment causes harm. |

This mapping is rendered ONLY when the framework's narrative or
structured field calls for a concern-domain annotation. It is
NOT a substitute for the LOE → rating mapping in §3.1.

#### 3.2.1 FHIR R5 representation

In a separate `Evidence.certainty[]` entry alongside the §3.1 entry:

```json
{
  "type": {
    "coding": [
      {
        "system": "http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/certainty-type",
        "code": "Overall"
      }
    ]
  },
  "rating": {
    "coding": [
      {
        "system": "http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/certainty-rating",
        "code": "<from §3.2 mapping>"
      }
    ]
  },
  "note": [
    {
      "text": "ACC/AHA COR <cor>; concern-domain annotation; primary grading is COR <cor>, LOE <loe>."
    }
  ]
}
```

### 3.3 Mitigation effect direction (Safety Case)

When the framework's Safety Case (`safety-hbp` at P23) records a
mitigation's effect on the residual likelihood of a hazard, the
mapping is:

| Mitigation effect | HL7 certainty rating | Use |
|---|---|---|
| Reduces likelihood significantly | `downgraded` | Mitigation is verified to reduce the hazard's likelihood by ≥ 1 ordinal class. |
| Reduces likelihood marginally | `no-change` | Mitigation is verified but the residual likelihood class does not change (rare; typical for monitoring-only mitigations). |
| Increases likelihood (never permitted) | `upgraded` | Reserved; the framework forbids mitigations that increase likelihood. Validators MUST refuse this rating in any Safety Case. |

The Safety Case's mitigation effect direction is recorded as a
`Provenance.signature` annotation on the corresponding mitigation
resource, NOT in the public-facing IG narrative. The narrative
renders only the LOE → rating mapping in §3.1 and (when
applicable) the COR → concern mapping in §3.2.

---

## 4. Cross-mapping invariants

Validators MUST enforce the following invariants at every render
of an HL7 certainty annotation:

### 4.1 LOE-to-rating closure
- Every (COR, LOE) pair from `schemas/acc-aha-grading.yaml` MUST
  produce exactly one (HL7 rating, HL7 type) pair under §3.1.
- Pairs not in the closed mapping → BLOCK with
  `acc-aha-to-hl7-mapping-violation`.

### 4.2 No-relaxation invariant
- For every artifact whose `acc_aha_cor == "III-Harm"`, the
  framework's policy is that the posture remains `hard-refuse`
  regardless of the HL7 rating. Validators MUST recompute the
  posture from `acc_aha_cor` and refuse any artifact whose posture
  has been mutated based on the HL7 rating.

### 4.3 Conservative-direction invariant
- For every (COR, LOE) pair, the framework's HL7 rating MUST be
  ≤ the rating an alternative mapping (e.g., a maximum-confidence
  mapping) would produce. Validators MUST recompute against the
  golden mapping table and refuse renderings that exceed the
  conservative bound.

### 4.4 Mapping-pack pinning
- The active manifest's `tools_lock.items[]` MUST contain a
  `kind == "acc-aha-to-hl7-certainty-mapping-pack"` entry whose
  `version` matches this document's version. Drift between the
  manifest pin and this document → BLOCK with
  `mapping-pack-pin-drift`.

### 4.5 Display rendering invariant
- Every HL7 rating annotation MUST be rendered with the literal
  "(primary)"/"(secondary)" annotation per §2.7. Renderings that
  omit either annotation → BLOCK with
  `mapping-display-annotation-missing`.

### 4.6 PCE-legacy literal absent
- The mapping document MUST NOT contain the literal `PCE-legacy`.
  Validators MUST recompute the document's hash and refuse
  documents that contain the literal.

### 4.7 Unicode-stable comparison
- All text comparisons (LOE codes, COR codes, HL7 codes, label
  strings) MUST be performed under Unicode NFC. Mismatch in
  normalization is a release blocker.

### 4.8 Closed mapping is total and disjoint
- §3.1 is total over all LOE values from
  `schemas/acc-aha-grading.yaml` and disjoint
  (every LOE maps to exactly one rating).
- §3.2 is total over all COR values and disjoint
  (every COR maps to exactly one rating).
- §3.3 is partial (only the three closed effect directions).
- Validators MUST refuse mappings that are not total or not
  disjoint.

### 4.9 Determinism
- The (COR, LOE) → (HL7 rating, HL7 type) function MUST be
  byte-stable across re-runs. Validators MUST recompute and
  compare.

### 4.10 Audit trail
- Every produced HL7 certainty annotation MUST be accompanied by a
  `Provenance.signature` entry with `signature.type ==
  "fixity-recorded"` and `signature.data ==` the SHA-256 of the
  mapping document at production time. Drift between the recorded
  document SHA and the active mapping pack → BLOCK with
  `mapping-pack-drift`.

---

## 5. Per-field rendering rules

The mapping is rendered into FHIR R5 resources at the following
field positions:

| Resource type | Field position | Mapping section |
|---|---|---|
| `Evidence` (contraindication; P14) | `Evidence.certainty[]` | §3.1 (LOE → rating) AND §3.2 (COR → concern) for COR III-Harm; §3.1 only for other CORs |
| `Evidence` (monitoring; P15) | `Evidence.certainty[]` | §3.1 only |
| `Evidence` (record-level; P9) | `Evidence.certainty[]` | §3.1 only |
| `EvidenceReport` (Safety Case hazard; P23) | `EvidenceReport.note[]` | §3.1 (per cited rule); §3.3 (per mitigation; in `Provenance.signature` only) |
| `PlanDefinition.action[]` | `action.note` | §3.1 only |
| `ActivityDefinition` | `note[]` | §3.1 only |
| `ServiceDefinition` | `note[]` | §3.1 only |
| `Library` | `note[]` | §3.1 only |
| `Citation` | (not applicable; no certainty rating on citations) | — |
| `ValueSet` / `ConceptMap` / `Group` / `StructureDefinition` | (not applicable) | — |
| Narrative (`Resource.text.div`) | per `docs/fhir-r5-narrative-templates.md` §2.7 | §3.1 only |

---

## 6. Worked examples

The following examples illustrate the mapping in production
contexts. Every example shows the primary ACC/AHA grading and the
secondary HL7 annotation in the canonical display order.

### 6.1 Pregnancy hard-block (COR III-Harm, LOE B-NR)

**Primary (ACC/AHA):**
- COR: `III-Harm`
- LOE: `B-NR`

**Secondary (HL7):**
- §3.1 LOE → rating: `moderate`
- §3.2 COR → concern: `extremely-serious-concern`

**Narrative rendering:**
> "ACC/AHA grading: COR **III-Harm**, LOE **B-NR** (primary). HL7
> certainty rating: *moderate* (secondary). Concern domain:
> *extremely-serious-concern*. Posture: order-select hard refuse.
> Attending override: not permitted. Documentation-only override:
> not permitted."

**FHIR R5 `Evidence.certainty[]`:**
```json
[
  { "type": { "coding": [ { "system": "http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/certainty-type", "code": "Overall" } ] }, "rating": { "coding": [ { "system": "http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/certainty-rating", "code": "moderate" } ] }, "note": [ { "text": "ACC/AHA COR III-Harm; LOE B-NR; native grading preserved as primary per ADR-HTN-001 D3." } ] },
  { "type": { "coding": [ { "system": "http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/certainty-type", "code": "Overall" } ] }, "rating": { "coding": [ { "system": "http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/certainty-rating", "code": "extremely-serious-concern" } ] }, "note": [ { "text": "ACC/AHA COR III-Harm; concern-domain annotation; primary grading is COR III-Harm, LOE B-NR." } ] }
]
```

### 6.2 First-line selection (COR I, LOE A)

**Primary (ACC/AHA):**
- COR: `I`
- LOE: `A`

**Secondary (HL7):**
- §3.1 LOE → rating: `high`
- §3.2 COR → concern: `no-concern` (rendered only when the
  framework calls for a concern annotation; typically omitted on
  COR I recommendations to avoid clutter)

**Narrative rendering:**
> "ACC/AHA grading: COR **I**, LOE **A** (primary). HL7 certainty
> rating: *high* (secondary)."

### 6.3 Older-adult dose-modifier (COR IIa, LOE B-NR)

**Primary (ACC/AHA):**
- COR: `IIa`
- LOE: `B-NR`

**Secondary (HL7):**
- §3.1 LOE → rating: `moderate`
- §3.2 COR → concern: `no-concern` (omitted in narrative)

**Narrative rendering:**
> "ACC/AHA grading: COR **IIa**, LOE **B-NR** (primary). HL7
> certainty rating: *moderate* (secondary)."

### 6.4 Expert-opinion-based recommendation (COR IIb, LOE C-EO)

**Primary (ACC/AHA):**
- COR: `IIb`
- LOE: `C-EO`

**Secondary (HL7):**
- §3.1 LOE → rating: `very-low`
- §3.2 COR → concern: `serious-concern`

**Narrative rendering:**
> "ACC/AHA grading: COR **IIb**, LOE **C-EO** (primary). HL7
> certainty rating: *very-low* (secondary). Concern domain:
> *serious-concern*."

## 7. Change control

Any change to this document (the closed LOE → rating mapping in
§3.1, the closed COR → concern mapping in §3.2, the closed
mitigation-effect mapping in §3.3, the cross-mapping invariants
in §4, the per-field rendering rules in §5, or the rendering
display annotations) requires:

- A change-controlled diff with regression evaluation against the
  golden HL7 certainty annotation set across every IG resource
  type.
- Panel-chair signoff AND medical-director acknowledgement (since
  this document directly governs the published interoperability
  surface of a safety-critical IG).
- Increment of the document's `Last reviewed` date and of the
  mapping pack version pinned in
  `manifests/guideline-manifest-hbp-2025.<version>.yaml` —
  `tools_lock.items[]` of `kind ==
  "acc-aha-to-hl7-certainty-mapping-pack"`.
- Coordinated update of every consuming skill's acceptance-test
  fixtures (`extract-contraindications`, `extract-monitoring`,
  `safety-hbp`, `fhir-implementation-guide-build`).
- ADR-HTN-001 amendment for any change affecting:
  - the LOE → rating mapping (any addition, removal, or change of
    a target rating),
  - the COR → concern mapping,
  - the mitigation-effect mapping,
  - the conservative-direction policy (§2.2),
  - the no-relaxation invariant (§2.4),
  - the primacy-of-ACC/AHA-grading policy (§2.1),
  - the closed-mapping property (§2.3),
  - the rendering display annotations (§2.7).
